BURHAN:v2p232/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p232/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p232/r5.claim: Singular forms also occur in descriptions of groups, including junub, ẓahīr, najiyy, and the generic singular al-ṭifl.
BURHAN:v2p232/r5.anchor: وفي الوصف كقوله تعالى ﴿ وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا ﴾ وقوله ﴿ والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير ﴾

ITQAN:v1p59/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p59/r11.speaker: الأسلع بن شريك
ITQAN:v1p59/r11.claim: Al-Aslaʿ ibn Sharīk reports that the tayammum verse in al-Nisāʾ was revealed on one of the Prophet’s journeys.
ITQAN:v1p59/r11.anchor: آية التيمم في النساء أخرج ابن مردويه عن الأسلع بن شريك أنها نزلت في بعض أسفار النبي

ITQAN:v1p60/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p60/r9.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v1p60/r9.claim: Aisha's report in the Sahih says the tayammum verse was revealed at al-Bayda while they were entering Medina, also phrased as al-Bayda or Dhat al-Jaysh.
ITQAN:v1p60/r9.anchor: في الصحيح عن عائشة أنها نزلت بالبيداء وهم داخلون المدينة وفي لفظ بالبيداء أو بذات الجيش

ITQAN:v1p60/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p60/r10.speaker: ابن عبد البر
ITQAN:v1p60/r10.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says the incident occurred during the Banu al-Mustaliq campaign; Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Hibban preceded him, while some later scholars object because of the locations Aisha names.
ITQAN:v1p60/r10.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر في التمهيد يقال إنه كان في غزوة بني المصطلق وجزم به في الاستذكار وسبقه إلى ذلك ابن سعد وابن حبان

ITQAN:v1p60/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p60/r11.speaker: أبو عبيد البكري
ITQAN:v1p60/r11.claim: Abu Ubayd al-Bakri locates al-Bayda as the rise before Dhu al-Hulayfa on the Mecca road, and Dhat al-Jaysh a day's post from Medina.
ITQAN:v1p60/r11.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد البكري البيداء هو الشرف الذي قدام ذي الحليفة من طريق مكة قال وذات الجيش من المدينة على بريد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r6.claim: The Qur'anic list includes ب as a particle that completes the expression; examples include wiping the face, wiping the head, and growing with oil.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r6.anchor: صلة في الكلام : ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.claim: Clay can serve as a place of prayer, and its elements, water and earth, purify ritually; fire instead is a means of punishment in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.anchor: water and earth—that serve as a means of ritual purification (see 4:43; 5:6), not fire

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r1.claim: One interpretation supplies an omitted مضاف: ‘the places of prayer,’ meaning mosques; the exception for crossing a path supports this in one reading.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r1.anchor: أن في الكلام حذف مضاف تقديره: مواضع الصلاة، والمراد بمواضعها المساجد

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r2.claim: Alternatively, there is no ellipsis: the prohibition concerns approaching prayer itself in this state.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه لا حذف، والنهي عن قربان نفس الصلاة في هذه الحالة.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r3.claim: أنتم سكارى is a subject–predicate clause functioning as a circumstantial clause of the subject of تقربوا.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r3.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر في محل نصب على الحال من فاعل " تقربوا ".

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r4.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r4.claim: The majority read سكارى with damma on sīn and alif; the author prefers analyzing it as a broken plural, as Sibawayh does.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: " سكارى " بضم السين وألف بعد الكاف، وفيه قولان، أحدهما: وهو الصحيح أنه جمع تكسير، نص عليه سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r5.speaker: ابن الباذش
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r5.claim: Ibn al-Badhish attributes to Sibawayh the alternative analysis that سكارى is a collective noun, arguing no plural pattern has this form.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r5.anchor: وزعم ابن الباذش أنه مذهب سيبويه، قال: " وهو القياس لأنه لم يأت من أبنية الجمع شيء على هذا الوزن ".

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r6.speaker: السيرافي
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r6.claim: Al-Sirafi records the disagreement and favors analyzing سكارى as a broken plural.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r6.anchor: وذكر السيرافي الخلاف، ورجح كونه تكسيرا.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r7.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r7.claim: Al-A'mash reads سكرى with damma on sīn and a still kāf, construing it as a feminine singular adjective on فعلى applied to a group.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: " سكرى " بضم السين وسكون الكاف/، وتوجيهها أنها صفة على فعلى كحبلى

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports جناح بن حبيش’s paired forms كسلى/كسلى, with the kāf rounded and open, as comparable adjective usage.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r8.anchor: وحكى جناح بن حبيش: " كسلى وكسلى " بضم الكاف وفتحها. قاله الزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r9.speaker: النخعي
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r9.claim: Al-Nakha‘i reads سكرى with fatḥa on sīn and still kāf; it may be the same adjective for a group or a broken plural like جرحى, موتى, and هلكى by analogy for affliction; the discussion recalls 2:85.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r9.anchor: وقرأ النخعي: " سكرى " بفتح السين وسكون الكاف، وهذه تحتمل وجهين

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r10.claim: A further reading سكارى with fatḥa on sīn and alif is a broken plural, by analogy with ندمان/ندامى and عطشان/عطاشى.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r10.anchor: وقرىء " سكارى " بفتح السين، والألف، وهذا جمع تكسير نحو: ندمان وندامى وعطشان وعطاشى.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r11.claim: The root sense of السكر is closure: intoxication blocks the link between a person and reason; the term usually means loss of reason through drink, but can also describe anger, love, and similar causes.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r11.anchor: والسكر لغة: السد، ومنه قيل لما يعرض للمرء من شرب المسكر؛ لأنه يسد مابين المرء وعقله

SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r12.claim: The cited line’s repeated سكر witnesses metaphorical intoxication by love alongside literal wine intoxication.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r1.claim: The cited line continues with the question of how a youth intoxicated by both love and wine could recover.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r2.claim: سكر with fatḥa on sīn and still kāf means a water barrier; kasra on sīn names the obstructed place, while the form with both vowels open means intoxicating drink, cited in 16:67.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r2.anchor: والسكر بالفتح وسكون الكاف حبس الماء، وبكسر السين نفس الموضع المسدود، وأما " السكر " بفتحهما فما يسكر به من المشروب

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r3.claim: Another usage takes السكر with damma and still kāf as a barrier; the cited poem uses it for being on and treating blockage with blockage.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: السكر بضم السين وسكون الكاف السد أي: الحاجز بين الشيئين

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r4.claim: The root’s general meaning is obstruction: it describes sleep clouding a hawk’s eye and a river ceasing to flow.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r4.anchor: أن أصل المادة الدلالة على الانسداد

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r5.claim: حتى is a preposition meaning إلى, attached to the prohibitive verb; the following verb is subjunctive with أن understood.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r5.anchor: جارة بمعنى " إلى " ، فهي متعلقة بفعل النهي

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r6.claim: ما can be relative or an indefinite noun qualified by a clause, with an omitted resumptive pronoun on either analysis, or a verbal noun particle; omission on the last analysis is only required by Ibn al-Sarraj and his followers.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#2/r6.anchor: أن تكون بمعنى الذي، أو نكرة موصوفة، والعائد على هذين القولين محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r1.claim: جنبا is accusative as a circumstantial element coordinated with the preceding circumstantial clause; a single term coordinates with the sentence because it carries its meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r1.anchor: عطف المفرد على الجملة لما كانت في تأويله

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r2.claim: Repeating لا marks a separate prohibition for each state; prohibition under both states together is still stronger and more fitting.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r2.anchor: تنبيها على أن النهي عن قربان الصلاة مع كل واحدة من هذين الحالين على انفرادهما

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r3.claim: جنب derives from جنابة, ‘distance’; a person is so called either for being distant from purity or for lying beside and touching another.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r4.claim: The cited verse uses جنابة in the sense relevant to the term جنب.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that جنب has one form for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine because it behaves like the verbal noun الإجناب.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " لجريانه مجرى المصدر الذي هو الإجناب "

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r6.claim: Some Arabs also inflect جنب: dual جنبان, sound plural جنبون, and broken plural أجناب, like شلل.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#3/r6.anchor: ومن العرب من يثنيه فيقول: " جنبان " ويجمعه سلامة فيقول: " جنبون " وتكسيرا فيقول: " أجناب "

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r1.claim: One parse makes عابري a circumstantial exception governed by the prohibition: do not approach in janāba except while traveling or crossing a mosque, depending on the interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r1.anchor: أنه منصوب على الحال، فهو استثناء مفرغ، والعامل فيها فعل النهي، والتقدير: لا تقربوا الصلاة في حال الجنابة

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the exception as a circumstantial phrase from the addressees generally, with travel as an additional excuse and crossing the path as its expression.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: { إلا عابري سبيل } استثناء من عامة أحوال المخاطبين

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, عابري describes جنبا, with إلا meaning غير: the prohibition concerns resident, unexcused people in janāba; this is clear if عبور means travel.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r3.anchor: صفة لقوله: " جنبا " وصفة ب " إلا " بمعنى " غير "

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r4.claim: If الصلاة means its locations, the phrase permits people in janāba to pass through mosques, because there is no other passage, or for another reason according to the disagreement.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r4.anchor: المعنى عنده: لاتقربوا المساجد جنبا إلا مجتازين

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r5.claim: العبور means passage; ناقة عبر الهواجر in the cited poetry attests the usage.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#4/r5.anchor: والعبور: الجواز، ومنه: " ناقة عبر الهواجر "

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r1.claim: حتى تغتسلوا has the same syntax as حتى تعلموا: حتى is attached to the prohibitive verb.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r1.anchor: وقوله: { حتى تغتسلوا } كقوله: { حتى تعلموا } فهي متعلقة بفعل النهي.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r2.claim: The Sheikh coordinates على سفر, جاء أحد, and لامستم with the predicate مرضى of كان, and infers that كان may take a past-tense verbal predicate without قد.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r2.anchor: كذا استدل به الشيخ، ولا دليل فيه لاحتمال أن يكون

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r3.claim: The author says the Sheikh’s inference is not decisive: Abu al-Baqa’s alternative coordinates جاء with كنتم and construes it as وإن جاء, a more evident parse.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r3.anchor: وإليه ذهب أبو البقاء وهو أظهر من الأول

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r4.claim: منكم is an adjective of أحد in the nominative, attached to an omitted element; من الغائط attaches to جاء as its object.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r4.anchor: و " من الغائط " متعلق ب " جاء " ، فهو مفعوله.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r5.claim: The majority form الغائط originally means low-lying ground, then euphemistically denotes the bodily event; غاط means going far out of sight, whereas تغوط means defecating.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: " الغائط " بزنة فاعل، وهو المكان المطمئن من الأرض، ثم عبر به عن نفس الحدث كناية للاستحياء

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r6.claim: Ibn Masud reads الغيط; Ibn Jinni analyzes it as a shortened فيعل form, like هين and ميت.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: " من الغيط " وفيه قولان، أحدهما: وإليه ذهب ابن جني أنه مخفف من فيعل

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r7.claim: A second analysis treats الغيط as a verbal noun, with dialect forms غاط يغيط غيطا and غاط يغوط غوطا.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r7.anchor: غاط يغيط غيطا، وغاط يغوط غوطا.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa calls الغيط a verbal noun of يغوط and explains its yāʾ as substituted wāw; the author objects that he missed the distinct yāʾ dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r8.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " هو مصدر " يغوط " فكان القياس

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r9.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r9.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read لمستم here and in 5:6; the others read لامستم.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان هنا وفي المائدة: " لمستم " والباقون: " لامستم "

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r10.claim: One interpretation makes فاعل equivalent to a simple verb; another says لمس means intercourse while لامس denotes touching short of intercourse.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r10.anchor: وقيل: لمس: جامع، ولامس لما دون الجماع.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r1.claim: The فَ in فلم تجدوا coordinates what follows with the conditional clause.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r1.anchor: الفاء عطفت ما بعدها على الشرط.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa instead attaches فلم تجدوا to جاء, since on his analysis جاء coordinates with كنتم and itself forms the condition.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " على جاء " ، لأنه جعل " جاء " عطفا على " كنتم " فهو شرط عنده.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r3.claim: The فَ in فتيمموا is the response to the condition.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r3.anchor: والفاء في قوله " فتيمموا " هي جواب الشرط

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r4.claim: The command’s pronoun covers every previously named person: the sick, traveler, one coming from the toilet, and one who touched or was touched.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r4.anchor: والضمير في " تيمموا " لكل من تقدم من مريض ومسافر ومتغوط وملامس أو لامس

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r5.claim: The shift to third person euphemistically avoids directly naming an embarrassing act; the source calls this elegant expression and compares 26:80.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r5.anchor: وما أحسن ما أتى هنا بالغيبة لأنه كناية عما يستحيا منه فلم يخاطبهم به

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r6.claim: وجد here means لقي and therefore takes one object.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r6.anchor: و " وجد " هنا بمعنى " لقي " فتعدت لواحد

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r7.claim: صعيدا is the direct object of تيمموا, meaning ‘intend’; the proposed analysis with an omitted preposition is not a valid analogy.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r7.anchor: و " صعيدا " مفعول به لقوله: " تيمموا " أي: اقصدوا، وقيل: هو على إسقاط حرف

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r8.claim: بوجوهكم attaches to امسحوا; Abu al-Baqa regards the preposition باء as extra.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r8.anchor: وهذه الباء تحتمل أن تكون زائدة، وبه قال أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r9.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r9.claim: Alternatively, باء is transitive: Sibawayh records مسحت رأسه وبرأسه, like نصحته ونصحت له.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r9.anchor: لأن سيبويه حكى: " مسحت رأسه وبرأسه " فيكون من باب: نصحته ونصحت له.

SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r10.claim: The object being wiped is omitted here and stated in 5:6 with منه, so this wording is understood in light of that verse.
SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r10.anchor: وحذف الممسوح به، وقد ظهر في آية المائدة في قوله " منه " فحمل عليه هذا.

ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r3.speaker: أصحاب النبي
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r3.claim: An occasion report says this verse preceded wine's final prohibition: companions drank, one led prayer and recited the opening of Sūrat al-Kāfirūn incorrectly, so the ban on approaching prayer while drunk was revealed.
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r3.anchor: قيل في التفسير: إنها نزلت قبل تحريم الخمر، لأن جماعة من أصحاب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - اجتمعوا فشربوا الخمر فبل تحريمها

ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r4.claim: A report has ʿUmar pray for God's command about wine because it harms reason and destroys wealth; the wine prohibition in al-Māʾida then came.
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r4.anchor: ويروى أن عمر بن الخطاب قال: اللهم إن الخمر تضر بالعقول. وتذهب بالمال، فأنزل فيها أمرك فنزل في سورة المائدة

ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r5.claim: Wine is textually forbidden because it is called sin in 2:219 and God forbids sin in 7:33; first the drunk were barred from prayer, then intoxication was prohibited, as the community agrees.
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r5.anchor: التحريم نص بقوله - عز وجل - (قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق).

ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r6.claim: The initial command barred a drunken person from prayer; later prohibition of intoxication is established by consensus, and Zajjāj says drunkenness was always forbidden.
ZAJJAJ:v2p54/r6.anchor: فأمر الله - عز وجل - في ذلك الوقت ألا يقرب الصلاة السكران وحرم بعد ذلك السكر

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r1.claim: A junub person must not approach prayer except as a traveler, since travelers may lack water; the same allowance applies to a sick person harmed by bathing.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r1.anchor: أي لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم جنب، إلا عابري سبيل، أي إلا مسافرين لأن المسافر يعوزه الماء، وكذلك المريض الذي يضر به الغسل.

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r2.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r2.claim: Another view takes the prohibition as not entering a place of prayer; it means do not pray while junub unless water is unavailable or bathing would cause serious harm, which occurs only in illness.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: لاتقربوا موضع الصلاة، حقيقته: لا تصلوا إذا كنتم جنبا حتى تغتسلوا، إلا أن لا تقدروا على الماء، وإلا أن تخافوا أن يضركم الغسل إضرارا شديدا

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r3.speaker: النبي
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r3.claim: A report says people washed a man with a severe skin disease and he died; the Prophet condemned them and said dry ablution would have sufficed.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r3.anchor: ويروى أن قوما غسلوا مجدرا فمات، فقال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: قتلوه قتلهم الله، كان يجزيه التيمم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r4.claim: Tayammam means to intend or head toward something, and ṣaʿīd is the face or surface of the earth.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r4.anchor: معنى تيمموا أقصدوا، والصعيد وجه الأرض.

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r5.claim: For dry ablution, strike the hands once and wipe the face with both, then strike again and wipe both hands.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r5.anchor: فعلى الإنسان في التيمم أن يضرب بيديه ضربة واحدة فيمسح بهما جميعا وجهه، وكذلك يضرب ضربة واحدة، فيمسح بهما يديه

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r6.claim: Ṭayyib means clean and pure; ṣaʿīd is any ground surface, not specifically soil, so bare rock can serve for dry ablution.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r6.anchor: والطيب هو النظيف الطاهر، ولا يبالي أكان في الموضع تراب أم لا، لأن الصعيد ليس هو التراب، إنما هو وجه الأرض، ترابا كان أو غيره.

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r7.claim: The ground becoming slippery in 18:40 shows that ṣaʿīd can be slick; ṣaʿadāt also means roads.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r7.anchor: قال الله عز وجل -: (فتصبح صعيدا زلقا) فأعلمك أن الصعيد يكون زلقا، والصعدات الطرقات.

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r8.claim: Ṣaʿīd is the highest surface reached by ascending from within the earth; language scholars agree it means the face of the earth.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r8.anchor: وإنما سمي صعيدا، لأنها نهاية ما يصعد إليه من باطن الأرض، لا أعلم بين أهل اللغة اختلافا في أن الصعيد وجه الأرض.

ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r9.claim: God accepts the concession and forgives; accepting dry ablution makes matters easier.
ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r9.anchor: أي يقبل منكم العفو ويغفر لكم، لأن قبوله التيمم تسهيل عليكم.

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r1.claim: The prayer instruction follows the Judgment Day discussion: prayer is an earthly spiritual encounter with God that reminds people of their responsibility to the Creator.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r1.anchor: The reference to prayer at this place arises from the mention, in the preceding verses, of the Day of Judgment, when man will have to answer before God for what he did during his life in this world

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r2.speaker: some of the commentators
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r2.claim: Some commentators regard the ban on praying drunk as an initial stage of total intoxicant prohibition, later abrogated by 5:90.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r2.anchor: some of the commentators assume that this ordinance represented the first stage of the total prohibition of intoxicants, and has been, consequently, "abrogated" by the promulgation of the law of total abstinence from all intoxicants (5:90).

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r3.claim: Asad rejects abrogation as untenable and says nothing warrants treating this continuing safeguard as redundant after the general intoxicant ban; he also rejects the abrogation doctrine in 2:106.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r3.anchor: the doctrine of "abrogation" is entirely untenable (see surah 2, verse 106), there is no warrant whatever for regarding the above verse as a "first step" which has become redundant

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r4.claim: Because people remain vulnerable to lapses, this verse prevents adding sinful prayer while drunk to the separate sin of using intoxicants.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r4.anchor: since "man has been created weak" (4:28), his lapse from the way of virtue is always a possibility: and it is to prevent him from adding the sin of praying while in a state of drunkenness to the sin of using intoxicants as such

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r5.claim: Sukr covers any mental disequilibrium, including drugs, giddiness, passion, or metaphorical drunkenness from sleep, not only alcohol.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r5.anchor: the expression "while you are in a state of drunkenness (sukara)" does not apply exclusively to alcoholic intoxication, since the term sukr, in its wider connotation, signifies any state of mental disequilibrium

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r6.claim: Since worship requires consciousness, prayer is allowed only when a person has full mental faculties and knows what they are saying.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n54/r6.anchor: the Qur'an insists throughout on consciousness as an indispensable element in every act of worship, prayer is permitted only when man is in full possession of his mental faculties and "knows what he is saying".

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n55/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n55/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n55/r1.claim: Junub describes the state after sexual intercourse; from janaba, “to make remote,” it denotes distance from prayer due to immersion in sexual passion.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n55/r1.anchor: The term junub (rendered by me as "in a state requiring total ablution") is derived from the verb janaba, "he made (a thing) remote", and signifies one's remoteness from prayer because of immersion in sexual passion.

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n56/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n56/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n56/r1.claim: The phrase literally refers to coming from the place where one relieves oneself.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n56/r1.anchor: Lit., "if one of you comes from the place in which one satisfies...", etc.

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r1.claim: Tayammum is performed by touching earth or a dust-bearing substance with the palms, then lightly wiping the face and hands.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r1.anchor: This symbolic ablution, called tayammum, consists in touching the earth, or anything supposed to contain dust, with the palms of one's hands and then passing them lightly over face and hands.

ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r2.claim: When water is unavailable or cannot be used due to illness, tayammum replaces both the full bath after intercourse and the partial pre-prayer ablution.
ASAD-NOTES:4:43#n57/r2.anchor: Whenever water is not within reach - or cannot be used because of illness - the tayammum takes the place of both the total ablution after sexual intercourse (ghusl) and the partial ablution before prayers (wudu).

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r7.claim: Al-Ma'idah details the full ablution and tayammum rulings, so it adds “from it” for clarification; al-Nisa' gives only some rulings and aptly leaves the phrase out.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r7.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه حيث كان السياق مجملاً أجمل في الذكر، وحيث كان مفصّلاً مبيناً زاد وبيّن

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r8.speaker: الكرماني
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r8.claim: Al-Kirmani likewise says al-Nisa' mentions only some ablution and tayammum rulings, making omission apt, while al-Ma'idah gives all the rulings and therefore states the phrase.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r8.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني: أنه اد في آية المائدة (منه)

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r1.claim: These readers read lāmastum with alif here and at 5:6.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر: أو لامستم بألف هاهنا، وفي المائدة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read lamastum without alif here and in al-Māʾida.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: لمستم بغير ألف، وفي المائدة مثله

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r3.claim: Touch can mean hand contact or extend beyond physical contact; Qurʾānic uses of touching heaven and a book show the broader sense, while ‘with their hands’ disambiguates the latter.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: اللمس يكون باليد، وقد اتسع فيه فأوقع على غيره

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r4.speaker: عمر وعلي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r4.claim: According to ʿUmar and ʿAlī, seclusion can have the legal standing of touch.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r4.anchor: وذاك أن الخلوة قد تكون في حكم المس في قول عمر وعلي

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r5.speaker: الصحابة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r5.claim: The Companions split between hand contact and intercourse; none combined the meanings, so interpreting both violates their agreement.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p163/r5.anchor: واختلف الصحابة في قوله: أو لامستم النساء على قولين: فحمله حاملون على المس باليد

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r5.claim: The form with alif makes the action mutual between man and woman; Arabic uses the reciprocal pattern in jāmaʿtu al-marʾa, not jamaʿtu.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r5.anchor: فالحجة لمن أثبتها أنه جعل الفعل للرجل والمرأة ودليله أن فعل الاثنين لم يأت عن فصحاء العرب إلا ب فاعلت

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r6.claim: Without alif, the verb is an action by the man alone, as in the wording if you marry believing women.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p124/r6.anchor: والحجة لمن طرحها أنه جعلها فعلا للرجل دون المرأة ودليله قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ﴾ ولم يقل ناكحتم

NASHR:v2p249/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p249/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p249/r4.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read without alif in both places; the others read with alif.
NASHR:v2p249/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بغير ألف فيهما، وقرأ الباقون فيهما بالألف

QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#1/r1.claim: Hamza elision in jāʾa with compensatory lengthening yields jā; this is canonical in the Seven readings.
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#1/r1.anchor: Hamza elision with compensatory lengthening — jāʾa becomes jā by dropping the hamza

QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#2/r1.claim: This variant softens or elides the initial hamza of aḥad while retaining the hamza of jāʾa.
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#2/r1.anchor: Hamza modification on aḥad — the initial hamza of aḥad is softened or elided

QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#3/r1.claim: Eliding hamza at the junction merges the two hamzas into a lengthened ā through canonical phonetic assimilation.
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#3/r1.anchor: Hamza elision with compensatory madd (lengthening) — the two hamzas at the junction merge

QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#4/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#4/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#4/r1.claim: Imāla tilts the fatḥa on jīm toward kasra, producing a sound between ja and ji for certain canonical readers.
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#4/r1.anchor: Imāla (vowel tilting) — the fatḥa on jīm tilts toward kasra

QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r1.speaker: Ḥamza and Kisāʾī
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r1.claim: Ḥamza and Kisāʾī read Form I lamasa instead of Form III lāmasa, removing the reciprocal morpheme and indicating one-sided touching.
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r1.anchor: reading of Ḥamza and Kisāʾī. Legally significant: Form I = one-sided touching

QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r2.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r2.speaker: Shāfiʿī
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r2.claim: The Shāfiʿī view takes Form I as one-sided touching, so any skin contact breaks wuḍūʾ.
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r2.anchor: Shāfiʿī: any skin contact breaks wuḍūʾ

QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r3.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r3.speaker: Ḥanafī
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r3.claim: The Ḥanafī view takes Form III mutual engagement as a euphemism for intercourse.
QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1/r3.anchor: Form III = mutual engagement (Ḥanafī: euphemism for intercourse)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r1.claim: Qatada says people avoided intoxication when prayer approached until this rule was abrogated by the prohibition of wine.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى ﴾ قال كانوا يجتنبون السكر عند حضور الصلوات ثم نسخت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r2.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r2.claim: Qatada and Mujahid say a traveler who becomes junub may perform tayammum and pray.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r2.anchor: عن قتادة وابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل ﴾ قالا هو الرجل يكون في السفر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allah b. Masʿud says the exception means a junub person passing through a mosque.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p163/r3.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود عن أبيه قال هو المار في المسجد

MUSLIM:816/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:816/r1.speaker: عائشة
MUSLIM:816/r1.claim: Aisha reports that her lost necklace halted the traveling party without water; God then revealed the tayammum verse, and the necklace was found beneath her camel.
MUSLIM:816/r1.anchor: قالت عائشة فبعثنا البعير الذي كنت عليه فوجدنا العقد تحته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r9.claim: سكر is blocked discernment from intoxicating drink, likened to an eye covered by sleep or a river whose channels are blocked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r9.anchor: السكر: انسداد طريق التمييز بشرب ما يسكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r10.claim: The noun سُكر can also mean a dam or blockage, while سَكر means an intoxicating substance that prevents discernment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r11.claim: A drinking poem plays on السكر as a stoppage or drunkenness in the phrase نداوي السكر بالسكر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r11.anchor: فما زلنا على الشرب ... نداوي السكر بالسكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r12.claim: الغائط means low ground; its plural is غيطان, with the variants غيط and غوط also reported.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r12.anchor: الغائط: ما انخفض من الأرض، وجمعه غيطان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r13.speaker: ابن جني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r13.claim: Ibn Jinnī analyzes غيط as فعيل from غيط, analogizing it to هين and سيد when reduced.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r13.anchor: وزعم ابن جني: أن غيطا فعيل، إذ أصله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says غيط is properly فعل, like غوط, because Arabic uses both غاط يغوط and غاط يغيط; غوط pluralizes as أغواط.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r14.anchor: والصحيح: أنه فعل. كما أن غوطا فعل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r15.claim: The verb تغوط means to relieve oneself; غاط في الأرض means to sink until hidden from view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r15.anchor: غاط في الأرض يغيط ويغوط غاب فيها حتى لا يظهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r16.claim: The low ground where a man sought privacy for defecation lent its name to the act itself, as in metonymic expressions like a river running.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p641/r16.anchor: وكان الرجل إذا أراد التبرز ارتاد غائطا من الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r1.claim: One occasion report says Companions drank before prohibition; at prayer, their leader recited al-Kāfirūn incorrectly, prompting revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r1.anchor: روي إن جماعة من الصحابة شربوا الخمر قبل التحريم، وحانت صلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r2.claim: Another account connects revelation to ʿUmar’s second plea for clear guidance on wine; they drank after ʿIshāʾ until a third plea brought its absolute prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r2.anchor: وقيل: نزلت بسبب قول عمر ثانيا: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r3.claim: The majority regard this verse as still legally operative.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās considers the verse abrogated by the prohibition in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r4.anchor: وذهب ابن عباس إلى أنها منسوخة بآية المائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r5.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says the prayer clause was abrogated by the ablution verse: first they could delay prayer until sober, then were commanded to pray in every state, before wine was prohibited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r5.anchor: إن قوله لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى منسوخ بقوله: إذا قمتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls ʿIkrima’s account objectionable: this verse neither licenses wine nor allows prayer while drunk, so it was not abrogated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r6.anchor: وأعجب من هذا قول عكرمة: إن قوله لا تقربوا الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās argues that the address implies drinking was allowed, since it forbade only approaching prayer while drunk; the wine ban superseded that implication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r7.anchor: ووجه قول ابن عباس: أن مفهوم الخطاب يدل على جواز السكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r8.claim: The command follows worship, filial kindness, good conduct, condemnation of miserliness, and the afterlife digression: prayer needed protection from wine’s disruption.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r8.anchor: لما أمر تعالى بعبادة الله والإخلاص فيها، وأمر ببر الوالدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r9.claim: The command calls for prayer in its proper form, joining sincere worship of God with good conduct toward other people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r9.anchor: فأمر تعالى بإتيانها على وجهها دون ما يفسدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r10.claim: The address is to sober people: the intoxicated person lacking discernment is not then addressed, but upon sobering must fulfill duties missed while intoxicated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r10.anchor: والخطاب بقوله: يا أيها الذين آمنوا للصاحين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r11.claim: Requiring the sober person to make up duties does not impose the impossible, despite the contrary position held by some.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p647/r11.anchor: وليس في هذا تكليف ما لا يطاق على ما ذهب إليه بعض الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r1.claim: لا تقربوا الصلاة is stronger than لا تصلوا وأنتم سكارى: forbidding approach to prayer intensifies the prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r1.anchor: وبالغ تعالى في النهي عن أن يصلي المؤمن وهو سكران بقوله: لا تقربوا الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r2.claim: The emphatic construction parallels prohibitions against approaching adultery, indecencies, and an orphan’s property.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r2.anchor: ومنه: ولا تقربوا الزنى ولا تقربوا الفواحش ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r3.claim: The phrase means do not come to prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r3.anchor: والمعنى: لا تغشوا الصلاة. وقيل: هو على حذف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r4.claim: Some supply an omitted noun, “the places of prayer,” making this a prohibition on entering mosques.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو على حذف مضاف أي: لا تقربوا مواضع الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r5.claim: The places-of-prayer interpretation is supported by reading ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل as referring to mosques.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r5.anchor: لقوله: ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل على أحد التأويلين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r6.claim: The places intended are mosques, supported by a prophetic report instructing that children and madmen be kept from mosques.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r6.anchor: ومواضع الصلاة هي المساجد لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r7.claim: The majority understand سكارى as intoxicated from wine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r7.anchor: والجمهور على أن المراد: وأنتم سكارى من الخمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r8.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the phrase as drowsy from sleep, citing the Prophet’s instruction to sleep if drowsiness impairs prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك: المراد السكر من النوم، لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r9.speaker: عبيدة السلماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r9.claim: ʿUbayda al-Salmānī interprets it as needing to urinate, citing the prohibition on praying while holding urine and a version about compressing one’s thighs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r9.anchor: وقال عبيدة السلماني: المراد بقوله وأنتم سكارى إذا كنتم حاقنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Ḍaḥḥāk’s and ʿUbayda’s readings weak and remote; al-Qurṭubī says they are sound in meaning because distractions diminish attentiveness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r10.anchor: واستضعف قول الضحاك وعبيدة واستبعد. وقال القرطبي: قولهما صحيح المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r11.speaker: القرطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r11.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says prayer requires heart and body engagement, so sleep, urinary pressure, hunger, and other distractions should be removed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r11.anchor: لأن المطلوب من المصلي الإقبال على عبادة الله تعالى بقلبه وقالبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r12.claim: The apparent meaning forbids approaching prayer while intoxicated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r12.anchor: وظاهر الآية يدل على النهي عن قربان الصلاة في حالة السكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r13.claim: Another view takes the command as a prohibition of intoxication itself, since prayer is obligatory but drunkenness is unpredictable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r13.anchor: وقيل: المراد النهي عن السكر، لأن الصلاة قد فرضت عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r14.claim: The amount of drink that causes drunkenness varies by quantity and temperament, so avoiding wine protects prayer observance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r14.anchor: لأن السكر قد يقع تارة بالقليل وتارة بالكثير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r15.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r15.claim: The majority read سكارى with ḍamma on س; grammarians debate whether it is a broken plural or a collective noun.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r16.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r16.claim: Sībawayh explicitly classifies سكارى as a broken plural on the فعالى pattern used for adjectives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r16.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه أنه جمع تكسير. قال سيبويه في حد تكسير الصفات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r17.speaker: ابن الباذش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r17.claim: Ibn al-Badhish mistakenly attributes to Sībawayh the view that سكارى is a collective noun, which he considers analogically plausible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r17.anchor: ووهم الأستاذ أبو الحسن بن الباذش فنسب إلى سيبويه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r18.claim: Abū Ḥayyān corrects Ibn al-Badhish: Sībawayh explicitly says it is a broken plural and distinguishes noun-patterns from adjective plurals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r18.anchor: وليس في الأبنية إلا نص سيبويه على أنه تكسير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r19.speaker: السيرافي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r19.claim: Al-Sīrāfī records both analyses and prefers the broken-plural parsing, which agrees with Sībawayh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r19.anchor: وحكى السيرافي فيه القولين، ورجح أنه تكسير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r20.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r20.claim: A group reads سكارى with fatḥa on س, as a broken plural analogous to ندمان and ندامى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r20.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: سكارى بفتح السين نحو ندمان وندامى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r21.speaker: النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r21.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī reads سكرى; it may be a feminine singular adjective applied to a group, or a plural of سكران on فعلى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p648/r21.anchor: وقرأ النخعي: سكرى، فاحتمل أن يكون صفة لواحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r1.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads سكرى with ḍamma on س, on the pattern حبلى, as an adjective of a collective group.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r1.anchor: سكرى بضم السين على وزن حبلى، وتخريجه على أنه صفة لجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r2.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r2.claim: Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh transmits كسلى with either ḍamma or fatḥa, as al-Zamakhsharī relates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r2.anchor: وحكى جناح بن حبيش: كسلى وكسلى بالضم والفتح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r3.claim: The phrase means until you recover and understand what you say; it names the intended result, since an intoxicated person does not understand speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r3.anchor: ومعنى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون: حتى تصحوا فتعلموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r4.claim: The verse indicates that an intoxicated person may not understand his words, underlying disagreement about the legal effect of his divorce.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r4.anchor: وظاهر الآية يدل على أن السكران لا يعلم ما يقول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r5.speaker: عثمان وابن عباس وطاووس وعطاء والقاسم وربيعة والليث وإسحاق وأبو ثور والمزني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r5.claim: ʿUthmān, Ibn ʿAbbās, and the named jurists hold that a drunk person’s divorce is not binding; al-Ṭabarī prefers this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r5.anchor: ذهب عثمان، وابن عباس، وطاووس، وعطاء، والقاسم، وربيعة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r6.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī argues that an imbecile’s divorce is invalid and the drunk is mentally impaired; loss of reason from anesthetic likewise invalidates divorce.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r6.anchor: واختاره الطبري. وقال أجمع العلماء: على أن طلاق المعتوه لا يجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r7.speaker: عمر ومعاوية وجماعة من التابعين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r7.claim: ʿUmar, Muʿāwiya, and a group of Successors hold that the drunk person’s divorce takes effect; Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Thawrī, and al-Awzāʿī agree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r7.anchor: وروي عن عمر ومعاوية وجماعة من التابعين: أن طلاقه نافذ عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa treats a drunk person’s acts and contracts like a sober person’s, except apostasy does not separate him from his wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r8.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: أفعاله وعقوده كلها ثابتة كأفعال الصاحي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r9.speaker: أبو يوسف والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r9.claim: Abū Yūsuf and al-Shāfiʿī say a drunk person is an apostate while intoxicated; al-Shāfiʿī does not execute or seek repentance then, and his position on divorce varied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r9.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف: يكون مرتدا في حال سكره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r10.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r10.claim: Mālik binds a drunk person to divorce and injury-related retaliation or compensation, but not to marriage or sale.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r10.anchor: وألزم مالك السكران الطلاق والقود في الجراح والعقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r11.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r11.claim: Al-Māwardī notes a rare report in their school that a drunk person’s divorce is not binding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r11.anchor: قال الماوردي: وقد رويت عندنا رواية شاذة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r12.speaker: محمد بن عبد الحكم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r12.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam says a drunk person’s divorce and emancipation are not binding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r12.anchor: وقال محمد بن عبد الحكم: لا يلزمه طلاق ولا عتاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r13.speaker: جماعة من السلف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r13.claim: Some early authorities, including the Ḥanafī school, define legally relevant drunkenness as inability to distinguish a man from a woman.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r13.anchor: فقيل: هو الذي لا يعرف صاحبه الرجل من المرأة قاله: جماعة من السلف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r14.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r14.claim: Al-Thawrī defines drunkenness as mental disturbance, such as garbling recitation and speaking without knowing what one says.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r14.anchor: وقال الثوري: السكر اختلال العقل، فإذا خلط في قراءته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r15.speaker: أحمد ومالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r15.claim: Aḥmad, and similarly Mālik, regard a person as drunk when his mind changes from its sober state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r15.anchor: وقال أحمد: إذا تغير عقله في حال الصحة فهو سكران

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r16.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r16.claim: Some infer that drinking was initially permitted in early Islam until it produced drunkenness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r16.anchor: قيل: وفي الآية دلالة على أن الشرب كان مباحا في أول الإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r17.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r17.claim: Al-Qaffāl suggests that stimulating drinks that encouraged generosity, courage, and zeal may have been allowed, but deliberate use of mind-destroying drink was not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r17.anchor: وقال القفال: يحتمل أنه كان أبيح لهم من الشراب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r18.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r18.claim: Al-Qaffāl adds that if someone unintentionally drank enough to lose reason, the legal burden was lifted from him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p649/r18.anchor: بل لو أنفق من غير قصد كان مرفوعا عن صاحبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r1.claim: ولا جنبا coordinates with the circumstantial clause وأنتم سكارى; the nominal sentence is more emphatic because of its repeated pronoun, and لا treats each condition separately, so their combination is even more prohibited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r1.anchor: ولا جنبا هذه حالة معطوفة على قوله: وأنتم سكارى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r2.speaker: الأعمش وداود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Dāwūd hold that ghusl is required only of one who has emitted semen; Abū Ḥayyān says the proofs belong in legal works.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r2.anchor: لا غسل إلا على من أنزل، وبه قال الأعمش وداود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r3.claim: Junub may derive from distance, since one is apart from purity, or from the side, since one lies with or touches another by his side.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r3.anchor: والجنب من الجنابة وهي البعد، كأنه جانب الطهر، أو من الجنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says junub has one form for singular and plural and for masculine and feminine, like the verbal noun ijnaab; Abū Ḥayyān calls it fluent, Qurʾānic usage and notes plural forms جنبون، أجناب and dual جنبان.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: الجنب يستوي فيه الواجد والجمع، والمذكر والمؤنث، لأنه اسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r5.claim: ʿĀbir means crossing or passing through; the cited verse uses عبر for traversing the heat of midday.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r5.anchor: العبور: الخطور والجواز، ومنه ناقة عير الهواجر وعبر أسفار قال:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r6.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī understands the passer as someone who walks through a mosque without staying there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r6.anchor: وعابر السبيل هو المار في المسجد من غير لبث فيه، وهو مذهب الشافعي قال:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r7.speaker: الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r7.claim: Al-Layth permits passing through only if the junub person's own door opens onto the mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r7.anchor: وقال الليث: لا يمر فيه إلا إن كان بابه إلى المسجد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r8.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r8.claim: Aḥmad and Isḥāq allow a junub who has performed ablution to sit in the mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r8.anchor: وقال أحمد وإسحاق: إذا توضأ الجنب فلا بأس به أن يقعد في المسجد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r9.claim: On the reading of prayer as the mosque, al-Zamakhsharī takes the exception to permit only passing through on a route to water, where water is in the mosque, or after a wet dream there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r9.anchor: من فسر الصلاة بالمسجد قال: معناه لا تقربوا المسجد جنبا إلا مجتازين فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r10.speaker: الأنصار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r10.claim: It is said some Anṣār had doors opening into the mosque and, after becoming junub, had no route except through it, so they received a concession.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن رجالا من الأنصار كانت أبوابهم في المسجد فتصيبهم الجنابة ولا يجدون ممرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r11.claim: A report says the Prophet forbade anyone to sit or pass through the mosque while junub except ʿAlī, whose house was inside it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p650/r11.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لم يأذن لأحد أن يجلس في المسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد والحكم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r1.claim: These authorities identify the passer as a traveler: a junub may not approach prayer until washing, except a traveler may use tayammum. Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions, Mālik, al-Thawrī, and others bar even mosque passage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r1.anchor: وقال علي وابن عباس أيضا وابن جبير ومجاهد والحكم وغيرهم: عابر السبيل المسافر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers taking الصلاة literally as prayer; taking it as prayer places is figurative and should be used only when the literal sense cannot work. Required recitation obstructs prayer while drunk, unlike mosque entry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r2.anchor: ورجح هذا القول بأن قوله: لا تقربوا الصلاة يبقى على ظاهره، وحقيقته بخلاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r3.claim: The traveler is called a passer of the road because he is on the road, as in the expression son of the road.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r3.anchor: وسمي المسافر عابر سبيل لأنه على الطريق، كما سمي ابن السبيل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r4.claim: The wording permits a junub without water to pray after tayammum, but tayammum does not end janāba because the person remains called junub.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r4.anchor: وأفاد الكلام معنيين: أحدهما: جواز التيمم للجنب إذا لم يجد الماء والصلاة به.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses the exception as a circumstantial exception from all addressees: they may approach prayer while junub only with the additional excuse of travel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r5.anchor: الاستثناء من عامة أحوال المخاطبين، وانتصابه على الحال. (فإن قلت) : كيف جمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also permits an adjectival parse: the restriction concerns junub residents without an excuse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن لا يكون حالا ولكن صفة كقوله: جنبا أي: ولا تقربوا الصلاة جنبا غير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r7.claim: To explain prayer while junub in travel, al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases the phrase as not washed until washing, except when traveling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r7.anchor: أريد بالجنب الذين لم يغتسلوا، كأنه قيل: لا تقربوا الصلاة غير مغتسلين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r8.claim: The majority prohibit junub men and menstruating women from reciting any Qurʾān until washing. Mālik permits a short protective verse and permits a menstruant to recite freely if she fears forgetting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r8.anchor: فالأولى أن يمنعه والحائض من قراءة القرآن، وبه قال الجمهور، فلا يجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the Qurʾān-recitation ruling has no exegetical connection to the wording at hand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p651/r9.anchor: وذكروا هذه المسألة ولا تعلق لها في التفسير بلفظ القرآن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r1.claim: The endpoint keeps a junub person from prayer until the whole body has been washed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r1.anchor: هذه غاية لامتناع الجنب من الصلاة، وهي داخلة في الحظر إلى أن يوقع الاغتسال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r2.speaker: مالك والمزني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r2.claim: The well-known Mālikī position and al-Muzanī require rubbing the body during ghusl; the majority say immersion or pouring water suffices without rubbing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r2.anchor: فمشهور مذهب مالك: أنه لا يجزئه حتى يتدلك، وبه قال المزني: ومذهب الجمهور:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r3.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r3.claim: Mālik has differing reports on whether the beard must be worked through during ghusl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r3.anchor: وهل يجب في الغسل تخليل اللحية؟ فيه عن مالك خلاف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r4.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa makes mouth rinsing and sniffing obligatory in ghusl but not ablution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r4.anchor: وأما المضمضة والاستنشاق في الغسل فذهب أبو حنيفة إلى فرضيتهما فيه لا في الوضوء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r5.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وإسحاق وأحمد وبعض أصحاب داود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r5.claim: Ibn Abī Laylā, Isḥāq, Aḥmad, and some of Dāwūd's followers require rinsing and sniffing in both ghusl and ablution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r5.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى وإسحاق وأحمد وبعض أصحاب داود: هما فرض فيهما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r6.speaker: عطاء والزهري ومجاهد ومالك والأوزاعي والليث والشافعي ومحمد بن جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, al-Zuhrī, Mujāhid, Mālik, al-Awzāʿī, al-Layth, al-Shāfiʿī, and Muḥammad ibn Jarīr do not make either act obligatory in either purification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد وجماعة من التابعين، ومالك، والأوزاعي، والليث، والشافعي، ومحمد بن جرير: ليسا بفرض فيهما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r7.speaker: أحمد وبعض أصحاب داود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r7.claim: One report from Aḥmad and some of Dāwūd's followers makes mouth rinsing sunnah and sniffing obligatory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r7.anchor: وروي عن أحمد: أن المضمضة سنة، والاستنشاق فرض، وقال به بعض أصحاب داود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r8.claim: The verse names washing without stating an intention requirement; Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions do not require intention for water purification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r8.anchor: وظاهر قوله: حتى تغتسلوا حصول الاغتسال، ولم يشترط فيه نية الاغتسال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r9.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r9.claim: Mālik's well-known position, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Abū Thawr require intention; al-Walīd ibn Muslim transmitted the contrary view from Mālik.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r9.anchor: وروى هذا الوليد بن مسلم عن مالك، ومشهور مذهبه أنه لا بد من النية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r10.claim: The majority say tayammum was revealed when the Companions lacked water on the al-Muraysīʿ expedition while searching for the necklace.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r10.anchor: قال الجمهور: نزلت بسبب عدم الصحابة الماء في غزوة المريسيع، حين أقام على التماس العقد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r11.speaker: النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r11.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī says the revelation concerned wounded people who became junub.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r11.anchor: وقال النخعي: في قوم أصابتهم جراح وأجنبوا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r12.claim: Another account says the occasion involved ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r12.anchor: وقيل: كان ذلك عبد الرحمن بن عوف، ومرضى يعني في الحضر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r13.speaker: داود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r13.claim: Dāwūd applies the general wording of illness without limits on severity or duration and allows tayammum to anyone who fits the name sick.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r13.anchor: ويدل على مطلق المرض قل أو كثر، زاد أو نقص، تأخر برؤه أو تعجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r14.speaker: العلماء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r14.claim: Other jurists restrict illness to conditions such as smallpox, measles, or dangerous ailments where water may harm; they agree tayammum is allowed when harm is feared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r14.anchor: وخصص العلماء غيره المرض بالجدري، والحصبة، والعلل المخوف عليها من الماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r15.speaker: عطاء والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r15.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥasan reportedly require washing even if the person dies; Abū Ḥayyān answers with the report of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ at Dhāt al-Salāsil, whose tayammum after fearing death was approved by the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r15.anchor: إلا ما روي عن عطاء والحسن: أنه يتطهر وإن مات، وهما محجوجان بحديث عمرو بن العاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r16.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r16.claim: At Dhāt al-Salāsil, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ feared bathing would kill him, performed tayammum, and was approved by the Prophet; Abū Ḥayyān cites Abū Dāwūd and al-Dāraquṭnī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p652/r16.anchor: حديث عمرو بن العاص في غزوة ذات السلاسل، وأنه أشفق أن يهلك إن اغتسل فتيمم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r1.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and Mālik permit tayammum when one fears illness will begin or worsen, or recovery will be delayed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r1.anchor: وإن خاف حدوث مرض أو زيادته، أو تأخر البرء، فذهب أبو حنيفة ومالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r2.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī's stated position disallows tayammum for that fear, though his correct view is reported to permit it when long illness is feared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r2.anchor: وقال الشافعي: لا يجوز، وقيل: الصحيح عن الشافعي أنه إذا خاف طول المرض جاز له التيمم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r3.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة ومحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r3.claim: Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, and Muḥammad permit a resident without water to use tayammum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r3.anchor: وظاهر قوله تعالى: أو على سفر مطلق السفر، فلو لم يجد الماء في الحضر جاز له التيمم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r4.speaker: الشافعي والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and al-Ṭabarī do not permit tayammum to a resident who lacks water.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r5.speaker: الليث والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r5.claim: Al-Layth and another report from al-Shāfiʿī allow tayammum and prayer when time would expire, but require repeating after water is found.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r5.anchor: وقال الليث والشافعي أيضا: إن خاف فوت الوقت تيمم وصلى، ثم إذا وجد الماء أعاد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r6.speaker: أبو يوسف وزفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r6.claim: Abū Yūsuf and Zufar allow tayammum only when there is fear of missing prayer time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r6.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف وزفر: لا يتيمم إلا لخوف الوقت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r7.claim: For the majority any travel allows the concession, whether or not it qualifies for shortening prayers; other jurists require a shortening journey, and another group requires travel for obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r7.anchor: والسفر المبيح عند الجمهور مطلق السفر، سواء أكان مما تقصر فيه الصلاة أو لا تقصر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa allows tayammum for someone who leaves town without intending travel if water is a mile away; another view sets the distance where people's voices cannot be heard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لو خرج من مصره لغير سفر فلم يجد الماء جاز له التيمم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r9.claim: Another view treats someone beyond hearing people's voices as being like a traveler.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r9.anchor: وقيل: إذا كان بحيث لا يسمع أصوات الناس، لأنه في معنى المسافر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r10.claim: If water is too scarce to use without risking thirst, the majority permit tayammum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r10.anchor: فلو وجد ماء قليلا إن توضأ به خاف على نفسه العطش تيمم على قول الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r11.speaker: الفقهاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r11.claim: There is no disagreement that a person who finds water at its ordinary price must buy it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r11.anchor: فلو وجده بثمن مثله فلا خلاف أنه يلزمه شراؤه، أو بما زاد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r12.claim: For water priced above its ordinary value, Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī allow tayammum, whereas Mālik requires buying it with all one's wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r12.anchor: فمذهب أبي حنيفة والشافعي. يتيمم. ومذهب مالك: يشتريه بماله كله ويبقى عديما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r13.claim: Being blocked from water by an enemy, predator, or other obstacle is treated like lacking water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r13.anchor: فلو حال بينه وبين الماء عدو أو سبع أو غير ذلك مما يحول فكالعادم للماء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r14.claim: Coming from the toilet euphemizes the bodily event and extends to wind, urine, semen, and pre-ejaculatory fluid; these six events all invalidate ablution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r14.anchor: ومجيئه من الغائط كناية عن الحدث بالغائط، وحمل عليه الريح والبول والمني والودي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r15.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read من الغيط; it may be a verbal noun from غاط يغيط or originally a فيعل form with deletion like ميت.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: من الغيط وخرج على وجهين: أحدهما: أنه مصدر إذ قالوا: غاط يغيط.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r16.speaker: عمرو بن مسعود وغيرهما
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r16.claim: ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd and others read the phrase as touching by hand; on this view a junub must wash or leave prayer until water is found.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r16.anchor: فقال عمرو بن مسعود وغيرهما: هو اللمس باليد، ولا ذكر للجنب إنما يغتسل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r17.speaker: أبو عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r17.claim: Abū ʿUmar says no regional jurists adopted the hand-touch view, citing reports about tayammum for a junub from ʿAmmār, Abū Dharr, and ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r17.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لم يقل بقولهم أحد من فقهاء الأمصار لحديث عمار، وأبي ذر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r18.speaker: علي وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r18.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and Qatāda interpret the phrase as intercourse, in which case a junub may use tayammum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653/r18.anchor: وقال علي وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة: المراد الجماع، والجنب يتيمم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r1.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa reads the phrase as intercourse, not hand-touch; even a kiss with desire does not invalidate ablution in his school.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r1.anchor: ولا ذكر للامس بيده، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة. فلو قبل ولو بلذة لم ينتقض الوضوء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r2.speaker: مالك وأحمد وإسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r2.claim: Mālik says intercourse requires tayammum and hand-touch does so only with pleasure; without desire there is no ablution. Aḥmad and Isḥāq agree on the desire distinction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r2.anchor: وقال مالك: الملامس بالجماع يتيمم، وكذا باليد إذا التذ فإن لمس بغير شهوة فلا وضوء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي وابن مسعود وابن عمر والزهري وربيعة وعبيدة والشعبي وإبراهيم ومنصور وابن سيرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and the listed authorities hold that any bodily contact with a woman's body invalidates purity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r3.anchor: وقال الشافعي: إذا أفضى بشيء من جسده إلى بدن المرأة نقض الطهارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r4.speaker: الأوزاعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r4.claim: Al-Awzāʿī says contact invalidates ablution when it is by hand, but not otherwise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r4.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي: إن كان باليد نقض وإلا فلا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r5.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read لمستم without the long alif; the other six of the seven canonical readers use the long alif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي: لمستم وباقي السبعة بالألف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r6.claim: The long-alif form can correspond to the simple verb, like جاوزت الشيء وجزته; its form does not distinguish active from passive though the meaning can, and al-Shāfiʿī applies it to both toucher and touched in his stronger view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r6.anchor: وفاعل هنا موافق فعل المجرد نحو: جاوزت الشيء وجزته، وليست لأقسام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r7.claim: أو على سفر is accusative by coordination with مرضى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r7.anchor: وقوله: أو على سفر في موضع نصب عطفا على مرضى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r8.claim: The past verbs جاء and لامستم can be predicates after كان without an implied قد; ellipsis is strained because they coordinate with the predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r8.anchor: وفي قوله: أو جاء، أو لامستم دليل على جواز وقوع الماضي خبرا لكان من غير قد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r9.claim: The pronoun in فلم تجدوا refers to those named in all four conditions, with a shift between direct address and the third-person أحد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r9.anchor: فلم تجدوا ماء الضمير عائد على من أسند إليهم الحكم في الأخبار الأربعة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r10.claim: The shift to third person in جاء أحد delicately avoids directly attributing the toilet need to the addressees, while illness, travel, and touching are said directly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r10.anchor: لما كنى عن الحاجة بالغائط كره إسناد ذلك إلى المخاطبين، فنزع به إلى لفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r11.claim: Not finding water normally means searching without reaching it; for the sick, existing water that cannot be used counts legally as absent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r11.anchor: وظاهر انتفاء الوجدان سبق تطلبه وعدم الوصول إليه، فأما في حق المريض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r12.claim: The water-finding clause coordinates with the conditional verbs, and tayammum is the response; the command applies if any of four causes occurs with water absent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p653#2/r12.anchor: وفلم تجدوا معطوف على فعل الشرط فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا هذا جواب الشرط،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that illness and travel are named first because they commonly create need for the concession, then the rule extends to anyone obliged to purify but lacking water through an enemy, beast, missing drawing tool, isolation, or similar cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: (فإن قلت) : كيف نظم في سلك واحد بين المرضى والمسافرين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes لمس النساء as intercourse resulting in janāba, following the Ḥanafī school, and reports no other school's view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r2.anchor: وفيه تفسيره: أو لمستم النساء أنه أريد به الجماع الذي تترتب عليه الجنابة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r3.speaker: author
