ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān summarizes al-Zamakhsharī's answer as justifying the early mention of illness and travel because they are more frequent and first deserving of a concession.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r3.anchor: وملخص ما طول به: أنه اعتذر عن تقديم المرض والسفر بما ذكر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r4.claim: Those who take touching literally can read the list as escalation from lesser to greater: illness, travel, relieving oneself, and then touching a woman.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r4.anchor: ومن يحمل اللمس على ظاهره يقول: إن هذا من باب الترقي من الأقل إلى الأكثر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ define ṣaʿīd as soil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والفراء: الصعيد التراب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r6.speaker: الليث وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r6.claim: Al-Layth and Qatāda define ṣaʿīd as level, smooth ground without trees or plants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r6.anchor: وقال الليث: الصعيد الأرض المستوية لا شيء فيها من غراس ونبات، وهو قول قتادة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r7.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r7.claim: Al-Khalīl says ṣaʿīd is what rises from the earth's surface, meaning the face of the earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r7.anchor: وقال الخليل: الصعيد ما صعد من وجه الأرض، يريد وجه الأرض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface, whether soil or another material, including bare rock; another scholar adds sand, minerals, and saline earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: الصعيد وجه الأرض ترابا كان أو غيره، وإن كان صخرا لا تراب عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r9.claim: One group takes ṭayyib as pure; Abū Ḥanīfa and Mālik hold this, and al-Ṭabarī chooses it, as in the description of the dead as pure from stains of disobedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r9.anchor: والطيب الطاهر وهذا تفسير طائفة، ومذهب أبي حنيفة ومالك واختيار الطبري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r10.claim: The pure reading is illustrated by the verse describing those whom the angels take as ṭayyibīn, meaning purified from disobedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r10.anchor: ومنه الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة طيبين أي طاهرين من أدناس المخالفات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r11.speaker: سفيان الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r11.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī and others say ṭayyib means lawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r11.anchor: وقال قوم: الطيب هنا الحلال، قاله سفيان الثوري وغيره.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r12.speaker: الشافعي وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and a group take ṭayyib as fertile; Ibn ʿAbbās cites the good land that produces vegetation, yielding soil as ṣaʿīd, while this group permits other materials too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r12.anchor: وقال الشافعي وجماعة: الطيب المنبت، وقاله ابن عباس لقوله تعالى: والبلد الطيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r13.claim: The fertile reading cites the verse والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r13.anchor: لقوله تعالى: والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته فالصعيد على هذا التراب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r14.claim: All agree clean, fertile, unmoved, unappropriated soil is valid for tayammum and forbid gold, silver, gems, food, and impure substances.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r14.anchor: فمحل الإجماع هو أن يتيمم بتراب منبت طاهر غير منقول ولا مغصوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r15.speaker: مالك والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r15.claim: Mālik permits minerals for tayammum, while al-Shāfiʿī prohibits them; salt, snow, moved soil, brick, walls, plants, sticks, and trees are disputed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r15.anchor: واختلف في المعادن: فأجيز، وهو مذهب مالك، ومنع وهو مذهب الشافعي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r16.speaker: الثوري وأحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r16.claim: Al-Thawrī and Aḥmad permit tayammum with dust on the hand.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r17.speaker: أحمد وأبو يوسف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r17.claim: Aḥmad and Abū Yūsuf limit material to soil and sand; most jurists allow saline earth except Ibn Rāhawayh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r17.anchor: وقال أحمد وأبو يوسف: لا يجوز إلا بالتراب والرمل، والجمهور على إجازته بالسباخ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r18.speaker: ابن علية وابن كيسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r18.claim: Ibn ʿUlayya and Ibn Kaysān permit tayammum using musk and saffron.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p654/r18.anchor: وأجاز ابن علية وابن كيسان التيمم بالمسك والزعفران.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r1.claim: The apparent instruction is to wipe face and hands using pure earth; that manner suffices, and the conjunction does not order face before hands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r1.anchor: وظاهر الكلام: أن التيمم مسح الوجه واليدين من الصعيد الطيب، فمتى حصلت هذه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r2.claim: The preposition باء may govern the verb or be absent without change of meaning; Sībawayh gives مسحت رأسه and مسحت برأسه, and the same alternation with the chest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r2.anchor: حكى سيبويه: مسحت رأسه وبرأسه، وخشنت صدره وبصدره على معنى واحد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r3.claim: The apparent wording requires wiping the whole face, as ablution washes it all; some jurists allow leaving the creases untraced.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r3.anchor: وظاهر مسح الوجه التعميم، فيمسحه جميعه كما يغسله بالماء جميعه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r4.claim: Some jurists permit not tracing the creases of the face.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r4.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم أن لا يتتبع الغضون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r5.speaker: ابن شهاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r5.claim: Because hands can linguistically extend to the shoulders, Ibn Shihāb says wipe to the armpits; this is also reported from Abū Bakr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r5.anchor: وهي تنطلق لغة إلى المناكب، وبه قال ابن شهاب، قال: يمسح إلى الآباط،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r6.claim: A report in Abū Dāwūd says the Prophet wiped to the middle of his forearms; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says no one followed that report as far as he knew.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r6.anchor: وفي سنن أبي داود: «أنه عليه السلام مسح إلى أنصاف ذراعيه»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says he knew of no scholar who followed the report about wiping to mid-forearm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: لم يقل أحد بهذا الحديث فيما حفظت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي والثوري والليث وابن أبي سلمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī, al-Thawrī, al-Layth, and others require wiping to the elbows; this is also attributed to Jābir, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan, and Ibrāhīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r8.anchor: وذهب أبو حنيفة والشافعي وأصحابهما والثوري وابن أبي سلمة والليث: أنه يمسح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r9.speaker: علي وعطاء والشعبي ومكحول والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق وداود والطبري والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r9.claim: Another group wipes only to the wrists; this is reported from Mālik and was al-Shāfiʿī's earlier position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r9.anchor: وذهب طائفة إلى أنه يبلغ به إلى الكوعين وهما الرسغان، وهو: قول علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r10.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r10.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says to wipe only the palms; some hadith jurists agree, and Abū Ḥayyān says this is the position to follow because its hadith is sound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r10.anchor: وذهب الشعبي إلى أنه يمسح كفيه فقط، وبه قال بعض فقهاء الحديث،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r11.speaker: عمار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r11.claim: A Muslim report from ʿAmmār has the Prophet say one strike on the ground, blowing off dust, then wiping the face and palms suffices.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r11.anchor: ففي مسلم من حديث عمار «إنما كان يكفيك أن تضرب بيدك الأرض ثم تنفخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r12.speaker: عمار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r12.claim: Another Muslim wording says the Prophet struck the earth, shook his hands, and wiped face and palms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r12.anchor: وعنه في هذا الحديث: «وضرب بيده الأرض فنفض يديه، فمسح وجهه وكفيه»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r13.speaker: عمار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r13.claim: Al-Bukhārī's version says the Prophet brought his hands near his mouth, then wiped face and palms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r13.anchor: وللبخاري: «ثم أدناهما من فيه، ثم مسح بهما وجهه وكفيه»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r14.speaker: عمار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r14.claim: Another Muslim report describes one strike, wiping the left over the right, the backs of the hands, and the face.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r14.anchor: وفي مسلم أيضا: «أما يكفيك أن تقول بيدك هكذا، ثم ضرب بيده الأرض ضربة واحدة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r15.speaker: عمار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r15.claim: Abū Dāwūd's version says the Prophet struck the earth, grasped the hands, rubbed each palm against the other, then wiped the face.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r15.anchor: وعند أبي داود «فضرب بيده الأرض فقبضها، ثم ضرب بشماله على يمينه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r16.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the sound reports clarify the location and manner of wiping that the verse leaves open to possibility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p655/r16.anchor: فهذه الأحاديث الصحيحة مبينة ما تطرق إليه الاحتمال في الآية من محل المسح وكيفيته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r1.speaker: عطاء والشعبي والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق وداود والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r1.claim: The apparent verse and sound reports indicate one strike for face and hands; this is held by ʿAṭāʾ, one report from al-Shaʿbī, al-Awzāʿī's best-known report, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Dāwūd, and al-Ṭabarī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r1.anchor: وظاهر هذه الأحاديث الصحيحة وظاهر الآية يدل على الاجتزاء بضربة واحدة للوجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r2.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي والثوري والليث وابن أبي سلمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r2.claim: Mālik in al-Mudawwana, Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī, al-Thawrī, al-Layth, and Ibn Abī Salama require two strikes, one for face and one for hands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r2.anchor: وذهب مالك في المدونة، والأوزاعي في رواية، وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وأصحابهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r3.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Laylā and al-Ḥasan also require two strikes, each wiping face, arms, and elbows; Abū Ḥayyān says no other scholar held this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r3.anchor: وذهب ابن أبي ليلى والحسن إلى أنه ضربتان، ويمسح بكل ضربة منهما وجهه وذراعيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r4.claim: Many tayammum rulings are treated in law books and al-Māʾida; its qualification is applied to this verse and supports al-Shāfiʿī's requirement that some material be transferred to the face and hands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r4.anchor: وأحكام التيمم ومسائله كثيرة مذكورة في كتب الفقه، ولم يذكر في هذه السورة منه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī asks how the al-Māʾida phrase فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه can require part of the earth when bare rock has no soil, and answers that من marks a starting point.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: (فإن قلت) : فما تصنع بقوله في سورة المائدة: فامسحوا بوجوهكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls the starting-point reading strained: Arabs understand مسحت برأسه من الدهن والماء والتراب as partitive, and he approves yielding to truth over disputation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r6.anchor: قولهم إنها لابتداء الغاية قول متعسف، ولا يفهم أحد من العرب من قول القائل:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the divine description as an allusion to legal concession and ease: God forgives and pardons, so He chooses ease over hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r7.anchor: إن الله كان عفوا غفورا كناية عن الترخيص والتيسير، لأن من كانت عادته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān criticizes al-Zamakhsharī for accepting the apparent sense here despite usually distorting wording for his school, and for speaking of forgiveness without the repentance qualification he usually requires.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p656/r8.anchor: والعجب منه إذ أذعن إلى الحق، وليس من عادته، بل عادته أن يحرف الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r1.claim: The prohibition purifies prayer, the chief act of worship, from blemish so believers combine sincere devotion to God with good conduct toward others, connecting this verse to the preceding discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r1.anchor: إرشاد لا خلاص الصلاة التى هى رأس العبادة من شوائب الكدر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r2.claim: Since the preceding passage forbade associating partners with God, this passage also forbids an unsuspected route that could lead to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال لما نهوا فيما سلف عن الاشراك به تعالى نهوا ههنا عما يؤدى إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r3.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r3.claim: Ali reports that after wine at Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's feast, the intoxicated Companions put him forward and he misrecited al-Kafirun; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan and al-Hakim authenticates it.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r3.anchor: عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : ' صنع لنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r4.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r4.claim: Another report from Ali says Abd al-Rahman led the people in the Maghrib prayer, while wine was still permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r4.anchor: وفي رواية ابن جرير . وابن المنذر عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r5.claim: The vocative and attention marker introduce the rule with special emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r5.anchor: وتصدير الكلام بحر في النداء والتنبيه اعتناءا بشأن الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r6.claim: Most interpreters understand prayer as the specific ritual act; approaching it means rising to perform it and entering into it, with the wording intensifying the prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r6.anchor: والمراد بالصلاة عند الكثير الهيئة المخصوصة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r7.claim: Intoxication is the settled state produced by drinking wine; its root conveys closure or obstruction, as in the phrase about eyes being sealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r7.anchor: وبالسكر الحالة المقررة التى تحصل لشارب الخمر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r8.claim: Do not pray while intoxicated until, before beginning, you know what you will say, which implies knowing what you will recite in prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r8.anchor: والمعنى لا تصلوا في حالة السكر حتى تعلموا قبل الشروع ما تقولونه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r9.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r9.claim: Ibn Jubayr, as reported by Ibn Abi Hatim, takes the phrase to mean being tipsy from drink until one knows what one recites in prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن جبير أن المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك وعكرمة والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak, Ikrima, and al-Hasan say prayer means its locations, by a state-for-place metaphor; the verse bars an intoxicated person from approaching a mosque out of reverence.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r1.anchor: والضحاك . وعكرمة . والحسن أن المراد من الصلاة مواضعها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r2.claim: The mosque reading is supported by a report that mosques should be kept away from children and madmen, but the phrase about knowing what one says weighs against it.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r2.anchor: فالآية مسوقة عن نهى قربان السكران المسجد تعظيما له

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i applies prayer to both the ritual act and its locations to accommodate both interpretations; al-Alusi rejects this because it combines literal and metaphorical senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r3.anchor: وروى عن الشافعى رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه حمل الصلاة على الهيئة المخصوصة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r4.speaker: جعفر والضحاك وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r4.claim: Ja'far, al-Dahhak, and one report from Ibn Abbas take intoxication here to mean overpowering sleep or drowsiness.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r4.anchor: وروى عن جعفر رضي الله تعالى عنه . والضحاك - وهو إحدى الروايتين عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r5.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r5.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet told a drowsy worshipper to leave, sleep, and return when he knows what he is saying; a similar report is attributed to Aisha.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r5.anchor: وأيد بما أخرجه البخاري عن أنس قال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r6.claim: The sleep interpretation is somewhat far-fetched, and combining sleep and wine intoxication is still less plausible because it mixes literal and metaphorical senses without a clear indicator.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r6.anchor: وفيه بعد - وأبعد منه حمله على سكر الخمر وسكر النوم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r7.claim: The prohibition targets the state of intoxication while the duty to pray remains; the qualifying state is the object of negation, and the general prayer obligation is not cancelled.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r7.anchor: فليس مرجع النهى هو المقيد مع بقاء القيد مرخصا بحاله بل إنما هو القيد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r8.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r8.claim: Al-Shihab says intoxication caused by one's own act does not remove the duty to pray; an intoxicated person's divorce and similar acts take effect, and a prayer time wholly spent drunk must be made up.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r8.anchor: والحاصل كما قال الشهاب : إنه مكلف بها في كل حال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r9.speaker: الجصاص
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r9.claim: Al-Jassas states that if intoxication spans the whole prayer time, the person still must make up the prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r9.anchor: وقد نص عليه الجصاص في الأحكام وفصله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r10.claim: Some say the prohibition concerned only praying in congregation with the Prophet, to honor him; al-Alusi rejects this as unsupported by transmission or reason and contrary to the apparent text and occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r10.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن النهي عن الصلاة نفسها لكن المراد بها الصلاة جماعة مع النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r11.claim: After the verse was revealed, people reportedly stopped drinking at prayer times, drank after the night prayer, and were sober and understood their words by morning.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r11.anchor: وقد روي أنهم كانوا بعد ما أنزلت الآية لا يشربون الخمر في أوقات الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r12.claim: The reading سكارى with fatHa is the plural of سكران, like ندمان and ندامى.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r12.anchor: وقرئ ( سكارى ) بفتح السين جمع سكران كندمان وندامى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r13.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r13.claim: Al-A'mash reads سكرى with a damma on the first letter, treating it as a feminine adjective describing a group.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r13.anchor: قرأ الأعمش سكرى بضم السين على أنه صفة كحبلى وقع صفة لجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r14.speaker: النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r14.claim: Al-Nakha'i reads سكرى with fatHa; it can be a singular adjective for a group or, according to Sibawayh, a broken plural, while others call it a collective noun; al-Alusi prefers Sibawayh's analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r14.anchor: والنخعي سكرى بالفتح وهو إما صفة مفردة صفة جماعة كما في الضم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r15.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the accusative state phrase while intoxicated, yielding the sense: do not approach prayer intoxicated or in a state of janaba.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r15.anchor: عطف على قوله تعالى : ( وأنتم سكارى ) فإنه في حيز النصب

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r16.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r16.claim: Al-Shihab, quoting al-Bahr and Abd al-Qahir, distinguishes a simple state adjective from a clause stating that the people were intoxicated independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r16.anchor: وقال الشهاب نقلا عن البحر : إن هذا حكم الإعراب

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r17.speaker: السبكي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r17.claim: Al-Subki applies the distinction to a vow of retreat while fasting: صائما requires a fast for that vow, whereas وأنا صائم requires concurrence and is fulfilled during Ramadan.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r17.anchor: ولذا قال السبكي في الأشباه : لو قال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r18.speaker: السبكي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r18.claim: For al-Subki, a circumstantial clause requires concurrence with fasting, so Ramadan can fulfill it; a single adjective makes fasting itself part of the vow.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p38#2/r18.anchor: ولذا قال السبكي في الأشباه : لو قال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r1.claim: Al-Tibi says intoxicated approach is incompatible with Muslim prayer and intimate address to God, while the junub need not lack inward attention and is therefore granted an excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r1.anchor: وبين العلامة الطيبي فائدتها غير أنه لم يتعرض لهذا الفرق فقال : فائدتها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r2.claim: Junub is invariant in the eloquent language across gender and number, though some Arabs inflect it; Abu al-Baqa derives it from separation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r2.anchor: والجنب من أصابته الجنابة يستوي فيه على اللغة الفصيحة المذكر والمؤنث والواحد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r3.claim: Those passing along a path are interpreted as travelers.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r4.claim: The phrase is an absolute exception from all states, accusative as a circumstantial expression attached to the prohibition insofar as it concerns the junub condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r4.anchor: والعامل فيه معنى النهي أي لا تقربوا الصلاة جنبا في حال من الأحوال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r5.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r5.claim: The exception indicates generally that the following case differs from the preceding rule, but does not by itself establish which individual cases are exempt or their legal status.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r5.anchor: قاله المولى شيخ الإسلام وقيل : هو صفة لجنبا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r6.claim: Some take the phrase as an adjective of junub, with إلا meaning غير; this is disputed because such adjectival use is usually needed only when exception is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r6.anchor: وقيل : هو صفة لجنبا على أن ( إلا ) بمعنى غير

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r7.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r7.claim: Ibn al-Hajib requires exception to be impossible before إلا can function descriptively, though grammarians disagree and some prefer the descriptive reading here.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r7.anchor: ذكره ابن الحاجب وقد خالفه فيه النحاة ورجح بعضهم الوصفية هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r8.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r8.claim: On the mosque interpretation of prayer, crossing through a mosque is allowed for a junub person; al-Shafi'i holds this, while the well-known Hanafi position forbids mosque entry absolutely.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r8.anchor: وبه قال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى والمشهور عندنا منع الجنب المسجد مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r9.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r9.claim: A report is cited for Ali allowing passage through a mosque for the junub; al-Alusi says the transmission that Ali first allowed it and later prohibited it is not established to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r9.anchor: ورخص علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه كما في خبر الترمذي عن أبي سعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r10.speaker: الجصاص
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r10.claim: Al-Jassas says entry is not allowed unless the water or the route is in the mosque.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r10.anchor: ونقل الجصاص في الأحكام أنه لا يجوز الدخول إلا أن يكون الماء أو الطريق فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r11.speaker: الليث
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r11.claim: Al-Layth allows a junub person to pass only when his door opens into the mosque; some Ansar had no other route, so they received a concession.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r11.anchor: وعن الليث أن الجنب لا يمر إلا أن يكون بابه في المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r12.claim: Until you wash marks the end of the prohibition on approaching prayer in janaba; placing the exception first signals that this rule is not absolute, unlike the intoxication rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r12.anchor: حتى تغتسلوا غاية للنهي عن قربان الصلاة حال الجنابة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r13.claim: Another explanation says washing is mentioned, though not the main point of validity while junub, to show that janaba ends only through ritual washing.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r13.anchor: وقيل : لما لم يكن لقوله سبحانه : ( حتى تغتسلوا ) مدخل في المقصود

ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r14.claim: The verse signals that worshippers should avoid distractions and purify the self; if the body must be purified, purifying the heart is even more fitting, since it is God's throne.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p39/r14.anchor: وفي الآية الكريمة رمز إلى أنه ينبغي للمصلي أن يتحرز عما يلهيه ويشغل قلبه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r1.claim: The sickness clause explains other cases treated like the travel exception; travel is singled out first to stress that dispensations turn on necessity, so those excluded lack a legally recognized excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r1.anchor: وبهذا يندفع الإيراد السابق على الحصر وإنما لم يقل

ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r2.claim: The wording's general expression followed by detail is more eloquent and emphatic than explicitly listing travelers and patients lacking water, while accommodating different levels of understanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r2.anchor: لما أن ما في النظم الكريم أبلغ وأوكد منه لما فيه من الإجمال والتفصيل

ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r3.claim: Illness means any condition that prevents water use, whether because water cannot be reached or cannot safely be used.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r3.anchor: والمراد بالمرض ما يمنع من استعمال الماء مطلقا سواء كان بتعذر الوصول إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says the patient allowed dry ablution includes a person with a fracture or wound; if he becomes junub, he should not wash an injury when that risks harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن جريج عن ابن مسعود أنه قال : المريض الذي قد أرخص له في التيمم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report raised to the Prophet, says a person with a wound, ulcers, or smallpox who fears washing while junub may use dry ablution.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r5.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في المعرفة عن ابن عباس يرفعه إذا كانت بالرجل الجراحة في سبيل الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r6.claim: The established Hanafi rule permits dry ablution when using water is expected to worsen illness, whether worsening comes from movement or water itself; fear of death is not required.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r6.anchor: والذي تقرر في الفروع : إن المريض الذي يخاف إذا استعمل الماء أن يشتد مرضه يتيمم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r7.claim: The verse's unrestricted wording appears to allow every sick person dry ablution, but other verses exclude those whose illness will not worsen; legal works detail the rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p40/r7.anchor: ولم يشترط أصحابنا خوف التلف لظاهر النص وهو بإطلاقه يبيح التيمم لكل مريض

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r1.claim: The phrase is coordinated with illness and covers journeys of any length; this wording is clearer than simply saying “travelers.”
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r1.anchor: عطف على مرضى أي أو كنتم على سفر ما طال أو قصر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r2.speaker: الهداية
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r2.claim: Al-Hidaya allows tayammum for someone without water who is traveling or at least a mile outside town.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r2.anchor: ومن لم يجد الماء وهو مسافر أو خارج المصر بينه وبين المصر ميل أو أكثر يتيمم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r3.claim: For a nontraveling person outside town, the same rule follows by analogy, not directly from the text.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن حكم من هو خارج المصر غير مسافر كما يقتضيه العطف معلوم بالقياس لا بالنص

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r4.speaker: من حمل الصلاة على مواضعها
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r4.claim: One parsing takes prayer as its locations and crossing as passing through them, so the later condition states a distinct rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r4.anchor: من حمل الصلاة على مواضعها وفسر العبور بالاجتياز بها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r5.claim: The recommended pause after “until you wash” and the spatial language of approaching, crossing, and travel support that interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r5.anchor: القراء كلهم استحبوا الوقف عند قوله سبحانه : ( حتى تغتسلوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r6.speaker: الكثير
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r6.claim: Many commentators take the passage otherwise than the spatial interpretation of prayer and crossing.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r6.anchor: إلا أن الكثير على خلافه وإنما قدم المرض على السفر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r7.claim: Travel is mentioned to connect illness with travel and equate them through inability to use water, even when water is present.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r7.anchor: وقيل : ذكر السفر هنا لإلحاق المرض به والتسوية بينه وبينه بإلحاق الواجد بالفاقد بجامع العجز عن الاستعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r8.claim: Illness precedes travel to signal its primacy and independent rulings, which do not occur in other cases.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r8.anchor: وإنما قدم المرض على السفر للإيذان بأصالته واستقلاله بأحكام لا توجد في غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r9.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r9.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i reports that wounded Companions developed widespread injuries, then janaba, complained to the Prophet, and the illness clause was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r9.anchor: أخرج ابن جريج عن إبراهيم النخعي قال : نال أصحاب النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم جراحة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r10.claim: The majority report revelation at al-Muraysiʿ: ʿAisha lost Asma's necklace during travel, the party lacked water, and tayammum was revealed; Usayd praised the blessing and relief granted to Aisha's family.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r10.anchor: هذا خلاف ما عليه الجمهور حيث رووا أن نزولها في غزوة المريسيع حين عرس رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r11.claim: Al-ghaʾiṭ originally means a low place; going there became a euphemism for relieving oneself because people concealed themselves from view.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r11.anchor: وهو المكان المنخفض وجاء الغيط بفتح الغين وسكون الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads al-ghayṭ with fatḥa on ghayn and a still yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r12.anchor: وبه قرأ ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r13.claim: One derivation treats ghayṭ as the verbal noun of yaghūṭ, with the expected wāw changed to yāʾ and made still.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r13.anchor: وهو في رأي مصدر يغوط وكان القياس غوطا فقلبت الواو ياءا وسكنت

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r14.claim: The preferable account treats ghayṭ as a lightened form, like the variant pair hayyin and hayyin.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r14.anchor: ولعل الأولى ما قيل : إنه تخفيف غيط كهين وهين

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r15.claim: The singular “someone” hints that people go alone when relieving themselves, as custom and proper conduct require.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r15.anchor: وفي ذكر ( أحد ) فيه دون غيره إيماء إلى أن الإنسان ينفرد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r16.claim: Another explanation says the singular subject avoids explicitly attributing an embarrassing or disagreeable act to the audience.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r16.anchor: وقيل : إنما ذكر وأسند المجئ إليه دون المخاطبين تفاديا عن التصريح

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r17.claim: The clause is coordinated with “you were”; the first prepositional phrase describes the preceding indefinite, and the second attaches to the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r17.anchor: والفعل عطف على ( كنتم ) والجار الأول متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة للنكرة قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r18.claim: “Touching women” euphemistically means intercourse, indicating major impurity, while the preceding clause indicates minor impurity.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r18.anchor: يريد سبحانه أو جامعتم النساء إلا أنه كنى بالملامسة عن الجماع

ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r19.speaker: علي وابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r19.claim: ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, and al-Hasan are cited for the intercourse reading, which indicates major impurity.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p41/r19.anchor: وإلى ذلك ذهب علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما والحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود والنخعي والشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud, al-Nakhaʿi, and al-Shaʿbi interpret the phrase as skin touching short of intercourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r1.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود والنخعي والشعبي أن المراد بالملامسة ما دون الجماع

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r2.speaker: الشافعي والزهري والأوزاعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r2.claim: Al-Shafiʿi infers that touching a woman invalidates ablution; al-Zuhri and al-Awzaʿi agree.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r2.anchor: وبه استدل الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه على أن اللمس ينقض الوضوء وبه قال الزهري والأوزاعي

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r3.speaker: مالك والليث بن سعد وأحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r3.claim: Malik, al-Layth, and one report from Ahmad say touching invalidates ablution only when accompanied by desire.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r3.anchor: وقال مالك والليث بن سعد وأحمد في إحدى الروايات عنه : إن كان اللمس بشهوة نقض وإلا فلا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that touching does not invalidate ablution, even with desire; another qualification says it does if erection occurs.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r4.anchor: وذهب أبو حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه إلى أنه لا ينتقض الوضوء بالمس ولو بشهوة قيل : ما لم يحدث الإنتشار

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r5.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r5.claim: Al-Shafiʿi differed over touching close relatives or a young unrelated woman; his sounder view is that it does not invalidate ablution, like touching teeth, nails, or hair.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r5.anchor: واختلف قول الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه في لمس المحارم كالأم والبنت والأخت وفي لمس الأجنبية الصغيرة وأصح القولين : إنه لا ينقض

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r6.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r6.claim: In al-Shafiʿi's stronger view, the person touched also loses ablution because both participants share the possibility of pleasure, as in intercourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r6.anchor: وينتقض عنده وضوء الملموسة كاللامس في الأظهر لاشتراكهما في مظنة اللذة كالمشتركين في الجماع

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r7.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi does not invalidate the touched person's ablution when their private part is touched, since that person did not touch a locus of pleasure.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r7.anchor: وإنما لم ينتقض وضوء الملموس فرجه على مذهبه لأنه لم يوجد منه مس لمظنة لذة أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r8.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r8.claim: Aisha reports placing her hand on the Prophet's feet while he prostrated, evidence cited against invalidating ablution for the person touched.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r8.anchor: حديث عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أنها وضعت يدها على قدميه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r9.claim: The literal sense is stronger, especially in Hamza and al-Kisaʾi's reading aw lamastum, since لمس is less established as a euphemism for intercourse than ملامسة.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r9.anchor: أن الحمل على الحقيقة هو الراجح لا سيما في قراءة حمزة والكسائي أو لمستم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r10.claim: Others prefer interpreting both readings as intercourse, privileging figurative usage and reconciling the readings; this matches the Hanafi position.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r10.anchor: ورجح بعضهم الحمل على الجماع في القراءتين ترجيحا للمجاز والمشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r11.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r11.claim: Some investigators say mutual bodily contact by any body part is the literal meaning, which includes intercourse; it is metaphor only when intercourse alone is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r11.anchor: إن الملامسة حقيقة في تماس البدنين بشئ من أجزائهما من غير تقييد باليد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r12.speaker: الجلال المحلي والكمال ابن أبي شريف
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r12.claim: Al-Jalal al-Mahalli calls touching by hand literal; Ibn Abi Sharif says this exemplifies one kind of touch rather than defining the full literal meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r12.anchor: وادعى الجلال المحلى أن الملامسة حقيقة في الجس باليد تمثيلا للملامسة بنوع من أنواعها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r13.claim: The bodily events trigger purification; lack of water or ability to use it is the actual condition licensing tayammum.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r13.anchor: ليس باعتبار أنفسهما بل باعتبار قيدهما المستفاد من قوله سبحانه : فلم تجدوا ماء بل هو السبب في الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r14.claim: The events prepare for the water condition and show that it licenses relief after the cause of purification arises for either minor or major impurity.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r14.anchor: وإنما ذكرا تمهيدا له وتنبيها على أنه سبب للرخصة بعد انعقاد سبب الطهارة بقسميها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r15.claim: One explanation says water absence also conditions illness and travel, but need not be repeated because major impurity is already clear there and minor impurity follows by textual implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42/r15.anchor: قيل : وتخصيص ذكره بهذه الصورة مع أنه معتبر أيضا في صورة المرض والسفر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r1.claim: A view makes lack of water a condition applying to all, including the purification implied by the two bodily-event clauses; al-Alusi says the syntax does not support it.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r1.anchor: إن هذا القيد راجع للكل وقيد وجوب التطهر المكنى عنه بالمجئ من الغائط

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r2.claim: A proposal reorders the verse: prohibit prayer in intoxication, janaba, or after either event, then command tayammum for illness or travel; al-Alusi objects that it splits condition and result without rationale.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r2.anchor: وفي الكشف عن بعضهم أن في الآية تقديما وتأخيرا والتقدير لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r3.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the apparent order: waterlessness can mean inability to use water and govern all cases, or retain its literal sense without attaching it to illness and travel.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r3.anchor: ولعل الأوجه في تقرير الآية والله تعالى أعلم أن يجعل عدم الوجدان عبارة عن عدم القدرة على استعمال الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r4.claim: Illness and travel need not be restricted to people already in minor or major impurity: the verse explains the switch from water purification to tayammum.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r4.anchor: وأن يبقى قوله سبحانه : ( مرضى أو على سفر ) على إطلاقه من غير تقييد بكونهم محدثين أو مجنبين

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r5.claim: People outside illness and travel illustrate that inability to use water for other reasons also licenses tayammum; the ritual event itself is not the cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r5.anchor: وأن يجعل ذكر المحدثين من غير القبيلين بيانا لسبب العدول وهو فقد القدرة من غير سفر ولا مرض

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r6.claim: Naming the events before waterlessness signals that lack of water licenses relief only after purification becomes obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r6.anchor: ولم يقل أو لم تجدوا دون ذكر السببين تنبيها على أن عدم الوجدان مرخص

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r7.claim: The first fa coordinates; the fa in the tayammum command answers the whole condition, whose pronoun covers all cases, so no separate command for the latrine clause is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r7.anchor: والفاء في ( فلم ) عاطفة وأما الفاء في قوله سبحانه : ( فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فواقعة في جواب الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r8.claim: Tayammum literally means intending; al-Aʿsha's line illustrates the sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r8.anchor: والتيمم لغة القصد قال الأعشى : ( تيممت قيسا )

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r9.speaker: الخليل وثعلب
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r9.claim: Al-Khalil and Thaʿlab define ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface; al-Zajjaj says linguists do not disagree.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r9.anchor: والصعيد وجه الأرض كما روي عن الخليل وثعلب وقال الزجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r10.claim: Ṣaʿīd may mean the furthest surface reached from the earth's interior or what is raised above the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r10.anchor: وسمي بذلك لأنه نهاية ما يصعد إليه من باطن الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r11.speaker: سفيان
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r11.claim: Sufyan glosses ṭayyib as lawful; another sense is plant-growing rather than saline, as in 7:58.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r11.anchor: وعن سفيان الحلال وقيل : المنبت دون السبخة كما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r12.claim: The sense pure best fits purification: aim for a clean part of the earth's surface.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r12.anchor: والحمل على الأول هو الأنسب بمقام الطهارة والمعنى فتعمدوا واقصدوا شيئا من وجه الأرض طاهرا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r13.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r13.claim: Abu Hanifa and one report from Muhammad permit tayammum with kohl, brick, litharge, gems, or coral without dust.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r13.anchor: وهذا دليل واضح لجواز التيمم بالكحل والآجر والمرداسنج والياقوت

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r14.speaker: محمد وأبو يوسف والشافعي وأحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r14.claim: Another report from Muhammad, with Abu Yusuf, al-Shafiʿi, and Ahmad, requires dust to adhere, citing the partitive من in 5:6; Hanafis read it as origination or customary wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r14.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه وهو قول أبي يوسف والشافعي وأحمد رضي الله تعالى عنهم أنه لا يجوز التيمم إلا أن يعلق باليد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r15.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r15.claim: Malik permits tayammum with snow; al-Alusi notes Shiite criticism and says he defended Malik in a separate work.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r15.anchor: وأغرب الإمام مالك فأجاز التيمم بالثلج وقد شنع الشيعة عليه بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r16.claim: Ṣaʿīdan is a direct object, or is accusative after an omitted preposition meaning “with a surface.”
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r16.anchor: ونصب ( صعيدا ) على أنه مفعول به وقيل : إنه منصوب بنزع الخافض

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r17.claim: The bāʾ is connective; the apparent ruling requires wiping the whole face and hands, so leaving any part unwiped invalidates tayammum.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r17.anchor: أي وجوهكم وأيديكم على أن الباء صلة والمراد استيعاب هذين العضوين بالمسح

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r18.speaker: الحسن عن الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r18.claim: A report from Hasan on Abu Hanifa's authority says wiping most of each area suffices, as full coverage is not required for wiping boots or head.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r18.anchor: وفي رواية الحسن عن الإمام رضي الله تعالى عنه أن الأكثر يقوم مقام الكل

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r19.claim: Al-Alusi prefers full coverage because tayammum substitutes for ablution, which requires it; fingers are separated and rings removed.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r19.anchor: ووجه الظاهر أن التيمم قائم مقام الوضوء ولهذا قالوا : يخلل الأصابع وينزع الخاتم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r20.claim: Yad can cover the hand through the wrist, elbow, or armpit; treating these ranges as literal explains early disagreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r20.anchor: وأيدي جمع يد وهي مشتركة بين معان من أطراف الأصابع إلى الرسغ وإلى المرفق

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r21.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r21.claim: Al-Tabari transmits al-Zuhri's view that tayammum wiping reaches the armpits.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r21.anchor: فأخرج ابن جرير عن الزهري أن التيمم إلى الآباط

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r22.speaker: مكحول
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r22.claim: Al-Tabari transmits Makḥul's view of a strike for the face and palms through the wrists.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r22.anchor: وأخرج عن مكحول أنه قال : التيمم ضربة للوجه والكفين إلى الكوع

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r23.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r23.claim: Al-Hakim reports from Ibn ʿUmar that they wiped from elbows to palms over the hair-bearing areas on both sides.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r23.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم عن ابن عمر في كيفية تيممهم مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r24.speaker: أبو داود
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r24.claim: A report in Abu Dawud says the Prophet wiped his hands to the elbows; al-Alusi identifies this as his school's, al-Shafiʿi's, and most scholars' view.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r24.anchor: ومن حديث أبي داود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تيمم ومسح يديه إلى مرفقيه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r25.claim: Wiping to the elbows is supported by analogy with ablution, the original purification; the majority also report its validity.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r25.anchor: ويشهد لهم القياس على الوضوء الذي هو أصله وإن كان الحدث والجنابة فيه كيفية سواء

ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r26.speaker: عمر وابن عمر وابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r26.claim: Reports from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Masʿud deny tayammum for janaba, menstruation, and postpartum impurity; they regard it as a nonanalogical concession for minor impurity only.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p42#2/r26.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : لا يتيمم الجنب والحائض والنفساء وهو المروي عن عمر وابنه وابن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r1.claim: Al-Alusi says the verse is nearly explicit that a person in janaba may use tayammum, even if touching women is not read as intercourse; hadith reports confirm this.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r1.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الآية كالصريح في جواز تيمم الجنب وإن لم تحمل الملامسة على الوقاع

ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r2.speaker: عمران بن حصين
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r2.claim: In a Bukhari report from ʿImran ibn Husayn, a man says he is in janaba without water, and the Prophet tells him to use earth, which suffices.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r2.anchor: أخرج البخاري عن عمران بن حصين أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم رأى رجلا معتزلا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r3.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r3.claim: People in sandy country with no water for a month or two, including people in janaba, menstruation, and postpartum impurity, are told by the Prophet to use their land.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r3.anchor: وروي أن قوما جاءوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وقالوا : إنا قوم نسكن هذه الرمال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r4.claim: Scholars disagree whether tayammum removes ritual impurity; on close inspection this verse proves neither position.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r4.anchor: وهل يرفع التيمم الحدث أم لا خلاف ولا دلالة في الآية على أحد الأمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r5.claim: The divine names explain and affirm the dispensation: God's settled practice is to pardon those at fault and forgive sinners, so He provides ease.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r5.anchor: تعليل لما يفهمه الكلام من الترخيص والتيسير وتقرير لهما فإن من عادته المستمرة أن يعفو

ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r6.claim: Another view takes ʿafw here to mean facilitation, citing the Prophet's statement that he waived alms on horses and slaves.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r6.anchor: وقيل : العفو هنا بمعنى التيسير كما في التيسير

ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says the facilitation sense in the hadith is not certain, and it is unlikely that forgiveness here specifically concerns those who prayed intoxicated and their recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p44/r7.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن حمل العفو على التيسير في الحديث غير متعين وكون ذكر المغفرة لما ذكر بعيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r1.speaker: الأكثرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r1.claim: Most interpreters take “drunk” to mean intoxicated by wine.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r1.anchor: والمراد من السكر: السكر من الخمر، عند الأكثرين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r2.claim: Before wine was prohibited, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf hosted Companions who drank, then one led Maghrib and omitted “not” while reciting al-Kāfirūn; this verse made them avoid drunkenness at prayer until wine was prohibited.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r2.anchor: وذلك أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله عنه صنع طعاما ودعا ناسا من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r3.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the drunkenness as sleepiness and the verse as forbidding prayer when sleep overwhelms a person.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك بن مزاحم: أراد به سكر النوم، نهى عن الصلاة عند غلبة النوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet instructed a drowsy worshipper to sleep until alert, lest he pray while sleepy and curse himself while intending to seek forgiveness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219/r4.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا نعس أحدكم وهو يصلي فليرقد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r1.claim: “Junub” is accusative as a circumstantial expression: do not approach prayer while in a state of janābah; the form is used for men, women, and plurals.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r1.anchor: نصب على الحال، يعني: ولا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم جنب، يقال: رجل جنب وامرأة جنب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r2.claim: Janābah originally means distance; a junub avoids the place of prayer or is separated from other people until washing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r2.anchor: وأصل الجنابة: البعد وسمي جنبا لأنه يتجنب موضع الصلاة، أو لمجانبته الناس وبعده منهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r3.speaker: علي وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r3.claim: They read the exception as allowing a traveler without water to perform tayammum and pray while junub.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r3.anchor: وهذا قول علي وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد رضي الله عنهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وسعيد بن المسيب والضحاك والحسن وعكرمة والنخعي والزهري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r4.claim: They take “prayer” to mean its place, the mosque: a junub may pass through to exit or cross but may not remain there.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r4.anchor: ومعناه: لا تقربوا المسجد وأنتم جنب إلا مجتازين فيه للخروج منه، مثل أن ينام في المسجد فيجنب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r5.claim: The passage exception addressed Anṣār whose homes opened into the mosque; when they became junub without water, their only route out passed through it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r5.anchor: وذلك أن قوما من الأنصار كانت أبوابهم في المسجد فتصيبهم الجنابة ولا ماء عندهم ولا ممر لهم إلا في المسجد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r6.speaker: الحسن ومالك والشافعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mālik, and al-Shāfiʿī permit a junub to pass through a mosque without restriction; the opinion scholars prohibit passage categorically, while another view requires tayammum.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r6.anchor: فأباح بعضهم المرور فيه على الإطلاق، وهو قول الحسن وبه قال مالك والشافعي رحمهم الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r7.claim: Most scholars forbid a junub from staying in a mosque, citing the report from ʿĀʾisha that the Prophet excluded menstruating women and the junub from the mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r7.anchor: لما روينا عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r8.claim: In a report from ʿĀʾisha, the Prophet says he does not permit a menstruating woman or a junub in the mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r8.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "وجهوا هذه البيوت عن المسجد فإني لا أحل المسجد لحائض ولا جنب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r9.speaker: أحمد والمزني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r9.claim: Aḥmad permits remaining in the mosque and regards the supporting report as weak because its transmitter is unknown; al-Muzanī agrees.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r9.anchor: وجوز أحمد المكث فيه وضعف الحديث لأن راويه مجهول، وبه قال المزني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r10.claim: A junub may neither perform ṭawāf, as with prayer, nor recite the Qurʾān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r10.anchor: ولا يجوز للجنب الطواف كما لا يجوز له الصلاة ولا يجوز له قراءة القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r11.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r11.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet read the Qurʾān and did ordinary activities, and that only janābah prevented him from reciting it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p219#2/r11.anchor: يقول: دخلت على علي رضي الله عنه فقال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقضي الحاجة ويأكل معنا اللحم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r1.claim: Ghusl for janābah becomes obligatory either when semen is emitted or when the circumcised parts meet through penetration, even without emission; the earlier exemption after intercourse without emission was abrogated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r1.anchor: وغسل الجنابة يجب بأحد الأمرين: إما بنزول المني أو بالتقاء الختانين، وهو تغييب الحشفة في الفرج وإن لم ينزل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r2.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r2.claim: Asked by Abū Mūsā about the meeting of the circumcised parts, ʿĀʾisha cites the Prophet: their meeting, or contact of one with the other, makes ghusl obligatory.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r2.anchor: فقالت عائشة: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا التقى الختانان، أو مس الختان الختان فقد وجب الغسل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r3.claim: The sick person meant is one harmed by water, such as with smallpox, or whose ablution site is wounded and water risks death or greater pain; tayammum is permitted even when water is available.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r3.anchor: مثل الجدري ونحوه، أو كان على موضع طهارته جراحة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r4.claim: When some ablution limbs are sound and others wounded, wash the sound limbs and use tayammum for the wounded ones.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r4.anchor: وإن كان بعض أعضاء طهارته صحيحا والبعض جريحا غسل الصحيح منها وتيمم للجريح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r5.claim: Jābir reports that a wounded traveler was wrongly told to wash, died, and the Prophet condemned those who advised him; tayammum, binding and wiping over the wound, and washing the rest would have sufficed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p221/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: خرجنا في سفر فأصاب رجلا منا حجر فشجه في رأسه، فاحتلم فسأل أصحابه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r1.speaker: أصحاب الرأي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r1.claim: The opinion scholars reject combining tayammum with washing: if most limbs are sound, wash them without tayammum; if most are wounded, tayammum alone suffices.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r1.anchor: الصحيح ولا يتيمم عليه، وإن كان الأكثر جريحا اقتصر على التيمم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r2.claim: The wounded traveler report supports combining tayammum with washing the sound parts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r2.anchor: والحديث حجة لمن أوجب الجمع بينهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r3.claim: On any journey, long or short, a person without water prays using tayammum and need not repeat the prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r3.anchor: أراد أنه إذا كان في سفر طويلا كان أو قصيرا، وعدم الماء فإنه يصلي بالتيمم ولا إعادة عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r4.claim: Abū Dharr reports the Prophet taught that pure earth is a Muslim’s means of purification even after ten years without water; upon finding water, he should apply it to his skin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r4.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الصعيد الطيب وضوء المسلم وإن لم يجد الماء عشر سنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r5.speaker: الشافعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r5.claim: For someone neither ill nor traveling who unexpectedly lacks water in a place where water is usually available, al-Shāfiʿī requires prayer with tayammum followed by repetition when water becomes available.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r5.anchor: فإنه يصلي بالتيمم ثم يعيد إذا قدر على الماء عند الشافعي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r6.speaker: مالك والأوزاعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r6.claim: Mālik and al-Awzāʿī say the person who unexpectedly lacks water in a normally supplied place need not repeat after finding water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r6.anchor: وعند مالك والأوزاعي لا إعادة عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says a person who unexpectedly lacks water in a normally supplied place should delay prayer until water is found.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222/r7.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه يؤخر الصلاة حتى يجد الماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.claim: “Ghaʾiṭ” originally means low-lying ground; Arabs went there to relieve themselves, so the place-name became a euphemism for defecation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.anchor: والغائط: اسم للمطمئن من الأرض، وكانت عادة العرب إتيان الغائط للحدث فكني عن الحدث بالغائط

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read “lamastum” here and in al-Māʾidah; the other readers read “lāmastum.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي " لمستم " هاهنا وفي المائدة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.claim: They interpret touching as intercourse, using touch as a euphemism because intercourse only happens through touching.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة، وكني باللمس [عن الجماع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر والشعبي والنخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r4.claim: They interpret touching as the meeting of two skins, whether or not intercourse occurs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: هما التقاء البشرتين سواء كان بجماع أو غير جماع، وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عمر، والشعبي والنخعي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر والزهري والأوزاعي والشافعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.claim: This group holds that direct contact between any part of a man’s and woman’s bodies, without a barrier, invalidates both ablutions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.anchor: فذهب جماعة إلى أنه إذا أفضى الرجل بشيء من بدنه إلى شيء من بدن المرأة ولا حائل بينهما، ينتقض وضوؤهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r6.speaker: مالك والليث بن سعد وأحمد وإسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r6.claim: Mālik, al-Layth, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq say touch invalidates ablution only when done with desire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r6.anchor: وقال مالك والليث بن سعد وأحمد وإسحاق: إن كان اللمس بشهوة نقض الطهر، وإن لم يكن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والثوري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and al-Thawrī say touch never invalidates ablution.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r7.anchor: وقال قوم: لا ينتقض الوضوء باللمس بحال، وهو قول ابن عباس وبه قال الحسن والثوري

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says touch invalidates ablution only if it causes an erection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه لا ينتقض إلا أن يحدث الانتشار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r9.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r9.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that she slept in front of the Prophet with her feet toward his prayer direction; when he prostrated, he nudged them, and she drew them in, without lamps in their homes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r9.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنها قالت: كنت أنام بين يدي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ورجلاي في قبلته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r10.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r10.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports feeling for the Prophet at night and touching his feet while he prostrated and recited a supplication seeking refuge in God’s approval and pardon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p222#2/r10.anchor: أن عائشة رضي الله عنها زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: كنت نائمة إلى جنب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ففقدته من الليل فلمسته بيدي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r1.speaker: سفيان الثوري وابن المبارك وأصحاب الرأي وأحمد وإسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r1.claim: They hold that vomiting, nosebleeds, bloodletting, and cupping invalidate ablution; they agree that small amounts and wind from outside the two usual outlets do not.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r1.anchor: وذهبت جماعة إلى إيجاب الوضوء بالقيء والرعاف والفصد والحجامة منهم سفيان الثوري وابن المبارك وأصحاب الرأي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r2.claim: Tayammum is a privilege of this Muslim community, which has been given the whole earth as a mosque and its soil as purification when water is unavailable.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r2.anchor: اعلم أن التيمم من خصائص هذه الأمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r3.claim: Ḥudhayfa reports the Prophet listing three favors: rows like the angels’ rows, the whole earth made a mosque, and its soil made purifying when water is unavailable.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r4.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha recounts that a lost necklace delayed the party at al-Bayḍāʾ or Dhāt al-Jaysh with no water; after Abū Bakr reproached her, the Prophet woke and tayammum was revealed, and the necklace was found beneath her camel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r4.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض أسفاره حتى إذا كنا بالبيداء أو بذات الجيش انقطع عقد لي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r5.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r5.claim: After the necklace was found, Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr called it another blessing for Abū Bakr’s family.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p225/r5.anchor: فقال أسيد بن حضير وهو أحد النقباء: ما هذه بأول بركتكم يا آل أبي بكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r1.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r1.claim: In another account, ʿĀʾisha says a necklace borrowed from Asmāʾ was lost; companions sent to search for it reached prayer time without ablution, and tayammum was revealed after they reported this to the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أنها استعارت من أسماء قلادة فهلكت: فأرسل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ناسا من أصحابه في طلبها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r2.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r2.claim: Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr thanked ʿĀʾisha, saying God always made a way out of her difficulties and made them a blessing for Muslims.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r2.anchor: فقال أسيد بن حضير: جزاك الله خيرا فوالله ما نزل بك أمر قط إلا جعل الله لك منه مخرجا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r3.claim: Tayammum means to intend or aim; “pure saʿīd” means clean, pure soil, and Ibn ʿAbbās specifically identifies saʿīd as soil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: الصعيد هو التراب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r4.speaker: الشافعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī restricts tayammum to soil that leaves dust on the hand, citing the Prophet’s report that its soil was made purifying.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r4.anchor: فذهب الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى إلى أنه يختص بما يقع عليه اسم التراب مما يعلق باليد منه غبار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r5.speaker: أصحاب الرأي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r5.claim: The opinion scholars permit tayammum using substances such as arsenic, gypsum, and lime, including rock with no dust or dust blown away before wiping.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r5.anchor: وجوز أصحاب الرأي التيمم بالزرنيخ والجص والنورة وغيرها من طبقات الأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r6.speaker: أصحاب الرأي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r6.claim: They define saʿīd as the face of the earth and cite Jābir’s general report that the earth was made a mosque and purification.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r6.anchor: وقالوا: الصعيد وجه الأرض، لما روي عن جابر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r7.claim: The general earth report is qualified by Ḥudhayfa’s report specifying soil; the specific report explains and takes precedence over the general one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r7.anchor: وهذا مجمل، وحديث حذيفة في تخصيص التراب مفسر، والمفسر من الحديث يقضي على المجمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r8.claim: Some permit tayammum with anything attached to the earth, including trees and plants, because they take saʿīd to mean what rises on the earth’s surface.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r8.anchor: وجوز بعضهم التيمم بكل ما هو متصل بالأرض من شجر ونبات، ونحوهما وقال: إن الصعيد اسم لما تصاعد على وجه الأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r9.claim: Intending the soil is a condition for valid tayammum; merely standing in wind so dust reaches the face, even with intention, is insufficient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p226/r9.anchor: والقصد إلى التراب شرط لصحة التيمم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r1.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r1.claim: Most scholars require two strikes: wipe the whole face, with no need to reach beneath facial hair, then strike again and wipe both hands to the elbows.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r1.anchor: فذهب أكثر أهل العلم إلى أنه يمسح الوجه واليدين مع المرفقين، بضربتين، يضرب كفيه على التراب فيمسح جميع وجهه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r2.speaker: أبو الصمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r2.claim: Abū al-Ṣimma reports that after relieving himself, the Prophet scraped a wall with a stick, wiped his face and forearms against it, and then returned the greeting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r2.anchor: عن أبي الصمة قال: مررت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يبول فسلمت عليه فلم يرد علي حتى قام إلى جدار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r3.claim: The report supports wiping to the elbows, as in ablution, and shows that dust must adhere: otherwise the Prophet would not have scraped the wall.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r3.anchor: ففيه دليل على وجوب مسح اليدين إلى المرفقين كما يجب غسلهما في الوضوء إلى المرفقين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r4.speaker: الزهري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r4.claim: Al-Zuhrī says to wipe the hands up to the shoulders, citing ʿAmmār’s report that they performed tayammum to the shoulders.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r4.anchor: وذهب الزهري إلى أنه يمسح اليدين إلى المنكبين، لما روي عن عمار أنه قال: تيممنا إلى المناكب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r5.claim: Baghawī rejects the shoulder evidence as a description of ʿAmmār’s own action, not the Prophet’s instruction; when asked, the Prophet directed wiping the face and palms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r5.anchor: وذلك حكاية فعله لم ينقله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، كما روي أنه قال: أجنبت فتمعكت في التراب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r6.speaker: علي وابن عباس والشعبي وعطاء ومكحول والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r6.claim: They hold that tayammum takes one strike for the face and palms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r6.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أن التيمم ضربة واحدة للوجه والكفين، وهو قول علي وابن عباس رضي الله عنهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r7.claim: ʿAmmār reports the Prophet taught that one strike sufficed: he struck the ground, blew on his hands, then wiped his face and palms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p227/r7.anchor: عن أبيه قال: جاء رجل إلى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه فقال: إني أجنبت فلم أصب الماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r1.claim: In another wording, ʿAmmār tells ʿUmar that after he rolled in dust while junub, the Prophet said wiping the face and palms was sufficient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r1.anchor: فقال عمار لعمر رضي الله عنه: تمعكت فأتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r2.claim: The report proves that a junub without water may pray after tayammum; menstruating or postpartum women may do so once purified if they lack water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث دليل على أن الجنب إذا لم يجد الماء يصلي بالتيمم، وكذا الحائض والنفساء إذا طهرتا وعدمتا الماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r3.speaker: عمر وابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r3.claim: ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd held that a junub must delay prayer until water is available, interpreting “touch women” as hand contact rather than intercourse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r3.anchor: وذهب عمر وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما إلى أن الجنب لا يصلي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r4.claim: Baghawī rejects that position: ʿAmmār’s report is proof for tayammum in janābah; ʿUmar had forgotten the incident ʿAmmār recalled and was not persuaded.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r4.anchor: وحديث عمار رضي الله عنه حجة، وكان عمر نسي ما ذكر له عمار فلم يقنع بقوله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to have later retracted his view and allowed tayammum for a junub.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r5.anchor: وروي أن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه رجع عن قوله وجوز التيمم للجنب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r6.claim: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn reports that the Prophet ordered a junub man to perform tayammum and pray, then wash once he found water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r6.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين رضي الله عنهم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر رجلا كان جنبا أن يتيمم ثم يصلي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r7.claim: Abū Dharr reports that he sometimes remained junub for five or six days without water; the Prophet said clean earth purifies for up to ten years and to apply water to the skin when found.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r7.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنهم قال: اجتمعت غنيمة من الصدقة عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا أبا ذر ابد فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r8.claim: Tayammum can replace full-body washing for the junub, menstruant, postpartum woman, and deceased; the four limbs’ washing for minor impurity; or washing a particular injured limb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p228/r8.anchor: ومسح الوجه واليدين في التيمم، تارة يكون بدلا من غسل جميع البدن في حق الجنب والحائض والنفساء والميت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن عمر والشعبي والنخعي وقتادة ومالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r1.claim: This group says tayammum is valid only after prayer time begins and cannot cover two obligatory prayers; the verse requires purification for each prayer, while one water ablution may cover several prayers as at the conquest of Mecca.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r1.anchor: ولا يصح التيمم لصلاة الوقت إلا بعد دخول الوقت، ولا يجوز أن يجمع بين فريضتين بتيمم واحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والحسن والزهري والثوري وأصحاب الرأي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r2.claim: They treat tayammum like water purification: it may precede prayer time and cover any number of obligatory prayers while the person remains in a state of purity.
