BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r2.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أن التيمم كالطهارة بالماء يجوز تقديمه على وقت الصلاة، ويجوز أن يصلي به ما شاء من الفرائض ما لم يحدث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r3.claim: All agree one tayammum also permits any number of voluntary prayers before or after the obligatory prayer and Qurʾān recitation even for a junub.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r3.anchor: واتفقوا على أنه يجوز أن يصلي بتيمم واحد مع الفريضة ما شاء من النوافل، قبل الفريضة وبعدها، وأن يقرأ القرآن إن كان جنبا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r4.claim: A traveler without water must search among his belongings and companions; in open desert he looks around, and if a nearby hill or wall blocks sight, he goes around it, since not finding water implies seeking it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r4.anchor: وإن كان تيممه بعذر السفر وعدم الماء فيشترط طلب الماء، وهو أن يطلبه من رحله ورفقائه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa does not require searching; water inaccessible because of an enemy, beast, or lack of a tool to draw it counts as unavailable, permitting prayer by tayammum without repetition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p229/r5.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه: طلب الماء ليس بشرط، فإن رأى الماء ولكن بينه وبين الماء حائل من عدو أو سبع يمنعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r1.claim: Do not enter prayer while intoxicated through sleep or wine until sober and understanding what you say in prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r1.anchor: أي لا تقوموا إليها وأنتم سكارى من نحو نوم أو خمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r2.claim: When wine was permitted, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf hosted Companions who drank until drunk; at Maghrib, one led prayer and recited a mistaken line, prompting this verse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r2.anchor: روي (أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله تعالى عنه صنع مأدبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r3.claim: Alternatively, “prayer” means its locations, the mosques; the point is to forbid excessive drinking and drunkenness rather than a drunk person approaching prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r3.anchor: وقيل أراد بالصلاة مواضعها وهي المساجد وليس المراد منه نهي السكران

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r4.claim: The form is read sukārā with fatḥa; another form may be a plural like halkā, a singular for an intoxicated people, or a collective adjective like ḥublā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r4.anchor: وقرىء { سكرى } بالفتح وسكرى على أنه جمه كهلكى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r5.claim: Junuban coordinates with the circumstantial clause “while you are intoxicated”; janub applies to all genders and numbers like a verbal noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r5.anchor: عطف على قوله { وأنتم سكرى } إذ الجملة في موضع النصب على الحال

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r6.claim: The exception attaches to “while junub,” exempting travel when water is unavailable and tayammum is used, as the following clause indicates.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r6.anchor: متعلق بقوله { ولا جنبا } ، استثناء من أعم الأحوال

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r7.claim: Alternatively, the phrase describes junub people, meaning “other than those passing through.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r7.anchor: أو صفة لقوله { جنبا } أي جنبا غير عابري سبيل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r8.claim: The exception is evidence that tayammum does not remove the state of ritual impurity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r8.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن التيمم لا يرفع الحدث.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r9.speaker: الشافعي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r9.claim: If prayer means mosques, those passing through are allowed to cross while junub; al-Shāfiʿī holds this view.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r9.anchor: وجوز الجنب عبور المسجد. وبه قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r10.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa bars a junub person from passing through a mosque unless it contains water or is the route.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه: لا يجوز له المرور في المسجد

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r11.claim: The phrase marks the end of the prohibition for a junub person; it also teaches worshippers to avoid distractions and purify the soul.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r11.anchor: غاية النهي عن القربان حال الجنابة، وفي الآية تنبيه على أن المصلي

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r12.claim: The illness may make water use dangerous or prevent reaching it; in either case, the person is treated as lacking water.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r12.anchor: يخاف معه من استعمال الماء، فإن الواجد كالفاقد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r13.claim: The traveler is excused when water is unavailable.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r14.claim: Coming from the privy means becoming impure through discharge from either outlet; ghāʾiṭ originally means a low-lying place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r14.anchor: فأحدث بخروج الخارج من أحد السبيلين، وأصل الغائط المكان المطمئن

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r15.claim: The phrase may mean skin touching skin; al-Shāfiʿī uses it as evidence that touching women invalidates ablution.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r15.anchor: أو ما مسستم بشرتهن ببشرتكم، وبه استدل الشافعي على أن اللمس

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r16.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means sexual intercourse; lamasa is less commonly used as a euphemism for intercourse than mulāmasa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r16.anchor: استعماله كناية عن الجماع أقل من الملامسة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r17.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r17.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read lāmastum here and in al-Māʾida.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r17.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي هنا وفي المائدة «لمستم»

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r18.claim: “Finding no water” includes being unable to use it, since what one is barred from using counts as unavailable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r18.anchor: فلم تتمكنوا من استعماله، إذ الممنوع عنه كالمفقود.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r19.claim: The classification covers minor or major impurity, usually prompted by illness or travel; it names the junub case and details ordinary and incidental causes for the other.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r19.anchor: ووجه هذا التقسيم أن المترخص بالتيمم إما محدث أو جنب

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r20.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r20.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r20.claim: Tayammum means deliberately turning to clean earth; the Ḥanafīs allow hard stone, while al-Bayḍāwī’s school requires dust to adhere, reading “from it” partitively.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43/r20.anchor: أي فتعمدوا شيئا من وجه الأرض طاهرا. ولذلك قالت الحنفية

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r1.claim: The Ḥanafīs allow striking hard stone, while al-Bayḍāwī’s school requires dust to adhere; min in the cited verse is partitive, and treating it as a starting point is strained.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r1.anchor: فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه [المائدة 6] أي بعضه

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r2.claim: Although hand can mean the limb up to the shoulder, a Prophetic report of wiping to the elbows and analogy with ablution establish the limit here.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r2.anchor: وما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام تيمم ومسح يديه إلى مرفقيه،

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r3.claim: God’s forgiveness explains the eased rule and dispensation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:43-44/r3.anchor: فلذلك يسر الأمر عليكم ورخص لكم.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r4.claim: The terrifying judgment scene makes sinners wish for nonexistence and prevents concealment; because salvation requires purity through faith and obedience, the discussion turns to worldly prayer and purification.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r4.anchor: لا ينجو فيه إلا من كان طاهر القلب والجوارح

BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r5.claim: The address means those who profess belief in the messengers and what they brought from God; the foremost duty is to avoid associating anything with Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r5.anchor: أقروا بالتصديق بالرسل وما أتوا به عن الله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r6.claim: “Do not approach prayer” means do not enter the place where it is performed, much less perform the prayer itself.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r6.anchor: بأن لا تكونوا في موضعها فضلا عن أن تفعلوها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r7.claim: Intoxication means loss of reason through wine or another cause; weakened reason lets Satan prompt the tongue toward verbal shirk even while the heart remains faithful, a statement that will cause anguish at judgment.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p258#2/r7.anchor: أي غائبو العقل من الخمر أو نحوها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r1.claim: The Arabic root sense of intoxication is blocking a path.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r1.anchor: وأصل السكر في اللغة : سد الطريق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r2.speaker: علي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r2.claim: Ali reports that an Anṣārī gave wine to him and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān before prohibition; while leading Maghrib, Ali recited al-Kāfirūn incorrectly, prompting the verse. Al-Buṣīrī grades the transmitters trustworthy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r2.anchor: عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه ( أن رجلا من الأنصار دعاه وعبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله تعالى عنه فسقاهما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r3.claim: Other transmitters clarify the mistaken recitation as “I worship what you worship”; al-Tirmidhī’s version says, “and we worship what you worship.”
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r3.anchor: وقد رواه أصحاب السنن الثلاثة وأحمد وعبد بن حميد والبزار والحاكم والطبري

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r4.claim: The prohibition lasts until intoxication passes and people understand their words, preventing them from altering what they say in prayer.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r5.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī takes prayer to mean both the prayer itself and its place, the mosque: the verse bars an intoxicated person from praying and a sexually impure person from being in the mosque.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r5.anchor: وعند الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه أن المراد بالصلاة نفسها وموضعها وهو المسجد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r6.claim: Junub refers to emission of semen, actual or near at hand through the meeting of the circumcised parts; it applies whether semen results from intercourse or otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r6.anchor: بالتقاء الختانين , لأن الجنابة المني سواء كان عن جماع أو لا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r7.claim: A junub may pass through the mosque without stopping or praying.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r7.anchor: أي مارين مرورا من غير مكث ولا صلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r8.claim: The restriction on junub remains until the body has been deliberately washed.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r9.claim: The verse orders concessions from the cases most in need of them toward those less in need, beginning with illness and travel.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r9.anchor: مرتبا لها على الأحوج إلى الرخصة فالأحوج

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r10.claim: The travel concession applies to short trips as well as long ones.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r10.anchor: سواء كان السفر طويلا أو قصيرا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r11.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ literally means a low, broad place used for relieving oneself; here it means returning from relieving oneself after a necessary bodily function.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r11.anchor: من التخلي فقضى حاجته التي لا بد له منها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r12.claim: The phrase can cover either skin touching skin or intercourse, whether or not ejaculation occurs; this is placed later because it is less avoidable and less frequent than relieving oneself.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r12.anchor: وأخر هذا لأنه مما منه بد , ولا يتكرر تكرر قضاء الحاجة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r13.claim: Not finding water includes either its absence or inability to use it.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r13.anchor: أي إما بفقده أو بالعجز عن استعماله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r14.claim: Tayammum means sincerely intending the act and entering into it with that intention; ṣaʿīd is soil and ṭayyib is pure and wholesome.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r14.anchor: اقصدوا قصدا صادقا بأن تلابسوا ناوين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r15.claim: The description ṭayyib is illustrated by the verse saying that good land brings forth its plants by its Lord’s permission.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r15.anchor: والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته بإذن ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r16.claim: Tayammum is a distinctive act of worship granted to this community.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r17.claim: The bāʾ in “your faces” limits the wiping action because dust cannot reach every part; wiping is valid even if it does not cover the hairline.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r17.anchor: ولما كان التراب لا يتمكن من جميع العضو وإن اجتهد الإنسان في ذلك أدخل الباء قاصرا للفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r18.claim: The hands are wiped from the earth, as Sūrat al-Māʾida makes explicit; the wording can indicate that a stone suffices.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r18.anchor: لا فيه ولا عليه مثلا , ليفهم التمعك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r19.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r19.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī allows lamastum to mean literal skin contact, intercourse caused by contact, or a particular kind of touching; intercourse can be named by its cause or the whole by a part.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r19.anchor: جوز الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه أيضا أن يراد بها المس - أي ملاقاة البشرتين -

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r20.claim: The prohibition also bars conduct approaching the sin of an intoxicated tongue uttering words unworthy of God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r20.anchor: نهى عما يدني من وقوع صورة الذنب الذي هو جري اللسان بما لا يليق به سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r21.claim: Tayammum alleviates the otherwise severe restriction when using water is difficult or impossible.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r22.claim: ʿAfw means that God leaves punishment for the offense, especially the error made while intoxicated.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r22.anchor: بترك العقاب على الذنب , وكأن هذا راجع إلى ما وقع حالة السكر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r23.claim: Ghafūr adds erasure of the sin; the author connects this to the tayammum concession, which makes prayer virtuous instead of leaving it or praying without purification.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r23.anchor: أي بترك العقاب وبمحو الذنب حتى لا ذكر بعد ذلك أصلا , وكأن ها راجع إلى التيمم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r24.claim: The concession is explained by God’s stated wish not to impose hardship on believers.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p259/r24.anchor: وذلك معنى قوله سبحانه وتعالى في المائدة

BURSEVI:v2p167/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p167/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p167/r4.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf hosted companions for food and wine while wine was permitted; a drunken prayer leader omitted la in al-Kafirun, so the verse was revealed, and they thereafter avoided drinking near prayer until its later prohibition.
BURSEVI:v2p167/r4.anchor: روي أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف صنع طعاما وشرابا فدعا نفرا من أفاضل الصحابة رضي الله عنهم حين كانت الخمر مباحة

BURSEVI:v2p167/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p167/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p167/r5.claim: The prohibition says not to approach prayer, though its intent is not to perform it while intoxicated, emphasizing the warning.
BURSEVI:v2p167/r5.anchor: وتوجيه النهي إلى قربان الصلاة مع أن المراد هو النهي عن إقامتها للمبالغة في ذلك

BURSEVI:v2p167/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p167/r6.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v2p167/r6.claim: Taysir says the prayer itself is not forbidden, since it is worship; rather, one must not become intoxicated so as to be unable to pray properly.
BURSEVI:v2p167/r6.anchor: قال في "التيسير" ثم النهي ليس عن عين الصلاة فإنها عبادة فلا ينهى عنها

BURSEVI:v2p167/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p167/r7.speaker: أبو منصور
BURSEVI:v2p167/r7.claim: Abu Mansur explains that wording such as no prayer for a runaway slave or disobedient wife condemns the disobedience, not the prayer; intoxication likewise does not cancel the obligation, so pray only when aware of what will be recited.
BURSEVI:v2p167/r7.anchor: قال الإمام أبو منصور رحمه الله : وكذلك قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "لا صلاة للعبد الآبق ولا للمرأة الناشزة"

BURSEVI:v2p168/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r1.claim: Sukara is the plural of sakran, on the pattern of كسالى from كسلان.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r1.anchor: والسكارى جمع سكران كالكسالى جمع كسلان

BURSEVI:v2p168/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r2.claim: Scholars agree that a drunk person’s sale and purchase are invalid, but hold him liable for damage, homicide, and penalties; Hanafis count divorce and manumission as effective punishment, unlike al-Shafi‘i.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r2.anchor: وأجمعوا على أنه لا يجوز بيع السكران وشراؤه ويؤاخذ بالاستهلاكات والقتل والحدود وصح طلاقه وعتاقه عقوبة له عندنا خلافا للشافعي

BURSEVI:v2p168/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r3.claim: Junuban is coordinated with the clause you are intoxicated, so the prohibition means not to approach prayer drunk or in a state of major impurity.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r3.anchor: {ولا جنبا} عطف على قوله : وأنتم سكارى فإنه في حيز النصب كأنه قيل : لا تقربوا الصلاة سكارى ولا جنبا

BURSEVI:v2p168/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r4.claim: Junub applies alike to masculine and feminine, singular and plural, because it functions like a verbal noun; janabah means distance, since it keeps one from recitation and prayer.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r4.anchor: والجنب من أصابته الجنابة يستوي في المؤنث والمذكر والواحد والجمع لجريانه مجرى المصدر وأصل الجنابة البعد

BURSEVI:v2p168/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r5.claim: The exception is unrestricted and accusative as a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in the prohibition, construed with the second state of impurity.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r5.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من أعم الأحوال محله النصب على أنه حال من ضمير لا تقربوا باعتبار تقيده بالحال الثانية

BURSEVI:v2p168/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r6.claim: A traveler excused by travel may pray using dry ablution while junub; the prohibition lasts until washing.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r6.anchor: أي لا تقربوا الصلاة جنبا في حال من الأحوال إلا حال كونكم مسافرين فتعذرون بالسفر فتصلون بالتيمم

BURSEVI:v2p168/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r7.claim: A worshipper should guard prayer from distractions that occupy the heart and purify the self from defilement, pursuing the highest attainable purification.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r7.anchor: وفي الآية الكريمة إشارة إلى أن المصلي حقه أن يتحرز عما يلهيه ويشغل قلبه وأن يزكي نفسه عما يدنسها ولا يكتفي بأدنى مراتب التزكية

BURSEVI:v2p168/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r8.claim: The verse gives three illness levels: water would cause death; it would cause severe pain, worsen or prolong illness; or it would leave only a feared blemish or bodily defect.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r8.anchor: {وإن كنتم مرضى} جمع مريض. والمرض على ثلاثة أقسام :

BURSEVI:v2p168/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r9.claim: Jurists permit dry ablution in the first two illness categories but not the third, where only a blemish or defect is feared.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r9.anchor: فالفقهاء جوزوا التيمم في القسمين الأولين وما جوزوه في القسم الثالث

BURSEVI:v2p168/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v2p168/r10.claim: Travel, short or long, is cited to establish the ruling and its procedure; the rule also applies wherever water cannot be used, and Abu Hanifa permits tayammum for janabah in town without hot water.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r10.anchor: أو كنتم على سفر ما طال أو قصر وإيراده مع سبق ذكره بطريق الاستثناء لبناء الحكم الشرعي عليه

BURSEVI:v2p168/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r11.claim: Al-ghait is a low, sunken place; coming from there is a euphemism for relieving oneself, since people went there to conceal themselves.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r11.anchor: وهو المكان المنخفض المطمئن والمجيء منه كناية عن الحدث لأن المعتاد أن من يريده يذهب إليه ليواري شخصه عن أعين الناس

BURSEVI:v2p168/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r12.claim: Touching women here means having intercourse with them.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r12.anchor: جامعتموهن يعني إذا أصابكم المرض أو السفر أو الحدث أو الجنابة

BURSEVI:v2p168/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168/r13.claim: Not finding water means being unable to use it because it is absent or distant, access tools are lacking, or a snake, beast, or enemy blocks it; tayammum means seeking clean earth.
BURSEVI:v2p168/r13.anchor: أي لم تقدروا على استعماله لعدمه أو لبعده أو لفقد آلة الوصول إليه من الدلو والرشاء أو المانع عنه من حية أو سبع أو عدو

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines ṣaʿid as the earth’s surface, whether soil or another material, including bare rock.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : الصعيد وجه الأرض ترابا أو غيره وإن كان صخرا لا تراب عليه

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r2.claim: According to Abu Hanifa, striking a bare rock and wiping with it suffices for dry ablution even when it has no dust.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r2.anchor: لو ضرب المتيمم يده عليه ومسح لكان ذلك طهوره وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة رحمه الله

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r3.claim: The hands are wiped to the elbows, based on a report that the Prophet did so and by analogy because tayammum replaces ablution and takes its measure.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r3.anchor: لما روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم تيمم ومسح يديه إلى مرفقيه ولأنه بدل من الوضوء فيتقدر بقدره

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r4.claim: The preposition bi is extra in the construction: wipe your faces and hands from the earth.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r4.anchor: والباء زائدة أي فامسحوا وجوهكم وأيديكم منه أي من الصعيد

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r5.claim: God’s pardon and forgiveness explain and affirm this permission and ease: His constant practice is to pardon sinners, so He makes matters easier rather than harder.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r5.anchor: تعليل للترخيص والتيسر وتقرير لهما فإن من عادته المستمرة أن يعفو عن الخطائين ويغفر للمذنبين

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r6.claim: Prayer is the believer’s ascension and appointed time for intimate conversation with God; the worshipper is one who converses with his Lord.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r6.anchor: والإشارة أن الصلاة معراج المؤمن وميقات مناجاته والمصلي هو الذي يناجي ربه

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r7.claim: The inward warning forbids approaching prayer intoxicated by heedlessness and desire: anything that distracts the heart from God is a kind of drunkenness.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r7.anchor: أي : لا تجدوا القربة في الصلاة وأنتم سكارى من الغفلات وتتبع الشهوات لأن كل ما أوجب للقلب الذهول عن الله فهو ملتحق بالسكر

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r8.claim: There is drunkenness from wine, from heedlessness caused by worldly love, and from the self; the hardest is self-intoxication, whose consequence is true separation.
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r8.anchor: ومن أجله جعل السكر على أقسام : فسكر من الخمر وسكر من الغفلة لاستيلاء حب الدنيا وأصعب السكر سكرك من نفسك

BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p168#2/r9.claim: The Persian poem depicts the self as its own trap and urges leaving selfhood and heedlessness to attain presence and union.

BURSEVI:v2p169/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r1.claim: At the opening takbir, Allahu akbar means that God is greater and more exalted than everything.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r1.anchor: ومعناه الله أعظم وأجل من كل شيء

BURSEVI:v2p169/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r2.claim: True takbir leaves no other greatness, remembrance, love, or desire in the heart alongside God; otherwise the speaker's state contradicts the words.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r2.anchor: فينبغي أن لا يكون في تلك الحالة في قلبك عظمة شيء آخر وأمارة ذلك

BURSEVI:v2p169/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r3.claim: Spiritual intoxication is heedlessness, which prevents nearness to God just as literal drunkenness prevents understanding prayer.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r3.anchor: كما لا تجدون القربة وأنتم سكارى من الغفلات أيضا لا تجدونها

BURSEVI:v2p169/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r4.claim: Nearness is conditioned on prostration, as the command to prostrate and draw near states.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r4.anchor: لأن القربة مشروطة بشرط السجود كما خوطب به

BURSEVI:v2p169/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r5.claim: Prostration means descending from the mount of one's existent attributes, carried by divine generosity to the threshold of divine being and a vision of beauty and majesty; this is the secret of sitting for tashahhud after prostration.

BURSEVI:v2p169/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r6.claim: Spiritual major impurity is attachment to the lowly world, which makes the seeker deserving of distance from God.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r6.anchor: لا تجدونها مع جنابة استحقاق البعد وهي ملابسة الدنيا الدنية

BURSEVI:v2p169/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r7.claim: One may cross worldly concerns only by the outward path of sacred law, taking food and drink to preserve life, clothing for protection and modesty, and sex to preserve offspring.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r7.anchor: إلا على طريق العبور بقدم ظاهر الشرع في سبيل الأوامر والنواهي

BURSEVI:v2p169/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r8.claim: Spiritual washing is achieved through nearness, repentance, sincere seeking, good intention, and purity of purpose from worldly attachment and desire.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r8.anchor: بماء القربة والإنابة وصدق الطلب وحسن الإرادة وخلوص النية

BURSEVI:v2p169/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r9.claim: Spiritual illness is a heart whose disposition has become crooked in seeking the Real.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r9.anchor: بانحراف مزاج القلب في طلب الحق

BURSEVI:v2p169/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r10.claim: Spiritual travel is wavering among pursuit of this world, the afterlife, and the Lord.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r10.anchor: التردد بين طلب الدنيا وطلب العقبى والمولى

BURSEVI:v2p169/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r11.claim: Coming from the privy signifies following one's caprice.

BURSEVI:v2p169/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r12.claim: Touching women signifies engagement in worldly occupations, which estranges the seeker from God after nearness to the sacred precincts and gardens of intimacy.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r12.anchor: أي لابستم الأشغال الدنيوية فأجنبتم وتباعدتم عن الله

BURSEVI:v2p169/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r13.claim: Lacking water signifies inability to repent and return sincerely to God by turning away from created beings.

BURSEVI:v2p169/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r14.claim: The pure earth is the dust of the feet of virtuous spiritual masters, cleansed of bad character and deeds.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r14.anchor: وهو تراب أقدام الرجال الطيبين من سوء الأخلاق والأعمال

BURSEVI:v2p169/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r15.claim: Wiping the face and hands means taking the masters' dust and clinging to their generous hems, submitting sincerely to their guidance.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r15.anchor: أذيال كرمهم مستسلمين بصدق الإرادة لأحكامهم

BURSEVI:v2p169/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r16.claim: God may pardon sectarian attachment and failure to turn wholly to Him, and may pardon worldly contamination through this praiseworthy spiritual discipline.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r16.anchor: يعفو عنكم التعصب وعدم الانقطاع إليه بالكلية ولعله يعفو عنكم التلوث بالدنيا

BURSEVI:v2p169/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p169/r17.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p169/r17.claim: God forgives traces of misery left by desire's dust; those who keep company with the virtuous attain felicity, for their companions do not suffer.
BURSEVI:v2p169/r17.anchor: غبار الشهوة فإنهم يسعد بهم لأنهم قوم لا يشقى بهم جليسهم

DURR-FULL:v2p544/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p544/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v2p544/r7.claim: Ali reports that after Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf served wine at a meal, intoxicated Ali led prayer and misrecited al-Kafirun; verse 4:43 then barred prayer while drunk. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan and al-Hakim authenticated it.
DURR-FULL:v2p544/r7.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: صنع لنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف طعاما فدعانا وسقانا من الخمر

DURR-FULL:v2p546/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r1.claim: Ali says the exception concerns a traveler who becomes sexually impure, lacks water, performs tayammum, and prays until water becomes available.
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r1.anchor: عن علي في قوله {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: نزلت هذه الآية في المسافر تصيبه الجنابة

DURR-FULL:v2p546/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says a sexually impure person may not approach prayer when water is available; without water, tayammum by wiping the earth is permitted.
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} يقول: لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم جنب إذا وجدتم الماء

DURR-FULL:v2p546/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the exception as a traveler who has no water and therefore performs tayammum and prays.
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: هو المسافر الذي لا يجد ماء

DURR-FULL:v2p546/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r4.claim: Mujahid says a junub person or menstruant may not pass through a mosque; the verse instead permits the traveler who lacks water to perform tayammum and pray.
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: لا يمر الجنب ولا الحائض في المسجد إنما نزلت {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل}

DURR-FULL:v2p546/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the exception as travelers who cannot find water.
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: مسافرين لا تجدون ماء

DURR-FULL:v2p546/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r6.speaker: الأسلع بن شريك
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r6.claim: Aslaʿ ibn Sharik reports that on a cold night he feared a bath after becoming junub, so he heated water with hot stones and bathed; revelation then came concerning prayer and the junub traveler.
DURR-FULL:v2p546/r6.anchor: عن الأسلع بن شريك قال: كنت أرحل ناقة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأصابتني جنابة في ليلة باردة

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r1.speaker: الأسلع بن شريك
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r1.claim: In another report, Aslaʿ says Gabriel brought the tayammum verse when he told the Prophet he was junub; the Prophet demonstrated striking the ground, wiping the face, striking again, and wiping both sides of the arms.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r1.anchor: قلت: يا رسول الله أصابتني جنابة فسكت عني ساعة حتى جاء جبريل بآية الصعيد فقال: قم يا أسلع فتيمم

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata al-Khurasani, says “prayer” here refers to the mosques.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {لا تقربوا الصلاة} قال: المساجد

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the junub may cross a mosque but must not remain seated there.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: لا تدخلوا المسجد وأنتم جنب إلا عابري سبيل

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r4.speaker: يزيد بن أبي حبيب
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r4.claim: Yazid ibn Abi Habib says the verse was revealed because some Anṣār had mosque doors but no route to water except through the mosque when they became junub.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r4.anchor: عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب في قوله {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: إن رجالا من الأنصار كانت أبوابهم في المسجد

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r5.claim: Ibn Masud interprets the exception as passing through the mosque; he elsewhere permits a junub person to cross it in transit.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: هو الممر في المسجد

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas allows menstruants and junub people to pass through the mosque provided they do not sit there.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لا بأس للحائض والجنب أن يمرا في المسجد ما لم يجلسا فيه

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda says the junub may pass through the mosque but may not sit in it.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r7.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة قال: الجنب يمر في المسجد ولا يجلس فيه ثم قرأ {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل}

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r8.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r8.claim: Ata says the junub may pass through the mosque.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r8.anchor: عن عطاء في قوله {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: الجنب يمر في المسجد

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r9.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r9.claim: Anas says a junub person may pass through the mosque but not remain there.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r9.anchor: عن أنس في قوله {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} قال: يجتاز ولا يجلس

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r10.speaker: جابر
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r10.claim: Jabir reports that people among them would cross the mosque while junub, passing through rather than staying.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r10.anchor: عن جابر قال: كان أحدنا يمر في المسجد وهو جنب مجتازا

DURR-FULL:v2p547/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r11.claim: Mujahid says the illness clause was revealed about an Anṣārī man too ill to rise for ablution and without a helper; he brought the problem to the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v2p547/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وإن كنتم مرضى} قال: نزلت في رجل من الأنصار كان مريضا

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person with smallpox, wounds, or ulcers who becomes junub and fears dying from bathing may perform tayammum.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإن كنتم مرضى} قال: هو الرجل المجدور أو به الجراح أو القرح

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r2.claim: A report raised to the Prophet applies the tayammum concession to a person with war wounds, sores, or smallpox who fears bathing would kill him.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رفعه في قوله {وإن كنتم مرضى} قال: إذا كانت بالرجل الجراحة في سبيل الله أو القروح

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r3.claim: Mujahid says a sick person who becomes junub and fears for his life receives the same tayammum concession as a traveler without water.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وإن كنتم مرضى} قال: هي للمريض تصيبه الجنابة إذا خاف على نفسه الرخصة في التيمم

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r4.claim: Mujahid says a person with smallpox or similar illness may omit ablution, adding that this is among the Quran's difficult interpretations.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال: للمريض المجدور وشبهه رخصة في أن لا يتوضأ وتلا {وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر}

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r5.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi says the verse was revealed after the Prophet's companions suffered worsening wounds and then became junub and complained to him.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي قال: نال أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جراحة ففشت فيهم ثم ابتلوا بالجنابة

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r6.claim: Ibn Masud says the sick allowed tayammum include the broken and wounded; when junub, they should not wash a wound if doing so risks harm.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {وإن كنتم مرضى} قال: المريض الذي قد أرخص له في التيمم هو الكسير والجريح

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid say a sick person who fears harm from bathing for janabah may perform tayammum like a traveler without water.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد قالا في المريض تصيبه الجنابة فيخاف على نفسه: هو بمنزلة المسافر

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says a sick person without anyone to bring water, who cannot reach it and has no helper, may perform tayammum and pray.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r8.anchor: عن ابن زيد في الآية قال: المريض الذي لا يجد أحدا يأتيه بالماء ولا يقدر عليه وليس له خادم

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r9.claim: Mujahid says al-ghaʾit means a valley.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط} قال: الغائط الوادي

DURR-FULL:v2p548/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r10.claim: Ibn Masud explains touching women as contact short of intercourse, including kissing, and says it requires ablution.
DURR-FULL:v2p548/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {أو لامستم النساء} قال: اللمس

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r1.claim: Ibn Masud also glosses touching women as ghamz, pressing or squeezing.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r1.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عن ابن مسعود أنه كان يقول في هذه الآية {أو لامستم النساء} هو الغمز

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r2.claim: Ibn Umar used to perform ablution after kissing a woman, saying that a kiss is touching.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه كان يتوضأ من قبلة المرأة ويقول: هي اللماس

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r3.claim: Ibn Umar says kissing one's wife or touching her by hand is contact that requires ablution.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قبلة الرجل امرأته وجسها بيده من الملامسة

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r4.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r4.claim: Umar says kissing is a form of touching and requires ablution.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r4.anchor: عن عمر قال: إن القبلة من اللمس فتوضأ منها

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r5.claim: Ali says “touching women” means sexual intercourse, expressed euphemistically by God.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r5.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: اللمس هو الجماع ولكن الله كنى عنه

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses touching women as sexual intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أو لامستم النساء} قال: هو الجماع

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r7.claim: In a discussion, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ata, and the non-Arab clients argued for hand-touch, while Ubayd ibn Umayr and the Arabs argued for intercourse; Ibn Abbas judged the Arabs right, since touch-related terms can euphemize intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: كنا في حجرة ابن عباس ومعنا عطاء بن أبي رباح ونفر من الموالي وعبيد بن عمير

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Nafi ibn al-Azraq that the verse means intercourse, though Hudhayl uses the word for hand-touch; he cites Labid and al-Aʿsha's poems as evidence for that Arabic usage.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله تعالى {أو لامستم النساء} قال: أو جامعتم النساء

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r9.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r9.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi read the phrase as “أو لمستم النساء” and understood it as contact short of intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r9.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي أنه كان يقرأ ((أو لمستم النساء)) قال: يعني ما دون الجماع

DURR-FULL:v2p549/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r10.speaker: عبيدة
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r10.claim: Ubayda demonstrated his interpretation to Muhammad ibn Sirin by closing his fingers as if grasping something.
DURR-FULL:v2p549/r10.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال: سألت عبيدة عن قوله {أو لامستم النساء} فأشار بيده وضم أصابعه

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r1.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Sirin says he was told Ibn Umar performed ablution after touching his private part; he took this and Ubayda's gesture to be the same interpretation.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r1.anchor: قال محمد: ونبئت عن ابن عمر أنه كان إذا مس مخرجه توضأ فظننت أن قول ابن عمر وعبيدة شيئا واحدا

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r2.claim: Abu Uthman interprets the contact as touching by hand.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r2.anchor: عن أبي عثمان قال: اللمس باليد

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda says the contact means what is short of intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r3.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة قال: ما دون الجماع

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r4.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r4.claim: Al-Shabi says the contact means what is short of intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r4.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: الملامسة دون الجماع

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r5.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the contact as sexual intercourse.

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r6.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r6.claim: Sufyan says tayammum means seeking or deliberately aiming for clean earth.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r6.anchor: عن سفيان في قوله {فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا} قال: تحروا تعمدوا صعيدا طيبا

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r7.claim: Qatada says pure earth is land with no trees or vegetation.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r7.anchor: عن قتادة {صعيدا طيبا} قال: التي ليس فيها شجر ولا نبات

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r8.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الملائي
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r8.claim: Amr ibn Qays al-Mulaʿi says al-saʿid means soil.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r8.anchor: عن عمرو بن قيس الملائي قال: الصعيد التراب

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r9.speaker: سعيد بن بشير
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn Bashir says clean earth is earth that rain has fallen on and purified.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن بشير في الآية قال: الطيب: ما أتت عليه الأمطار وطهرته

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r10.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r10.claim: Sufyan says “clean” means lawful for you.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r10.anchor: عن سفيان في قوله {صعيدا طيبا} قال: حلالا لكم

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the best earth for tayammum is cultivated land.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن أطيب الصعيد أرض الحرث

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r12.speaker: حماد
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r12.claim: Hammad says anything touched by one's hands counts as saʿid, even dust from a saddle pad, and may be used for tayammum.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r12.anchor: عن حماد قال: كل شيء وضعت يدك عليه فهو صعيد حتى غبار لبدك فتيمم به

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r13.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says, in answer to a question, that cultivated earth is the purest soil.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل أي الصعيد أطيب قال: أرض الحرث

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when he sought guidance about tayammum, the Prophet urinated, struck the ground with his hands, and wiped his face and palms.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r14.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: لما نزلت آية التيمم لم أدر كيف أصنع فأتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r15.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r15.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet demonstrated tayammum with one strike for the face and another for the hands.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r15.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: لما نزلت آية التيمم ضرب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده على الأرض

DURR-FULL:v2p550/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r16.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r16.claim: Ammar ibn Yasir reports that after he became junub while traveling and rolled in dust, the Prophet taught him that tayammum requires only striking the earth and wiping the face and palms.
DURR-FULL:v2p550/r16.anchor: عن عمار بن ياسر قال: كنت في سفر فاجنبت فتمعكت فصليت ثم ذكرت ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r1.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says tayammum uses two strikes: one for the face and one for the arms up to the elbows.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: التيمم ضربتان: ضربة للوجه وضربة لليدين إلى المرفقين

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports the companions struck the earth twice, wiping the face after the first strike and the arms from elbows to wrists after the second.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: تيممنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فضربنا بأيدينا على الصعيد الطيب

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r3.claim: Abu Malik reports that Ammar performed tayammum by wiping his face and hands without wiping his forearm.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال: تيمم عمار فمسح وجهه ويديه ولم يمسح الذراع

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r4.speaker: مكحول
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r4.claim: Makhul limits tayammum to the face and hands through the wrists: unlike ablution, this verse does not specify elbows, and the thief's hand is cut at the wrist joint.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r4.anchor: عن مكحول قال: التيمم ضربة للوجه والكفين إلى الكوع فإن الله قال في الوضوء (وأيديكم إلى المرافق)

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r5.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri says tayammum reaches the armpits.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r5.anchor: عن الزهري قال: التيمم إلى الآباط

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r6.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r6.claim: Ammar reports that when a lost necklace delayed travel, the tayammum concession was revealed and they wiped the face and arms to the shoulders and armpits; al-Shafiʿi rejects this as abrogated by later tayammum reports.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r6.anchor: عن عمار بن ياسر قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فهلك عقد لعائشة فأقام رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r7.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying pure earth serves as a Muslim's ablution for up to ten years without water; when water is found, it should touch the skin.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r7.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: اجتمعت غنيمة عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا أبا ذر ابد فيها

DURR-FULL:v2p552/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r8.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r8.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet saying that earth was made a purifying substance for the community when water is unavailable.
DURR-FULL:v2p552/r8.anchor: عن حذيفة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: جعلت تربتها لنا طهورا إذا لم نجد الماء

IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r1.claim: Umar prayed for a clear ruling on wine: first 2:219 was revealed, then this verse, and finally the prohibition in 5:90–91, ending with “Will you not then desist?”
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن شرحبيل قال : قال عمر : اللهم بين لنا في الخمر ، فنزلت : قل فيهما اثم كبير ومنافع للناس

IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r2.claim: Ali says that after Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf served wine at a meal, the intoxicated guests misrecited al-Kafirun at prayer; this verse was then revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : صنع لنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف طعاما فدعانا وسقانا من الخمر

IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r3.speaker: سعد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r3.claim: Saad says an Ansari meal led to drinking and drunken boasting before wine was prohibited; a man struck Saad’s nose with a camel jawbone, and the verse was revealed about the incident.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r3.anchor: عن سعد قال : نزلت في اربع آيات ، صنع رجل من الانصار ، فاكلنا وشربنا حتى سكرنا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says this rule was abrogated by the later direction to wash when rising for prayer; Ikrima, Mujahid, Hasan, al-Dahhak, Qatada, Ata al-Khurasani, and Zayd ibn Aslam also call it abrogated.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p958/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس يا ايها الذين امنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وانتم سكارى قال : نسختها

IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “prayer” here as the mosques.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله في سورة النساء : لا تقربوا الصلاة قال : صلاة المساجد

IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قوله : لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى قال : السكر : النوم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r3.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains “intoxicated” as drunk from wine.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : وأنتم سكارى يعني : نشاوى من الشراب

IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains this as knowing what one recites in prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r4.anchor: وبه عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : حتى تعلموا ما تقولون يعني : ما تقراون

IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r5.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r5.claim: Ali says the exception concerns a traveler who becomes sexually impure, lacks water, and prays by dry ablution until finding water, when he bathes and prays.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r5.anchor: عن علي قال : نزلت هذه الاية في المسافر : ولا جنبا الا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas gives another reading of the exception: pass through a mosque without sitting; Ibn Masud, Anas, Abu Ubayda, Said ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, and many others are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p959/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : ولا جنبا الا عابري سبيل قال : تمر به مرا ولا تجلس

IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sick person includes someone wounded or injured who fears bathing may kill him and therefore uses dry ablution; several other authorities are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وان كنتم مرضى أو على سفر قال : هو الرجل المحدود أو به الجرح

IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r2.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r2.claim: In discussing a person under legal restriction, Ata says the clause about finding no water is sufficient: the concession applies to anyone who lacks water.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r2.anchor: قال : حسبك فان لم تجدوا ماء فانما ذلك اذا لم تجدوا ماء فليتطهروا ، قلت : وان احتلم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r3.claim: Ata al-Khurasani allows dry ablution and prayer for smallpox and serious wounds; al-Zuhri instead says to bathe while leaving the wound areas unwashed.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r3.anchor: عن عطاء الخرساني في قوله : وان كنتم مرضى أو على سفر قال : الجدري والجائفة ، والمامومة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r4.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about a sick Ansari who could not rise to perform ablution and had no servant to bring him water; he asked the Prophet about his predicament.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ولا جنبا الا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا وان كنتم مرضى أو على سفر قال : نزلت

IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r5.claim: Mujahid says al-ghait means a valley.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p960/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : او على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط والغائط : الوادي

IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains touching women here as sexual intercourse; Ali, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mujahid, Tawus, al-Hasan, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Qatada, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : أو لامستم النساء قال : الجماع

IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r2.claim: Abdullah explains touching as contact short of intercourse; Ibn Umar, Ubayda, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, Abu Ubayda, al-Sha'bi, Thabit ibn al-Hajjaj, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Zayd ibn Aslam are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله قال : اللمس : ما دون الجماع

IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r3.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r3.claim: Ali says a person made junub who cannot find water performs tayammum and prays until water becomes available.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r3.anchor: عن علي يعني قوله : فلم تجدوا ماء قال : تصيبه الجنابة لا يجد الماء يتيمم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r4.claim: Aisha recounts that Asma's lost necklace prompted a search; prayer came with no water or ablution, and God then revealed the tayammum ruling.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r4.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : هلكت قلادة لاسماء ، فبعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says a sick person who fears for himself may perform tayammum.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا قال : المريض اذا خاف على نفسه تيمم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r6.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r6.claim: Sufyan glosses the instruction to perform tayammum on clean earth as seeking or aiming for it.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p961/r6.anchor: سمعت سفيان يقول : فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا قال : تحروا تيمموا صعيدا طيبا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the best ṣaʿīd is cultivated earth.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ان اطيب الصعيد ارض الحرث

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r2.speaker: حماد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r2.claim: Hammad says anything touched by the hand counts as ṣaʿīd, even dust on the hand, which can be used for tayammum.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r2.anchor: عن حماد ، قال : كل شيء وضعت عليه يدك فهو صعيد حتى غبار يدك فتيمم به

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r3.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r3.claim: Sufyan glosses clean or good as lawful for you.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r3.anchor: عن سفيان قوله : فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا قال : حلال لكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r4.speaker: سعيد بن بشير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Bashir says the clean earth is that on which rain has fallen and which it has purified.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r4.anchor: سالت سعيد بن بشير عن قول الله تعالى : فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا ما الطيب ؟

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r5.claim: Qatada describes tayammum by placing the hands in earth, shaking them, and wiping the face and palms.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : فامسحوا بوجوهكم وايديكم فان اعياك الماء ، فلا يعييك الصعيد ان تضع فيه كفك ، ثم تنفضهما

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r6.claim: Qatada says that after tayammum and prayer, someone who later finds water must perform the required washing, but the prayer already offered counts.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r6.anchor: فمن تيمم بالصعيد وصلى ثم قدر على الماء بعد . فعليه الغسل وحسبه صلاته التي كان صلى

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r7.speaker: سلمة بن وهرام
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r7.claim: Salama ibn Wahrām says God named Himself al-ʿAfuww and al-Ghafūr so that He may pardon and forgive.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r7.anchor: قال ذكر سلمة بن وهرام صاحب طاوس ، ان الله تبارك وتعالى انما سمى نفسه العفو

IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says that nothing is dearer to him than pardon.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال : ليس شيء احب الي من عفو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r1.claim: The verse resumes to explain two prayer rulings; the contemporaneous need to regulate wine placed this ruling between surrounding verses, apparently interrupting their sequence when the occasion arose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r1.anchor: هذه الآية استئناف لبيان حكمين يتعلقان بالصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r2.claim: Wine was still originally lawful and some Muslims drank it; after 2:219 some argued they drank for its benefits rather than its sin, while the verse signaled likely prohibition and prepared them for it without yet removing the allowance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r2.anchor: ونزل قوله تعالى : { يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس } ( البقرة : 219 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r3.claim: Ali reports that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf served food and wine; when Ali led prayer while intoxicated, he recited al-Kāfirūn incorrectly, and this verse was revealed. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r3.anchor: ما رواه الترمذي عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : صنع لنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r4.claim: Here “approach” is metaphorical for engaging in an act; literally, qaruba or qaribahu means to be near a place or person, and both forms have the same sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r4.anchor: والقرب هنا مستعمل في معناه المجازي وهو التلبس بالفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r5.claim: Some distinguish the kasra form as exclusively metaphorical, but Ibn ʿAshur says that distinction is incorrect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p60/r5.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن مكسور الراء للقرب المجازي خاصة ، ولا يصح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r1.claim: Choosing “do not approach prayer” instead of “do not pray” presents intoxication as incompatible with prayer and the drinker as unworthy of Islam’s best act, discouraging wine and signaling a change in its status.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r1.anchor: وإنما اختير هذا الفعل دون لا تصلوا ونحوه للإشارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r2.claim: Some exegetes take “prayer” to mean the mosque by naming the place for the state; Ibn ʿAshur calls this far-fetched and contrary to well-known reports.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r2.anchor: ومن المفسرين من تأول الصلاة هنا بالمسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r3.claim: They report that some Companions drank wine and then came to the mosque to pray with the Prophet, prompting this prohibition; Ibn ʿAshur says this conflicts with the well-known reports.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r3.anchor: ونقل عن ابن عباس ، وابن مسعود ، والحسن قالوا : كان جماعة من الصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r4.claim: “Until you know what you say” gives the prohibition’s limit and hints at its rationale; impaired speech signals the earlier disruption of prayer’s actions as reason fails.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r4.anchor: وقوله : { حتى تعلموا ما تقولون } غاية للنهي وإيماء إلى علته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r5.claim: The wording may imply that mild intoxication did not then bar prayer; alternatively, the limit may mean the end of drunkenness, after which some exhilaration remains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r5.anchor: وفي الآية إيذان بأن السكر الخفيف لا يمنع الصلاة يومئذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r6.claim: “Sukārā” is the plural of sakrān, whose reason is closed or blocked, as when a pool or door is shut; compare the eyes being obscured in 15:15.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r6.anchor: وسكارى جمع سكران ، والسكران من أخذ عقله في الانغلاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r7.claim: After revelation, Muslims avoided wine around prayer, drinking only after the night prayer or after dawn prayer because of the long intervals; the later rule also prohibited prayer without purification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r7.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية اجتنب المسلمون شرب الخمر في أوقات الصلوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r8.claim: “Wa-lā junuban” is coordinated with the circumstantial clause “while you are intoxicated”; its accusative form confirms that the circumstantial clause occupies an accusative position.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r8.anchor: عطف على جملة { وأنتم سكارى } لأنا في محل الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r9.claim: Junub may be a verbal noun or an adjective like ajadd; here it means being distant from prayer and worship after intercourse until bathing, as at 4:36.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p61/r9.anchor: والجنب فعل ، قيل : مصدر ، وقيل : وصف مثل أجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r1.claim: As a verbal-noun adjective, junub does not take a plural form even though it describes a plural subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r1.anchor: ووصف جنب وصف بالمصدر فلذلك لم يجمع إذ أخبر به عن جمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r2.claim: The command to avoid prayer while in janāba means not to pray until one has performed the ritual bath.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r2.anchor: والمعنى لا تصلوا في حال الجنابة حتى تغتسلوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r3.claim: The term and ritual bath were known before Islam, perhaps inherited from ḥanīf practice or borrowed from Jews.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r3.anchor: وإطلاق الجنابة على هذا المعنى من عهد الجاهلية ، فإن الاغتسال من الجنابة كان معروفا عندهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAshur says he has not found Arabic usage evidencing mention of ritual bathing from janāba.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r4.anchor: ولم أقف على شيء من كلام العرب يدل على ذكر غسل الجنابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq’s Sīra says Abū Sufyān, returning defeated from Badr, swore not to touch his head with the bath of janāba until he fought Muḥammad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r5.anchor: وذكر ابن إسحاق في ( السيرة ) أن أبا سفيان ، لما رجع مهزوما من بدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r6.claim: Mention of janāba is an embedded transition to the new rule of tayammum, since the requirement of ritual bathing was already established.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r6.anchor: والمقصود من قوله : { ولا جنبا } التمهيد للتخلص إلى شرع التيمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r7.claim: Tayammum was instituted during the campaign of al-Muraysīʿ, in either year five or six AH according to the preferred chronology.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r7.anchor: والتيمم شرع في غزوة المريسيع على الصحيح ، وكانت سنة ست أو سنة خمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r8.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r8.claim: A report from Malik via Aisha says the tayammum verse was revealed at al-Muraysīʿ; Ibn ʿAshur infers this likely means the Nisa verse, since its discussion there mentions only tayammum.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r8.anchor: وظاهر حديث مالك عن عائشة أن الآية التي نزلت في غزوة المريسيع هي آية التيمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r9.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r9.claim: A report from ʿAmr via Aisha, recorded by al-Bukhari, identifies the verse revealed at al-Muraysīʿ as the tayammum instruction in al-Maʾida.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r9.anchor: ووقع في حديث عمرو عن عائشة أن الآية التي نزلت هي قوله :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r10.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r10.claim: Al-Qurṭubī firmly identifies the verse revealed at al-Muraysīʿ as this verse in al-Nisa, since al-Maʾida’s verse is called the verse of ablution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r10.anchor: وقد جزم القرطبي بأن الآية التي نزلت في غزوة المريسيع هي آية سورة النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r11.speaker: الواحدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r11.claim: Al-Wāḥidī places Aisha’s report about the occasion of revelation under the Nisa verse in his Asbāb al-nuzūl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r11.anchor: وكذلك الواحدي أورد في أسباب النزول حديث عائشة في سبب نزول آية سورة النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r12.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r12.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī calls this a difficult problem without a solution, since it is unclear which of the two verses Aisha intended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r12.anchor: وقال ابن العربي هذه معضلة ما وجدت لدائها من دواء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r13.claim: Although the order of al-Nisa and al-Maʾida is disputed, Ibn ʿAshur prefers the view that al-Nisa was revealed first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r13.anchor: والأصح أن سورة النساء نزلت قبل سورة المائدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r14.claim: The exception is taken from the general set of circumstances implied by “junub,” an indefinite circumstantial phrase under a negation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r14.anchor: استثناء من عموم الأحوال المستفاد من وقوع ( جنبا )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r15.claim: In Arabic, a traveler while on a journey is an “ʿābir al-sabīl,” from crossing or passing through a river or road.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r15.anchor: وعابر السبيل ، في كلام العرب : المسافر حين سيره في سفره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r16.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r16.claim: Some scholars understand “passing through” as passing through a mosque, on the premise that “prayer” means mosque; the exception then permits a junub person to cross without staying.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r16.anchor: ومن العلماء من فسر { عابري سبيل } بمارين في طريق ، وقال : المراد منه طريق المسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r17.speaker: أنس بن مالك وأبو عبيدة وابن المسيب والضحاك وعطاء ومجاهد ومسروق والنخعي وزيد بن أسلم وعمرو بن دينار وعكرمة وابن شهاب وقتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r17.claim: These authorities are reported to say the mosque-passage license belonged to an early period when many Emigrants and Helpers had doors opening into the mosque; it was later superseded after the doors were closed except Abū Bakr’s wicket, with reports also naming the Prophet and Abū Bakr, or ʿAlī, as exceptions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r17.anchor: ونسب أيضا إلى أنس بن مالك ، وأبي عبيدة ، وابن المسيب ، والضحاك ، وعطاء ، ومجاهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r18.claim: A claim that ʿAlī’s daughter’s wicket remained in the mosque is also reported, but Ibn ʿAshur says it is unsound.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p62/r18.anchor: وقيل : أبقيت خوخة بنت علي في المسجد ، ولم يصح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r1.claim: For those who read prayer as the mosque and travelers as passers through it, the exception clearly removes passers-by from the general prohibition on a junub person’s states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r1.anchor: وفائدة هذا الاستثناء عند من فسر { تقربوا الصلاة } بدخول المسجد ، وفسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r2.claim: For the majority’s literal reading, the exception seems redundant beside the later mention of travel and the restriction of the general rule; Ibn ʿAshur says it is placed here because travel commonly prevents bathing when water must be conserved, while illness is rarer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r2.anchor: وأما عند الجمهور الذين حملوا الآية على ظاهرها في معنى تقربوا الصلاة ، وفي معنى عابري السبيل فلا تظهر له فائدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r3.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī treats tayammum as a necessity-based permission, not removal of ritual impurity: a person who tayammums remains junub and may pray only as necessity permits, so the exception is connected.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r3.anchor: وهذا قول الشافعي ، فهو عنده بدل ضروري يقدر بقدر الضرورة ، ودليله ظاهر الاستثناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r4.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa treats tayammum as removing ritual impurity until invalidated, so the exception is disconnected; after tayammum for janāba, a later nullifier requires wudu. Ibn ʿAshur calls this the apparent view, with no Sunna evidence against it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r4.anchor: وهذا قول أبي حنيفة ، فلذلك إذا تيمم الجنب وصلى وصار منه حدث ناقض للوضوء يتوضأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r5.claim: The well-known transmission from Ibn al-Qāsim says tayammum permits prayer without removing impurity, so each tayammum covers only one obligatory prayer; after a nullifier following tayammum for janāba, one tayammums again for wudu.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r5.anchor: فالمشهور من رواية ابن القاسم أن التيمم مبيح للصلاة وليس رافعا للحدث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r6.claim: In the Baghdadi transmission, a patient unable to use water may perform multiple prayers with one tayammum until a nullifier; this also applies to missed prayers, and no Malik report addresses a junub person who then loses wudu.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p63/r6.anchor: وعن مالك ، في رواية البغداديين : أن المريض الذي لا يقدر على مس الماء يتيمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r1.claim: Among scholars who use legal implications, the unqualified traveler exception is further limited by “if you find no water”; the general prohibition on junub people is otherwise narrowed by the later illness-or-travel condition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r1.anchor: وفي مفهوم هذا الاستثناء ، عند القائلين بالمفاهيم من الجمهور ، على هذا المحمل تفصيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r2.claim: If Muslims already understood that prayer may occur without purification, the traveler exception awaits clarification and the following conditions clarify it; otherwise, those conditions introduce tayammum rules anew.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r2.anchor: ثم إن كان قد تقرر عند المسلمين أن الصلاة تقع بدون طهارة يبق قوله : { إلا عابري سبيل } مجملا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r3.claim: The exception is placed before the statement’s restriction is complete, an uncommon order used for emphasis, as illustrated by a line from Musa ibn Jabir al-Hanafi al-Umawi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r3.anchor: وتقديم المستثنى في قوله : { إلا عابري سبيل } قبل تمام الكلام المقصود قصره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r4.claim: The cited poetic line by Musa ibn Jabir al-Hanafi al-Umawi exemplifies placing the exception early for emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p64/r4.anchor: كقول موسى بن جابر الحنفي أموي : لا أشتهي يا قوم إلا كارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r1.claim: The endpoint forbids prayer while junub until washing; since prayer is never waived, the verse establishes ghusl as obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r1.anchor: فهو تشريع للغسل من الجنابة وإيجاب له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r2.claim: Ghusl provides cleanliness and joins bodily completeness in prayer to inward completeness in communion and humility before God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r2.anchor: ونيط ذلك بأداء الصلاة ليكون المصلي في حالة كمال الجسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r3.claim: The law avoids a subjective dirt threshold and ties washing to a regular, objective bodily condition that tracks strength and bodily residue while serving the aim of cleanliness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r3.anchor: فنيط وجوب الغسل بحالة لا تنفك عن القوة البشرية في مدة متعارف أعمار البشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r4.claim: He adds that washing after sexual discharge renews the nervous system, which physicians say becomes sluggish after the body's vital force is spent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r4.anchor: وهي تجديد نشاط المجموع العصبي الذي يعتريه فتور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r5.claim: Malik requires rubbing the body during ghusl, based on the Arabic sense of washing and the agreed need to rub during wudu.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65/r5.anchor: فشرطه مالك رحمه الله بناء على أنه المعروف من معنى الغسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r1.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r1.claim: The majority hold that pouring water over the body or immersing oneself suffices for ghusl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r1.anchor: وقال جمهور العلماء : يجزىء في الغسل إحاطة البدن بالماء بالصب أو الانغماس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r2.speaker: ميمونة وعائشة
