IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r2.claim: Reports from Maimuna and Aisha say the Prophet poured water over his body; Ibn Ashur says their silence does not show that he omitted rubbing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r2.anchor: واحتجوا بحديث ميمونة وعائشة رضي الله عنهما في غسل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أفاض الماء على جسده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r3.claim: A weak report from Malik, transmitted by Abu al-Faraj and Marwan ibn Muhammad al-Tatari, also supports sufficiency of water coverage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r3.anchor: وهذا أيضا رواية عن مالك رواها عنه أبو الفرج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r4.claim: The illness and travel clauses give the concession from ghusl and wudu; wudu was detailed in al-Maida, revealed earlier, and this passage sets out the full tayammum rule.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r4.anchor: ذكر حالة الرخصة في ترك الاغتسال وترك الوضوء الذي لم يذكر في هذه السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r5.claim: The collected concession also specifies the earlier general prohibition on approaching prayer while junub.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p65#2/r5.anchor: وفي جمع هذه الأشياء في نسق حصل هذا المقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r1.claim: The travel clause explains the earlier phrase about passing through, if that phrase is ambiguous; otherwise it introduces a new ruling.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r1.anchor: وإلا فهو استئناف حكم جديد كما تقدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r2.claim: Mentioning discharge from the privy adds tayammum as a substitute for wudu, completing the two kinds of tayammum; other causes can be inferred by analogy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r2.anchor: وغير ذلك من أسبابه يؤخذ بالقياس على المذكور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r3.claim: The sick person meant here is one whose condition makes washing harmful or likely to worsen the illness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r3.anchor: فالمريض أريد به الذي اختل نظام صحته بحيث صار الاغتسال يضره أو يزيد علته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r4.claim: Coming from the privy is a euphemism for relieving oneself, chosen because direct mention was considered repellent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r4.anchor: كناية عن قضاء الحاجة البشرية ، شاع في كلامهم التكني بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66/r5.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ originally means a low place hidden from view; Arabs went outside the settlement to such places, then the euphemism became commonplace and jurists used it for the resulting state and its acts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r1.claim: The reciprocal and non-reciprocal forms of the verb are, in Ibn Ashur's view, equivalent in meaning; he dismisses attempts to distinguish them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r1.anchor: وهما بمعنى واحد على التحقيق . ومن حاول التفصيل لم يأت بما فيه تحصيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r2.claim: Touch literally means bodily contact, and metaphorically can mean seeking or finding, descending, or sexual intercourse; the cited poem witnesses the sense of descending, while 2:237 uses it for intercourse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r2.anchor: أصل اللمس المباشرة باليد أو بشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi reads the phrase literally and makes a man's touching a woman's body with his hand invalidate wudu; Ibn Ashur calls this an implausible reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r3.anchor: وبذلك فسره الشافعي ، فجعل لمس الرجل بيده جسد امرأته موجبا للوضوء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers the euphemistic sense of intercourse: the list gathers common causes of minor and major purification, and the concession context calls for explicit mention rather than relying on implication.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r4.anchor: فالمحمل الصحيح أن الملامسة كناية عن الجماع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r5.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r5.claim: The majority, including Malik and Abu Hanifa, do not require wudu after touching one's wife unless something is emitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r5.anchor: وإلى هذا مال الجمهور فلذلك لم يجب عند مالك وأبي حنيفة الوضوء من لمس الرجل امرأته ما لم يخرج منه شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r6.claim: Malik treats the phrase as both literal and euphemistic but invalidates wudu for literal touch only with pleasure or intent to take pleasure; Ibn Ashur attributes this to early reports, not the verse's intended sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r6.anchor: إلا أن مالكا قال : إذا التذ اللامس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur thinks Malik relied on reports from early authorities for the pleasure-based rule, but does not think that rule is what this verse means.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p66#2/r7.anchor: وأرى مالكا اعتمد في هذا على الآثار المروية عن أيمة السلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r1.claim: Most readers recite lāmastum with an alif; Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf recite lamastum without one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r1.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف { لمستم } بدون ألف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r2.claim: The failure to find water is attached to the conditional clause and limits the traveler, one coming from the privy, and one touching women.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r2.anchor: وهو قيد في المسافر ، ومن جاء من الغائط ، ومن لامس النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r3.claim: The water condition does not restrict the sick person's tayammum, because the meaning of illness already indicates the concession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r3.anchor: أما المريض فلا يتقيد تيممه بعدم وجدان الماء لأنه يتيمم مطلقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r4.claim: The sick person is not merely someone chronically bedridden, since someone can usually bring water to such a person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r4.anchor: ولا يكون المقصود من المريض الزمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r5.claim: Tayammum means intending, and saʿid means the earth's surface; Dhu al-Rumma's verse about an animal on the saʿid supports that sense.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r6.claim: Tayyib means pure, extending the permitted surface material to soil, sand, and stone when free of filth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r6.anchor: والطيب : الطاهر الذي لم تلوثه نجاسة ولا قذر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r7.claim: Calling for the surface of the earth discourages excessive efforts to seek soil or sand buried beneath the surface in pursuit of perfect purity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r7.anchor: وإنما عبر بالصعيد ليصرف المسلمين عن هوس أن يتطلبوا التراب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r8.claim: The verse either legislated tayammum or confirmed its earlier legislation in al-Maida; Ibn Ashur prefers that it had already been legislated there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r8.anchor: وقد شرع بهذه الآية حكم التيمم أو قرر شرعه السابق في سورة المائدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r9.claim: Tayammum was legislated in year six during the expedition of al-Muraysiʿ, after the group found itself without water while searching for Aisha's lost necklace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r9.anchor: وكان شرع التيمم سنة ست في غزوة المريسيع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r10.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r10.claim: Aisha reports in a sound collection that the Prophet stopped the party at al-Bayda or Dhat al-Jaysh to search for her lost necklace; they had no water, the verse of tayammum came down, and the necklace was found beneath her camel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r10.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : خرجنا مع رسول الله في بعض أسفاره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r11.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r11.claim: After the tayammum ruling, Usayd ibn Hudayr told Aisha that this was not the first blessing God had brought through her family.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p67/r11.anchor: فقال أسيد بن الحضير : ما هي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r1.speaker: جابر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r1.claim: The Prophet listed among five gifts unique to him that the earth was made a mosque and a purifier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r1.anchor: حديث جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur's proposed wisdom is to preserve the believer's sense that purification is obligatory and prayer is sacred, leaving no situation in which one approaches prayer without ritual preparation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r2.anchor: وأحسب أن حكمة تشريعه تقرير لزوم الطهارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r3.claim: Touching earth with the hands evokes purification because earth is the source of water and is also used to clean vessels, garments, bodies, and through istijmar; it reminds the waterless person to seek water once able.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r3.anchor: وجعل ذلك بمباشرة اليدين صعيد الأرض التي هي منبع الماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r4.claim: Because tayammum is symbolic purification, the law requires only the face and hands for both minor and major impurity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r4.anchor: وإذ قد كان التيمم طهارة رمزية اقتنعت الشريعة فيه بالوجه والكفين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r5.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r5.claim: Al-Shafiʿi requires soil specifically and transfer of it to the face and hands; Ibn Ashur conjectures that this reflects the cleaning analogy, though no early authority is reported to have held it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r5.anchor: وكأن الشافعي لما اشترط أن يكون التيمم بالتراب خاصة وأن ينقل المتيمم منه إلى وجهه ويديه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r6.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r6.claim: When Ammar could not perform ghusl, he rolled in dust; the Prophet told him that wiping the face and hands was sufficient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r6.anchor: وهو ما سبق إلى خاطر عمار بن ياسر حين تمرغ في التراب لما تعذر عليه الاغتسال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r7.speaker: عمر وابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r7.claim: Umar and Ibn Masud hold that tayammum substitutes for wudu only, not ghusl, so a junub person must wait for water even at home or on a journey.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r7.anchor: فقال عمر وابن مسعود : لا يقع التيمم بدلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r8.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r8.claim: In a debate recorded by al-Bukhari, Abu Musa asks Ibn Masud what a junub person without water should do, citing Ammar's instruction and the tayammum verse; Ibn Masud first answers that he must wait for water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r8.anchor: قال أبو موسى لا بن مسعود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r9.claim: Ibn Masud invokes Umar's dissatisfaction with Ammar's report and fears that people would choose tayammum whenever cold; when Abu Musa points to the verse, he has no answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r9.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : ألم تر عمر لم يقنع منه بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r10.claim: Ibn Ashur says Umar and Ibn Masud understood passing through as permission to pass through a mosque and took touching women as literal, wudu-breaking contact, as al-Shafiʿi does.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r10.anchor: تأولا آية النساء فجعلا قوله : { إلا عابري سبيل } رخصة لمرور المسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r11.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r11.claim: All other jurists reject Umar and Ibn Masud's restriction; the majority allow tayammum for lack of water or fear that washing will cause death, illness, or worsening, even a cold or fever.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r11.anchor: فقال الجمهور : يتيمم فاقد الماء ومن يخاف على نفسه الهلاك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r12.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r12.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits tayammum only for lack of water or fear of death, reasoning that worsening illness is uncertain; Ibn Ashur replies that both outcomes are uncertain and God imposes no hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r12.anchor: وقال الشافعي : لا يتيمم إلا فاقد الماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r13.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r13.claim: On a cold night in the expedition of Dhat al-Salasil, Amr performed tayammum and led prayer; when asked, he cited 4:29 against killing oneself, and the Prophet laughed without objecting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p68/r13.anchor: وقد تيمم عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه في ليلة باردة في غزوة ذات السلاسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r1.claim: Tayammum is limited to the face and hands, excluding the rest of wudu and ghusl, because its aim is symbolic readiness for prayer rather than physical cleansing or renewed bodily energy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r1.anchor: جعل التيمم قاصرا على مسح الوجه واليدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r2.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r2.claim: Ammar reports that, while traveling and junub, he rolled in dust and prayed; the Prophet answered that wiping the face and hands sufficed, confirming that tayammum for ghusl is like tayammum for wudu.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r2.anchor: عن عمار بن ياسر ، قال : كنت في سفر فأجنبت فتمعكت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r3.claim: The bāʾ is emphatic, as in 19:25 and al-Nabigha's verse; the meaning is simply wipe your faces and hands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r3.anchor: والباء للتأكيد مثل : ( وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r4.claim: Using bāʾ with the wiped areas, in wudu and tayammum, signals thorough wiping and prevents extending the concession beyond what is needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p70/r4.anchor: وقد ذكرت هذه الباء مع الممسوح في الوضوء ومع التيمم للدلالة على تمكن المسح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p71/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p71/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p71/r1.claim: The closing names explain the concession: God excuses people who are ill or lack water from washing and avoids requiring them to wait until prayers accumulate and become difficult to make up.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p71/r1.anchor: تذييل لحكم الرخصة إذ عفا عن المسلمين فلم يكلفهم الغسل أو الوضوء عند المرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r1.claim: The author describes semantics and rhetoric as especially useful, after legal foundations, for discerning God’s intent, interpreting ambiguities, uncovering subtleties, and recognizing inimitability.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r2.speaker: عبد القاهر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r2.claim: ʿAbd al-Qahir warns that interpreters who take metaphorical or illustrative wording literally corrupt its meaning and purpose and obscure its eloquence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r2.anchor: ومن عادة قوم ممن يتعاطى التفسير بغير علم ، أن يتوهموا ألباب الألفاظ الموضوعة على المجاز والتمثيل أنها على ظواهرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r3.claim: Immersion in Arabic sermons, poems, proverbs, customs, and conversation gives later learners a taste analogous to native instinct; taste perceives eloquent speech’s qualities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r3.anchor: وأما استعمال العرب ، فهو التملي من أساليبهم في خطبهم وأشعارهم وأمثالهم وعوائدهم ومحادثاتهم ، ليحصل بذلك لممارسة المولد ذوق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r4.speaker: الوزير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r4.claim: The author’s grandfather, the vizier, says non-Arabs can acquire taste by tracking eloquent usage and reflecting on recognized excellent speech; it strengthens with familiarity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r4.anchor: قال شيخنا الجد الوزير وهي ناشئة عن تتبع استعمال البلغاء فتحصل لغير العربي بتتبع موارد الاستعمال والتدبر في الكلام المقطوع ببلوغه غاية البلاغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r5.claim: The practitioner should study speech recognized as eloquent, such as the Muʿallaqat, Hamasa, Nahj al-Balagha, Hariri’s Maqamat, and Badiʿ al-Zaman’s epistles.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r5.anchor: نحو المعلقات والحماسة ونحو نهج البلاغة ومقامات الحريري ورسائل بديع الزمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r6.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r6.claim: Al-Sakkaki says an outsider may imitate an expert’s judgments when taste is lacking until time and study supply it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r6.anchor: فلا بأس على الدخيل في علم المعاني ، أن يقلد صاحبه في بعض فتاواه إن فاته الذوق هناك إلى أن يتكامل له على مهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r7.claim: Poetry and Arab usage clarify difficult meanings and persuade learners; rhetoric, beyond grammatical rules, reveals meanings and can tip a choice between interpretations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p20/r7.anchor: لم يكن غنى للمفسر في بعض المواضع من الاستشهاد على المراد في الآية ، ببيت من الشعر ، أو بشيء من كلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r5.claim: Variants such as yathurna/yattahharna and lamastum/lamastum increase the possible meanings of a verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r5.anchor: نحو ) حتى يطهرن ( بفتح الطاء المشددة والهاء المشددة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وأبو بكر وعمر وعبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r1.claim: A reported occasion says Companions drank wine before prohibition; when prayer came, ʿAlī led and garbled Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn (109:1). Another version names ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf as leader.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r1.anchor: أن جماعة من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شربت الخمر عند أحدهم قبل التحريم، فيهم أبو بكر وعمر وعلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r2.claim: Another transmission says the prayer leader in the occasion was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r2.anchor: وروي أن المصلي عبد الرحمن بن عوف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r3.speaker: جمهور المفسرين والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r3.claim: Most commentators understand intoxication as wine; al-Ḍaḥḥāk instead says sleep intoxication, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya judges weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r3.anchor: وجمهور المفسرين على أن المراد سكر الخمر، إلا الضحاك، فإنه قال: إنما المراد سكر النوم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r4.claim: The address is to competent believers; a drunk person without discernment is not addressed while intoxicated, but on recovery must fulfill obligations and make up rulings already imposed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r4.anchor: والخطاب لجميع الأمة الصالحين، وأما السكران إذا عدم الميز لسكره فليس بمخاطب في ذلك الوقت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r5.speaker: فرقة والأعمش والنخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r5.claim: Readings include سكارى and سكرى with differing vowels; Abū al-Fatḥ explains the forms as broken plural or feminine adjectives.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r5.anchor: وقرأت فرقة سكارى جمع سكران، وقرأت فرقة «سكرى» بفتح السين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r6.speaker: أبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ explains سكرى with fatḥa as a broken plural of سكران, like روبى, but allows it as a collective feminine singular; the ḍamma form is a feminine adjective like حبلى.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: هو تكسير سكران على سكارى، كما قالوا: روبى نياما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r7.claim: سكر means closure of understanding, related to saying سكرت الماء when one blocks the water's passage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r7.anchor: والسكر انسداد الفهم، ومنه سكرت الماء إذا سددت طريقه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r8.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r8.claim: One group takes الصلاة to mean the familiar ritual prayer, consistent with the occasion of revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r8.anchor: وقالت طائفة: الصلاة هنا العبادة المعروفة، حسب السبب في نزول الآية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r9.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r9.claim: Another group takes الصلاة to include both prayer and its place, since people then went to the mosque only for prayer and prayed only in congregation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p56#2/r9.anchor: وقالت طائفة: الصلاة هنا المراد بها موضع الصلاة والصلاة معا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r1.claim: The dispute over what counts as crossing the way is why commentators differed over whether الصلاة here is prayer itself or the mosque.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وإنما احتيج إلى هذا الخلاف بحسب ما يأتي في تفسير عابري السبيل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عفان وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r2.claim: Uthmān and others held that a drunk person's divorce does not take effect, since the verse shows the intoxicated person does not know what he says.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه وغيره: إن السكران لا يلزمه طلاقه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r3.claim: When a man confessed to adultery, the Prophet asked whether he was intoxicated; Ibn ʿAṭiyya infers an intoxicated confession would not bind him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r3.anchor: ولقول النبي عليه السلام للذي أقر بالزنى أسكران أنت؟ فمعناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r4.claim: Human claims such as divorce, financial admission, or slander affect others' rights, so a drunk person's claim not to know is suspect; adultery confession concerns God's right, so after sobering a claimed lack of awareness is accepted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r4.anchor: وبين طلاق السكران وإقراره بالزنى فرق، وذلك أن الطلاق والإقرار بالمال والقذف وما أشبهه هذا يتعلق به حقوق الغير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r5.claim: All criminal penalties remain binding on the intoxicated person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r5.anchor: وأما أحكام الجنايات، فهي كلها لازمة للسكران

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r6.claim: أنتم سكارى is a subject-and-predicate clause functioning circumstantially.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r6.anchor: وأنتم سكارى ابتداء وخبر، جملة في موضع الحال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r7.speaker: ابن فورك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r7.claim: Ibn Fūrak says the verse prohibits drinking itself so people will not approach prayer intoxicated; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is not the apparent meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r7.anchor: وحكي عن ابن فورك أنه قال: معنى الآية النهي عن السكر، أي لا يكن منكم سكر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r8.speaker: الصحابة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r8.claim: A report says that after this verse the Companions continued drinking but timed or limited it around dawn and evening prayer so no prayer found them intoxicated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r8.anchor: وقد روي: أن الصحابة بعد هذه الآية كانوا يشربون ويقللون أثر الصبح وأثر العتمة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r9.claim: ولا جنبا coordinates with the syntactic position of the preceding clause, which is accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r9.anchor: وقوله: ولا جنبا عطف على موضع هذه الجملة المنصوبة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r10.speaker: جمهور الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r10.claim: Most of the community define junub as one impure through emission or meeting of the circumcised parts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r10.anchor: والجنب هو غير الطاهر من إنزال أو مجاوزة ختان،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r11.speaker: بعض الصحابة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r11.claim: Some Companions held that ghusl is required only when semen is emitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r11.anchor: وروي عن بعض الصحابة: لا غسل إلا على من أنزل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r12.claim: Junub may derive from distance, as if separated from purity, or from lying beside someone and touching with one's side.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r12.anchor: وهي: البعد، كأنه جانب الطهر أو من الجنب، كأنه ضاجع ومس بجنبه جنبا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r13.claim: One group reads junuban with a vowelless nūn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r14.claim: عبور means crossing or passing through, with examples of a ship crossing a river and a camel traversing wilderness.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r15.speaker: الشاعرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r15.claim: A woman's poem describes a swift camel crossing the wilderness at midday, illustrating traversing in عابري سبيل.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r15.anchor: قال الشاعر: وهي امرأة: [الكامل] عيرانة سرح اليدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r16.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد والحكم وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r16.claim: They take the wayfarer to be a traveler: one may not approach prayer while junub until bathing, except a traveler may use tayammum.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r16.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد والحكم وغيرهم: عابر السبيل هو المسافر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r17.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وعكرمة والنخعي وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r17.claim: They take عابر السبيل to mean someone passing through a mosque; this depends on understanding الصلاة as the mosque and prayer place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r17.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وابن مسعود وعكرمة والنخعي وغيرهم: عابر السبيل الخاطر في المسجد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r18.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r18.claim: One reported occasion says some Anṣār had home doors opening into the mosque, so when junub they needed to cross it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r18.anchor: وروى بعضهم: أن سبب الآية: أن قوما من الأنصار كانت أبواب دورهم شارعة في المسجد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r19.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r19.claim: Most commentators say the later tayammum clause was revealed when Companions lacked water during the Muraysīʿ expedition while searching for ʿĀʾisha's necklace.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r19.anchor: ثم نزلت وإن كنتم مرضى إلى آخر الآية، بسبب عدم الصحابة الماء في غزوة المريسيع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r20.speaker: النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r20.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī says the verse was revealed for wounded people who became junub and told the Prophet about their situation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r20.anchor: وقال النخعي: نزلت في قوم أصابتهم جراح ثم أجنبوا، فذكروا ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r21.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r21.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says the verse was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p57/r21.anchor: فنزلت هذه الآية، ذكر النقاش: أن ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r1.claim: The sick person intended here is a resident. Tayammum is unanimously permitted for someone who fears death from cold water or illness, apart from a report from ʿAṭāʾ that he must purify even if he dies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r1.anchor: والمريض المقصود في هذه الآية هو الحضري، والذي يصح له التيمم هو الذي يخاف الموت لبرد الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r2.claim: Within the Mālikī school, as far as Ibn ʿAṭiyya recalls, tayammum is also allowed for someone fearing a new or worsening illness or delayed recovery.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r2.anchor: والذي يخاف حدوث علة على علة أو زيادة علة، والذي يخاف بطء برء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r3.claim: A sick person may lack access to water because no one can bring it, or because of the health risks described.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r3.anchor: والأسباب التي لا يجد المريض بها الماء هي إما عدم المناول، وإما خوف ما ذكرناه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r4.speaker: داود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r4.claim: Dāwūd permits tayammum for anyone called sick; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says scholars restrict it to serious conditions such as smallpox, measles, and illnesses endangered by water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r4.anchor: وقال داود: كل من انطلق عليه اسم المريض فجائز له التيمم، وهذا قول خلف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r5.speaker: مالك وجمهور الفقهاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r5.claim: Travel here means being away from settled habitation, whether or not the journey qualifies one to shorten prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r5.anchor: والمسافر في هذه الآية: هو الغائب عن الحضر، كان السفر مما تقصر فيه الصلاة أو لا تقصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r6.speaker: الشافعي وقوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī reports a view that tayammum is allowed only on travel that permits shortening prayer; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r6.anchor: وقال الشافعي في كتاب الأشراف: وقال قوم: لا يتيمم إلا في سفر يجوز فيه التقصير، وهذا ضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r7.claim: Another group disallows tayammum during sinful travel; Ibn ʿAṭiyya also judges this weak.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r8.claim: A traveler may lack water because none exists, searching risks missing companions, baggage is endangered, or predators or other harm threaten.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r8.anchor: والأسباب التي لا يجد بها المسافر الماء هي إما عدمه جملة، وإما خوف فوات الرفيق بسبب طلبه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r9.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r9.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī places tayammum at time's start, Abū Ḥanīfa and others at its end, while Mālik distinguishes the hopeless, hopeful, and uninformed about finding water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r9.anchor: واختلف في وقت إيقاعه التيمم، فقال الشافعي: في أول الوقت، وقال أبو حنيفة وغيره: في آخر الوقت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r10.speaker: إسحق بن راهويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r10.claim: Isḥāq ibn Rāhwayh says a traveler need search only ahead and nearby.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r10.anchor: وقال إسحق بن راهويه: لا يلزم المسافر طلب الماء إلا بين يديه وحوله،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r11.claim: Another group requires searching out to about two bowshots or similar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r11.anchor: وقالت طائفة: يخرج من طلبه الغلوتين ونحوهما،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r12.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r12.claim: In the Mālikī school, one walks three miles while looking for water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r12.anchor: وفي مذهب مالك يمشي في طلبه ثلاثة أميال،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r13.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r13.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires searching without risking loss of companions or prayer time; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this a good view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58/r13.anchor: وقال الشافعي: يمشي في طلبه ما لم يخف فوات رفيق أو فوات الوقت.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls al-Shāfiʿī's rule for searching for water a good view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قول حسن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r2.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ originally meant low ground where Arabs went to relieve themselves; frequent use made it a conventional euphemism.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r2.anchor: وأصل الغائط ما انخفض من الأرض، وكانت العرب تقصد بقضاء حاجتها ذلك الصنف من المواضع،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r3.speaker: قتادة والزهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r3.claim: Qatāda and al-Zuhrī read من الغيط with a silent yāʾ and no alif; Ibn Jinnī derives it from فيعل and says the medial radical was originally wāw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ قتادة والزهري «من الغيط» ساكنة الياء من غير ألف، قال ابن جني: هو محذوف من فيعل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r4.claim: Mālik's preferred classification recognizes three kinds of minor impurity: customary output from the passages, loss of reason, and touching.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r4.anchor: وأنبل ما اعتقد في ذلك: أن أنواع الأحداث ثلاثة، ما خرج من السبيلين معتاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa counts any impurity leaving the body, regardless of where it exits, and does not count touching.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r5.anchor: وعلى مذهب أبي حنيفة ما خرج من النجاسات من الجسد، ولا يراعى المخرج ولا غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r6.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī counts anything leaving either of the two passages, whether customary or not.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r6.anchor: وعلى مذهب الشافعي ما خرج من السبيلين، ولا يراعى الاعتياد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r7.claim: Nine kinds unanimously invalidate minor ablution: urine, semen, wadi, madhy, menstrual blood, wind and feces, and loss of reason through insanity, fainting, or deep sleep; other cases remain disputed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r7.anchor: أربعة من الذكر، وهي البول والمني والودي والمذي،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r8.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim read لامستم; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read لمستم. The word can mean intercourse, hand contact, or kissing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم لامستم وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «لمستم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r9.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r9.claim: Mālik gives the wording full scope: intercourse and hand-touching both require tayammum because touching invalidates ablution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r9.anchor: يقول: اللفظة هنا على أتم عمومها تقتضي الوجهين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r10.speaker: عمر وعبد الله بن مسعود وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r10.claim: A group reported from ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd restricts the word to hand contact and says a junub person must bathe or wait for water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r10.anchor: روي هذا القول عن عمر رضي الله عنه وعن عبد الله بن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r11.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa restricts the word to intercourse; touching is not a ritual impurity and a pleasurable kiss does not invalidate ablution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r11.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: هي هنا مخصصة للمس الذي هو الجماع،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r12.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r12.claim: Mālik rules that touching invalidates ablution when done for pleasure, but not without that intent or when the woman touched is one's daughter or mother.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r12.anchor: ومالك رحمه الله يرى: أن اللمس ينقض إذا كان للذة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r13.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r13.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī applies النساء generally: touching one's mother or daughter in any manner invalidates ablution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r13.anchor: والشافعي رحمه الله يعمم لفظة النساء، فإذا لمس الرجل عنده أمه أو ابنته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r14.claim: Lack of water applies to sick people and travelers; a healthy resident may also qualify when prices are universally exorbitant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r14.anchor: وعدم وجود الماء يترتب للمريض وللمسافر حسبما ذكرناه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r15.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan says one must buy water at any cost, even spending all one's money and becoming destitute; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as inconsistent with ease and absence of hardship (2:185; 22:78).
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r15.anchor: فقال الحسن: يشتري الرجل الماء بماله كله ويبقى عديما، وهذا قول ضعيف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r16.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r16.claim: One group requires purchase unless the cost exceeds the usual price by a third or more.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r16.anchor: وقالت طائفة: يشتري ما لم يزد على القيمة الثلث فصاعدا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r17.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r17.claim: Another group requires paying two or three dirhams for water ordinarily worth one; Ibn ʿAṭiyya places these views within the Mālikī school.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r17.anchor: وقالت طائفة: يشتري قيمة الدرهم بالدرهمين والثلاثة، ونحو هذا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r18.speaker: أشهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r18.claim: Asked whether one must buy a water-skin for ten dirhams, Ashhab says he does not think this is required of people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p58#2/r18.anchor: وقيل لأشهب: أيشتري القربة بعشرة دراهم؟ فقال ما أرى ذلك على الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r1.claim: When obtaining water requires purchase, the duty depends on the buyer’s means and need; he should buy it unless its high price causes harm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r1.anchor: إنما هو بحسب غنى المشتري وحاجته، والوجه عندي أن يشتري ما لم يؤذ غلاؤه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r2.speaker: مالك وابن نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r2.claim: For a healthy resident restrained from accessing water, they say he neither prays nor makes up the prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r2.anchor: فقال مالك وابن نافع: لا يصلي ولا يعيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r3.speaker: ابن القاسم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r3.claim: For a healthy resident restrained from water, Ibn al-Qasim says to pray and repeat the prayer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r4.speaker: أشهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r4.claim: For a healthy resident restrained from water, Ashhab says to pray without repeating.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r5.speaker: أصبغ
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r5.claim: Asbagh says the restrained resident does not pray but makes it up if using water would make him miss the prayer time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r5.anchor: وقال أصبغ: لا يصلي ويقضي، إذا خاف الحضري فوات الوقت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r6.claim: Malik has two positions in the Mudawwana: perform tayammum without repeating, or repeat; in other works he says to obtain water and wash even after sunrise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r6.anchor: فلمالك رحمه الله قولان في المدونة: إنه يتيمم ولا يعيد، وقال: إنه يعيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r7.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r7.claim: If a person tayammums with enough time left for ablution and one rakʿa, some say he must repeat and others say he need not.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r8.claim: Tayammum in Arabic means to intend or head toward something; Ibn ʿAtiyya supports the sense with verses by Imruʾ al-Qays and al-Aʿshā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r8.anchor: ومعنى قوله فتيمموا في اللغة: اقصدوا، ومنه قول امرئ القيس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r9.claim: The verb’s sense of intending is also shown by al-Aʿshā of Thaʿlaba’s line about heading toward Qays.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r9.anchor: ومنه قول أعشى بني ثعلبة: [المتقارب] تيممت قيسا وكم دونه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r10.claim: In religious usage, tayammum became the established name for the known act of worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r10.anchor: ثم غلب هذا الاسم في الشرع على العبادة المعروفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r11.speaker: الخليل وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r11.claim: Al-Khalil and others explain ṣaʿīd as the face or surface of the earth; Dhu al-Rumma’s verse supplies poetic evidence for the term.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r11.anchor: والصعيد في اللغة: وجه الأرض، قاله الخليل وغيره، ومنه قول ذي الرمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r12.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r12.claim: Malik permits tayammum on any part of the earth—soil, sand, stones, minerals, or saline ground—understanding ṭayyib as pure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r12.anchor: فقالت طائفة: يتيمم بوجه الأرض، ترابا كان أو رملا أو حجارة أو معدنا أو سبخة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r13.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r13.claim: One group reads ṭayyib as meaning lawful, a sense Ibn ʿAtiyya considers awkward in this context.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r13.anchor: وقالت طائفة منهم: «الطيب» بمعنى الحلال، وهذا في هذا الموضع قلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r14.speaker: الشافعي وطائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r14.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and a group understand ṭayyib as growth-producing, like 7:58, so ṣaʿīd means soil and tayammum is not allowed on other materials.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r14.anchor: وقال الشافعي وطائفة: «الطيب» بمعنى المنبت، كما قال جل ذكره والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r15.claim: The agreed valid case is tayammum on pure, fertile soil that has not been moved or usurped.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p59/r15.anchor: فمكان الإجماع: أن يتيمم الرجل في تراب منبت طاهر غير منقول ولا مغصوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r1.claim: Jurists agree tayammum is forbidden on pure gold, silver, precious stones, food, and impure substances.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r1.anchor: أو الفضة والياقوت والزمرد، أو الأطعمة، كالخبز واللحم وغيرهما، أو على النجاسات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r2.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r2.claim: Malik allows tayammum on minerals, while al-Shafiʿi forbids it; al-Lakhmi notes disagreement within the Maliki school as well.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r2.anchor: فأجيز، وهو مذهب مالك، ومنع، وهو مذهب الشافعي، وأشار أبو الحسن اللخمي إلى أن الخلاف فيه موجود في المذهب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r3.speaker: أهل المذهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r3.claim: The Maliki school allows tayammum on both mineral salt and solid salt; other views forbid both or allow mineral salt but forbid solid salt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r3.anchor: وأما الملح فأجيز في المذهب المعدني والجامد، ومنعا، وأجيز المعدني ومنع الجامد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r4.claim: The Mudawwana allows tayammum with snow, while Malik prohibits it in other works.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r4.anchor: والثلج في المدونة جوازه، ولمالك في غيرها منعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r5.speaker: ابن علية وابن كيسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r5.claim: Al-Naqqash reports that Ibn ʿUlayya and Ibn Kaysan allowed tayammum with musk and saffron; Ibn ʿAtiyya rejects this as wholly erroneous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r5.anchor: وذكر النقاش عن ابن علية وابن كيسان: أنهما أجازا التيمم بالمسك والزعفران

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya calls the permission to use musk and saffron for tayammum wholly erroneous.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r7.speaker: جمهور المذهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r7.claim: Most Maliki jurists permit tayammum with soil carried in a dish, though some within the school and many outside it prohibit it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r7.anchor: فجمهور المذهب جواز التيمم به، وفي المذهب المنع، وهو في غير المذهب أكثر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r8.speaker: أهل المذهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r8.claim: The school has two positions on tayammum with baked materials such as brick or plaster: permitted or forbidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r8.anchor: وأما ما طبخ كالآجر والجص ففيه في المذهب قولان، الإجازة والمنع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r9.claim: Jurists disagree over whether tayammum may be performed on a wall.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r10.speaker: جمهور المذهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r10.claim: Most Maliki jurists forbid tayammum on wood, while the Mukhtaṣar of al-Waqqar allows it; the school also differs about plants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r10.anchor: فاختلف فيه في مذهب مالك، فالجمهور على منع التيمم على العود، وفي مختصر الوقار: أنه جائز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r11.claim: Al-Tabari records four explanations of ṣaʿīd: smooth land, level land, soil, or the face of the earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60/r11.anchor: وحكى الطبري في لفظة «الصعيد» اختلافا: أنها الأرض الملساء وأنها الأرض المستوية، وأن «الصعيد» التراب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r1.claim: The majority follows the Qurʾanic order by wiping the face before the hands; some routes of ʿAmmar’s hadith in al-Bukhari put the hands first, as do scholars reasoning by analogy with reversing ablution order.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r1.anchor: وترتيب القرآن الوجه قبل اليدين، وبه قال الجمهور، ووقع في حديث عمار في البخاري في بعض الطرق تقديم اليدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r2.claim: The majority requires wiping the whole face within its known ablution boundaries, carefully ensuring no part is left untouched.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r2.anchor: وتراعى في الوجه حدوده المعلومة في الوضوء، فالجمهور على أن استيعابه بالمسح في التيمم واجب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن مسلمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r3.claim: Some permit leaving hard-to-reach folds and the spaces between fingers unwiped, by analogy with folds in leather socks; this is Muhammad ibn Maslama’s Maliki position.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r3.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم أن لا يتتبع كالغضون في الخفين، وما بين الأصابع في اليدين، وهو في المذهب قول محمد بن مسلمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r4.claim: Malik’s Mudawwana prescribes two strikes for tayammum; Ibn al-Jahm says one, and Malik elsewhere says one suffices.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r4.anchor: ومذهب مالك في المدونة: أن التيمم بضربتين، وقال ابن الجهم: التيمم واحدة، وقال مالك في كتاب محمد: إن تيمم بضربة أجزاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r5.speaker: غيره في المذهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r5.claim: Some Maliki jurists require repeating tayammum within the prayer time after using one strike, while Ibn Nafiʿ requires repeating it ever after.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r5.anchor: وقال غيره في المذهب: يعيد في الوقت، وقال ابن نافع: يعيد أبدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r6.claim: Malik’s Mudawwana describes wiping left fingertips over the right fingers and up to the elbow, then the inner forearm to the wrist, and repeating on the other arm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r6.anchor: يبدأ بأصابع اليسرى على أصابع اليمنى، ثم يمر كذلك إلى المرفق، ثم يلوي بالكف اليسرى على باطن الذراع الأيمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r7.speaker: ابن حبيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r7.claim: Ibn Habib says the palms should then be wiped against each other; al-Lakhmi interprets the Mudawwana as requiring this, making Ibn Habib’s statement explanatory rather than contradictory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن حبيب: يمر بعد ذلك كفيه، فهذا مع تحكيم ظاهر المدونة خلاف، قال اللخمي: في كلام المدونة يريد ثم يمسح كفه بالأخرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r8.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r8.claim: One group begins with the left hand, reaches the wrist, continues across that palm, and then repeats on the right, to avoid returning to a limb after moving on.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r8.anchor: فإذا وصل على باطن الذراع إلى الرسغ، مشى على الكف، ثم كذلك باليمنى في اليسرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r9.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r9.claim: Another group handles soil in the same manner as water, applying it by a wiping motion but without a prescribed sequence of rank.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r9.anchor: يتناول بالتراب كما يتناول بالماء في صورة الإمرار دون رتبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r10.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r10.claim: Malik’s Mudawwana requires wiping to the elbows; stopping at the wrists requires repeating within the time, while Ibn Nafiʿ says to repeat ever after.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r10.anchor: وقال مالك في المدونة: يمسح يديه إلى المرفقين، فإن مسح إلى الكوعين أعاد في الوقت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r11.speaker: مكحول وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r11.claim: Some Maliki jurists require wiping only to the wrists; outside the school, some require only the palms, following ʿAmmar’s hadith and al-Shaʿbi’s position.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r11.anchor: قال غيرهما: في المذهب يمسح إلى الكوعين وهذا قول مكحول وجماعة من العلماء، وفي غير المذهب يمسح الكفين فقط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r12.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r12.claim: Al-Tabari relates that Abu Bakr told ʿAʾisha the tayammum dispensation was a blessing, and that they struck once for the face and once for hands up to shoulders or armpits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p60#2/r12.anchor: وذكره الطبري عن أبي بكر الصديق أنه قال لعائشة حين نزلت آية التيمم: إنك لمباركة، نزلت فيه رخصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r1.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r1.claim: A report from al-Aʿmash says the Prophet wiped to halfway up the forearms; Ibn ʿAtiyya knows of no scholar who followed this report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r1.anchor: أنصاف ذراعيه، ولم يقل بهذا الحديث أحد من العلماء فيما حفظت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r2.speaker: الداودي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r2.claim: Al-Dawudi classifies the wrists as obligatory, elbows as sunnah, and armpits as meritorious; Ibn ʿAtiyya says this lacks analogy or evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r2.anchor: وما حكي الداودي من أن الكوعين فرض والمرافق سنة والآباط فضيلة، فكلام لا يعضده قياس ولا دليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r3.claim: Some generalize the word “hands” to require wiping from the shoulders.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r3.anchor: وإنما عمم قوم لفظة اليد فأوجبوه من المنكب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r4.claim: Others analogize tayammum to ablution and require wiping to the elbows; the majority also extend the wipe to the elbows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r4.anchor: وقاس قوم على الوضوء فأوجبوه من المرافق، وعمم جمهور الأمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r5.claim: Some stop at the wrists, following the hadith; others analogize purification in tayammum to the legal hand amputation limit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r5.anchor: ووقف قوم مع الحديث في الكوعين، وقيس أيضا على القطع، إذ هو حكم شرعي وتطهير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r6.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r6.claim: Others follow ʿAmmar’s hadith and wipe only the palms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r6.anchor: ووقف آخرون مع حديث عمار في الكفين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r7.speaker: أهل المذهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r7.claim: The Maliki school differs over whether moving a ring and rubbing between the fingers are obligatory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p61/r7.anchor: واختلف المذهب في تحريك الخاتم وتخليل الأصابع على قولين، يجب ولا يجب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.claim: The prohibition came gradually: after incidents including Hamza damaging camel humps and ʿAli’s drunken misrecitation at Maghrib, the prayer restriction of 4:43 came before this final prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.anchor: ثم لم تزل النوازل تحزب الناس بسببها حتى نزلت هذه الآية، فحرمت بالمدينة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r1.claim: In a report from ʿAlī through Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf hosted food and wine; the intoxicated group prayed and garbled the opening of Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, after which the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r1.anchor: روى أبو عبدالرحمن السلمي عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال صنع لنا عبدالرحمن بن عوف طعاما فدعانا وسقانا من الخمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r2.claim: A second version says ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was the person they put forward to lead prayer and who mixed up the sūra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r2.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن أبي عبدالرحمن عن علي رضي الله عنه أن الذي قدموه وخلط في هذه السورة عبدالرحمن بن عوف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r3.claim: The phrase is interpreted either as not exposing oneself to intoxication at prayer times or as not entering prayer while intoxicated; the author prefers the first because an intoxicated person cannot understand what is addressed to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r3.anchor: والأول أصح لأن السكران لا يعقل ما يخاطب به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r4.claim: Most exegetes say the intoxication is from wine.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r4.anchor: أحدهما من الخمر قاله الجمهور والثاني من النوم قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the intoxication is from sleep; the author considers this far-fetched.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r5.anchor: والثاني من النوم قاله الضحاك وفيه بعد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r6.claim: This verse temporarily allowed drinking outside prayer times, then the later prohibition of wine abrogated that allowance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p88/r6.anchor: وهذه الآية اقتضت إباحة السكر في غير أوقات الصلاة ثم نسخت بتحريم الخمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says junub derives from distance or separation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj notes that junub has the same form for one man, two men, and a group, as raḍī does.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج يقال رجل جنب ورجلان جنب ورجال جنب كما يقال رجل رضى وقوم رضى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r3.claim: One explanation for the term is that semen has moved away from its proper place.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r4.claim: Another explanation is that a person in this state must avoid prayer, Qurʾān recitation, touching the muṣḥaf, and entering a mosque.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r4.anchor: والثاني لما يلزمه من اجتناب الصلاة وقراءة القرآن ومس المصحف ودخول المسجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r5.speaker: علي، مجاهد، الحكم، قتادة، ابن زيد، مقاتل، الفراء، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r5.claim: One interpretation permits a traveler without water to perform tayammum and pray while junub; on this view, passing by means being a traveler and approaching prayer means performing it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r5.anchor: فتيمموا وتصلوا وهذا المعنى مروي عن علي رضي الله عنه ومجاهد والحكم وقتادة وابن زيد ومقاتل والفراء والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود، أنس بن مالك، الحسن، سعيد بن المسيب، عكرمة، عطاء الخراساني، الزهري، عمرو بن دينار، أبو الضحى، أحمد، الشافعي، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r6.claim: Another interpretation bars a junub person from entering or sitting in mosques except to pass through; Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr are reported with both views.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p90/r6.anchor: والثاني لا تقربوا مواضع الصلاة وهي المساجد وأنتم جنب إلا مجتازين ولا تقعدوا وهذا المعنى مروي عن ابن مسعود وأنس بن مالك والحسن وسعيد بن المسيب وعكرمة وعطاء الخراساني والزهري وعمرو بن دينار وأبي الضحى وأحمد والشافعي وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the verse came down after a sick Anṣārī man unable to rise for ablution and without a servant asked the Prophet for help.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r1.anchor: فذكر له ذلك فنزلت هذه الآية ﴿ وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر ﴾ قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī says the verse came down after the Prophet's companions suffered spreading wounds while becoming junub and brought their difficulty to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r2.anchor: فنزلت ﴿ وإن كنتم مرضى ﴾ الآية كلها قاله إبراهيم النخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r3.claim: Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā says illness allows tayammum when using water would cause harm, whether or not death is feared; travel allows it with no water on short or long journeys. Lack of water is not required for the ill, but harm is; it is required for travelers, while travel itself is not a condition because water is commonly absent on journeys.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو يعلى وظاهر الآية يقتضي جواز التيمم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r1.claim: The “or” functions like “and”; otherwise the sick and traveler would owe purification even without the occurrence of ritual impurity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r1.anchor: أو بمعنى الواو لأنها لو لم تكن كذلك لكان وجوب الطهارة على المريض والمسافر غير متعلق بالحدث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r2.claim: Al-Ghāʾiṭ literally means low, level ground; the place is used euphemistically for the act of excretion, like other container or vehicle terms used for their contents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r2.anchor: والغائط المكان المطمئن من الأرض فكني عن الحدث بمكانه قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r3.claim: The author gives parallels: rāwiya is properly the camel carrying water, and ẓaʿāʾin are properly the howdahs carrying women; ʿadhira likewise names excretion from the courtyards where it was left.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك قالوا للمزادة راوية وإنما الراوية للبعير الذي يسقى عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، عاصم، ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir read lāmastum with an alif here and in al-Māʾida.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر أو لامستم بألف هاهنا وفي المائدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r5.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، خلف، المفضل عن عاصم، الوليد بن عتبة عن ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r5.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and the cited transmitters from ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read lamastum without an alif here and in al-Māʾida.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف في اختياره والمفضل عن عاصم والوليد بن عتبة عن ابن عامر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r6.speaker: علي، ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r6.claim: One legal interpretation takes touching women to mean sexual intercourse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r6.anchor: أحدهما أنها الجماع قاله علي وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن عمر، الشعبي، عبيدة، عطاء، ابن سيرين، النخعي، النهدي، الحكم، حماد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r7.claim: Another legal interpretation takes the phrase as touching a woman with the hand.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r7.anchor: والثاني أنها الملامسة باليد قاله ابن مسعود وابن عمر والشعبي وعبيدة وعطاء وابن سيرين والنخعي والنهدي والحكم وحماد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r8.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī says touch can mean contact by hand but is extended to other kinds of contact; 72:8 uses “we touched the heaven” for attempting to reach its secrets.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي اللمس يكون باليد وقد اتسع فيه فأوقع على غيره فمن ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r9.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r9.claim: The wording “they touched it with their hands” in 6:7 specifies hands to distinguish literal touching from the extended sense; likewise “sons from your loins” in 4:23 distinguishes biological sons from merely named sons.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p91#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي اللمس يكون باليد وقد اتسع فيه فأوقع على غيره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r1.claim: The Prophet and ʿĀʾisha were traveling without water when her necklace was lost; the search delayed them, and the tayammum verse was revealed. Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr called it another blessing for Abū Bakr's family. Both al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit this account.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r1.anchor: أن عائشة رضي الله عنها كانت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض أسفاره فانقطع عقد لها فأقام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على التماسه وليسوا على ماء وليس معهم ماء فنزلت هذه الآية فقال أسيد ابن حضير ما هي بأول بركتكم يا آل أبي بكر أخرجه البخاري ومسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r2.claim: A second account says ʿĀʾisha borrowed a necklace from Asmāʾ and lost it; the Prophet sent men to search, and when prayer came without water they prayed without ablution and reported it, whereupon the tayammum verse was revealed. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r2.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى أخرجها البخاري ومسلم أيضا أن عائشة استعارت من أسماء قلادة فهلكت فبعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجالا في طلبها فأدركتهم الصلاة وليس معهم ماء فصلوا بغير وضوء وشكوا ذلك إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزلت آية التيمم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r3.claim: Tayammum means to intend or aim; the author says he discussed this earlier under “do not aim at the bad.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r3.anchor: والتيمم في اللغة القصد وقد ذكرناه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r4.speaker: علي، ابن مسعود، الفراء، أبو عبيد، الزجاج، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r4.claim: These authorities say al-ṣaʿīd means soil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r4.anchor: وأما الصعيد فهو التراب قاله علي وابن مسعود والفراء وأبو عبيد والزجاج وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r5.speaker: الشافعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says the name al-ṣaʿīd applies only to soil that has dust.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r5.anchor: وقال الشافعي لا يقع اسم الصعيد إلى على تراب ذي غبار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r6.claim: Two interpretations of ṭayyib are pure and lawful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p93/r6.anchor: وفي الطيب قولان أحدهما أنه الطاهر والثاني الحلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r1.claim: The part of the face wiped in tayammum is the same area delimited for washing in ablution.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r1.anchor: الوجه الممسوح في التيمم هو المحدود في الوضوء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r2.speaker: عمار عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r2.claim: One view limits the hands to the wrists, citing the Prophet's report that tayammum is one strike for the face and palms; this is held by Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, ʿIkrima, al-Awzāʿī, Makḥūl, Mālik, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Dāwūd.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه إلى الكوعين حيث يقطع السارق روى عمار عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال التيمم ضربة للوجه والكفين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r3.claim: A second view extends wiping to the elbows, citing Ibn ʿAbbās's report that the Prophet wiped his forearms; it is held by Ibn ʿUmar, his son Sālim, al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥanīfa, and al-Shāfiʿī, while al-Shaʿbī is reported with both views.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه إلى المرفقين روى ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه تيمم فمسح ذراعيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r4.speaker: عمار بن ياسر، الزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r4.claim: A third view extends wiping from the fingertips to the armpits, citing ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir's report of a travel concession and two strikes, one for the face and one to the shoulders and armpits; al-Zuhrī holds this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p95/r4.anchor: والثالث أنه يجب المسح من رؤوس الأنامل إلى الآباط روى عمار بن ياسر قال كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفر فنزلت الرخصة في المسح فضربنا بأيدينا ضربة لوجوهنا وضربة لأيدينا إلى المناكب والآباط وهذا قول الزهري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r1.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r1.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says ʿafuww is an intensive form and means pardoning sins and leaving the wrongdoer unpunished.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r1.anchor: قال الخطابي العفو بناء للمبالغة والعفو الصفح عن الذنوب وترك مجازاة المسيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r2.claim: Another explanation derives the word from wind erasing a trace: the pardoner wipes away sins through pardon.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p96/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه مأخوذ من عفت الريح الأثر إذا درسته وكأن العافي عن الذنوب يمحوه بصفحه عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r1.claim: The verse forbids prayer while intoxicated enough not to know one's words and forbids a junub person from entering a mosque except to pass through without staying; this preceded the final wine prohibition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r1.anchor: ينهى تعالى عباده المؤمنين عن فعل الصلاة في حال السكر، الذي لا يدري معه المصلي ما يقول، وعن قربان محلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir places the restriction in the staged prohibition of wine: after 2:219, people avoided drinking at prayer times; after 4:43 came the final ban in 5:90–91, to which Umar replied that they had stopped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r2.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية، تلاها عليه، فقال: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا. فكانوا لا يشربون الخمر في أوقات الصلوات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r3.claim: In the account related through Isra'il from Abu Ishaq and Amr ibn Shurahbil, Umar says the verse was revealed and the Prophet's caller announced that no drunk person should approach prayer; Abu Dawud transmits this wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r3.anchor: عن عمرو -وهو ابن شرحبيل-عن عمر بن الخطاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r1.claim: Sa'd reports that after an Anṣari hosted and served wine to migrants and Anṣar, they became drunk and boastful; a man struck Sa'd's nose with a camel jaw, and the verse then descended before wine was prohibited. Muslim transmits the full report; other Sunan collections transmit it except Ibn Majah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r1.anchor: مصعب بن سعد يحدث عن سعد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r2.claim: Ali reports that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf served food and wine; when the drunken group prayed, their reciter confused the words of al-Kafirun, prompting the verse. Al-Tirmidhi calls this version hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي، عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: صنع لنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف طعاما، فدعانا وسقانا من الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r3.claim: Another account from Ali says he, Abd al-Rahman, and a third man drank before wine was forbidden; Abd al-Rahman led and garbled al-Kafirun, and the verse descended. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i transmit al-Thawri's route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r3.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب، عن أبي عبد الرحمن، عن علي؛ أنه كان هو وعبد الرحمن ورجل آخر شربوا الخمر،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r4.claim: A further report says Ali and companions drank at Abd al-Rahman's house before the ban; Ali led and failed to recite al-Kafirun properly, so the verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r4.anchor: عن جرير، عن عطاء، عن أبي عبد الله السلمي قال: كان علي في نفر من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بيت عبد الرحمن بن عوف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r1.claim: A report says Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf served food and drink and led Maghrib for companions; their garbled recitation of al-Kafirun was followed by revelation of the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن حبيب -وهو أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي؛ أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف صنع طعاما وشرابا، فدعا نفرا من أصحاب النبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says men used to come to prayer drunk before wine was prohibited; Abu Razin and Mujahid give the same explanation, and Ibn Jarir transmits it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r3.claim: Qatada says they avoided intoxication when prayer times arrived, and the final prohibition of wine later abrogated this rule.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق، عن معمر عن قتادة: كانوا يجتنبون السكر عند حضور الصلوات ثم نسخ بتحريم الخمر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the intoxication here as sleepiness, not wine intoxication; Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك في قوله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى} لم يعن بها سكر الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers wine intoxication and says the command addresses someone capable of understanding responsibility, not one so drunk that he cannot understand speech, who is legally like an insane person.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r5.anchor: ثم قال ابن جرير: والصواب أن المراد سكر الشراب. قال: ولم يتوجه النهي إلى السكران الذي لا يفهم الخطاب؛ لأن ذاك في حكم المجنون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r6.claim: The legal address applies to one who understands speech, since understanding is a condition of legal responsibility; several legal theorists state this principle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r6.anchor: وهو أن الخطاب يتوجه إلى من يفهم الكلام، دون السكران الذي لا يدري ما يقال له؛ فإن الفهم شرط التكليف.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r7.claim: The verse may indirectly prohibit intoxication altogether: a regular drinker cannot consistently perform the five daily prayers at their times; Ibn Kathir compares this to the exhortation to prepare to die Muslim in 3:102.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r7.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المراد التعريض بالنهي عن السكر بالكلية؛ لكونهم مأمورين بالصلاة في الخمسة الأوقات من الليل والنهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.claim: The best definition of intoxication is being unable to know what one is saying; drunkenness muddles recitation and removes reflection and humility.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.anchor: هذا أحسن ما يقال في حد السكران

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that a person who becomes drowsy in prayer should stop and sleep until able to know what he is saying; Bukhari and al-Nasa'i transmit it, and another wording warns he might curse himself while seeking forgiveness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي قلابة، عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نعس أحدكم وهو يصلي، فلينصرف فليتم حتى يعلم ما يقول.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the exception as allowing a junub person to pass through a mosque without sitting; Ibn Kathir lists many authorities who agree, including Ibn Masud, Anas, Abu Ubayda, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Qatada, and others.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.speaker: يزيد بن أبي حبيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.claim: Yazid ibn Abi Habib says the verse addressed Anṣar whose homes opened into the mosque: when junub and without water, they had to cross the mosque to reach water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.anchor: أن رجالا من الأنصار كانت أبوابهم في المسجد، فكانت تصيبهم الجنابة ولا ماء عندهم، فيردون الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.claim: A sound Bukhari report says the Prophet ordered every opening into the mosque closed except Abu Bakr's; Ibn Kathir links this late command to Abu Bakr's future leadership and need for mosque access.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "سدوا كل خوخة في المسجد إلا خوخة أبي بكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects reports that the Prophet ordered mosque doors closed except Ali's as mistaken; the sound report names Abu Bakr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.anchor: ومن روى: "إلا باب علي" كما وقع في بعض السنن، فهو خطأ، والصحيح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r7.claim: Many imams say a junub person may not remain in a mosque but may pass through; menstruating and postpartum women are analogous.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r7.anchor: ومن هذه الآية احتج كثير من الأئمة على أنه يحرم على الجنب اللبث في المسجد، ويجوز له المرور، وكذا الحائض والنفساء أيضا في معناه؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.speaker: بعض الأئمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.claim: Some authorities prohibit menstruating and postpartum women from passing through a mosque because of possible contamination.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.anchor: إلا أن بعضهم قال: يمنع مرورهما لاحتمال التلويث.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r9.speaker: بعض الأئمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r9.claim: Other authorities allow menstruating and postpartum women to pass if they can avoid contamination, and otherwise forbid passage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r9.anchor: ومنهم من قال: إن أمنت كل واحدة منهما التلويث في حال المرور جاز لهما المرور وإلا فلا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r1.claim: Aisha reports that when she said she was menstruating after the Prophet asked her to pass him a prayer mat from the mosque, he said menstruation was not in her hand; Abu Hurayra reports a similar exchange. Muslim transmits both, supporting a menstruating woman's passage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r1.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها قالت: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
