QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r10.claim: The Prophet directed worshippers to begin eating when dinner is served at the time prayer is called, removing a distraction so they can approach worship with an unoccupied, humble heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r10.anchor: إذا حضر العشاء وأقيمت الصلاة فابدئوا بالعشاء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r11.claim: Al-Qurtubi connects the command to the description of successful believers as humble in their prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r11.anchor:
ويدخل في هذه الآية:
قد أفلح المؤمنون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prohibition on praying drunk was abrogated by 5:6: first they were told not to pray intoxicated, then to pray in every state; this preceded alcohol's final prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r13.claim: Mujahid, Ikrima, and Qatada say the verse was abrogated by the final prohibition of wine; al-Qurtubi calls this the correct view because of Ali's report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نسخت بتحريم الخمر. وكذلك قال عكرمة وقتادة، وهو الصحيح في الباب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r14.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r14.claim: Al-Nahhas cites Umar recalling that a caller of the Prophet announced that no drunk person should approach prayer; on the sleepiness or urinary-need readings, al-Qurtubi says the verse is not abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#2/r14.anchor: وروي أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: أقيمت الصلاة فنادى منادي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r1.claim: The use of 'prayers' for places of prayer appears in 22:40; the exception for a junub person passing through supports the mosque reading because it permits passage, not prayer there.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r1.anchor: فسمى مواضع الصلاة صلاة. ويدل على هذا التأويل قوله تعالى { ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa reads the junub traveler passing through as a traveler without water, who performs dry ablution and prays.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: المراد بقوله تعالى { ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل } المسافر إذا لم يجد الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r3.speaker: طائفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r3.claim: Another group takes the wording to include both prayer and its place, since people then went to the mosque only for prayer and prayed only in congregation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r3.anchor: وقالت طائفة: المراد الموضع والصلاة معا لأنهم كانوا حينئذ لا يأتون المسجد إلا للصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r4.claim: 'While you are intoxicated' is a subject-predicate clause functioning circumstantially with 'do not approach'; سكارى is a plural of سكران, like كسالى from كسلان.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r4.anchor: } ابتداء وخبر، جملة في موضع الحال من «تقربوا»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r5.speaker: النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r5.claim: Al-Nakha'i reads سكرى with an open sin on the pattern فعلى, a broken plural of سكران, by analogy with صرعى because intoxication is an affliction of the mind.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ النخعي «سكرى» بفتح السين على مثال فعلى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r6.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r6.claim: Al-A'mash reads سكرى like حبلى as a singular adjective, which may describe a plural group.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «سكرى» كحبلى فهو صفة مفردة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r7.claim: Intoxication is the opposite of sobriety; the verb means to become intoxicated, an eye can become bewildered, and a crack can be blocked. The drunk person is cut off from his former reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r7.anchor: والسكر: نقيض الصحو يقال: سكر يسكر سكرا، من باب حمد يحمد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the verse plainly shows drinking was permitted in early Islam until it brought the drinker to intoxication.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r8.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل بل نص على أن الشرب كان مباحا في أول الإسلام حتى ينتهي بصاحبه إلى السكر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r9.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r9.claim: Some say intoxication is rationally forbidden and was never permitted by any religion, so they interpret the verse's intoxication as sleep.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: السكر محرم في العقل وما أبيح في شيء من الأديان وحملوا السكر في هذه الآية على النوم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r10.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r10.claim: Al-Qaffal suggests that the permitted drink may have been only enough to stir generosity, bravery, and spirited honor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r10.anchor: وقال القفال: يحتمل أنه كان أبيح لهم من الشراب ما يحرك الطبع إلى السخاء والشجاعة والحمية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r11.speaker: حسان
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r11.claim: Hassan's line 'we drink it and it makes us kings' is cited as poetic evidence for the drink's association with generosity and courage.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r11.anchor: وقد قال حسان: ونشربها فتتركنا ملوكا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r12.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r12.claim: Al-Qaffal says deliberately drinking enough to remove reason into insanity or unconsciousness was not permitted; if this happened unintentionally, the person is excused, a position al-Qurtubi affirms.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r12.anchor: قال القفال: فأما ما يزيل العقل حتى يصير صاحبه في حد الجنون والإغماء فما أبيح قصده

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r13.claim: After this verse, Muslims avoided drink at prayer times but drank after the night prayer until wine was prohibited in 5:91.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#3/r13.anchor: وكان المسلمون لما نزلت هذه الآية يجتنبون الشرب أوقات الصلوات، فإذا صلوا العشاء شربوها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r1.claim: The phrase means that the worshipper must know what he says with certainty and without error.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r1.anchor: أي حتى تعلموه متيقنين فيه من غير غلط

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r2.claim: Uthman held that a drunk person's divorce does not take effect because the drunk person does not know what he says.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه: إن السكران لا يلزمه طلاقه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وطاوس وعطاء والقاسم وربيعة والليث وإسحاق وأبو ثور والمزني والطحاوي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r3.claim: These authorities hold that an intoxicated person's divorce is ineffective; al-Tahawi adopts this position.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وطاوس وعطاء والقاسم وربيعة، وهو قول الليث بن سعد وإسحاق وأبي ثور والمزني واختاره الطحاوي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r4.speaker: الطحاوي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r4.claim: Al-Tahawi argues that scholars agree a mentally impaired person's divorce is invalid, and the drunk is impaired like one afflicted by delusion; a person whose mind is lost through banj likewise has no effective divorce.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r4.anchor: وقال: أجمع العلماء على أن طلاق المعتوه لا يجوز، والسكران معتوه كالموسوس معتوه بالوسواس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r5.speaker: عمر ومعاوية وجماعة من التابعين وأبو حنيفة والثوري والأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r5.claim: Another group allows the drunkard's divorce: this is reported from Umar, Muawiya, and successors, and is the position of Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, and al-Awzai; al-Shafi'i differed within his school.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r5.anchor: وأجازت طائفة طلاقه وروي عن عمر بن الخطاب ومعاوية وجماعة من التابعين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r6.claim: Malik counts divorce and retaliatory liability for wounds or killing as effective for a drunk, but not marriage or sale.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r6.anchor: وألزمه مالك الطلاق والقود في الجراح والقتل، ولم يلزمه النكاح والبيع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa validates all a drunkard's acts and contracts as if sober, except that an apostasy does not dissolve his marriage as a discretionary exception.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: أفعال السكران وعقوده كلها ثابتة كأفعال الصاحي، إلا الردة فإنه إذا ارتد فإنه لا تبين منه امرأته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r8.speaker: أبو يوسف والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r8.claim: Abu Yusuf and al-Shafi'i consider the drunk apostate an apostate, although al-Shafi'i would not kill him or call on him to repent while intoxicated.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r8.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف: يكون مرتدا في حال سكره وهو قول الشافعي إلا أنه لا يقتله في حال سكره ولا يستتيبه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r9.speaker: المازري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r9.claim: Al-Maziri says a rare report among Malikis holds that the drunkard's divorce does not take effect.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r9.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو عبد الله المازري: وقد رويت عندنا رواية شاذة أنه لا يلزم طلاق السكران

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r10.speaker: محمد بن عبد الحكم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r10.claim: Ibn Abd al-Hakam says a drunkard's divorce and emancipation do not take effect.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r10.anchor: وقال محمد بن عبد الحكم: لا يلزمه طلاق ولا عتاق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r11.speaker: ابن شاس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r11.claim: Ibn Shas locates the disagreement in the muddled person who retains some reason; one wholly unable to distinguish heaven from earth or man from woman is unanimously treated as insane, except some say missed prayer remains due because intoxication was self-induced.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r11.anchor: ونزل الشيخ أبو الوليد الخلاف على المخلط الذي معه بقية من عقله إلا أنه لا يملك الاختلاط من نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r12.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r12.claim: Al-Thawri defines intoxication as mental derangement; a person who confuses his recitation and speaks without knowing what he says is flogged.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r12.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: حد السكر اختلال العقل فإذا استقرىء فخلط في قراءته وتكلم بما لا يعرف جلد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r13.speaker: أحمد ومالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r13.claim: Ahmad defines intoxication as a change from sound reason, and a similar view is related from Malik.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r13.anchor: وقال أحمد: إذا تغير عقله عن حال الصحة فهو سكران وحكي عن مالك نحوه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r14.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r14.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir takes confused recitation as evidence of intoxication; one who does not know what he says must avoid the mosque, has no valid prayer, and must make it up, while one who knows what he says is treated as sober if he prays.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r14.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: إذا خلط في قراءته فهو سكران استدلالا بقول الله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r15.claim: 'Nor while junub' is coordinated with the syntactically accusative clause 'until you know what you say': do not pray while in a state of major ritual impurity.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r15.anchor: عطف على موضع الجملة المنصوبة في قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r16.claim: The forms تجنبتم, أجنبتم, and جنبتم all convey becoming junub; junub is generally indeclinable for gender, number, and plurality as a verbal noun-like form, though variants exist.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r16.anchor: ويقال: تجنبتم وأجنبتم وجنبتم بمعنى. ولفظ الجنب لا يؤنث ولا يثنى ولا يجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r17.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r17.claim: Some readers pronounce the word in its shortened form جنب.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r17.anchor: وربما خففوه فقالوا: جنب وقد قرأه كذلك قوم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r18.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r18.claim: Al-Farra says one may say that a man became junub or ajnaba.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r18.anchor: وقال الفراء: يقال جنب الرجل وأجنب من الجنابة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r19.claim: Some Arabic usage pluralizes junub as أجناب, like عنق/أعناق and طنب/أطناب; those who use جانب for the singular say جناب in the plural, like راكب/ركاب.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r19.anchor: وقيل: يجمع الجنب في لغة على أجناب مثل عنق وأعناق، وطنب وأطناب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r20.claim: The root sense is distance: major emission leaves the person distant from the state required for prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#4/r20.anchor: والأصل البعد كأن الجنب بعد بخروج الماء الدافق عن حال الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r1.claim: In the cited poetic usage, junub means a stranger; janāba also denotes a man's intercourse with a woman.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r1.anchor: ورجل جنب: غريب. والجنابة مخالطة الرجل المرأة.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r2.speaker: الجمهور من الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r2.claim: The majority define a junub as one impure through emission or penetration of the circumcised parts.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r2.anchor: والجمهور من الأمة على أن الجنب هو غير الطاهر من إنزال أو مجاوزة ختان.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r3.speaker: بعض الصحابة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r3.claim: Some Companions held that ghusl is required only after emission, citing the report that water is due from water.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r3.anchor: وروي عن بعض الصحابة ألا غسل إلا من إنزال لقوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r4.claim: Ubayy reports that the Prophet instructed a man who had intercourse without emission to wash the affected area, perform ablution, and pray.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r4.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أنه قال: يا رسول الله، إذا جامع الرجل المرأة فلم ينزل؟

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r5.claim: Abu ʿAbd Allāh calls ghusl the safer ruling and says the contrary report was included because scholars differed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله: الغسل أحوط وذلك الآخر إنما بيناه لاختلافهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r6.speaker: أبو العلاء بن الشخير
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r6.claim: Ibn al-Shikhkhīr says the Prophet's reports abrogated one another, just as Qur'anic verses do.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r6.anchor: قال أبو العلاء بن الشخير كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينسخ حديثه بعضه بعضا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r7.claim: Abū Isḥāq considers the report excusing ghusl after intercourse without emission abrogated.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r8.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r8.claim: Al-Tirmidhī says the no-ghusl ruling applied in early Islam and was later abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r8.anchor: وقال الترمذي: كان هذا الحكم في أول الإسلام ثم نسخ.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r9.claim: The author aligns with the scholars of the community: ghusl becomes obligatory upon penetration of the circumcised parts, whether or not emission occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r9.anchor: قلت: على هذا جماعة العلماء من الصحابة والتابعين وفقهاء الأمصار، وأن الغسل يجب بنفس التقاء الختانين.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r10.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r10.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet ruled that ghusl is obligatory when the circumcised parts touch after intercourse.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r10.anchor: رواية عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا جلس بين شعبها الأربع ومس الختان الختان فقد وجب الغسل "

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r11.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet made ghusl obligatory after intercourse, with Muslim adding that this applies even without emission.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r11.anchor: من حديث أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا قعد بين شعبها الأربع ثم جهدها فقد وجب عليه الغسل "

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r12.speaker: ابن القصار
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r12.claim: Ibn al-Qaṣṣār says later generations of scholars agreed to follow the report about the two circumcised parts, ending the earlier disagreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r12.anchor: قال ابن القصار: وأجمع التابعون ومن بعدهم بعد خلاف من قبلهم على الأخذ بحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r13.speaker: القاضي عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r13.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ knows of no later adherents to the no-ghusl view except al-Aʿmash and, afterward, Dāwūd al-Iṣfahānī.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r13.anchor: قال القاضي عياض: لا نعلم أحدا قال به بعد خلاف الصحابة إلا ما حكي عن الأعمش ثم بعده داود الأصبهاني

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r14.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r14.claim: ʿUmar reportedly made people abandon the report that ghusl is required only when water is emitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r14.anchor: وقد روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه حمل الناس على ترك الأخذ بحديث:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets water-from-water as emission during a wet dream; without emission, even a dream of intercourse does not require ghusl, a rule the author says is undisputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r15.anchor: وتأوله ابن عباس على الاحتلام أي إنما يجب الاغتسال بالماء من إنزال الماء في الاحتلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r16.claim: The verb ʿabara describes crossing a road or river from one side to the other.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r16.anchor: يقال: عبرت الطريق أي قطعته من جانب إلى جانب.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r17.claim: ʿĀbir al-sabīl means a passerby or traveler on the road.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r17.anchor: وهذا عابر السبيل أي مار الطريق.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r18.claim: An ʿabr-asfār camel is one that repeatedly crosses deserts and hot midday terrain because it walks quickly.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#5/r18.anchor: وناقة عبر أسفار: لا تزال يسافر عليها ويقطع بها الفلاة والهاجرة لسرعة مشيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r1.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r1.claim: The poet's line depicts a swift camel traversing the heat, illustrating the travel sense of ʿabr.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r1.anchor: عيرانة سرح اليدين شملة عبر الهواجر كالهزف الخاضب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r2.claim: The expression ʿabara al-qawm means that the people died; the accompanying poem contrasts dying with surviving until death.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r2.anchor: وعبر القوم ماتوا. وأنشد: قضاء الله يغلب كل شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r3.claim: The poem means that if the people die they have peers, while if they survive they remain destined to die.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r3.anchor: يقول: إن متنا فلنا أقران، وإن بقينا فلا بد لنا من الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r4.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد والحكم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r4.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, and al-Ḥakam interpret the exception as referring to a traveler.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r4.anchor: فقال علي رضي الله عنه وابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد والحكم: عابر السبيل المسافر.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa applies the traveler interpretation: residents generally have water and must bathe, while a traveler without water may use tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r5.anchor: وهذا قول أبي حنيفة لأن الغالب في الماء لا يعدم في الحضر فالحاضر يغتسل لوجود الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r6.speaker: أصحاب الرأي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r6.claim: The adherents of raʾy allow a traveling junub to perform tayammum, enter a mosque to draw water from its spring, and leave with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r6.anchor: وقال أصحاب الرأي في الجنب المسافر يمر على مسجد فيه عين ماء يتيمم الصعيد ويدخل المسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r7.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r7.claim: A group permits a junub to enter a mosque, citing the Prophet's statement that a believer is not impure; Ibn al-Mundhir endorses this position.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وعكرمة والنخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿIkrima, and al-Nakhaʿī interpret the exception as someone passing through, as do ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, Mālik, and al-Shāfiʿī.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وابن مسعود وعكرمة والنخعي: عابر السبيل الخاطر المجتاز

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r9.speaker: الثوري وإسحاق بن راهويه
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r9.claim: Al-Thawrī and Isḥāq ibn Rāhwayh say a junub may cross a mosque only when necessary, after performing tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r9.anchor: هكذا قال الثوري وإسحاق بن راهويه.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r10.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r10.claim: Aḥmad and Isḥāq allow a junub to sit in the mosque after performing ablution, according to Ibn al-Mundhir.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r10.anchor: وقال أحمد وإسحاق في الجنب: إذا توضأ لا بأس أن يجلس في المسجد حكاه ابن المنذر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r11.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r11.claim: Some reports explain the verse by saying Ansar homes opened onto the mosque, so junub residents had to cross it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r11.anchor: وروى بعضهم في سبب الآية أن قوما من الأنصار كانت أبواب دورهم شارعة في المسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r12.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r12.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet ordered houses opening onto the mosque to be redirected, explaining that he permits neither a menstruating woman nor a junub to remain in it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#6/r12.anchor: عن جسرة بنت دجاجة قالت سمعت عائشة رضي الله عنها تقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r1.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim has the Prophet order that every small opening into the mosque be closed except Abū Bakr's.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r1.anchor: لا تبقين في المسجد خوخة إلا خوخة أبي بكر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r2.claim: The order blocked using the mosque as a passage; Abū Bakr's opening was excepted as an honor because he and the Prophet were usually together.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r2.anchor: فأمر صلى الله عليه وسلم بسد الأبواب لما كان يؤدي ذلك إلى اتخاذ المسجد طريقا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet allowed no one to pass through or sit in the mosque except ʿAlī.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r3.anchor: وقد روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لم يكن أذن لأحد أن يمر في المسجد ولا يجلس فيه إلا علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r4.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports the Prophet said that no Muslim should become junub in the mosque except the Prophet and ʿAlī.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r4.anchor: ورواه عطية العوفي عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r5.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r5.claim: The scholars suggest the Prophet's and ʿAlī's homes were within or attached to the mosque, with their doors opening into it, explaining their passage while junub.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r5.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وهذا يجوز أن يكون ذلك لأن بيت علي كان في المسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar points to the Prophet's house and ʿAlī's adjacent house, saying no other houses were in the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r6.anchor: ما رواه ابن شهاب عن سالم بن عبد الله قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r7.claim: The author offers a second explanation: the Prophet may have specially exempted himself and then ʿAlī, as he had other exclusive privileges.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك تخصيصا لهما وقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خص بأشياء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r8.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maymūn reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet ordered all doors closed except ʿAlī's.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#7/r8.anchor: وروى عمرو بن ميمون عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r1.claim: The author distinguishes the small windows or openings called khukhāt from ʿAlī's ordinary entrance door and Abū Bakr's opening.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r1.anchor: والخوخات كالكوى والمشاكي، وباب علي كان باب البيت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar's statement that only the Prophet's and ʿAlī's houses were in the mosque explains their household access.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r2.anchor: وقد فسر ابن عمر ذلك بقوله: ولم يكن في المسجد غيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r3.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār reports that some Companions who became junub performed ablution, then came to the mosque and conversed there.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r3.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار أنه قال: كان رجال من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تصيبهم الجنابة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r4.claim: Against the permissive report, the author argues that ablution does not remove major impurity and that a junub should not enter a mosque set apart for worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r4.anchor: أن الوضوء لا يرفع حدث الجنابة، وكل موضع وضع للعبادة وأكرم عن النجاسة الظاهرة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r5.claim: The author answers the comparison with minor impurity by saying it occurs often and cleansing it would cause hardship; the verse's crossing exception suffices.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r5.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: { ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل } ما يغني ويكفي.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r6.claim: If a junub may not remain in a mosque, the author argues a fortiori that he may neither touch the muṣḥaf nor recite there.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r6.anchor: وإذا كان لا يجوز له اللبث في المسجد فأحرى ألا يجوز له مس المصحف ولا القراءة فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r7.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r7.claim: The author's scholars generally prohibit a junub from reciting Qur'an, allowing only a few short verses for seeking protection.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r7.anchor: ويمنع الجنب عند علمائنا من قراءة القرآن غالبا إلا الآيات اليسيرة للتعوذ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar attributes to the Prophet a prohibition on any Qur'anic recitation by a junub or menstruating woman.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r8.anchor: لا يقرأ الجنب والحائض شيئا من القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r9.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r9.claim: ʿAlī reports that nothing kept the Prophet from reciting Qur'an except janāba; Shuʿba praised the report and the author calls its chain sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#8/r9.anchor: عن علي قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يحجبه عن قراءة القرآن شيء إلا أن يكون جنبا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r1.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa says the Prophet forbade reciting Qur'an while junub.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس عن عبد الله بن رواحة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى أن يقرأ أحدنا القرآن وهو جنب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r2.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r2.claim: ʿIkrima recounts Ibn Rawāḥa's wife finding him with a slave girl; he recites verses to show he is not junub, she trusts God over her sight, and the Prophet later smiles at the story.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r2.anchor: وروى عن عكرمة قال: كان ابن رواحة مضطجعا إلى جنب امرأته فقام إلى جارية له في ناحية الحجرة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r3.claim: The poem attributed to Ibn Rawāḥa praises the Prophet as a messenger reciting scripture and bringing guidance in which believers trust.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r3.anchor: أتانا رسول الله يتلو كتابه كما لاح مشهور من الفجر ساطع أتى بالهدى بعد العمى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r4.claim: Ghusl in Arabic involves passing the hand with water over what is washed; Arabic distinguishes washing cloth from merely pouring or immersing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r4.anchor: يعبر به عن إمرار اليد مع الماء على المغسول ولذلك فرقت العرب بين قولهم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r5.claim: The well-known Mālikī position and al-Muzanī require a junub to rub the body while washing, by analogy with rubbing the face and hands in ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r5.anchor: المشهور من مذهب مالك أنه لا يجزئه حتى يتدلك لأن الله سبحانه وتعالى أمر الجنب بالاغتسال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r6.speaker: أبو الفرج عمرو بن محمد المالكي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r6.claim: Abū al-Faraj argues that ghusl linguistically denotes active washing; one who only pours or immerses water is called a pourer or immersed person, not a washer.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#9/r6.anchor: قال أبو الفرج عمرو بن محمد المالكي: وهذا هو المعقول من لفظ الغسل لأن الاغتسال في اللغة هو الافتعال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r1.speaker: أبو الفرج عمرو بن محمد المالكي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r1.claim: Abū al-Faraj cites a report that water must reach beneath every hair and the skin be thoroughly cleaned, which he takes to support rubbing.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r1.anchor: قال: وإنقاؤه والله أعلم لا يكون إلا بتتبعه على حد ما ذكرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r2.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna instead interprets cleaning the skin as washing and cleaning the genitals, not rubbing the whole body.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r2.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة: المراد بقوله عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r3.speaker: أبو داود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r3.claim: Abū Dāwūd grades the report about janāba under every hair weak; al-Ḥārith ibn Wajīh is weak and his reports are rejected, so the author rejects it as proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r3.anchor: الثاني أن الحديث أخرجه أبو داود في سننه وقال فيه: وهذا الحديث ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r4.speaker: عائشة وأم قيس بنت محصن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r4.claim: Muslim records from ʿĀʾisha and Umm Qays that the Prophet poured water on a child after it urinated without rubbing, an analogy supporting sufficiency of pouring.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r4.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتي بصبي فبال عليه، فدعا بماء فأتبعه بوله ولم يغسله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r5.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r5.claim: The majority hold that complete water coverage by pouring or immersion suffices for ghusl, without rubbing, based on reports describing the Prophet's bath.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r5.anchor: وقال الجمهور من العلماء وجماعة الفقهاء: يجزىء الجنب صب الماء والانغماس فيه إذا أسبغ وعم وإن لم يتدلك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r6.speaker: محمد بن عبد الحكم وأبو الفرج
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam holds that pouring suffices; Abū al-Faraj later returned to this position and transmitted it from Mālik.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r6.anchor: وبه قال محمد بن عبد الحكم، وإليه رجع أبو الفرج ورواه عن مالك قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r7.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī criticizes Abū al-Faraj, saying Mālik never expressly or by inference held that ghusl without rubbing sufficed and that this was Abū al-Faraj's error.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r7.anchor: وقال ابن العربي: وأعجب لأبي الفرج الذي روى وحكى عن صاحب المذهب أن الغسل دون ذلك يجزىء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r8.speaker: مروان بن محمد الظاهري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r8.claim: Marwān ibn Muḥammad al-Ẓāhirī, described as trustworthy, says Mālik ruled valid a junub's prayer after immersion without ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r8.anchor: قد روي هذا عن مالك نصا قال مروان بن محمد الظاهري وهو ثقة من ثقات الشاميين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r9.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r9.claim: Abū ʿUmar says the Mālik report explicitly validates immersion without rubbing or ablution, while the well-known Mālikī position requires rubbing by analogy with ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r9.anchor: قال أبو عمر: فهذه الرواية فيها لم يتدلك ولا توضأ، وقد أجزأه عند مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r10.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r10.claim: Abū ʿUmar argues that Arabic can call either rubbing with water or pouring water a washing; ablution and ghusl may therefore be independent forms, not analogized to each other.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#10/r10.anchor: وغير نكير أن يكون الغسل في لسان العرب مرة بالعرك ومرة بالصب والإفاضة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r1.speaker: ابن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr says the report of Ibn ʿAbbās washing his hands and genitals seven times is countered by the reports of ʿĀʾisha and Maymūna.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r1.anchor: حديث ميمونة وعائشة يرد ما رواه شعبة مولى ابن عباس عن ابن عباس أنه كان إذا اغتسل من الجنابة غسل يديه سبعا وفرجه سبعا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r2.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar says prayer was reduced from fifty to five, ghusl from seven washes to one, and washing urine from clothing likewise to one; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr calls its chain weak and notes Shuʿba is not strong.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r2.anchor: وقد روى عن ابن عمر قال: كانت الصلاة خمسين، والغسل من الجنابة سبع مرار، وغسل البول من الثوب سبع مرار

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r3.speaker: سحنون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r3.claim: Saḥnūn says someone unable to rub their own body should have another person do it or use a cloth.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r3.anchor: قال سحنون: يجعل من يلي ذلك منه، أو يعالجه بخرقة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r4.speaker: الواضحة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r4.claim: Al-Wāḍiḥa says to rub the accessible parts of the body, then pour water over the rest until all of it is covered.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r4.anchor: وفي الواضحة: يمر يديه على ما يدركه من جسده، ثم يفيض الماء حتى يعم ما لم تبلغه يداه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r5.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qāsim transmits Mālik's position that a junub need not work water through the beard.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r5.anchor: فروى ابن القاسم عنه أنه قال: ليس عليه ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r6.speaker: أشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r6.claim: Ashhab transmits the contrary position from Mālik: a junub must work water through the beard.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r6.anchor: وروى أشهب عنه أن عليه ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r7.speaker: ابن عبد الحكم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam prefers working water through the beard because the Prophet worked water through his hair; the author reasons that the skin beneath the beard is part of the body to be washed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r7.anchor: قال ابن عبد الحكم: ذلك هو أحب إلينا لأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخلل شعره في غسل الجنابة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r8.claim: The author says lighter ablution rules, such as wiping over footwear, do not transfer to ghusl, which requires water to reach the entire body.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r8.anchor: وإنما انتقل الفرض إلى الشعر في الطهارة الصغرى لأنها مبنية على التخفيف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and others require rinsing the mouth and nose in ghusl because both are part of the face; omission requires repeating prayer, though omission in ablution does not.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r9.anchor: منهم أبو حنيفة ولأنهما من جملة الوجه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r10.claim: Mālik, al-Ṭabarī, al-Layth, al-Awzāʿī, and others do not require mouth or nose rinsing in ghusl or ablution because these are internal parts.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r10.anchor: وقال مالك: ليستا بفرض لا في الجنابة ولا في الوضوء لأنهما باطنان فلا يجب كداخل الجسد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r11.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وحماد بن أبي سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r11.claim: Ibn Abī Laylā, Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān, Isḥāq, Aḥmad, some of Dāwūd's companions, and reports from al-Zuhrī and ʿAṭāʾ require both rinses in both ghusl and ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r11.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى وحماد بن أبي سليمان: هما فرض في الوضوء والغسل جميعا وهو قول إسحاق وأحمد بن حنبل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r12.speaker: أحمد وبعض أصحاب داود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r12.claim: Another report from Aḥmad makes mouth rinsing recommended but nose rinsing obligatory, a position also held by some of Dāwūd's companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#11/r12.anchor: وروي عن أحمد أيضا أن المضمضة سنة والاستنشاق فرض وقال به بعض أصحاب داود

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r1.speaker: من لم يوجبهما
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r1.claim: Those who do not require the rinses argue that scripture and the Prophet do not command them and there is no consensus; obligations require such proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r1.anchor: وحجة من لم يوجبهما أن الله سبحانه لم يذكرهما في كتابه،

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r2.speaker: من أوجبهما
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r2.claim: Those who require the rinses cite this verse and the command to wash faces, adding that the Prophet never omitted them in ablution or ghusl.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r2.anchor: احتج من أوجبهما بالآية، وقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r3.speaker: من فرق بينهما
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r3.claim: Those who distinguish the two say the Prophet performed mouth rinsing without commanding it, but both performed and commanded nose rinsing, whose command signifies obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r3.anchor: احتج من فرق بينهما بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل المضمضة ولم يأمر بها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r4.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r4.claim: The author's scholars require intention for ghusl, as do Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Abū Thawr; they also require it for ablution and tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r4.anchor: قال علماؤنا: ولا بد في غسل الجنابة من النية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r5.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r5.claim: This group supports requiring intention with the command to worship sincerely in 98:5 and the Prophet's statement that actions depend on intentions.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r5.anchor: وعضدوا هذا بقوله تعالى: ومآ أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r6.speaker: الأوزاعي والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r6.claim: Al-Awzāʿī and al-Ḥasan say ablution and tayammum are valid without intention.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r6.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي والحسن: يجزىء الوضوء والتيمم بغير نية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions require intention for tayammum but not water purification, by analogy with removing physical impurity without intention; al-Walīd transmits this from Mālik.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: كل طهارة بالماء فإنها تجزىء بغير نية، ولا يجزىء التيمم إلا بنية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r8.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r8.claim: Mālik reports from ʿĀʾisha that the Prophet bathed from a vessel called a farq; its rāʾ may be vocalized or vowelless.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r8.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كان يغتسل من إناء هو الفرق من الجنابة.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r9.speaker: ابن وهب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r9.claim: Ibn Wahb defines a farq as a wooden measure; Ibn Shihāb said it held five Umayyad measures called qisṭs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r9.anchor: قال ابن وهب: «الفرق» مكيال من الخشب،

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r10.speaker: محمد بن عيسى الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r10.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Aʿshā says a farq equals three ṣāʿs, or five qisṭs and twelve Prophetic mudd measures; Sufyān likewise says it is three ṣāʿs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r10.anchor: وقد فسر محمد بن عيسى الأعشى «الفرق» فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r11.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r11.claim: Anas reports the Prophet used one mudd for ablution and one ṣāʿ to five mudds for ghusl; another version gives five makākīk for ghusl and one for ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r11.anchor: وعن أنس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضأ بالمد ويغتسل بالصاع إلى خمسة أمداد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r12.claim: These reports recommend using only the water needed, without fixed measure; excess is wasteful and blameworthy, while the author calls the Ibāḍī practice of using much water satanic.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r12.anchor: وهذه الأحاديث تدل على استحباب تقليل الماء من غير كيل ولا وزن،

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r13.claim: One account says the tayammum verse was revealed for the wounded and junub ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, then its permission became general.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#12/r13.anchor: هذه آية التيمم، نزلت في عبد الرحمن ابن عوف أصابته جنابة وهو جريح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r1.claim: A second account places the revelation at al-Muraysīʿ, when the Companions lacked water after ʿĀʾisha's necklace was lost; Mālik transmits it from her through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim and his father.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r1.anchor: أخرج الحديث مالك من رواية عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن أبيه عن عائشة.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r2.claim: Al-Bukhārī's report says a necklace belonging to Asmāʾ was lost; the Prophet sent men to find it, prayer came without water or ablution, and the tayammum verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r2.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: هلكت قلادة لأسماء فبعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في طلبها رجالا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r3.claim: The author notes that al-Bukhārī gives no location and names Asmāʾ as owner, unlike Mālik's account naming ʿĀʾisha.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r3.anchor: قلت: وهذه الرواية ليس فيها ذكر للموضع، وفيها أن القلادة كانت لأسماء خلاف حديث مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r4.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r4.claim: Al-Nasāʾī reports that ʿĀʾisha borrowed Asmāʾ's necklace, which slipped from her during travel at al-Ṣalṣal.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r4.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أنها استعارت من أسماء قلادة لها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r5.claim: The al-Nasāʾī account explains Mālik's attribution to ʿĀʾisha and al-Bukhārī's attribution to Asmāʾ: ʿĀʾisha was the borrower.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r5.anchor: ففي هذه الرواية عن هشام أن القلادة كانت لأسماء، وأن عائشة استعارتها من أسماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r6.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r6.claim: Al-Tirmidhī's report says the necklace fell at al-Abwāʾ and the Prophet sent two men to search for it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أنها سقطت قلادتها ليلة الأبواء، فأرسل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلين في طلبها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r7.claim: The author reads al-Tirmidhī's attribution of the necklace to ʿĀʾisha as naming the borrower; its al-Abwāʾ location agrees with Mālik's report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r7.anchor: ففي هذه الرواية عن هشام أيضا إضافة القلادة إليها، لكن إضافة مستعير بدليل حديث النسائي.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r8.claim: The differences in necklace ownership and location do not weaken the reports because the point is the revelation of tayammum, and the necklace reports are established.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r8.anchor: وهذا كله صحيح المعنى، وليس اختلاف النقلة في العقد والقلادة ولا في الموضع ما يقدح في الحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r9.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r9.claim: One of the two searchers was reportedly Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr; they may explain al-Bukhārī's plural wording, or others may have joined them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r9.anchor: قيل: أحدهما أسيد بن حضير. ولعلهما المراد بالرجال في حديث البخاري

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r10.claim: The searchers found nothing on their route, but when they returned and raised the camel, they found the necklace beneath it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r10.anchor: فبعثوا في طلبها فطلبوا فلم يجدوا شيئا في وجهتهم، فلما رجعوا أثاروا البعير فوجدوه تحته.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r11.speaker: أصحاب رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r11.claim: Another report says wounded Companions later suffered janāba and complained to the Prophet, whereupon the verse was revealed; the author sees no conflict with the necklace account.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#13/r11.anchor: وقد روي أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أصابتهم جراحة ففشت فيهم ثم ابتلوا بالجنابة فشكوا ذلك لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزلت هذه الآية

QASHANI:4:42-43/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r4.claim: The address is to those with intellectual faith; a believer with direct faith would not be heedless in prayer.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r4.anchor: بالإيمان العلمي، فإن المؤمن بالإيمان العيني لا يكون في صلاته غافلا

QASHANI:4:42-43/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r5.claim: Prayer means the station of presence and intimate conversation with God.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r5.anchor: لا تقربوا مقام الحضور والمناجاة مع الله في حال كونكم

QASHANI:4:42-43/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r6.claim: Drunkenness means sleep of heedlessness or intoxication with caprice and love of the world.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r6.anchor: من نوم الغفلة، أو من خمور الهوى ومحبة الدنيا

QASHANI:4:42-43/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r7.claim: Before praying, know what you say and keep the heart from worldly occupations and distracting whispers.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r7.anchor: ولا تشتغل قلوبكم بأشغال الدنيا ووساوسها فتذهلوا عنه

QASHANI:4:42-43/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r8.claim: Sexual impurity means distance from truth through attachment to the soul and its pleasures; passing through means meeting only necessary needs, not being wholly absorbed in them.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r8.anchor: بعداء عن الحق بشدة الميل إلى النفس ومباشرة لذاتها وشهواتها

QASHANI:4:42-43/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r9.claim: Passing through worldly pleasures is limited to necessity and benefit, such as food, clothing, and procreation, to avoid being imprinted by total absorption.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r9.anchor: أي: مارين عليها، سالكي طريق من طرق تمتعاتها بقدر الضرورة

QASHANI:4:42-43/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r10.claim: Washing means cleansing attachment to the lower realm through repentance, seeking forgiveness, and regret.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r10.anchor: أي: تتطهروا عن تلك الهيئة الحاصلة من الانجذاب إلى الجهة السفلية

QASHANI:4:42-43/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r11.claim: Illness is false belief and deadly vice of the heart; travel is wandering in ignorance and confusion while greed seeks selfish pleasure and impure substance.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r11.anchor: القلوب، فاقدي سلامتها بأمراض العقائد الفاسدة والرذائل المهلكة

QASHANI:4:42-43/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r12.claim: Travel signifies wandering in ignorance and confusion to seek the soul's pleasure and impure matter through greed.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r12.anchor: في تيه الجهل والحيرة لطلب لذة النفس ومادة الرجس بالحرص

QASHANI:4:42-43/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r13.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r13.claim: Coming from the privy signifies engaging in tainted wealth and acquisition, with a lasting imprint of love and inclination.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r13.anchor: من الاشتغال بلوث المال وكسب الحطام ملوثا بهيئة محبته وميله

QASHANI:4:42-43/r14.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r14.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r14.claim: Touching women signifies attachment to souls and direct engagement in their pleasures and desires.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r14.anchor: لازمتم النفوس وباشرتموها في لذاتها وشهواتها

QASHANI:4:42-43/r15.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r15.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r15.claim: Lacking water means lacking knowledge that guides release from these states and purifies from them.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r15.anchor: علما يهديكم إلى التفصي منها ويهذبكم بالتطهر عنها

QASHANI:4:42-43/r16.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r16.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r16.claim: Tayammum means turning toward pure preparedness and returning to the original innate disposition.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r16.anchor: فتوجهوا صعيد استعدادكم الطيب، واقصدوه وارجعوا إلى أصل الاستعداد الفطري

QASHANI:4:42-43/r17.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r17.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r17.claim: Wiping means erasing acquired lower dispositions from the self and its descended attributes; the soil removes their traces and restores purity.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r17.anchor: أي: ذواتكم الموجودة وصفاتكم بالنزول ومحو هيئات العلق بها

QASHANI:4:42-43/r18.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r18.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r18.claim: God's pardon removes dark, entrenched dispositions when abandoned, clearing preparedness for encounter; His forgiveness veils creatures' attributes and essences with His own.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r18.anchor: يعفو عن تلك الهيئات المظلمة ورسوخ تلك الملكات الحاجبة بتركها والإعراض عنها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r1.claim: The necklace loss occurred during the Banu al-Mustaliq raid, the same expedition also called al-Muraysiʿ.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r1.anchor: إن ضياع العقد كان في غزاة بني المصطلق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r2.claim: Khalifa b. Khayyat and Abu ʿUmar date the raid to Shaʿban 6 AH; Abu Dharr or Namilah b. ʿAbd Allah is named as Medina's acting governor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r2.anchor: خليفة بن خياط وأبو عمر بن عبد البر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r3.claim: The Prophet surprised Banu al-Mustaliq at al-Muraysiʿ while they were unaware, taking captives; their battle cry was Amit amit.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r3.anchor: وأغار رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على بني المصطلق وهم غارون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r4.claim: Another account says Banu al-Mustaliq had assembled to attack the Prophet, who went out to meet them after hearing of it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r4.anchor: إن بني المصطلق جمعوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأرادوه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi identifies this expedition account as the occasion that initiated the tayammum dispensation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r5.anchor: فهذا ما جاء في بدء التيمم والسبب فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r6.claim: Some identify the tayammum verse as the one in al-Maʾida; Abu ʿUmar allows either al-Maʾida's ablution verse or this verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r7.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r7.claim: Abu ʿUmar says tayammum occurs only in the two Medinan verses in al-Maʾida and al-Nisaʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r7.anchor: ليس التيمم مذكورا في غير هاتين الآيتين وهما مدنيتان

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r8.claim: Illness is the body's departure from its ordinary, balanced condition; it may be severe or slight.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r8.anchor: المرض عبارة عن خروج البدن عن حد الاعتدال والاعتياد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r9.speaker: الحسن وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r9.claim: Severe illness that risks death from water or loss of a limb permits tayammum by consensus; al-Hasan and ʿAtaʾ dissent, but al-Qurtubi rejects their view by the no-hardship and no-self-killing verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r9.anchor: فهذا يتيمم بإجماع إلا ما روي عن الحسن وعطاء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says a wounded, sore-covered, or smallpox patient in janaba who fears dying from bathing may perform tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r10.anchor: إذا كانت بالرجل الجراحة في سبيل الله أو القروح أو الجدري

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r11.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the sick person was granted permission to use clean earth for tayammum.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r12.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r12.claim: ʿAmr b. al-ʿAs performed tayammum when severe cold made bathing dangerous, and the Prophet did not order him to wash or repeat.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r12.anchor: وتيمم عمرو بن العاص لما خاف أن يهلك من شدة البرد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r13.claim: Within the Maliki school, even less severe illness permits tayammum when water risks causing, worsening, or prolonging illness; Ibn ʿAtiyya says this is what he recalls as consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r13.anchor: فإن كان يسيرا إلا أنه يخاف معه حدوث علة أو زيادتها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r14.claim: Al-Baji reports that Qadi Abu al-Hasan and Abu Hanifa permit tayammum for a healthy person fearing a cold or fever, and for a patient fearing worsening illness.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r14.anchor: مثل أن يخاف الصحيح نزلة أو حمى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r15.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r15.claim: A stricter view attributed to al-Shafiʿi allows tayammum only when death is feared; Qadi Abu al-Hasan also reports this from Malik.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r15.anchor: لا يجوز له التيمم مع وجود الماء إلا أن يخاف التلف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r16.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r16.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi argues that worsening illness is uncertain, so it cannot justify abandoning the certain duty to use water.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#14/r16.anchor: قال الشافعي لا يباح التيمم للمريض إلا إذا خاف التلف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi answers that if fear of death from cold permits tayammum, fear of illness should also suffice, since both illness and death are harms.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r1.anchor: قد ناقضت فإنك قلت إذا خاف التلف من البرد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r2.speaker: أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r2.claim: Al-Qushayri gives the sound Shafiʿi position: fear of death or losing a limb permits tayammum, and the sound view also permits it to avoid prolonged illness.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r2.anchor: والمرض الذي يباح له التيمم هو الذي يخاف فيه فوت الروح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r3.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r3.claim: In the cold Dhat al-Salasil campaign, ʿAmr b. al-ʿAs feared bathing would kill him, used tayammum, and led dawn prayer while junub; the Prophet laughed after hearing his reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r3.anchor: احتلمت في ليلة باردة في غزوة ذات السلاسل فأشفقت إن اغتسلت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r4.claim: The report shows fear, not certainty, suffices; it calls a person who tayammums junub and supports his leading worshippers with ablution, which al-Qurtubi prefers among two Maliki views.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r4.anchor: فدل هذا الحديث على إباحة التيمم مع الخوف لا مع اليقين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r5.claim: The other Maliki view bars a tayammum imam from leading people with ablution because the imam should have the higher ritual rank.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني أنه لا يصلي لأنه أنقص فضيلة من المتوضىء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r6.claim: A report from Jabir says a tayammum imam must not lead worshippers who have ablution; al-Daraqutni grades its chain weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r6.anchor: روى الدارقطني من حديث جابر بن عبد الله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r7.speaker: جابر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r7.claim: Jabir recounts that a companion with a head wound and janaba was told to bathe, died, and the Prophet blamed those who failed to tell him to tayammum and bind the wound, wipe over it, and wash the rest.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#15/r7.anchor: فأصاب رجلا منا حجر فشجه في رأسه ثم احتلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r1.speaker: الدارقطني
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r1.claim: Al-Daraqutni says the Jabir wound report is weak through al-Zubayr b. Khurayq; al-Awzaʿi's Ibn ʿAbbas route is the sounder version, while another route is mursal. Ibn Abi Hatim records a musnad route.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r1.anchor: لم يروه عن عطاء عن جابر غير الزبير بن خريق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r2.speaker: داود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r2.claim: Dawud reads the term sick literally: anyone who can be called ill may use tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r2.anchor: كل من انطلق عليه اسم المريض فجائز له التيمم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya calls Dawud's view an outlier; scholars mean illness harmed by water, such as smallpox or fever, as in Ibn ʿAbbas's report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r3.anchor: إنما هو عند علماء الأمة لمن خاف من استعمال الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r4.claim: When water is unavailable, tayammum is allowed on a journey of any length under Malik and most scholars; requiring a prayer-shortening or devotional journey is weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r4.anchor: يجوز التيمم بسبب السفر طال أو قصر عند عدم الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r5.claim: Scholars agree tayammum is allowed while travelling, but disagree about residence: Malik, his followers, Abu Hanifa, and Muhammad allow it there too.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r5.anchor: أجمع العلماء على جواز التيمم في السفر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r6.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and al-Tabari bar tayammum for a healthy resident except when death is feared; they, al-Layth, and al-Tabari require prayer repetition when resident water is absent and time is feared.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r6.anchor: لا يجوز للحاضر الصحيح أن يتيمم إلا أن يخاف التلف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r7.speaker: أبو يوسف وزفر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r7.claim: Abu Yusuf and Zufar prohibit tayammum for residents, whether the reason is illness or fear that prayer time will end.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r7.anchor: لا يجوز التيمم في الحضر لا لمرض ولا لخوف الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r8.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r8.claim: Malik treats illness and travel as the usual cases where water is absent: residents and healthy people may analogically use tayammum if water is unavailable, obstructed, or time would pass.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r8.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى المرضى والمسافرين في شرط التيمم خرج على الأغلب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r9.claim: Those who exclude healthy residents argue that the text conditioned this concession on illness or travel, like fasting exemption and shortened prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r9.anchor: إن الله تعالى جعل التيمم رخصة للمريض والمسافر كالفطر وقصر الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿAtaʾ say the explicit condition of finding no water bars everyone from tayammum when water is available; Abu ʿUmar says this would be sound without the majority view and transmitted reports.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#16/r10.anchor: إنما شرطه الله تعالى مع عدم الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r1.claim: Since the Prophet allowed travelling ʿAmr to use tayammum when bathing risked death, a sick person is even more entitled to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r1.anchor: وقد أجاز رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التيمم لعمرو بن العاص

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r2.speaker: أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r2.claim: Al-Qushayri reads the toilet clause as covering a resident who lacks water, and says the rare residential case raises disagreement about repeating the prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r2.anchor: يعني المقيم إذا عدم الماء تيمم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r3.claim: For a resident who tayammums, the famous and correct Maliki view does not require repeating once water is found; Ibn Habib and Muhammad b. ʿAbd al-Hakam require repetition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r3.anchor: المشهور من مذهب مالك أنه لا يعيد وهو الصحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r4.speaker: أبو الجهيم بن الحارث بن الصمة الأنصاري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r4.claim: Abu al-Juhaym reports that the Prophet delayed answering a man's greeting until he wiped his face and hands on a wall; another route says he lacked ritual purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r4.anchor: عن أبي الجهيم بن الحارث بن الصمة الأنصاري

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r5.claim: Al-ghaʾit originally meant a hollow in the land; because people used secluded hollows to relieve themselves, the word came to denote human excretion.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r5.anchor: الغائط أصله ما انخفض من الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r6.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r6.claim: Al-Zuhri reads al-ghayt; al-Qurtubi says it may be a lightened form of al-ghayt or a y-for-waw reversal from al-ghawt.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r6.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: «من الغيط» فيحتمل أن يكون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r7.claim: One interpretation takes aw as wa, making the cause tayammum the minor event itself and supporting its use by residents.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r7.anchor: إن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر وجاء أحد منكم من الغائط

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers aw in its ordinary sense, with ellipsis: illness preventing water use, or travel with no water and a need for it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r8.anchor: أنها على بابها عند أهل النظر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r9.claim: Al-ghaʾit covers minor ablution nullifiers; the strongest Maliki classification groups them as loss of reason, customary discharge, and touching.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#17/r9.anchor: يجمع بالمعنى جميع الأحداث الناقضة للطهارة الصغرى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r1.claim: The Maliki nullifiers fall into three kinds; Hanafis count impure bodily emissions regardless of outlet but exclude touching.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r1.anchor: وعلى مذهب أبي حنيفة ما خرج من الجسد من النجاسات

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r2.speaker: الشافعي ومحمد بن عبد الحكم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r2.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and Muhammad b. ʿAbd al-Hakam count anything from either outlet, even if unusual, and include touching.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r2.anchor: وعلى مذهب الشافعي ومحمد بن عبد الحكم ما خرج من السبيلين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r3.claim: Muslims agree that fainting, insanity, and intoxication, as losses of reason, require ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r3.anchor: المسلمين أجمعوا على أن من زال عقله بإغماء أو جنون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r4.claim: Sleep has three positions: it is itself an invalidator, never an invalidator without another event, or a middle case based on its depth or posture.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في النوم هل هو حدث كسائر الأحداث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r5.speaker: المزني أبو إبراهيم إسماعيل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r5.claim: Al-Muzani treats any amount of sleep as an invalidator; this is implied by Malik's Muwatta wording and by the Safwan report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r5.anchor: ذهب المزني أبو إبراهيم إسماعيل إلى أنه حدث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r6.speaker: صفوان بن عسال المرادي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r6.claim: Safwan reports the Prophet allowed wiping over the khuffs after urine, stool, or sleep, removing them only for janaba; al-Qurtubi says al-Tirmidhi authenticated the report.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r7.claim: Proponents equate sleep with urine and stool because deep sleep overwhelms reason; they also cite Ali's general report that sleep loosens the anal tether and requires ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r7.anchor: والقياس أنه لما كان كثيره وما غلب على العقل منه حدثا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r8.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r8.claim: Abu Musa regarded sleep as no invalidator at all unless another event occurred; he would sleep under guard and pray on waking, as did ʿUbayda, Saʿid b. al-Musayyab, and al-Awzaʿi in one report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r8.anchor: فروي عن أبي موسى الأشعري ما يدل على أن النوم عنده ليس بحدث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r9.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r9.claim: Malik requires ablution after deep, prolonged sleep in any posture; al-Zuhri, Rabiʿa, and al-Awzaʿi in one narration agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r9.anchor: وطال نومه على أي حال كان

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r10.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r10.claim: Ahmad says light sleep does not matter if it neither penetrates nor overwhelms the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r10.anchor: فإن كان النوم خفيفا لا يخامر القلب ولا يغمره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r11.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions require ablution only for someone sleeping on a side or sitting with weight shifted.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r11.anchor: لا وضوء إلا على من نام مضطجعا أو متوركا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r12.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says sitting sleep does not invalidate ablution; Ibn Wahb also transmits this from Malik.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r12.anchor: من نام جالسا فلا وضوء عليه ورواه ابن وهب عن مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r13.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r13.claim: Al-Qurtubi considers Malik's well-known position the soundest of these views.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#18/r13.anchor: والصحيح من هذه الأقوال مشهور مذهب مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet delayed ʿIsha while worshippers repeatedly slept and woke, then said only they were waiting for prayer; al-Qurtubi calls it the strongest report by chain and practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شغل عنها ليلة يعني العشاء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi interprets Malik's and Safwan's references to sleep as heavy sleep that dominates the sleeper, in light of Ibn ʿUmar's report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r2.anchor: ونوم ثقيل غالب على النفس بدليل هذا الحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r3.speaker: وكيع
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r3.claim: Wakiʿ's Safwan route says or wind instead of or sleep; Daraqutni says no one else transmits that wording, and Wakiʿ is trustworthy, weakening the use of Safwan as proof that sleep itself invalidates ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r3.anchor: وكيع ثقة إمام أخرج له البخاري ومسلم وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r4.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet slept prostrating, then said only side-sleep relaxes the joints and requires ablution; al-Daraqutni, Abu Dawud, and Abu ʿUmar call it unsound or munkar.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r4.anchor: تفرد به أبو خالد عن قتادة ولا يصح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r5.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r5.claim: Al-Shafiʿi, al-Tabari, and Dawud require ablution after sleep in any position except sitting, which is unlikely to become deep; this is also reported from Ali, Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn ʿUmar.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r5.anchor: وأما قول الشافعي على كل نائم الوضوء إلا على الجالس وحده

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r6.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r6.claim: ʿAmr b. Shuʿayb transmits a prophetic report distinguishing sitting sleep, which does not require ablution, from lying on one's side, which does.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#19/r6.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r1.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r1.claim: The report says a person who sleeps sitting does not need ablution, but one who lies down does.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r1.anchor: من نام جالسا فلا وضوء عليه ومن وضع جنبه فعليه الوضوء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r2.claim: Bukhari reports that a wife of the Prophet in retreat saw blood and yellow discharge beneath her while praying; al-Qurtubi treats it as an abnormal, illness-related discharge.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r2.anchor: اعتكفت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم امرأة من أزواجه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r3.claim: Malik does not make this unusual outlet obligatorily invalidate ablution, unlike al-Shafiʿi; this supports Malik's distinction from the Hanafi rule based on impurity alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r3.anchor: وإنما هو عرق انقطع فهو مرض

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r4.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, and Ibn ʿAmir read lamastum; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read lamistum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r4.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r5.claim: The three reported meanings are intercourse, physical contact, or a word covering both; most readers treat the two readings as equivalent in sense.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r6.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r6.claim: Muhammad b. Yazid says lamastum more naturally means kissing or the like, since each party acts; lamistum means intercourse or touching, where the woman does not act.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن يزيد أنه قال الأولى في اللغة أن يكون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r7.speaker: عمر وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r7.claim: One view limits mulamasa to hand-touch and says a junub person is not covered by the illness clause, so he must bathe or wait for water; it is reported from ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿud.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r7.anchor: والجنب لا ذكر له إلا مع الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r8.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r8.claim: Abu ʿUmar says no leading jurist followed ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿud here, likely because reports from ʿAmmar, ʿImran b. Husayn, and Abu Dharr allow a junub person to tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r8.anchor: لم يقل بقول عمر وعبد الله في هذه المسألة أحد من فقهاء الأمصار

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa takes mulamasa to mean intercourse alone: a junub person may tayammum, but hand-touch and a pleasurable kiss do not invalidate ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#20/r9.anchor: الملامسة هنا مختصة باللمس الذي هو الجماع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r1.claim: Hanafis cite a Daraqutni report from ʿAisha that the Prophet kissed a wife and prayed without renewing ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل بعض نسائه ثم خرج إلى الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r2.claim: When ʿUrwa asked which wife the Prophet kissed, ʿAisha laughed, leaving open that she herself was the one.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r3.claim: Malik says intercourse calls for tayammum; hand-touch calls for ablution if pleasure is felt, while touch without desire does not, a view also held by Ahmad and Ishaq.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r4.speaker: علي بن زياد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r4.claim: Ali b. Ziyad says touching through a thick garment has no effect, but touching through a thin one requires ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r4.anchor: وإن كان عليها ثوب كثيف فلا شيء عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r5.speaker: عبد الملك بن الماجشون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r5.claim: Ibn al-Majishun requires ablution for intentionally touching one's wife by hand for play, whether or not pleasure follows.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r5.anchor: من تعمد مس امرأته بيده لملاعبة فليتوضأ التذ أو لم يلتذ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو الوليد الباجي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r6.claim: Al-Baji clarifies the Maliki rule: intending pleasure by touching requires ablution whether pleasure actually occurs or not.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r7.claim: Ibn Nafiʿ transmits from Malik that erection alone requires neither ablution nor washing the penis unless accompanied by touch or pre-seminal fluid; Abu Ishaq says erection alone breaks ablution, citing the Mudawwana.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r7.anchor: عن مالك أنه لا يوجب وضوءا ولا غسل ذكر حتى يكون معه لمس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r8.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r8.claim: Al-Shafiʿi requires ablution when any part of a man's body contacts a woman's body without a barrier, regardless of desire; this is also attributed to Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Zuhri, and Rabiʿa.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r8.anchor: إذا أفضى الرجل بشيء من بدنه إلى بدن المرأة سواء كان باليد
