QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r9.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r9.claim: Al-Awzaʿi says hand-touch invalidates ablution but other bodily contact does not, citing the verse about touching with their hands.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#21/r9.anchor: إذا كان اللمس باليد نقض الطهر وإن كان بغير اليد لم ينقضه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls the Maliki position strongest: touch short of intercourse invalidates ablution, as reported from ʿUmar, his son, and Ibn Masʿud and held by most jurists.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r1.anchor: فهذه خمسة مذاهب أسدها مذهب مالك وهو مروي عن عمر وابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says the verse assigns three clauses to three rulings: janaba, minor impurity, and touch or kissing; treating touch as intercourse would repeat the meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r3.speaker: الدارقطني
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r3.claim: The kiss report used by Abu Hanifa is mursal: Daraqutni notes that Habib b. Abi Thabit did not hear from ʿUrwa, as Yahya b. Saʿid says Sufyan al-Thawri maintained.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r3.anchor: حبيبا لم يسمع من عروة شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r4.claim: Although Malikis accept mursal reports in principle, al-Qurtubi rejects this one because the verse's apparent sense and the Companions' practice oppose it.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r5.claim: Against the claim that Ibn ʿAbbas interpreted mulamasa as intercourse, al-Qurtubi notes that ʿUmar, his son, and Ibn Masʿud opposed it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r5.anchor: قد خالفه الفاروق وابنه وتابعهما عبدالله بن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r6.claim: Although the reciprocal form mulamasa is said to require two actors, al-Qurtubi answers that both parties can be described as toucher and touched; Arabic also uses reciprocal verbs for one actor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r6.anchor: الملامسة مقتضاها التقاء البشرتين سواء كان ذلك من واحد أو من اثنين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r7.claim: The objection that the verse pairs the toilet event with janaba does not exclude touch: al-Qurtubi says the word can carry both touch and intercourse and convey both rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r7.anchor: لا نمنع حمل اللفظ على الجماع واللمس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r8.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r8.claim: Al-Shafiʿi's view that uncovered skin-contact with a woman breaks ablution follows the apparent wording, whether he touches her or she touches him.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r8.anchor: من لمس الرجل المرأة ببعض أعضائه لا حائل بينه وبينها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r9.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r9.claim: In al-Shafiʿi's view, touching hair, teeth, or nails does not break ablution; precaution favors ablution after touching hair.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#22/r9.anchor: وكذلك السن والظفر فإن ذلك مخالف للبشرة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r1.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi says it is good precaution to perform ablution after touching a woman's hair.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r1.anchor: ولو احتاط فتوضأ إذا مس شعرها كان حسنا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r2.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r2.claim: Touching through clothing does not break ablution even with pleasure; direct skin contact counts whether deliberate or forgetful and whether the unrelated woman is alive or dead.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r2.anchor: من فوق الثوب فالتذ بذلك أو لم يلتذ لم يكن عليهما شيء حتى يفضي إلى البشرة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r3.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi has two views on touching a young girl, elderly woman, or unmarriageable female: it breaks ablution under the verse's general wording, or does not because desire is irrelevant to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r3.anchor: إذا لمس صبية صغيرة أو عجوزا كبيرة بيده أو واحدة من ذوات محارمه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r4.speaker: المروزي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r4.claim: Al-Marwazi prefers the unrestricted Shafiʿi view because the verse does not condition touch on desire, as also reflected by Companions and most Successors.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r4.anchor: قول الشافعي أشبه بظاهر الكتاب لأن الله عز وجل قال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r5.speaker: المروزي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r5.claim: Al-Marwazi says only Malik and al-Layth require ablution when pleasure comes through clothing; al-Qurtubi adds that Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr also attributes this rule to Ishaq and Ahmad and reports it from other early authorities.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r5.anchor: من مراعاة الشهوة واللذة من فوق الثوب يوجب الوضوء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r6.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r6.claim: A sound report from ʿAisha says the Prophet nudged her feet when they lay before him during prayer; they had no lamps, and Bukhari records the report.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects the objection that the Prophet could not touch ʿAisha through clothing: the report expressly describes him as touching her, and the Sunnah specifies that touch without desire or intent does not invalidate ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r7.anchor: فكان واجبا لظاهر الآية انتقاض وضوء كل ملامس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says ghamz is pressing with the hand, like feeling a ram to test whether it is fat, not striking someone with a sleeve.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#23/r8.anchor: حقيقة الغمز إنما هو باليد ومنه غمزك الكبش أي تجسه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r1.claim: Aisha describes the Prophet moving her legs when he prostrated and her extending them again when he stood; Qurtubi treats this as direct contact without an intervening barrier.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r1.anchor: وقد جاء صريحا عنها قالت: «كنت أمد رجلي في قبلة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r2.claim: Aisha reports that while searching for the Prophet at night in the mosque, her hand touched the soles of his feet as he prayed in prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r2.anchor: وهو ما روته عائشة أيضا رضي الله عنها قالت: فقدت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة من الفراش

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r3.claim: The reports show that direct touch does not invalidate ablution for every person who touches; Qurtubi's rule distinguishes touch according to pleasure.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r3.anchor: كان دليلا على أن الوضوء لا ينتقض إلا على بعض الملامسين دون بعض

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r4.speaker: المزني
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r4.claim: Al-Muzani proposes that a barrier covered the Prophet's foot; Qurtubi rejects this because the default is direct contact unless a barrier is established.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r4.anchor: فإن قيل: كان على قدمه حائل كما قاله المزنى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r5.speaker: الخصم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r5.claim: An opponent argues by consensus that forced intercourse without pleasure still obligates ghusl, so any touching or kissing should break ablution regardless of desire.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r5.anchor: فإن قيل: فقد أجمعت الأمة على أن رجلا لو استكره امرأة فمس ختانه ختانها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r6.claim: Qurtubi says the alleged consensus is disputed because al-A'mash and others disagreed; even if granted, it begs the question, while sound reports support his position.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r6.anchor: قد ذكرنا أن الأعمش وغيره قد خالف فيما ادعيتموه من الإجماع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r7.claim: Qurtubi invokes the maxim to follow an authenticated report over one's own opinion, noting Malik, al-Shafi'i's teacher, was already known to say it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r7.anchor: وقد قال الشافعي فيما زعمتم إنه لم يسبق إليه، وقد سبقه إليه شيخه مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r8.claim: The claim that the mere act of touching invalidates ablution would also make a man lose ablution by slapping his wife to discipline her, an implication Qurtubi says no one accepts.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#24/r8.anchor: ويلزم على مذهبكم أن من ضرب امرأته فلطمها بيده تأديبا لها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r1.claim: The Prophet carried Umama, daughter of Zaynab, during prayer, setting her down for bowing and lifting her after prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r1.anchor: كان يصلي وأمامة بنت أبي العاص ابنة زينب بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على عاتقه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r2.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r2.claim: One Shafi'i opinion says touching even a little girl invalidates ablution based on the word “women”; Qurtubi rejects it, likening a child's touch to touching a wall.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r2.anchor: وهذا يرد ما قاله الشافعي في أحد قوليه: لو لمس صغيرة لانتقض طهره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r3.claim: Qurtubi says pleasure is the criterion: wherever pleasure occurs, the ruling of required ablution follows; he contrasts this with al-Shafi'i's treatment of unmarriageable kin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r3.anchor: واختلف قوله في ذوات المحارم لأجل أنه لا يعتبر اللذة، ونحن اعتبرنا اللذة فحيث وجدت وجد الحكم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r4.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r4.claim: Al-Awza'i limits legally relevant touch to the hand because that is the organ most commonly meant by the term; foot contact with a wife's private parts or belly would not invalidate ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r4.anchor: وأما قول الأوزاعي في اعتباره اليد خاصة فلأن اللمس أكثر ما يستعمل باليد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r5.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r5.claim: Al-Awza'i says he would advise a man who asks about kissing his wife to renew ablution, but would not blame him if he did not.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r5.anchor: وقال في الرجل يقبل امرأته: إن جاء يسألني قلت يتوضأ، وإن لم يتوضأ لم أعبه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r6.speaker: أبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r6.claim: Abu Thawr holds that kissing, intimate contact, or touching one's wife does not require ablution; Qurtubi associates this with the Hanafi school.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r6.anchor: وقال أبو ثور: لا وضوء على من قبل آمرأته أو باشرها أو لمسها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r7.claim: A traveler may tayammum if water is entirely or partly unavailable, or seeking it risks losing companions or baggage, encountering thieves or beasts, missing prayer time, or causing thirst to oneself or another; cooking necessary food also counts.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r7.anchor: الأسباب التي لا يجد المسافر معها الماء هي إما عدمه جملة أو عدم بعضه، وإما أن يخاف فوات الرفيق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r8.claim: Illness counts when no one can hand over water or its use is feared harmful; a healthy resident may also lack usable water through widespread exorbitant prices, imprisonment, or restraint.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r8.anchor: ويترتب عدمه للمريض بألا يجد من يناوله، أو يخاف من ضرره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says a person should buy water even by spending all his wealth and becoming destitute; Qurtubi calls this weak because religion is ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r9.anchor: قال الحسن: يشتري الرجل الماء بماله كله ويبقى عديما، وهذا ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r10.speaker: طائفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r10.claim: One group allows paying for water only up to a one-third increase over its ordinary price; another allows paying two or three times its value, positions Qurtubi says occur in Maliki law.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r10.anchor: وقالت طائفة: يشتريه ما لم يزد على القيمة الثلث فصاعدا. وقالت طائفة: يشتري قيمة الدرهم بالدرهمين والثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r11.speaker: أشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r11.claim: Ashhab says people should not be required to buy a water-skin for ten dirhams.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r11.anchor: وقيل لأشهب: أتشترى القربة بعشرة دراهم؟ فقال: ما أرى ذلك على الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r12.claim: Al-Shafi'i rejects paying an increased price for water.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r13.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r13.claim: Malik's apparent position, shared by al-Shafi'i, makes searching for water a condition for valid tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r13.anchor: فظاهر مذهب مالك أن ذلك شرط وهو قول الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r14.claim: Abu Hanifa and Qadi Abu Muhammad ibn Nasr hold that searching for water is not a condition of valid tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r14.anchor: وذهب القاضي أبومحمد بن نصر إلى أن ذلك ليس بشرط في صحة التيمم وهو قول أبي حنيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r15.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r15.claim: Ibn Umar reportedly would not leave his travel route to seek water even when it lay two bowshots away; Ishaq says one need search only where one is.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r15.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر أنه كان يكون في السفر على غلوتين من طريقه فلا يعدل إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r16.claim: Qurtubi prefers requiring a search: the verse's “not finding water” presupposes looking, and a substitute is usable only when inability to obtain the original is certain.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r16.anchor: والأول أصح وهو المشهور من مذهب مالك في الموطأ لقوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r17.claim: When water seems impossible to find during the prayer time, tayammum and prayer early are recommended so the worshipper secures the virtue of praying early.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r17.anchor: فالأول يستحب له التيمم والصلاة في أول الوقت لأنه إذا فاتته فضيلة الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r18.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r18.claim: When water is likely to appear, Malik's companions report delaying prayer to mid-time in hope of water, provided the delay does not forfeit the virtue of praying early.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#25/r18.anchor: الثاني يتيمم وسط الوقت حكاه أصحاب مالك عنه، فيؤخر الصلاة رجاء إدراك فضيلة الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r1.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r1.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says that someone who knows water will be available at the end of the time may pray with tayammum early, but must repeat within the time if water later appears.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r1.anchor: فقد قال ابن القاسم: يجزئه، فإن وجد الماء أعاد في الوقت خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r2.speaker: ابن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r2.claim: When the chances of finding water or not finding it are equal, delay prayer until the end of the chosen time because water's agreed virtue outweighs the disputed virtue of praying early; Ibn Habib identifies the endpoint.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r2.anchor: الثالث يؤخر الصلاة إلى أن يجد الماء في آخر الوقت لأن فضيلة الماء أعظم من فضيلة أول الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r3.speaker: عبد الملك بن الماجشون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r3.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Majishun says that if water is found later, the worshipper must repeat the prayer without time limitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الملك بن الماجشون: إن وجد الماء بعد أعاد أبدا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r4.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r4.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi'i in one opinion, and most scholars require enough water for the whole purification; less than the needed amount is treated as unavailable and is not used.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r4.anchor: والذي يراعى من وجود الماء أن يجد منه ما يكفيه لطهارته، فإن وجد أقل من كفايته تيمم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r5.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r5.claim: Al-Shafi'i's other opinion requires using the water at hand and then performing tayammum for the part left without water, since the person initially possessed water.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r5.anchor: وقال الشافعي في القول: الآخر: يستعمل ما معه من الماء ويتيمم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r6.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r6.claim: On forgetting water in one's baggage and using tayammum, al-Shafi'i's sounder view requires repeating because the water was present and the person was negligent; another view, also attributed to Malik, waives repetition if it was unknown.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r6.anchor: واختلف قول الشافعي أيضا فيما إذا نسي الماء في رحله فتيمم والصحيح أنه يعيد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa permits ablution with water whose qualities have changed, arguing that the indefinite “water” in the verse is linguistically general.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r7.anchor: وأجاز أبو حنيفة الوضوء بالماء المتغير لقوله تعالى: { فلم تجدوا مآء }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r8.claim: Qurtubi answers that the generality covers kinds within the genus of water, such as rain, rivers, springs, fresh, and salt water, not other liquids such as bean or rose water.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r8.anchor: ولكن في الجنس، فهو عام في كل ماء كان من سماء أو نهر أو عين عذب أو ملح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r9.claim: Scholars agree that only nabidh is even discussed as a substitute drink for water in ablution or ghusl, but the verse's command to tayammum rules that substitution out.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r9.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن الوضوء والاغتسال لا يجوز بشيء من الأشربة سوى النبيذ عند عدم الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r10.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r10.claim: The report that Ibn Mas'ud performed ablution with nabidh is not established because its narrator Abu Zayd is unknown and not known as a companion of Abdullah, according to Ibn al-Mundhir and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r10.anchor: والحديث الذي فيه ذكر الوضوء بالنبيذ رواه ابن مسعود، وليس بثابت لأن الذي رواه أبو زيد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r11.claim: The water whose absence permits tayammum is pure and purifying water that remains in its original qualities.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r11.anchor: الماء الذي يبيح عدمه التيمم هو الطاهر المطهر الباقي على أوصاف خلقته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r12.speaker: بعض من ألف في أحكام القرآن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r12.claim: A writer on Quranic rulings argues that because “water” is indefinite, tayammum is forbidden whenever any amount of water exists, mixed with other matter or alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#26/r12.anchor: وقال بعض من ألف في أحكام القرآن لما قال تعالى: { فلم تجدوا مآء فتيمموا }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r1.claim: The Kufans, including Abu Hanifa and his followers, argue that date nabidh counts as water and prevents tayammum; Qurtubi says their supporting reports are weak and treats the issue later in al-Furqan.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r1.anchor: ولا يمتنع أحد أن يقول في نبيذ التمر ماء فلما كان كذلك لم يجز التيمم مع وجوده

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r2.claim: The Prophet says the Muslim community was favored with three gifts, including making all earth a mosque and its soil a purifier; Qurtubi links the concession's revelation to the necklace incident.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r2.anchor: فضلنا على الناس بثلاث جعلت لنا الأرض كلها مسجدا وجعلت تربتها لنا طهورا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r3.claim: In Arabic, tayammum means intending or aiming: one aims at a thing or deliberately turns toward soil; usage later narrowed toward ritual wiping.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r3.anchor: التيمم لغة هو القصد. تيممت الشيء قصدته، وتيممت الصعيد تعمدته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r4.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r4.claim: Al-Khalil rejects replacing tayammam with ammam in the cited verse because shazran means obliquely, from the side, rather than straight ahead.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r4.anchor: قال الخليل: من قال في هذا البيت أممته فقد أخطأ لأنه قال «شزرا»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r5.claim: Imru al-Qays uses tayammam for heading toward a destination, in two poems about traveling toward a place and a spring.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r5.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: تيممتها من أذرعات وأهلها بيثرب أدنى دارها نظر عال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r6.speaker: آخر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses the verb for directing a camel toward another country when dissatisfied with the current land.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r6.anchor: آخر: إني كذاك إذا ما ساءني بلد يممت بعيري غيره بلدا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r7.speaker: أعشى باهلة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r7.claim: Al-A'sha of Bahila's verse uses tayammam for setting out toward Qays across difficult terrain.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r7.anchor: وقال أعشى باهلة: تيممت قيسا وكم دونه من الأرض من مهمه ذي شزن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r8.speaker: حميد بن ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r8.claim: Hamid ibn Thawr's verse uses the verb to ask where someone directed herself, illustrating its sense of intending or setting out.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r8.anchor: وقال حميد بن ثور: سل الربع أني يممت أم طارق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r9.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r9.claim: Al-Shafi'i's verse says that wherever he aims, he carries his knowledge with him, another witness for tayammum as intention.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r9.anchor: وللشافعي رضي الله عنه: علمي معي حيثما يممت أحمله بطني وعاء له لا بطن صندوق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r10.speaker: ابن السكيت
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r10.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit glosses the Quranic command as “aim” or “intend”; repeated usage then made the word denote wiping face and hands with soil.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r10.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: قوله تعالى: { فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا } أي اقصدوا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r11.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains saying a man has tayammama as having wiped soil on his face and hands; Qurtubi identifies this as ritual tayammum when done as worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#27/r11.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري في قولهم: «قد تيمم الرجل» معناه قد مسح التراب على وجهه ويديه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r1.claim: Two cited verses use mayammam for a person who directs himself toward a noble house, illustrating the word's sense of aiming or being directed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r1.anchor:
إنا وجدنا أعصر بن سعد
ميمم البيت رفيع المجد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r2.claim: The word tayammum occurs in al-Baqara, this sura, and al-Ma'ida; Qurtubi identifies the present verse as the tayammum verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r2.anchor: لفظ التيمم ذكره الله تعالى في كتابه في «البقرة» وفي هذه السورة و «المائدة»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi asks which of the two passages on tayammum Aisha meant when she said its verse was revealed, and observes that her report suggests the practice was previously unknown.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r3.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر ابن العربي: هذه معضلة ما وجدت لدائها من دواء عند أحد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r4.claim: Qurtubi answers that Aisha meant this verse in al-Nisa, and agrees that tayammum was not known or practiced before its revelation, as historical accounts attest.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r4.anchor: قلت: أما قوله: «فلا نعلم أية آية عنت عائشة» فهي هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r5.claim: Qurtubi says ghusl for major ritual impurity was not prescribed before ablution, while historians agree the Prophet used ablution for prayer in Mecca; thus the new ruling then revealed was tayammum, not ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r5.anchor: أنه معلوم عند جميع أهل السير أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم منذ افترضت عليه الصلاة بمكة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r6.claim: The wording “the tayammum verse was revealed,” rather than “the ablution verse,” shows that the newly taught rule was tayammum; the ablution obligation already existed and was now recited in revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r6.anchor: ولم يقل آية الوضوء ما يبين أن الذي طرأ لهم من العلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r7.claim: Tayammum is obligatory for every accountable person owing prayer when water is absent and prayer time has entered.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r7.anchor: التيمم يلزم كل مكلف لزمته الصلاة إذا عدم الماء ودخل وقت الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa, his two companions, and al-Muzani allow tayammum before the prayer time because searching for water is not a condition, analogizing to voluntary prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وصاحباه والمزني صاحب الشافعي: يجوز قبله لأن طلب الماء عندهم ليس بشرط

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r9.claim: The Prophet tells Abu Dharr that clean earth is a Muslim's purification even without water for ten years; the opposing jurists treat this as equating soil purification with water ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r9.anchor: الصعيد الطيب وضوء المسلم ولو لم يجد الماء عشر حجج

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r10.claim: Qurtubi argues that “not finding water” means one must first seek it, and tayammum is a necessity purification like that of a woman with continuous bleeding.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#28/r10.anchor: ودليلنا قوله تعالى: { فلم تجدوا مآء } ولا يقال: لم يجد الماء إلا لمن طلب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r1.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r1.claim: The rule to perform tayammum and pray wherever prayer catches a person is al-Shafi'i's and Ahmad's view, and is also reported from Ali, Ibn Umar, and Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r1.anchor: وهو قول الشافعي وأحمد، وهو مروي عن علي وابن عمر وابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r2.claim: Scholars agree that tayammum does not remove major or minor ritual impurity; finding water restores the person to the prior state, based on the Prophet's instruction to Abu Dharr to let water touch his skin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r2.anchor: وأجمع العلماء على أن التيمم لا يرفع الجنابة ولا الحدث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r3.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r3.claim: Abu Salama reportedly says a junub person who finds water after tayammum remains purified and needs neither ghusl nor ablution until a new occurrence.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r3.anchor: إلا شيء روي عن أبي سلمة بن عبدالرحمن، رواه ابن جريج وعبد الحميد بن جبير بن شيبة عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r4.speaker: ابن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r4.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr calls Abu Salama's reports contradictory and poorly considered, adding that Abu Salama was not as learned as his Medinan Successor peers.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r4.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر: وهذا تناقض وقلة روية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r5.claim: There is agreement that finding water before beginning prayer invalidates tayammum and requires using the water.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r5.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن من تيمم ثم وجد الماء قبل الدخول في الصلاة بطل تيممه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r6.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r6.claim: The majority hold that a completed prayer after diligent water-search remains valid even if water is then found; some recommend repeating within the time after ablution or ghusl.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r6.anchor: والجمهور على أن من تيمم وصلى وفرغ من صلاته، وقد كان اجتهد في طلبه الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r7.speaker: طاووس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r7.claim: Tawus, Ata, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Makhul, Ibn Sirin, al-Zuhri, and Rabi'a all say that a person who finds water after the prayer repeats it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r7.anchor: وروي عن طاووس وعطاء والقاسم بن محمد ومكحول وابن سيرين والزهري وربيعة كلهم يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r8.claim: In the report of Abu Said, two travelers pray after tayammum; the Prophet says the one who does not repeat followed the Sunna and the one who repeats earns double reward.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r9.speaker: أبو داود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r9.claim: Abu Dawud transmits the two-traveler report and notes that the Abu Said link is not preserved in other narrations; al-Daraqutni's version specifies finding water within the prayer time.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r9.anchor: أخرجه أبو داود وقال: وغير ابن نافع يرويه عن الليث عن عميرة بن أبي ناجية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r10.claim: If water appears during prayer, Malik says not to interrupt: complete the prayer and use water for later prayers; al-Shafi'i and Ibn al-Mundhir agree, while Abu Hanifa, Ahmad, al-Muzani, and others require stopping and restarting.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#29/r10.anchor: فقال مالك: ليس عليه قطع الصلاة واستعمال الماء وليتم صلاته وليتوضأ لما يستقبل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r1.claim: Qurtubi cites “do not invalidate your works” as support for completing a prayer begun validly with tayammum; no Sunna or consensus requires cutting it when water appears.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r2.claim: By analogy, someone fasting most of an expiation fast does not discard it upon finding an enslaved person to free; likewise, one who began prayer with tayammum completes it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r2.anchor: أن من وجب عليه الصوم في ظهار أو قتل فصام منه أكثره ثم وجد رقبة لا يلغي صومه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r3.speaker: شريك بن عبد الله القاضي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r3.claim: Sharik ibn Abd Allah al-Qadi requires a new tayammum for every prayer, voluntary or obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r3.anchor: فقال شريك بن عبدالله القاضي: يتيمم لكل صلاة نافلة وفريضة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r4.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r4.claim: Malik requires a separate tayammum for each obligatory prayer because the worshipper must seek water anew for each one.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r4.anchor: وقال مالك: لكل فريضة لأن عليه أن يبتغي الماء لكل صلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, al-Layth, Hasan ibn Hayy, and Dawud allow as many prayers as desired with one tayammum until ritual impurity occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة والثوري والليث والحسن بن حي وداود: يصلي ما شاء بتيمم واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r6.claim: Qurtubi prefers a new tayammum for each prayer: God requires seeking water for each prayer, and tayammum is an incomplete necessity-purity that consensus says ends when water appears.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r6.anchor: وما قلناه أصح لأن الله عز وجل أوجب على كل قائم إلى الصلاة طلب الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r7.claim: Al-Shafi'i and the first group disallow tayammum before prayer time because the verse links it to a need that does not exist before the time.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا لا يصلى فرضين بتيمم واحد، وهذا بين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r8.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r8.claim: One transmission from Ibn al-Qasim says the second of two obligatory prayers performed with one tayammum must be repeated while its time remains.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r8.anchor: فروى يحيى بن يحيى عن ابن القاسم: يعيد الثانية ما دام في الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r9.speaker: مطرف
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r9.claim: A transmission from Ibn al-Qasim through Abu Zayd, and reports from Mutarrif and Ibn al-Majishun, require repeating the second prayer forever because seeking water is a condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r9.anchor: وكذلك روي عن مطرف وابن الماجشون يعيد الثانية أبدا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r10.speaker: أبو الفرج
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r10.claim: Abu al-Faraj permits making up multiple missed prayers with one tayammum; this assumes water-search is not a condition, which Qurtubi rejects.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#30/r10.anchor: وقال أبو الفرج فيمن ذكر صلوات: إن قضاهن بتيمم واحد فلا شيء عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r1.claim: Qurtubi cites 18:8, describing barren ground, to illustrate ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r1.anchor: أي أرضا غليظة لا تنبت شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r2.claim: Qurtubi explains ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface and traces its name to being the upper limit to which one rises.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r2.anchor: وإنما سمي صعيدا لأنه نهاية ما يصعد إليه من الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r3.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses ṣaʿīd for the ground, describing an insect striking it with its snout.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r3.anchor: ومنه قول ذي الرمة: كأنه بالضحى ترمي الصعيد به

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r4.claim: Ṣaʿīd has the plural ṣaʿidat; the hadith warning against sitting in public roads uses that plural.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r5.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, and al-Tabari allow tayammum on any part of the earth, including soil, sand, stones, minerals, or saline ground; here ṭayyib means pure.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r5.anchor: فقالت طائفة: يتيمم بوجه الأرض كله ترابا كان أو رملا أو حجارة أو معدنا أو سبخة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r6.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r6.claim: Another group interprets ṭayyib as lawful, a reading Qurtubi calls strained.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r7.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Abu Yusuf restrict ṣaʿīd to fertile, growing soil and read ṭayyib as good soil, citing the verse that good land yields plants; al-Shafi'i requires dusty soil.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r7.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأبو يوسف: الصعيد للتراب المنبت وهو الطيب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas answers that cultivated earth is the best ṣaʿīd; Abu Umar says this implies ṣaʿīd can also refer to earth that is not cultivated.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r8.anchor: وذكر عبدالرزاق عن ابن عباس أنه سئل أي الصعيد أطيب؟ فقال الحرث

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r9.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r9.claim: Ali says ṣaʿīd means soil specifically.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r9.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه: هو التراب خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r10.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r10.claim: Al-Khalil's lexicon, as cited by Ibn Faris, glosses tayammum with ṣaʿīd as taking its dust, implying soil because smooth stone has no dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r10.anchor: وفي كتاب الخليل: تيمم بالصعيد، أي خذ من غباره حكاه ابن فارس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r11.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r11.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari says al-Shafi'i requires dust to adhere to the hand and be transferred to the body parts, analogizing earth to water; he admits ṣaʿīd alone does not prove this restriction.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r11.anchor: واشترط الشافعي أن يعلق التراب باليد ويتيمم به نقلا إلى أعضاء التيمم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r12.claim: Qurtubi rejects treating the hadith naming soil as a restriction on the general earth term, comparing it to a verse that names dates and pomegranates among fruits.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#31/r12.anchor: إنما هو من باب النص على بعض أشخاص العموم كما قال تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r1.claim: Qurtubi's analogy also points to the al-Baqara verse listing angels, messengers, Gabriel, and Michael, where naming examples does not restrict the broader class.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r2.claim: If ṣaʿīd means the earth's surface, it is a place where tayammum is performed; if it means soil, it is the direct object with an omitted preposition, and ṭayyib is its adjective or, in the lawful reading, an adverbial or verbal noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r2.anchor: ف «صعيدا» على هذا ظرف مكان. ومن جعله للتراب فهو مفعول به بتقدير حذف الباء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r3.claim: The Prophet tells a junub person to use ṣaʿīd because it suffices; Qurtubi cites this to support the earth-surface interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r3.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم للجنب: «عليك بالصعيد فإنه يكفيك»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r4.claim: The consensus case for tayammum is clean, fertile soil that has not been moved or usurped; consensus bars gold, silver, gems, food, and impure substances.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r4.anchor: مكان الإجماع مما ذكرناه أن يتيمم الرجل على تراب منبت طاهر غير منقول ولا مغصوب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r5.claim: Malik and others allow tayammum on minerals, while al-Shafi'i and others prohibit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r5.anchor: واختلف في غير هذا كالمعادن فأجيز وهو مذهب مالك وغيره. ومنع وهو مذهب الشافعي وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r6.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r6.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says Malik permits tayammum on grass if it lies beneath the earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r6.anchor: وقال ابن خويز منداد: ويجوز عند مالك التيمم على الحشيش إذا كان دون الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r7.claim: Maliki sources differ on snow: the Mudawwana and al-Mabsut allow it, while other sources prohibit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r7.anchor: واختلف عنه في التيمم على الثلج ففي المدونة والمبسوط جوازه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r8.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r8.claim: Most jurists prohibit tayammum on wood, though Mukhtasar al-Waqqar allows it; one view distinguishes attached from detached wood.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r8.anchor: واختلف المذهب في التيمم على العود فالجمهور على المنع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r9.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r9.claim: Al-Awza'i and al-Thawri allow tayammum on earth and everything on it, including trees, stones, rocks, ice, and snow; al-Tha'labi attributes to Malik permission to strike a tree and wipe with the hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r9.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي والثوري: يجوز بالأرض وكل ما عليها من الشجر والحجر والمدر وغيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya says most Malikis allow tayammum on moved soil, though a Maliki minority forbids it; baked lime and brick have two views, and the wall is disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#32/r10.anchor: وأما التراب المنقول من طين أو غيره فجمهور المذهب على جواز التيمم به

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r1.claim: Qurtubi says the Bukhari-transmitted report of the Prophet wiping on a wall proves tayammum is valid without soil, supporting Malik over al-Shafi'i.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r1.anchor: أخرجه البخاري. وهو دليل على صحة التيمم بغير التراب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r2.claim: Qurtubi says the wall report proves tayammum is valid without soil, against al-Shafi'i's requirement for pure, adherent dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r2.anchor: وهو دليل على صحة التيمم بغير التراب كما يقوله مالك ومن وافقه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r3.claim: Al-Naqqash reports that Ibn Ulayya and Ibn Kaysan permit tayammum with musk or saffron; Ibn Atiyya calls this completely mistaken.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r3.anchor: وذكر النقاش عن ابن علية وابن كيسان أنهما أجازا التيمم بالمسك والزعفران

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r4.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r4.claim: Abu Umar says the scholars generally allow tayammum on saline ground, with Ishaq ibn Rahawayh the exception.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r4.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وجماعة العلماء على إجازة التيمم بالسباخ إلا إسحاق بن راهويه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person who reaches the point of tayammum while in mud should coat part of the body with mud and, once dry, use it for tayammum.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس فيمن أدركه التيمم وهو في طين قال يأخذ من الطين فيطلي به بعض جسده

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r6.speaker: الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r6.claim: Al-Thawri and Ahmad permit tayammum with dust from felt.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r6.anchor: وقال الثوري وأحمد: يجوز التيمم بغبار اللبد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r7.claim: Al-Tha'labi says Abu Hanifa permits tayammum with kohl, arsenic, lime, gypsum, and powdered gems, but not metal filings because they are not of the earth's genus.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r7.anchor: وأجاز أبو حنيفة التيمم بالكحل والزرنيخ والنورة والجص والجوهر المسحوق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r8.claim: Masḥ can mean intercourse, cutting with a sword, a camel's day's travel, a woman without buttocks, or a touch of beauty; here it means dragging the hand across the object.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r8.anchor: المسح لفظ مشترك يكون بمعنى الجماع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r9.claim: When wiping is done with an instrument, the hand carries and moves that instrument across the surface being wiped.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r9.anchor: والمراد هنا بالمسح عبارة عن جر اليد على الممسوح خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r10.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r10.claim: Al-Shafi'i reads “from it” in al-Ma'ida as requiring soil to be transferred to the limbs; Qurtubi and Malik do not require transfer because the Prophet struck the ground, lifted and blew or shook his hands, and also wiped on a wall.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r10.anchor: فقوله «منه» يدل على أنه لا بد من نقل التراب إلى محل التيمم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r11.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r11.claim: Al-Shafi'i analogizes tayammum to wiping the head: just as water must be carried to the head, soil must be carried to the limbs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r11.anchor: قال الشافعي: لما لم يكن بد في مسح الرأس بالماء من بلل ينقل إلى الرأس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r12.speaker: محمد بن مسلمة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r12.claim: There is no dispute that the whole face must be covered in ablution and tayammum; some exempt folds and spaces between fingers, a position in the Maliki school attributed to Muhammad ibn Maslama by Ibn Atiyya.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r12.anchor: ولا خلاف في أن حكم الوجه في التيمم والوضوء الاستيعاب وتتبع مواضعه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r13.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r13.claim: The majority follow the verse's order, wiping the face before the hands; a report in al-Bukhari's chapter on one-strike tayammum mentions the hands first, as do some scholars by analogy with reversing ablution order.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r13.anchor: فبدأ بالوجه قبل اليدين وبه قال الجمهور

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r14.speaker: ابن شهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r14.claim: Ibn Shihab says the hand wipe reaches the shoulders, a position also reported from Abu Bakr.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r14.anchor: فقال ابن شهاب: إلى المناكب. روي عن أبي بكر الصديق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r15.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r15.claim: A report from al-A'mash in Abu Dawud's Musannaf says the Prophet wiped to the middle of his forearms; Ibn Atiyya says he knew of no one who followed this report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#33/r15.anchor: وفي مصنف أبي داود عن الأعمش أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مسح إلى أنصاف ذراعيه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي وأصحابهما والثوري وابن أبي سلمة والليث
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r1.claim: They require tayammum to reach the elbows by analogy with ablution; Ibn Nafi requires repeating forever if one stops at the wrists, while Malik requires repetition within prayer time.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r1.anchor: وهو قول أبي حنيفة والشافعي وأصحابهما والثوري وابن أبي سلمة والليث كلهم يرون بلوغ المرفقين بالتيمم فرضا واجبا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبدالله وابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r2.claim: Jabir and Ibn Umar transmit from the Prophet that tayammum reaches the elbows; Ibn Umar held this practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r2.anchor: وروى التيمم إلى المرفقين عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جابر بن عبدالله وابن عمر وبه كان يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r3.claim: Asked about travel tayammum, Qatada reports Ibn Umar’s elbow limit; al-Hasan and Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i also held it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r3.anchor: سئل قتادة عن التيمم في السفر فقال: كان ابن عمر يقول إلى المرفقين. وكان الحسن وإبراهيم النخعي يقولان إلى المرفقين.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r4.claim: A report through al-Sha‘bi, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza, and ʿAmmar ibn Yasir has the Prophet specify wiping to the elbows.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r4.anchor: عن الشعبي عن عبدالرحمن بن أبزى عن عمار بن ياسر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r5.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r5.claim: When Abu Ishaq mentioned the elbow report from ʿAmmar, Ahmad admired it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r5.anchor: فذكرته لأحمد بن حنبل فعجب منه وقال ما أحسنه!.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والأوزاعي وعطاء والشعبي وأحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق بن راهويه
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r6.claim: Another group makes the wrists the obligatory limit; the view is also reported from Malik and was al-Shafi‘i’s earlier position.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r6.anchor: روي عن علي بن أبي طالب والأوزاعي وعطاء والشعبي في رواية، وبه قال أحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق بن راهويه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r7.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r7.claim: Al-Zuhri argues from the general word ‘hands’ for wiping to the armpits; Makhul counters by asking where the hand is cut in the theft verse and says he defeated the argument.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r7.anchor: فقال الزهري: المسح إلى الآباط. فقلت: عمن أخذت هذا؟ فقال: عن كتاب الله عز وجل،

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r8.speaker: الدراوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r8.claim: Al-Darawardi is reported to distinguish the wrists as obligatory and the armpits as meritorious.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r8.anchor: وحكي عن الدراوردي أن الكوعين فرض والآباط فضيلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the armpit view lacks evidence; others infer from the general word ‘hand,’ analogy with ablution, wrist reports, analogy with amputation, or ʿAmmar’s palm report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هذا قول لا يعضده قياس ولا دليل وإنما عمم قوم لفظ اليد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r10.speaker: مالك والأوزاعي والشافعي وأبو حنيفة والثوري والليث
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r10.claim: They require two strikes, one for the face and another for the hands; this method is transmitted from the Prophet by Jabir and Ibn Umar.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r10.anchor: ذهب مالك في المدونة أن التيمم بضربتين: ضربة للوجه وضربة لليدين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r11.speaker: ابن أبي الجهم والأوزاعي وعطاء والشعبي وأحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق وداود والطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r11.claim: They hold that tayammum uses one strike; the author calls the report from ʿAmmar the strongest established evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r11.anchor: وقال ابن أبي الجهم التيمم بضربة واحدة. وروي عن الأوزاعي في الأشهر عنه وهو قول عطاء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r12.speaker: عمار
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r12.claim: The author judges the one-strike report from ʿAmmar the strongest established evidence about the number of strikes.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r12.anchor: وهو أثبت ما روي في ذلك من حديث عمار.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r13.speaker: مالك وابن نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r13.claim: Malik says one strike suffices, whereas Ibn Nafi requires repeating the prayer forever.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r13.anchor: قال مالك في كتاب محمد: إن تيمم بضربة واحدة أجزأه. وقال ابن نافع: يعيد أبدا.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r14.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى والحسن بن حي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r14.claim: They require two strikes, each wiping the face, forearms, and elbows.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#34/r14.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى والحسن بن حي: ضربتان يمسح بكل ضربة منهما وجهه وذراعيه ومرفقيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r1.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r1.claim: Abu ʿUmar resolves conflicting reports by the Qur’an’s apparent wording: two strikes, face then hands to the elbows, by analogy with ablution and following Ibn Umar; a sound Prophetic report would govern.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r1.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لما اختلفت الآثار في كيفية التيمم وتعارضت كان الواجب في ذلك الرجوع إلى ظاهر الكتاب،

QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r2.claim: God has always accepted pardon and been gentle, covering sin’s punishment rather than punishing.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:43#35/r2.anchor: أي لم يزل كائنا يقبل العفو وهو السهل، ويغفر الذنب أي يستر عقوبته فلا يعاقب.

RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r1.claim: One occasion report says ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf served food and drink to companions while wine was still permitted; after drinking, an imam garbled the recitation at Maghrib, prompting the verse. They then avoided wine at prayer times until sober, before its final prohibition in al-Māʾida.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r1.anchor: أكلوا وشربوا ، فلما ثلموا جاء وقت صلاة المغرب فقدموا أحدهم

RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r2.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r2.claim: When ʿUmar heard the ruling, he prayed that God issue a command about wine because it harms minds and property; the revelation of al-Māʾida came the next morning.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r2.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه لما بلغه ذلك قال : اللهم إن الخمر تضر بالعقول والأموال

RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives another occasion: before wine was forbidden, senior Companions drank and came to the mosque to pray with the Messenger, so God prohibited this.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r3.anchor: الثاني : قال ابن عباس : نزلت في جماعة من أكابر الصحابة قبل تحريم الخمر

RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن والشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and al-Ḥasan take ‘prayer’ to mean the mosque, and al-Shāfiʿī adopts this view; it can mean ‘place of prayer’ by common ellipsis, as ṣalawāt means prayer sites at 22:40.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r4.anchor: المراد منه المسجد ، وهو قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن ، وإليه ذهب الشافعي

RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r5.claim: The majority take ṣalāt here to mean the prayer itself: do not perform it while intoxicated.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : وعليه الأكثرون : أن المراد بالصلاة في هذه الآية نفس الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r1.claim: If ṣalāt means the mosque, the verse bars entering it drunk or while junub except to pass through, allowing a junub person to cross the mosque, as al-Shāfiʿī holds.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r1.anchor: يكون المعنى : لا تقربوا المسجد وأنتم سكارى ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r2.claim: If ṣalāt means the prayer, the verse bars praying drunk or junub except for a traveling wayfarer, allowing a junub traveler unable to find water to pray by tayammum.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بعابر السبيل المسافر ، فيكون هذا الاستثناء دليلا على أنه يجوز للجنب الاقدام على الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r3.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī’s adherents prefer the mosque reading because ‘approach’ naturally applies to a place, whereas it does not literally apply to the prayer itself.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r3.anchor: أنه قال : { لا تقربوا الصلواة } والقرب والبعد لا يصحان على نفس الصلاة على سبيل الحقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r4.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r4.claim: They argue the exception works under the mosque reading; under the prayer reading it fails because a sick nontraveler unable to use water may still pray by tayammum.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r4.anchor: أنا لو حملناه على ما قلنا لكان الاستثناء صحيحا ، أما لو حملناه على ما قلتم

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r5.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r5.claim: If the wayfarer means a junub traveler, the alternative reading requires unstated conditions about having water or needing tayammum; the mosque reading requires no such additions.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r5.anchor: فحينئذ يحتاج إلى إضمار هذا الاستثناء في الآية ، وإن لم يكن واجدا للماء لم يجز له الصلاة إلا مع التيمم

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r6.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r6.claim: They argue the travel and water ruling follows as a separate rule: readers prefer pausing at ‘until you wash,’ so the earlier exception should not depend on the later verse’s condition.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r6.anchor: والذي يؤكده أن القراء كلهم استحبوا الوقف عند قوله : { حتى تغتسلوا } ثم يستأنف قوله

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r7.speaker: من نصر القول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r7.claim: Proponents of the prayer reading argue that ‘until you know what you say’ concerns prayer, which has prescribed speech, while no prescribed speech in the mosque is affected by drunkenness.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r7.anchor: ولمن نصر القول الثاني أن يقول : إن قوله تعالى : { حتى تعلموا ما تقولون } يدل على أن المراد

RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r8.claim: The mosque reading answers that people ordinarily go to the mosque for prayer, so whatever prevents prayer also counts as a reason not to go to the mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v10p87#2/r8.anchor: فما يخل بالصلاة كان كالمانع من الذهاب إلى المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says sukkārā is the plural of sakrān; adjectives on faʿlān take the plural patterns fuʿālā and fuʿālā, as in kasālā.
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r1.anchor: الواحدي رحمه الله : السكارى جمع سكران

RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r2.claim: The root sense of sakr is blocking a path: it describes stopping a water channel, a confused eye, or water diverted from its course; wine blocks reason from penetrating as it does in sobriety. At 15:15, vision is veiled from true perception.
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r2.anchor: وأصل السكر في اللغة سد الطريق ، ومن ذلك سكر البثق وهو سده ، وسكرت عينه سكرا

RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r3.speaker: جمهور الصحابة والتابعين
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r3.claim: The majority of Companions and Successors understand the word as intoxication from wine, the opposite of sobriety.
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r3.anchor: المراد منه السكر من الخمر وهو نقيض الصحو ، وهو قول الجمهور من الصحابة والتابعين

RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r4.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the word means sleep rather than wine intoxication: sleep blocks the channels of the spirit, preventing sight and hearing from reaching the body’s exterior.
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r4.anchor: وهو قول الضحاك : وهو أنه ليس المراد منه سكر الخمر ، إنما المراد منه سكر النوم

RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r5.speaker: الفرزدق
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r5.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line compares sleep to wine, supporting the use of sakr for sleep.
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r5.anchor: من السير والادلاج يحسب انما سقاه الكرى في كل منزلة خمرا

RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk argues that the verse describes sleep because an unaware person cannot be charged with a duty; the Prophet’s report lifts the pen from children, the insane, and sleepers until they wake or recover.
RAZI-FULL:v10p88/r6.anchor: فهو قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( رفع القلم عن ثلاث عن الصبي حتى يبلغ وعن المجنون حتى

RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r1.claim: The Prophet said that when someone grows drowsy during prayer, they should sleep until the drowsiness passes, lest they seek forgiveness while actually cursing themselves; al-Ḍaḥḥāk uses this to support the sleep interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r1.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إذا نعس أحدكم وهو في الصلاة فليرقد حتى يذهب عنه النوم فإنه إذا صلى وهو ينعس

RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers wine intoxication: sakr literally means drunkenness from wine, while intoxication from passion, anger, fear, or sleep is figurative and normally qualified; he cites 50:19 and 22:2.
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r2.anchor: واعلم أن الصحيح هو القول الأول ، ويدل عليه وجهان : الأول : أن لفظ السكر حقيقة في السكر

RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r3.claim: All exegetes agree the verse was revealed about wine, so that cause must be included; the command targets drinking that would impair understanding when prayer is due, not prayer by a person already unaware. The sleep hadith does not prove that sakr means sleep.
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r3.anchor: أن جميع المفسرين اتفقوا على أن هذه الآية إنما نزلت في شرب الخمر

RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r4.claim: Some call the verse abrogated by al-Māʾida; al-Rāzī says the abrogated implication is that prayer becomes permitted once a drinker can understand, which the later total ban on wine removes.
RAZI-FULL:v10p89/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : هذه الآية منسوخة بآية المائدة ، وأقول : الذي يمكن ادعاء النسخ فيه أنه يقال

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r1.claim: A traveler who lacks water must use tayammum whether the journey is long or short.
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r1.anchor: والآية تدل على أن المسافر إذا لم يجد الماء تيمم ، طال سفره أو قصر

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r2.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ originally means a low, concealing place; people sought one to relieve themselves out of sight, and the bodily event later took the place’s name. Its plural is ghīṭān.
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r2.anchor: والغائط المكان المطمئن من الأرض وجمعه الغيطان . وكان الرجل إذا أراد قضاء الحاجة طلب غائطا

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r3.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read lāmastum without alif, from lams; the other readers have the alif form, mulāmasa.
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r3.anchor: المسألة الأولى : قرأ حمزة والكسائي : { لامستم } بغير ألف من اللمس ، والباقون { لامستم } بالألف من الملامسة

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وأبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Abū Ḥanīfa take touching women to mean intercourse, since touching by hand does not invalidate ablution.
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r4.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة ، وقول أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه ، لأن اللمس باليد لا ينقض الطهارة

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر والشعبي والنخعي والشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Shaʿbī, al-Nakhaʿī, and al-Shāfiʿī understand the phrase as skin contact, with or without intercourse.
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r5.anchor: وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عمر والشعبي والنخعي وقول الشافعي رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers skin contact: lams literally means touching by hand, while restricting it to intercourse is figurative; mulāmasa also does not literally mean intercourse, so the two canonical readings should retain compatible literal senses.
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r6.anchor: واعلم أن هذا القول أرجح من الأول ، وذلك لأن إحدى القراءتين هي قوله تعالى : { أو لامستم النساء } واللمس حقيقته المس باليد

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r7.speaker: أنصار قول الجماع
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r7.claim: Supporters of the intercourse interpretation cite Qur’anic euphemisms for intercourse at 2:37 and 58:3; Ibn ʿAbbās says God is modest and noble, veiling the meaning with ‘touching.’
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r7.anchor: واحتج من قال : المراد باللمس الجماع ، بأن لفظ اللمس والمس وردا في القرآن بمعنى الجماع

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God is modest and noble and uses euphemism, calling sexual intimacy ‘touching.’
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال : إن الله حيي كريم يعف ويكني ، فعبر عن المباشرة بالملامسة

RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r9.speaker: أنصار قول الجماع
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r9.claim: They also argue that ‘coming from the place of need’ already covers minor impurity; if touching women also meant minor impurity, the verse would omit major impurity, so it must mean intercourse.
RAZI-FULL:v10p90/r9.anchor: وأيضا الحدث نوعان : الأصغر ، وهو المراد بقوله : { أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط } فلو حملنا قوله

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r1.claim: Rāzī rejects the preceding interpretations as unsupported departures from the wording; reading this part as janāba would repeat the ruling already stated.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r1.anchor: كل ما ذكروه عدول عن ظاهر اللفظ بغير دليل ، فوجب أن لا يجوز . وأيضا فحكم الجنابة تقدم في قوله : { ولا جنبا }

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r2.speaker: أهل الظاهر
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r2.claim: The literalists hold that only the person who touches a woman loses ablution; the person touched does not.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r2.anchor: قال أهل الظاهر : إنما ينتقض وضوء اللامس لظاهر قوله

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that both the toucher and the person touched lose ablution.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r3.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : بل ينتقض وضوءهما معا

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires a fresh search for water when each prayer time begins after a person has prayed using tayammum, since not finding it implies prior searching.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r4.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : إذا دخل وقت الصلاة فطلب الماء ولم يجده وتيمم وصلى

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that a person who already searched and prayed with tayammum need not search again when the next prayer time begins.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه لا يجب

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r6.claim: An objection says the verb found does not itself imply prior searching, as Qur’anic uses of finding describe matters for which searching by God is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r6.anchor: قولنا : وجد ، لا يشعر بسبق الطلب ، بدليل قوله تعالى : { ووجدك ضالا فهدى

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r7.claim: Rāzī answers that divine seeking is figurative: God singled out Muḥammad and commanded people, whose failure is like seeking something and not finding it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r7.anchor: الطلب وإن كان في حقه تعالى محالا ، إلا أنه لما أخرج محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم من بين قومه بما لم يكن لائقا لقومه صار ذلك كأنه طلبه

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r8.claim: There is consensus that someone who has water but needs it for their own thirst or that of a protected animal may perform tayammum.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r8.anchor: أجمعوا على أنه لو وجد الماء لكنه يحتاج إليه لعطشه أو عطش حيوان محترم جاز له التيمم

RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r9.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r9.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires using any available amount insufficient for full ablution together with tayammum, relying on the verse’s apparent wording.
RAZI-FULL:v10p91/r9.anchor: قد أوجبه الشافعي رضي الله عنه ، متمسكا بظاهر لفظ الآية

RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r1.claim: Tayammum means intending or aiming; the forms ammamtuhu, tayammamtuhu, and taʾammamtuhu all mean I intended it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r1.anchor: التيمم في اللغة عبارة عن القصد ، يقال : أممته وتيممته وتأممته ، أي قصدته

RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains ṣaʿīd as the face of the earth, whether soil or another material.
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : الصعيد وجه الأرض ، ترابا كان أو غيره

RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits tayammum by striking and wiping on bare rock without dust, since ṣaʿīd means what rises from the earth and the command is to intend land.
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r3.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه : لو فرضنا صخرا لا تراب عليه فضرب المتيمم يده عليه ومسح كان ذلك كافيا

RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires soil that sticks to the hand for tayammum.
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r4.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : بل لا بد من تراب يلتصق بيده

RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that the unrestricted wording here is restricted by 5:6, where min in wiping from it indicates taking a portion of soil; al-Kashshāf says Arabs understand such phrasing partitivally.
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r5.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : لا يفهم أحد من العرب من قول القائل : مسحت برأسه من الدهن ومن الماء ومن التراب : إلا معنى التبعيض

RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r6.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r6.claim: Al-Wāḥidī argues that good earth is earth that grows plants, as 7:58 says, so the command to use good ṣaʿīd requires soil rather than barren rock.
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r6.anchor: ما ذكره الواحدي رحمه الله ، وهو أنه تعالى أوجب في هذه الآية كون الصعيد طيبا ، والأرض الطيبة هي التي تنبت بدليل قوله

RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r7.claim: Rāzī favors soil as the cautious meaning of good ṣaʿīd: non-saline earth, whose use is agreed valid, is specified in Prophetic reports as purifier.
RAZI-FULL:v10p92/r7.anchor: وجب حمل الصعيد الطيب عليه رعاية لقاعدة الاحتياط ، لا سيما وقد خصص النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام التراب بهذه الصفة

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r1.claim: The four passages progress from wine as provision (16:67), to mixed benefit and sin (2:219), avoiding prayer while drunk here, and finally complete prohibition (5:90).
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r1.anchor: four verses address the consumption of wine or intoxicating drinks, and only one of them bans wine explicitly

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r2.claim: Jurisprudence treats 5:90 as the authoritative final ruling, based on Prophetic sayings and practice, abrogating the other passages’ legal implications.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r2.anchor: Islamic jurisprudence, basing itself upon Prophetic sayings

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r3.claim: Believers must not approach prayer, its mosque, or prepare for it while drunk; they may do so once sober and able to understand their recitation.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r3.anchor: not to approach the prayer itself or the mosque(ṣalāh/ṣalawāt

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r4.claim: Ṣalāh or ṣalawāt can mean the place of prayer as well as prayer itself.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r4.anchor: ṣalāh/ṣalawāt, or “prayer(s),” can also connote the place of prayer; cf. 22:40

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r5.speaker: Companions of the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r5.claim: A report says the verse followed Companions praying after drinking wine while drinking was still permitted and reciting a Quranic passage incorrectly.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r5.anchor: This part of the verse was reportedly revealed when some Companions of the Prophet attempted to pray after having drunk wine

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r6.speaker: Muslims
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r6.claim: After the verse, Muslims reportedly drank only after the evening prayer until wine was forbidden.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r6.anchor: Muslims would drink wine only after they had completed the evening prayer (ʿishāʾ)

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r7.speaker: minority tradition
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r7.claim: A minority tradition includes excessive sleepiness in drunkenness, since it impairs prayer; on this reading the verse was not wholly abrogated by the wine ban.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r7.anchor: A minority tradition extends the meaning of“drunkenness”

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r8.claim: Junub means major ritual impurity and derives from a root meaning distance; the impure should keep distant from prayer and its places until purified, paralleling intoxication.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r8.anchor: Ritual impurity translates junub, which denotes major ritual impurity and derives from a root meaning to be distant from something

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r9.speaker: legal scholars
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r9.claim: Legal scholars hold that major ritual impurity also prohibits touching or reciting the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r9.anchor: According to legal scholars, the state of junub also prohibits one from touching or reciting the Quran

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r10.claim: Washing means completing major ritual ablution through full immersion, such as a bath or shower.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r10.anchor: Until you have washed refers to completing the major ritual ablution, which requires full immersion (as in a bath or shower)

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r11.claim: The exception covers junub travelers seeking temporary shelter in a mosque and Companions whose adjacent homes required crossing the Prophet’s mosque to leave.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r11.anchor: An exception is made for those passing through, that is, travelers in a state of junub who need to seek shelter temporarily in a mosque

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r12.claim: Clean earth substitutes for water when illness prevents seeking or safely using water, or on a journey where water is unavailable.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r12.anchor: This verse also establishes an important easing of the rules of ritual purity by allowing the substitution of clean earth for water

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r13.claim: Verse 5:6 gives nearly identical ritual-purity instructions.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r13.anchor: see also 5:6 for a nearly identical set of injunctions related to purity

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r14.speaker: the Prophet’s wife ʿĀʾishah
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r14.claim: The verse reportedly followed ʿĀʾishah losing a necklace while traveling with the Prophet. The group camped to search, lacked water, complained they could not wash, and the verse came at dawn prayer.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r14.anchor: the Prophet’s wife ʿĀʾishah lost a necklace while journeying with the Prophet and a group of Muslims

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r15.claim: The ablution is called tayammum after the verse’s verb tayammamū, “resort to.”
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r15.anchor: came to be known as tayammum, from the verb tayammamū

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r16.speaker: a ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r16.claim: A hadith lists God’s making dust purifying for Muslims among His blessings favoring them over other peoples.
