STUDYQURAN:4:43/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r17.claim: Ṣaʿīd may mean high, hard, or rocky ground; ṭayyib may mean good, pure, or wholesome, leading some to suggest arable soil.

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r18.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r18.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says ṣaʿīd is any pure or clean part of the earth’s surface; dust adhering to the hands purifies.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r18.anchor: Al-Ṭabarī asserts that it refers to any pure or clean part of the surface of the earth

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r19.claim: Precious metals and gems are unsuitable as clean earth for tayammum.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r19.anchor: Precious metals and gems are not suitable as sources of clean earth for the tayammum

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r20.speaker: legal schools
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r20.claim: Schools differ on water-search requirements, illness threshold, whether tayammum removes impurity or temporarily permits prayer, and whether prayer must be repeated if water is found before prayer time ends.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r20.anchor: There are differences among the legal schools as to whether the absence of water is a condition for the acceptability of the tayammum

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r21.speaker: legal scholars
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r21.claim: Scholars disagree whether “touching women” means intercourse only or any touch, regardless of desire.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r21.anchor: They also disagree about the extent to which one would have to “touch women” in order to become impure

STUDYQURAN:4:43/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r22.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r22.claim: Tayammum requires intention, then two contacts with earth or stone: one to wipe the face, one to wipe the hands.
STUDYQURAN:4:43/r22.anchor: make the niyyah or intention to perform the tayammum then to touch the earth or rub a piece of stone twice

TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r1.claim: God tells believers not to pray while intoxicated until they understand what they say in prayer, including the recitation commanded or encouraged and what they are forbidden to say.
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r1.anchor: لا تقربوا الصلاة} [النساء: 43] : لا تصلوا، {وأنتم سكارى}

TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r2.claim: Sukārā is the plural form of sakrān, meaning a drunk person.
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r2.anchor: وأنتم سكارى} [النساء: 43] : وهو جمع سكران , {حتى تعلموا ما تقولون}

TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r3.claim: Ali reports that he, Abd al-Rahman, and another man drank wine; Abd al-Rahman led them in prayer and confused the recitation of al-Kāfirūn, occasioning this verse.
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r3.anchor: عن علي: أنه كان هو وعبد الرحمن ورجل آخر شربوا الخمر، فصلى بهم عبد الرحمن

TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن حبيب
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r4.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf hosted companions with food and drink; after they became drunk, Ali led Maghrib and recited the sūra incorrectly, and the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن حبيب: أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف، صنع طعاما وشرابا

TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prohibition on approaching prayer while drunk came before wine was forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى} [النساء: 43] قبل أن تحرم الخمر

TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r6.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r6.claim: Abu Razin says the verse was revealed while people were drinking wine, before the general prohibition of wine.
TAB-FULL:v7p45#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي رزين، في قوله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى}

TAB-FULL:v7p48/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r1.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r1.claim: Abu Razin says people continued drinking after the verses in al-Baqara and al-Nisaʾ, and stopped when the verse in al-Maʾida was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r1.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن أبي رزين، قال: «كانوا يشربون بعد ما أنزلت التي في البقرة، وبعد التي في النساء

TAB-FULL:v7p48/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r2.claim: Mujahid says they were forbidden to pray while drunk, then this restriction was superseded by the prohibition of wine.
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون} [النساء: 43] قال: «نهوا أن يصلوا وهم سكارى، ثم نسخها تحريم الخمر»

TAB-FULL:v7p48/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r3.claim: Qatada says people avoided intoxication at prayer times, and the rule was later superseded by wine's prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى} [النساء: 43] قال: «كانوا يجتنبون السكر عند حضور الصلوات، ثم نسخ بتحريم الخمر»

TAB-FULL:v7p48/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r4.speaker: أبو وائل، أبو رزين، إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r4.claim: Abu Waʾil, Abu Razin, and Ibrahim say the cited passages about wine and intoxication all preceded the prohibition of wine.
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r4.anchor: عن أبي وائل، وأبي رزين وإبراهيم

TAB-FULL:v7p48/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak offers a different reading: the intoxication meant here is sleep, not wine.
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك: {لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى} [النساء: 43] قال: «سكر النوم»

TAB-FULL:v7p48/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers intoxication from drink before wine was forbidden, citing the widespread reports from the Prophet's Companions that the verse addressed the described drinking incident; he rejects sleep as the intended meaning.
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r6.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى القولين في ذلك بتأويل الآية، تأويل من قال ذلك نهي من الله المؤمنين

TAB-FULL:v7p48/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r7.claim: The addressed drunk person still understands what he does, though wine burdens the tongue and numbs the body so he cannot recite or perform prayer properly; one who no longer understands has become deranged and is counted among the insane, not the person addressed.
TAB-FULL:v7p48/r7.anchor: ولكن السكران هو الذي يفهم ما يأتي ويذر، غير أن الشراب قد أثقل لسانه

TAB-FULL:v7p50/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Abu Majliz interpret the exception as a traveler; Ibn Abbas adds that a junub with water must not pray, while one without water may wipe with earth.
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] يقول: «لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم جنب

TAB-FULL:v7p50/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r2.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r2.claim: Ali interprets the exception as travelers who lack water and therefore perform tayammum; he also says the verse was revealed concerning travel.
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r2.anchor: عن علي، رضي الله عنه: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل}

TAB-FULL:v7p50/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr interprets the exception as the traveler.
TAB-FULL:v7p50/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {ولا جنبا} [النساء: 43] إلا عابري سبيل قال: «المسافر»

TAB-FULL:v7p53/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r1.claim: Mujahid says the phrase concerns a man who becomes junub while traveling and performs tayammum to pray; other versions add that he has no water and remains on tayammum until he finds water and can wash.
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] قال: «هو الرجل يكون في السفر فتصيبه الجنابة فيتيمم ويصلي»

TAB-FULL:v7p53/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r2.speaker: الحسن بن مسلم
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r2.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Muslim interprets the exception as travelers who have no water and use tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r2.anchor: عن الحسن بن مسلم، في قوله: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] قال: «إلا أن يكونوا مسافرين، فلا يجدوا الماء فيتيمموا»

TAB-FULL:v7p53/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r3.speaker: الحكم
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r3.claim: Al-Hakam says the phrase concerns a traveler who becomes junub, finds no water, and performs tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r3.anchor: عن الحكم: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] قال: «المسافر تصيبه الجنابة، فلا يجد ماء فيتيمم»

TAB-FULL:v7p53/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، الحكم
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Hakam say a traveler who is junub and lacks water performs tayammum and prays.
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، وعن منصور، عن الحكم

TAB-FULL:v7p53/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says they used to hear that this refers to travel.
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن كثير، قال: «كنا نسمع أنه في السفر»

TAB-FULL:v7p53/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase concerns a traveler without water, who must use tayammum and pray; his father held this view too.
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل}

TAB-FULL:v7p53/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r7.claim: Other interpreters take prayer to mean the prayer place or mosque: do not enter it while intoxicated before understanding, or while junub before washing, except to pass through; they explain the wording by Muslims' customary attendance at congregational prayer in mosques.
TAB-FULL:v7p53/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: لا تقربوا المصلى للصلاة وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون، ولا تقربوه جنبا

TAB-FULL:v7p58/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda ibn ʿAbd Allah, reporting from his father, interprets the exception as a passage through the mosque.
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة بن عبد الله

TAB-FULL:v7p58/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says not to enter a mosque except to pass through when one's route goes through it, without sitting.
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] قال: «لا تقرب المسجد إلا أن يكون طريقك فيه، فتمر مرا ولا تجلس»

TAB-FULL:v7p58/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r3.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r3.claim: Saʿid says a junub person may pass through the mosque while standing, without sitting or having wudu.
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، عن سعيد: في الجنب يمر في المسجد مجتازا وهو قائم لا يجلس وليس بمتوضئ، وتلا هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v7p58/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas permits menstruating women and people in janaba to pass through a mosque so long as they do not sit there.

TAB-FULL:v7p58/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r5.speaker: أبو الزبير
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r5.claim: Abu al-Zubayr reports that one of them used to pass through the mosque while junub.
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r5.anchor: أخبرنا أبو الزبير، قال: «كان أحدنا يمر في المسجد وهو جنب مجتازا»

TAB-FULL:v7p58/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says a junub person may pass through the mosque but may not sit in it.

TAB-FULL:v7p58/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r7.claim: Ibrahim permits a junub person to cross the mosque when there is no other route.
TAB-FULL:v7p58/r7.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] قال: «إذا لم يجد طريقا إلا المسجد يمر فيه»

TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan permits menstruating women and people in janaba to pass through a mosque without sitting there.
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: «لا بأس للحائض والجنب أن يمرا في المسجد ولا يقعدا فيه»

TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r2.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri says a junub person was granted permission to pass through a mosque.
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r2.anchor: عن عمرو، عن سعيد، عن الزهري، قال: «رخص للجنب أن يمر، في المسجد»

TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r3.speaker: يزيد بن أبي حبيب
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r3.claim: Yazid ibn Abi Habib relates that some Ansar had doors opening into the mosque, became junub without water, and could reach water only by crossing the mosque; the verse was revealed in response.
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r3.anchor: ثني يزيد بن أبي حبيب، عن قول الله: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] أن رجالا من الأنصار كانت أبوابهم في المسجد

TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim says a junub person should pass through the mosque only when no other route is available.
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] قال: «لا يجتاز في المسجد إلا أن لا يجد طريقا غيره»

TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says a junub person should not make the mosque a route.
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه: «لا يمر الجنب في المسجد يتخذه طريقا»

TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers reading the exception as passing through the mosque, not as a traveler without water: the following clause already states the traveler's tayammum rule, so treating this exception as travel would needlessly repeat it.
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى القولين بالتأويل لذلك تأويل من تأوله: {ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل} [النساء: 43] إلا مجتازي طريق فيه

TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r7.claim: A ʿābir al-sabīl is one who crosses and passes through; the verb ʿabara is used for crossing a road.
TAB-FULL:v7p58#2/r7.anchor: والعابر السبيل: المجتازه مرا وقطعا، يقال منه: عبرت هذا الطريق فأنا أعبره

TAB-FULL:v7p59/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p59/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p59/r1.claim: The verb ʿabara means to cross or traverse, including crossing a river; a powerful she-camel able to endure long journeys is also called ʿibr asfār.
TAB-FULL:v7p59/r1.anchor: ومنه قيل للناقة القوية على الأسفار

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r1.claim: Here the sick are people with wounds or smallpox while junub; illness excuses tayammum when water would harm or cannot be used safely.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، قوله: {وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر} [النساء: 43] قال: «المريض الذي قد أرخص له في التيمم

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the sick person excused to use tayammum is broken or wounded: a broken person who becomes junub washes, while a wound is washed only if it is not at risk of harm.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، قوله: {وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر} [النساء: 43] قال: «المريض الذي قد أرخص له في التيمم هو الكسير والجريح

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r3.claim: Abu Malik says the exemption applies to a patient whose wound might be harmed by washing, so tayammum is permitted.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك، قال في هذه الآية: {وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر} [النساء: 43] قال: «هي للمريض الذي به الجراحة

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r4.claim: Al-Suddi defines the illness as a wound or injury that water may harm, in which case the person uses tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r4.anchor: عن السدي: وإن كنتم مرضى والمرض: هو الجراح والجراحة التي يتخوف عليها من الماء إن أصابه ضر صاحبه

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says a person with wounds, sores, or ulcers performs tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {وإن كنتم مرضى} [النساء: 43] قال: «إذا كان به جروح أو قروح يتيمم»

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r6.claim: Ibrahim specifies sores on the arms as the illness meant here.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم: {وإن كنتم مرضى} [النساء: 43] قال: «من القروح تكون في الذراعين»

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says a person with a feared injury uses tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r7.anchor: عن عمرو، عن جويبر، عن الضحاك , قال

TAB-FULL:v7p61/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r8.claim: Mujahid says illness includes a wound, sore, or smallpox when cold or water may cause harm; the person uses clean earth as does a traveler without water.
TAB-FULL:v7p61/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وإن كنتم مرضى} [النساء: 43] والمرض: أن يصيب الرجل الجرح أو القرح أو الجدري، فيخاف على نفسه من برد الماء وأذاه

TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r1.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r1.claim: Asked about a person with smallpox who becomes junub, al-Shaʿbi answers that the two champions of this verse have departed; al-Tabari gives no gloss of the saying.
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي، أنه سئل عن المجدور، تصيبه الجنابة؟ قال: «ذهب فرسان هذه الآية»

TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says an incapacitated resident unable to reach or obtain water, with no helper to bring it, should use tayammum and pray when prayer time comes; his father held this view and regarded him as more excused than a traveler.
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر} [النساء: 43]

TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r3.claim: The sick here are residents with wounds, sores, a fracture, or another condition preventing ghusl; the traveler may be healthy but junub, and either may use tayammum when water is unavailable or cannot be used.
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r3.anchor: فتأويل الآية إذا: وإن كنتم جرحى أو بكم قروح أو كسر أو علة لا تقدرون معها على الاغتسال من الجنابة

TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r4.claim: The clause about coming from the ghāʾiṭ concerns a healthy traveler who has relieved himself; he should perform tayammum when water is unavailable.
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r4.anchor: وكذلك تأويل قوله: {أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط} [النساء: 43] يقول:

TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r5.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ originally means a broad, descending valley; because Arabs commonly relieved themselves in such places, the term became a euphemism for relieving oneself anywhere, so coming from al-ghāʾiṭ means having answered nature.
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r5.anchor: والغائط: ما اتسع من الأودية وتصوب، وجعل كناية عن قضاء حاجة الإنسان , لأن العرب كانت تختار قضاء حاجتها في الغيطان

TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses al-ghāʾiṭ as a valley.
TAB-FULL:v7p61#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد: {أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط}

TAB-FULL:v7p64/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that the mawālī understood lamas as something short of intercourse, while the Arabs understood it as intercourse.
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: ذكروا اللمس، فقال ناس من الموالي:

TAB-FULL:v7p64/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says mass, lams, and mubāshara all mean intercourse, with God using euphemism as He chooses.
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه قال: {أو لامستم النساء} [النساء: 43] قال: «هو الجماع»

TAB-FULL:v7p64/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، عطاء، عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿAṭāʾ take lams as touching short of intercourse; ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr takes it as intercourse, which Ibn ʿAbbās endorses as the Arabs' correct usage.
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r3.anchor: قال عبيد بن عمير: هو الجماع، وقلت أنا وعطاء: هو اللمس.

TAB-FULL:v7p64/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r4.claim: In another exchange, Ibn ʿAbbās says the Arabs were right that lams means intercourse, though he says the mawālī prevailed, and notes God's euphemism.
TAB-FULL:v7p64/r4.anchor: قال: فدخلنا على ابن عباس، فسألناه، فقال: «غلب فريق الموالي وأصابت العرب، هو الجماع، ولكن الله يعف ويكني»

TAB-FULL:v7p67/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās repeatedly explains lams, mass, and mubāshara as intercourse, saying God may use euphemistic wording.
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: " اللمس والمس والمباشرة: الجماع، ولكن الله يكني بما شاء "

TAB-FULL:v7p67/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr recounts the dispute at Ibn ʿAbbās's door: Arabs said intercourse and mawālī said touching by hand; Ibn ʿAbbās answers that lams means intercourse.
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: اختلفت العرب والموالي في الملامسة على باب ابن عباس قالت العرب:

TAB-FULL:v7p67/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also calls the phrase intercourse and says God is generous in using euphemism.
TAB-FULL:v7p67/r3.anchor: عن بكر بن عبد الله، عن ابن عباس قال: " الملامسة: الجماع، ولكن الله كريم يكني عما شاء "

TAB-FULL:v7p68/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies lams as intercourse, also phrased as nikāḥ.
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: " اللمس: الجماع "

TAB-FULL:v7p68/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r2.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي، عن علي، رضي الله عنه قال: «الجماع»

TAB-FULL:v7p68/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r3.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan describe the intended act as intercourse with women.

TAB-FULL:v7p68/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r4.claim: Another group understands the phrase as any unmediated bodily touch and requires ablution when any part of a person's body touches a woman's body.
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: عنى الله بذلك كل لمس بيد كان أو بغيرها من أعضاء جسد الإنسان.

TAB-FULL:v7p68/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r5.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says lams means contact short of intercourse.
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r5.anchor: عن طارق بن شهاب، عن عبد الله، أنه قال شيئا هذا معناه: " الملامسة: ما دون الجماع "

TAB-FULL:v7p68/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r6.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reports ʿAbd Allāh's statement that a kiss is a kind of lams.
TAB-FULL:v7p68/r6.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن أبي عبيدة، عن عبد الله قال: «القبلة من اللمس»

TAB-FULL:v7p70/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a kiss is a kind of lams and requires ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: «القبلة من اللمس، وفيها الوضوء»

TAB-FULL:v7p70/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r2.speaker: عبيدة
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r2.claim: When asked about the verse, ʿUbayda gestures with his hand and closes his fingers; another account describes a grasping motion, indicating manual touch.
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r2.anchor: عن محمد، قال: سألت عبيدة عن قوله: {أو لامستم النساء} [النساء: 43] قال: «فأشار بيده هكذا، وحكاه سليم

TAB-FULL:v7p70/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar performed ablution after kissing a woman and considered a kiss to be lamas.
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r3.anchor: عن نافع: أن ابن عمر، كان يتوضأ من قبلة المرأة، ويرى فيها الوضوء، ويقول: هي من اللماس

TAB-FULL:v7p70/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r4.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r4.claim: ʿĀmir says lams means touching short of intercourse.
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r4.anchor: عن إسماعيل، عن عامر، قال: " الملامسة: ما دون الجماع "

TAB-FULL:v7p70/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm says touching with sexual desire invalidates ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p70/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال: «اللمس من شهوة ينقض الوضوء»

TAB-FULL:v7p74/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r1.speaker: الحكم، حماد، عطاء
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r1.claim: Al-Ḥakam, Ḥammād, and ʿAṭāʾ say lams means touching short of intercourse; reports from Ibn Masʿūd's circle give the same interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r1.anchor: عن الحكم , وحماد، أنهما قالا: «اللمس ما دون الجماع»

TAB-FULL:v7p74/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's view is reported alongside his recitation of the clause about finding no water, linking touch short of intercourse to the need for purification.
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r2.anchor: عن أبي معشر، عن إبراهيم قال: قال عبد الله: الملامسة: ما دون الجماع، ثم قرأ: {أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء}

TAB-FULL:v7p74/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda counts a kiss among the meanings of lams.
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r3.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، قال: «القبلة من اللمس»

TAB-FULL:v7p74/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the report from ʿĀʾisha is sound: the Prophet kissed a wife and prayed without renewing ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r4.anchor: عن عائشة، قالت: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضأ ثم يقبل، ثم يصلي ولا يتوضأ

TAB-FULL:v7p74/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers intercourse as the meaning of lams, not other forms of touch, because the sound report says the Prophet kissed a wife and did not renew ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p74/r5.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال

TAB-FULL:v7p75/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r1.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r1.claim: A report through Zaynab al-Sahmiyya says the Prophet used to kiss and then pray without performing ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r1.anchor: عن زينب السهمية، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أنه كان يقبل، ثم يصلي ولا يتوضأ»

TAB-FULL:v7p75/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r2.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet kissed her after ablution and did not repeat ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r2.anchor: عن أبي روق، عن إبراهيم التيمي، عن عائشة قالت: «كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينال مني القبلة

TAB-FULL:v7p75/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r3.speaker: أم سلمة
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r3.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet kissed her while fasting and neither broke his fast nor performed ablution afterward.
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r3.anchor: عن أم سلمة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقبلها وهو صائم، ثم لا يفطر، ولا يحدث وضوءا

TAB-FULL:v7p75/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī concludes that the sound reports clearly show lams here means intercourse, rather than every sense of touching.
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r4.anchor: ففي صحة الخبر فيما ذكرنا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الدلالة الواضحة على أن اللمس في هذا الموضع لمس الجماع لا جميع معاني اللمس

TAB-FULL:v7p75/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r5.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r5.claim: An unnamed poet uses lamas for intercourse: the line's phrase ننك لميسا means ننك لماسا.
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r5.anchor: إن تصدق الطير ننك لميسا يعني بذلك: ننك لماسا.

TAB-FULL:v7p75/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm reports that wounded Companions became junub and complained to the Prophet; the verse was revealed, and the report says a sick person unable to wash may use tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في المريض لا يستطيع الغسل من الجنابة أو الحائض قال: يجزيهم التيمم، ونال أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جراحة

TAB-FULL:v7p75/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r7.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r7.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that her lost necklace delayed the party at Dhat al-Jaysh; when the Prophet awoke and found no water for prayer, the tayammum verse was revealed, and Usayd praised the blessing to her family.
TAB-FULL:v7p75/r7.anchor: عن عائشة، أنها قالت: كنت في مسير مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، حتى إذا كنا بذات الجيش، ضل عقدي

TAB-FULL:v7p77/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r1.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r1.claim: Ibn Abī Mulayka reports that a lost necklace halted the Prophet's travel party without water; the necklace was found by the camel's resting place, and people praised ʿĀʾisha's blessing after the tayammum verse came down.
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان في سفر، ففقدت عائشة قلادة لها

TAB-FULL:v7p77/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r2.speaker: الأسلع
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r2.claim: Al-Aslaʿ reports that while junub and unable to ready the Prophet's mount, he received the tayammum instruction; Gabriel brought the verse, and the Prophet demonstrated strokes for the face and hands up to the elbows.
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r2.anchor: «يا أسلع قم فأرحل لي» قلت: يا رسول الله أصابتني جنابة. فسكت ساعة

TAB-FULL:v7p77/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās tells ʿĀʾisha that her lost necklace at al-Abwāʾ led to the tayammum verse and the dispensation God granted this community.
TAB-FULL:v7p77/r3.anchor: قال: ثني عبد الله بن عبيد الله بن أبي مليكة أنه حدثه ذكوان أبو عمرو، حاجب عائشة: أن ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v7p79/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r1.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet sent men to look for her borrowed necklace; unable to find water, they prayed without ablution, and the tayammum verse was revealed. Usayd praised her blessing to the Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r1.anchor: عن عائشة: أنها استعارت من أسماء قلادة

TAB-FULL:v7p79/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r2.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r2.claim: In another account, ʿĀʾisha's necklace fell at al-Bayḍāʾ; at morning prayer no water was found, and the account identifies the verse beginning If you rise for prayer as revealed.
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r2.anchor: عن عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنها قالت: سقطت قلادة لي بالبيداء ونحن داخلون إلى المدينة

TAB-FULL:v7p79/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās tells ʿĀʾisha that her lost necklace at al-Abwāʾ made her a great blessing to the Muslims because it occasioned the tayammum verse.
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي مليكة، قال: دخل ابن عباس على عائشة، فقال: كنت أعظم المسلمين بركة على المسلمين

TAB-FULL:v7p79/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r4.speaker: قراء أهل المدينة وبعض البصريين والكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r4.claim: Most Medinan reciters and some Basrans and Kufans read lāmastum, expressing reciprocal touching between a man and his wife.
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r4.anchor: فقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل المدينة وبعض البصريين والكوفيين: {أو لامستم}

TAB-FULL:v7p79/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r5.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r5.claim: Most Kufan reciters read lamastum, phrased as men touching their women.
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r5.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفيين: «أو لمستم النساء» بمعنى: أو لمستم أنتم أيها الرجال نساءكم

TAB-FULL:v7p79/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the readings are close in meaning and either is correct: each expresses touching between the spouses.
TAB-FULL:v7p79/r6.anchor: فبأي القراءتين قرأ ذلك القارئ فمصيب لاتفاق معنييهما

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r1.claim: Tayammum means to intend and head toward something; the verb derives from the expression for intending a destination, with related forms yimimmuhu, ayyamtahu, ammamtuhu, and taʾammamtu.

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r2.speaker: الأعشى
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse uses tayammamtu to mean that he intended and headed for Qays.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r2.anchor: تيممت قيسا وكم دونه … من الأرض من مهمة ذي شزن

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading has fa-ammū ṣaʿīdan, supporting the sense intend or head toward.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر أنها في قراءة عبد الله: فأموا صعيدا

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r4.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r4.claim: Sufyān glosses the command as seeking and deliberately intending clean ṣaʿīd.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r4.anchor: سمعت سفيان، يقول في قوله: فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا قال: «تحروا وتعمدوا صعيدا طيبا»

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r5.claim: Qatāda says ṣaʿīd is barren earth with no trees or vegetation.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: {صعيدا طيبا} [النساء: 43] قال: «التي ليس فيها شجر ولا نبات»

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd defines ṣaʿīd as level ground.

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r7.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الملائي
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r7.claim: ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Mulāʾī says ṣaʿīd means soil.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r7.anchor: ثنا عمرو بن قيس الملائي، قال: " الصعيد: التراب "

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r8.claim: Some define ṣaʿīd simply as the face or surface of the earth.

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r9.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r9.claim: Others restrict ṣaʿīd to the face of the earth bearing soil and dust.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل هو وجه الأرض ذات التراب والغبار.

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers level ground that is the earth's surface, free of vegetation, trees, and buildings; Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses ṣaʿīd for the ground's surface.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r10.anchor: وأولى ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: هو وجه الأرض الخالية من النبات والغروس والبناء المستوية

TAB-FULL:v7p81/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r11.claim: Ṭayyiban means pure and free from filth and impurities.
TAB-FULL:v7p81/r11.anchor: وأما قوله: طيبا، فإنه يعني به: طاهرا من الأقذار والنجاسات

TAB-FULL:v7p82/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r1.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r1.claim: A view transmitted by Sufyān takes ṭayyib as meaning lawful.
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r1.anchor: سمعت سفيان، يقول في قوله: {صعيدا طيبا} [النساء: 43] قال: قال بعضهم: حلالا

TAB-FULL:v7p82/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says ṭayyib means the ground around a person; even barren, hard ground that is not an abṭaḥ suffices for tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قراءة قال: قلت لعطاء: {فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا} [النساء: 43] قال: " الطيب: ما حولك.

TAB-FULL:v7p82/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r3.claim: If people in the listed conditions lack water and intend to pray, they should aim at pure earth and wipe their faces and hands.
TAB-FULL:v7p82/r3.anchor: فإن لم تجدوا ماء أيها الناس، وكنتم مرضى، أو على سفر، أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r1.claim: The command implies wiping with the earth; منه is omitted because the context makes it understood.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r1.anchor: وجهه، فإن كان الذي علق به الغبار كثيرا

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r2.claim: For the face, strike clean earth or its equivalent with the hands and wipe using adhering dust.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r2.anchor: وجهه، فإن كان الذي علق به الغبار كثيرا، فنفخ عن يديه

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r3.claim: Excess dust may be blown or shaken off the hands before wiping.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r3.anchor: فإن كان الذي علق به الغبار كثيرا، فنفخ عن يديه أو نفضه، فهو جائز.

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r4.claim: Tayammum is valid even when no dust adheres: consensus accepts striking sandy ground, showing the command requires contact with earth, not collecting soil.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r4.anchor: لإجماع جميع الحجة على أن المتيمم لو ضرب بيديه الصعيد وهو أرض رمل فلم يعلق بيديه منها شيء

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r5.claim: One view limits the obligatory hand wipe to the palms through the wrists, excluding the forearms.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r5.anchor: فقال بعضهم: حد ذلك الكفان إلى الزندين، وليس على المتيمم مسح ما وراء ذلك من الساعدين

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r6.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r6.claim: Abu Malik reports Ammar struck, wiped his hands against one another and his face, then worked his hands together without wiping the forearms.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r6.anchor: أبي مالك، قال: تيمم عمار فضرب بيديه إلى التراب ضربة واحدة

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r7.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī demonstrated one strike for the face and another for the palms, without mentioning a forearm wipe.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r7.anchor: عن ابن أبي خالد، قال: رأيت الشعبي وصف لنا التيمم

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r8.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r8.claim: Abu Malik reports Ammar struck the soil, blew on his hands, wiped his face and palms, and said this was tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r8.anchor: عن أبي مالك، قال: وضع عمار بن ياسر كفيه في التراب

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r9.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r9.claim: ʿIkrima says tayammum uses two strikes, one for the face and one for the palms.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r9.anchor: عكرمة، يقول: " التيمم ضربتان: ضربة للوجه، وضربة للكفين "

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r10.speaker: مكحول
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r10.claim: Makḥūl limits the wipe to face and palms up to the wrist, arguing that this verse gives no elbow limit as the ablution verse does.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r10.anchor: أن مكحولا، كان يقول: التيمم ضربة للوجه والكفين إلى الكوع

TAB-FULL:v7p83/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r11.speaker: مكحول
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r11.claim: Makḥūl supports the wrist limit by comparing tayammum with the hand cut for theft, severed at the wrist joint.
TAB-FULL:v7p83/r11.anchor: قال مكحول: قال الله: {والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما} [المائدة: 38] فإنما تقطع يد السارق

TAB-FULL:v7p86/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r1.speaker: ابن جابر
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r1.claim: Ibn Jābir saw Makḥūl strike the ground once and wipe his face and palms with that strike.
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r1.anchor: عن ابن جابر: أنه رأى 7659 مكحولا يتيمم يضرب بيديه على الصعيد، ثم يمسح بهما وجهه

TAB-FULL:v7p86/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī states that tayammum is one strike for the face and palms.
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r2.anchor: عن داود، عن الشعبي , قال: التيمم: ضربة للوجه والكفين

TAB-FULL:v7p86/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r3.speaker: رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r3.claim: In response to Ammar, the Prophet is reported to say that one wipe of the palms and face suffices.
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r3.anchor: عن عمار بن ياسر: أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن التيمم، فقال: «مرة للكفين والوجه»

TAB-FULL:v7p86/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r4.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r4.claim: Ammar recalled to ʿUmar that the Prophet taught wiping the face and palms once as sufficient.
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r4.anchor: فقال له عمار: أما تذكر أنا في مسير على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأجنبت

TAB-FULL:v7p86/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r5.claim: Another view requires wiping the whole face and both hands up to the elbows.
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: حد المسح الذي أمر الله به في التيمم أن يمسح جميع الوجه واليدين إلى المرفقين

TAB-FULL:v7p86/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r6.claim: Nāfiʿ reports Ibn ʿUmar practiced two strikes, wiping the face with one and the hands to the elbows with the other.
TAB-FULL:v7p86/r6.anchor: أن ابن عمر، تيمم بمربد النعم، فضرب ضربة فمسح وجهه

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar is reported to prescribe one strike for the face and one for the palms through the elbows.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r1.anchor: ابن عمر في التيمم قال: ضربة للوجه، وضربة للكفين إلى المرفقين

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r2.claim: Another report says Ibn ʿUmar held that the wipe in tayammum reaches the elbows.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r2.anchor: عن عبيد الله، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر قال: كان يقول في المسح في التيمم إلى المرفقين

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan demonstrated wiping the face, then both the outer and inner sides of the forearms after another strike.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r3.anchor: سألت الحسن عن التيمم، فضرب بيديه على الأرض فمسح بهما وجهه، وضرب بيديه فمسح بهما ذراعيه

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r4.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r4.claim: ʿĀmir reasons that tayammum wipes what ablution washes, while omitting the head and feet that ablution wipes.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r4.anchor: عن عامر، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r5.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī is reported to require a strike for the face and another for the hands to the elbows.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r5.anchor: عن داود، عن الشعبي، في التيمم قال: ضربة للوجه، وضربة لليدين إلى المرفقين

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r6.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the tayammum command applies to the limbs commanded to be washed.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r6.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن الشعبي، قال: أمر بالتيمم فيما أمر بالغسل

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r7.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r7.claim: Sālim b. ʿAbd Allāh practiced two strikes, wiping the face and then the hands to the elbows.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r7.anchor: سألت سالم بن عبد الله عن التيمم، فضرب بيديه على الأرض ضربة فمسح بهما وجهه

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to strike once for the face and again to wipe the hands to the elbows.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r8.anchor: عن الحسن، أنه سئل عن التيمم، فقال: ضربة يمسح بها وجهه، ثم ضربة أخرى يمسح بها يديه

TAB-FULL:v7p88/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r9.speaker: القائلون بالمرفقين
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r9.claim: Proponents of the elbow limit treat tayammum as a substitute for ablution and extend earth to the same limits as water.
TAB-FULL:v7p88/r9.anchor: وعلة من قال هذه المقالة أن التيمم بدل من الوضوء على المتيمم أن يبلغ بالتراب من وجهه ويديه

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r1.speaker: أبو جهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r1.claim: Abū Juḥaym reports seeing the Prophet wipe his face and hands to the elbows after urinating, then return his greeting.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r1.anchor: عن أبي جهيم، قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يبول فسلمت عليه فلم يرد علي

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r2.claim: Another group sets the required reach of the hand wipe at the armpits.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: الحد الذي أمر الله أن يبلغ بالتراب إليه في التيمم الآباط

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r3.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r3.claim: Al-Zuhrī states that tayammum extends to the armpits.

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r4.speaker: القائلون بالآباط
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r4.claim: Those favoring the armpits argue that the whole hand must be wiped as the whole face is, and the arm extends from palm to armpit.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r4.anchor: أن الله أمر بمسح اليد في التيمم كما أمر بمسح الوجه، وقد اجمعوا أن عليه أن يمسح جميع الوجه

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r5.speaker: أبو اليقظان
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r5.claim: Abū al-Yaqẓān reports the necklace incident: after the tayammum concession, they struck once for faces and once up to shoulders and armpits.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r5.anchor: عن أبي اليقظان، قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فهلك عقد لعائشة

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r6.claim: The minimum valid hand wipe is palms to wrists by consensus; beyond that, wiping to the elbows or armpits is optional because no further limit is established.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r6.anchor: الكفان إلى الزندين لإجماع الجميع على أن التقصير عن ذلك غير جائز

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r7.claim: The palms-to-wrists minimum is established by consensus; other extents remain disputed, and wiping within the verse’s general wording fulfills the duty.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r7.anchor: وكان الماسح بكفيه داخلا في عموم الآية كان خارجا مما لزمه من فرض ذلك

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r8.speaker: جماعة من أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r8.claim: A broad group of early interpreters holds that a junub person without water may use tayammum like anyone with a lesser ritual impurity.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r8.anchor: فقال جماعة من أهل التأويل من الصحابة والتابعين ومن بعدهم من الخالفين: حكم الجنب فيما لزمه من التيمم

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r9.speaker: جماعة من أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r9.claim: They support the junub person’s concession by transmission from the Prophet, and read لمس النساء here as intercourse.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r9.anchor: بإجماع الحجة على ذلك نقلا عن نبيها صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي يقطع العذر، ويزيل الشك

TAB-FULL:v7p90/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r10.speaker: جماعة من المتقدمين
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r10.claim: Some early authorities deny tayammum to a junub person, requiring water washing and disallowing prayer with dry ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p90/r10.anchor: وقال جماعة من المتقدمين: لا يجزئ الجنب غير الاغتسال بالماء، وليس له أن يصلي بالتيمم

TAB-FULL:v7p92/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r1.speaker: جماعة من المتقدمين
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r1.claim: Those denying tayammum to the junub argue that the verse permits crossing a prayer place until bathing, not dry purification.
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r1.anchor: نهى الله الجنب أن يقرب مصلى المسلمين إلا مجتازا فيه حتى يغتسل

TAB-FULL:v7p92/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r2.speaker: جماعة من المتقدمين
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r2.claim: They interpret touching women as contact by hand, excluding the genitals and sexual intercourse.
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r2.anchor: قالوا: وتأويل قوله: {أو لامستم النساء} [النساء: 43] أو لامستموهن باليد دون الفرج

TAB-FULL:v7p92/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd tells Abū Mūsā that a junub person must not use tayammum even after a month without water.
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r3.anchor: فقال عبد الله: لا يتيمم وإن لم يجد الماء شهرا

TAB-FULL:v7p92/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r4.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r4.claim: Abū Mūsā challenges Ibn Masʿūd’s ruling by invoking the verse commanding tayammum when water is unavailable.
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r4.anchor: فقال أبو موسى: فكيف تصنعون بهذه الآية في سورة المائدة: {فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا}

TAB-FULL:v7p92/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd objects that allowing tayammum would lead people to choose it whenever water felt cold.
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r5.anchor: إن رخص لهم في هذا لأوشكوا إذا برد عليهم الماء أن يتيمموا بالصعيد.

TAB-FULL:v7p92/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r6.speaker: رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r6.claim: Abū Mūsā cites Ammar’s account that the Prophet said one strike and wiping the face and palms sufficed; Ibn Masʿūd notes that ʿUmar did not accept the report.
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r6.anchor: فذكرت ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: «إنما يكفيك أن تصنع هكذا» وضرب بكفيه ضربة واحدة

TAB-FULL:v7p92/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r7.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r7.claim: Ammar recalls that the Prophet said earth sufficed and demonstrated wiping the face and part of the arms; ʿUmar tells him to fear God, then leaves the matter to him.
TAB-FULL:v7p92/r7.anchor: قال عمار بن ياسر: أتذكر يا أمير المؤمنين حيث كنا بمكان كذا وكذا، ونحن نرعى الإبل

TAB-FULL:v7p93/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm says he would not pray if he were junub and could not find water.
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r1.anchor: إبراهيم، في دكان مسلم الأعور، فقلت: أرأيت إن لم تجد الماء وأنت جنب؟

TAB-FULL:v7p93/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r2.claim: The junub person is included in the command to perform tayammum and pray when water is absent; the author reads touching women as intercourse, citing unanimous transmission and prophetic reports.
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r2.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: والصواب من القول في ذلك، أن الجنب ممن أمره الله بالتيمم

TAB-FULL:v7p93/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r3.claim: The dispute is whether tayammum must be renewed whenever water must be sought, even absent a new impurity, or only after impurity.
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r3.anchor: واختلف أهل التأويل في تأويل قوله: {فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا} [النساء: 43] هل ذلك أمر من الله

TAB-FULL:v7p93/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r4.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r4.claim: One view requires fresh tayammum for every prayer after seeking water, whether or not a new impurity occurred.
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r4.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه كان يقول: «التيمم لكل صلاة»

TAB-FULL:v7p93/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ reports the same rule from Ibn ʿUmar: tayammum for each prayer.

TAB-FULL:v7p93/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r6.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says one tayammum may be used for only one prayer.
TAB-FULL:v7p93/r6.anchor: عن الشعبي , قال: «لا يصلى بالتيمم إلا صلاة واحدة»

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r1.claim: Qatāda says to perform tayammum for every prayer, interpreting the verse’s water-search clause accordingly.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " يتيمم لكل صلاة.

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد وعبد الكريم بن ربيعة
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r2.claim: Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd and ʿAbd al-Karīm b. Rabīʿa hold that tayammum is renewed for every prayer.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r2.anchor: عن يحيى بن سعيد، وعبد الكريم بن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن، قالوا: «التيمم لكل صلاة»

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r3.speaker: النخعي
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r3.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī is also reported to require tayammum for every prayer.

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r4.claim: The opposing view treats tayammum like ablution: it remains valid until a new impurity, and finding water then requires ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل ذلك أمر من الله بالتيمم بعد طلب الماء من لزمه فرض الطلب إذا كان محدثا

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says tayammum has the same status as ablution.

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says one may pray with the same tayammum until a new impurity; if water appears, perform ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: «يصلي المتيمم بتيممه ما لم يحدث، فإن وجد الماء فليتوضأ»

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan compares tayammum to ablution, which a person could use for all prayers until invalidated.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r7.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: «يصلي المتيمم بتيممه ما لم يحدث، فإن وجد الماء فليتوضأ»

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r8.claim: A further report from al-Ḥasan says a person may pray multiple prayers with tayammum while no new impurity occurs.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r8.anchor: عن الحسن قال: يصلي الصلوات بالتيمم ما لم يحدث

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r9.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r9.claim: ʿAṭāʾ likewise says tayammum is like ablution.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عطاء، قال: التيمم بمنزلة الوضوء

TAB-FULL:v7p95/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r10.claim: The author prefers a new tayammum for each prayer after seeking water: every person rising to pray is commanded to purify, and the prophetic exemption for prior ablution does not extend to prior tayammum.
TAB-FULL:v7p95/r10.anchor: قول من قال: يتيمم المصلي لكل صلاة لزمه طلب الماء للتطهر لها فرضا

TAB-FULL:v7p97/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p97/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p97/r1.claim: The verse recalls God’s pardoning the believers’ earlier drunken prayer and warns them not to repeat it, lest they incur punishment.
TAB-FULL:v7p97/r1.anchor: فلا تعودوا لمثلها فينالكم بعودكم لما قد نهيتكم عنه من ذلك منكلة

TAB-FULL:v7p97/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p97/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p97/r2.claim: God conceals sins and delays punishment, as He did for their drunken prayer.
TAB-FULL:v7p97/r2.anchor: يستر عليهم ذنوبهم بتركه معاجلتهم العذاب على خطاياهم

SULAMI:v1p149/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p149/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p149/r1.claim: Intoxication includes wine as well as heedlessness, desire, worldly life, wealth, family, children, sins, and even acts of obedience; all can prevent full prayer and standing apart from other concerns.
SULAMI:v1p149/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : السكر على أنواع : منها سكر الخمر وهو أسرعها إفاقة ، وسكر الغفلة وسكر الهوى

SULAMI:v1p149/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p149/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p149/r2.claim: The command means not to approach communion with God unless separated from all contingent beings and everything in them.
SULAMI:v1p149/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله في هذه الآية : لا تقربوا يعني لا تتقربوا إلى مواصلتي ، إلا وأنت منفصل

TABATABAI:4:43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43/r1.claim: Combining the five wine passages yields this sequence: al-Naḥl 16:67, al-Aʿrāf 7:33, al-Nisāʾ 4:43, al-Baqara 2:219, then al-Māʾida 5:90, the last to be revealed.
TABATABAI:4:43/r1.anchor: وأن ضم هذه الآيات بعضها إلى بعض يفيد أن هذه الآية

TABATABAI:4:43/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43/r2.claim: He also considers an alternate sequence: al-Naḥl, al-Aʿrāf, al-Baqara, al-Nisāʾ, then al-Māʾida, implying that the prayer restriction followed the prohibition in al-Baqara.
TABATABAI:4:43/r2.anchor: فتكون النازلة أولا آية النحل ثم الأعراف ثم البقرة ثم النساء ثم المائدة

TABATABAI:4:43/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43/r3.claim: He favors the first chronology: the explicit prohibition in al-Baqara makes it unlikely that this later prayer-only restriction came afterward, unless intoxication means sluggishness in prayer as some reports say.
TABATABAI:4:43/r3.anchor: ولعلك إن تدبرت في مضامين الآيات رجحت الترتيب السابق على هذا الترتيب

TABATABAI:4:43/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43/r4.claim: An apparent insertion can occur when verses with one connected context descend gradually and another verse is sent down as a need arises; it may clarify a point rather than be unrelated.
TABATABAI:4:43/r4.anchor: وهو جواز أن تتنزل عدة من الآيات ذات سياق واحد متصل منسجم تدريجا في خلال أيام ثم تمس الحاجة إلى نزول آية أو آيات

TABATABAI:4:43#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r1.claim: He illustrates an inserted passage with al-Qiyāma 75:14–20, where the command not to move the tongue interrupts the surrounding sequence.
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r1.anchor: لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به

TABATABAI:4:43#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r2.claim: There is no need to force a link to adjacent verses: the Qur'an descended in installments, and coherence is required only for passages revealed together or clearly connected.
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا فلا حاجة إلى التكلف في بيان وجه ارتباط الآية بما قبلها وارتباط ما بعدها بها

TABATABAI:4:43#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r3.claim: Al-ṣalāt here means the mosque, because the exception for passers-through fits a rule about a junub entering the mosque.
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى { يا أيها الذين آمنوا } إلى قوله { ما تقولون } المراد بالصلاة المسجد

TABATABAI:4:43#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r4.claim: The stated reason evokes prayer as standing before divine majesty and speaking to the Lord; intoxication destroys the reason and prevents awareness of one's words.
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r4.anchor: في حال الصلاة تواجهون مقام العظمة والكبرياء وتخاطبون رب العالمين فلا يصلح لكم أن تسكروا

TABATABAI:4:43#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r5.claim: Because prayers were commonly performed congregationally in mosques and the verse also addresses a junub's mosque entry, its wording is compressed in this way.
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r5.anchor: لما كانت أكثر ما تقع تقع في المسجد جماعة

TABATABAI:4:43#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r6.claim: Until you know what you say gives the reason for avoiding drink that leaves one intoxicated at prayer time; it is not an endpoint after which drinking to intoxication is allowed.
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r6.anchor: لغاية أن تعلموا ما تقولون وليس غاية للحكم

TABATABAI:4:43#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r7.claim: He defers detailed discussion of the junub and tayammum rulings to the commentary on al-Māʾida 5:6.
TABATABAI:4:43#2/r7.anchor: سيأتي الكلام في الآية في تفسير قوله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r1.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits from Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl from Abu al-Ḥasan that this verse came before wine was prohibited; no grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن الفضل عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام في قول الله { لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون } قال هذا قبل أن تحرم الخمر

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r2.claim: He reads the report as referring to explicit clarification of wine's prohibition; otherwise it conflicts with al-Aʿrāf 7:33 and al-Baqara 2:219, which already call wine sin, and with their Meccan and Medinan chronology.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r2.anchor: ينبغي أن تحمل الرواية على أن المراد بتحريم الخمر توضيح تحريمها وإلا فهي مخالفة للكتاب

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r3.claim: Since al-Aʿrāf is Meccan and al-Nisāʾ is Medinan, wine was prohibited in Mecca under the earlier verses; no one disputes this verse's Medinan status.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r3.anchor: فقد حرمت الخمر في مكة قبل الهجرة لكون سورة الأعراف مكية ولم يختلف أحد في أن هذه الآية آية النساء مدنية

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r4.speaker: روايات من طرق أهل السنة
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r4.claim: Several Sunni reports likewise say the verse preceded wine's prohibition; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī allows that they may mean the prohibition of praying sluggishly.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r4.anchor: ومثل هذه الرواية عدة روايات من طرق أهل السنة تصرح بكون الآية نازلة قبل تحريم الخمر

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r5.claim: Zurāra reports from al-Bāqir: do not rise for prayer lazily, drowsily, or heavily, since this is a trait of hypocrisy; the drunkenness meant is sleep. No grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r5.anchor: عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال لا تقم إلى الصلاة متكاسلا ولا متناعسا ولا متثاقلا فإنها من خلل النفاق

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r6.claim: The Imam infers the hypocrisy warning from the address to believers: one who defies that address is not truly a believer.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r6.anchor: فالمتمرد عن هذا الخطاب منافق غير مؤمن

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r7.claim: The phrase meaning from sleep may be the narrator's gloss or the Imam's; if the Imam's, it may be an inner reading or the verse's outward meaning.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r7.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون من كلام الراوي ويحتمل أن يكون من كلامه عليه السلام ويكون تفسيرا للآية من قبيل بطن القرآن

TABATABAI:4:43#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r8.speaker: الحلبي وزيد الشحام وزرارة وأنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r8.claim: Other sleep interpretations are transmitted by al-Ḥalabī in two reports, al-Kulaynī from Zayd al-Shahhām and Zurāra from the Imams, and al-Bukhārī from Anas from the Prophet; no grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:43#3/r8.anchor: رواها العياشي في تفسيره عن الحلبي في روايتين والكليني في الكافي بإسناده عن زيد الشحام عن الصادق

AKHFASH:v1p258/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p258/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p258/r3.claim: جنبا is singular in form but applies to plural men and women; فعول and فعيل can be singular forms for duals and plurals, as in the cited examples.

AKHFASH:v1p258/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p258/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p258/r4.claim: ولا جنبا is coordinated with the circumstantial وأنتم سكارى: do not approach prayer while in major impurity, except as travelers passing through.
AKHFASH:v1p258/r4.anchor: قوله {وأنتم سكارى} في موضع نصب على الحال، فقال {ولا جنبا} على العطف

TABRISI:4:43/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
TABRISI:4:43/r1.claim: The Kufans except Asim read لمستم without an alif here and in al-Maida.
TABRISI:4:43/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم أو لمستم بغير ألف ههنا، وفي المائدة

TABRISI:4:43/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:4:43/r2.claim: The other readers use the alif form لامستم; form III can carry the sense of form I.

TABRISI:4:43/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r3.claim: The argument for لمستم points to Quranic uses of form I touch, including phrases about Paradise’s women and Mary not being touched by a man.
TABRISI:4:43/r3.anchor: حجة من قرأ لمستم إن هذا المعنى جاء في التنزيل على فعلتم

TABRISI:4:43/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r4.claim: Qaraba can be transitive or intransitive; qurb al-maʾ means to approach or reach water.
TABRISI:4:43/r4.anchor: يقال قرب يقرب متعد وقرب يقرب لازم وقرب الماء يقربه إذا ورده

TABRISI:4:43/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r5.claim: Sukr derives from blocking a water channel; intoxication blocks the path of understanding, and sakrat al-mawt means death’s swoon.
TABRISI:4:43/r5.anchor: وأصل السكر من السكر، وهو سد مجرى الماء، واسم الموضع السكر

TABRISI:4:43/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r6.claim: The forms for a man are sakran and plural sukara; a woman is also described as sukra.
TABRISI:4:43/r6.anchor: ورجل سكران من قوم سكارى، وسكرى. والمرأة سكرى أيضا.

TABRISI:4:43/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r7.claim: Junub applies to male or female, singular or plural, describing a person in janaba.
TABRISI:4:43/r7.anchor: ويقال رجل جنب إذا جنب ويستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث الواحد والجمع

TABRISI:4:43/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r8.claim: Abir means crossing from one side of a river or road to the other.
TABRISI:4:43/r8.anchor: عبرت النهر والطريق عبورا إذا قطعته من هذا الجانب إلى الجانب الآخر

TABRISI:4:43/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r9.claim: Ghait means a low place where people relieved themselves out of sight; its name became a euphemism for the act or result. Another account says it was named for what people discarded there; Murajj defines it as a basin ringed by hills.
TABRISI:4:43/r9.anchor: وكانوا يتبرزون هناك ليغيبوا عن عيون الناس ثم كثر ذلك حتى قالوا للحدث غائط

TABRISI:4:43/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r10.claim: Touch first referred to the hand and then broadened beyond literal contact; iltamas means to seek.
TABRISI:4:43/r10.anchor: واللمس: يكون باليد ثم اتسع فيه فأوقع على غيره

TABRISI:4:43/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r11.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:4:43/r11.claim: The cited verse’s explanation says talmas means seek.
TABRISI:4:43/r11.anchor: أراد أيهم تطلب وملتمس المعروف طالبه

TABRISI:4:43/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r12.claim: Tayammum means intending; in law it is the specific act of aiming at the earth and applying soil to designated limbs.
TABRISI:4:43/r12.anchor: والتيمم القصد ومثله التأمم قال الأعشى

TABRISI:4:43/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r13.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:4:43/r13.claim: Al-Asha’s verse uses tayaammamtu to mean that he set out for or intended Qays despite rugged country between.
TABRISI:4:43/r13.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
تيممت قيسا وكم دونه

TABRISI:4:43/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r14.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:4:43/r14.claim: A second cited verse uses tayaammamtu to mean intending a home.
TABRISI:4:43/r14.anchor:
وقال آخر:
تيممت دارا ويممن دارا

TABRISI:4:43/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43/r15.claim: Saʿid is the earth’s surface without vegetation or trees.
TABRISI:4:43/r15.anchor: والصعيد وجه الأرض من غير نبات ولا شجر وقال ذو الرمة

TABRISI:4:43#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r1.speaker: ذو الرمة
TABRISI:4:43#2/r1.claim: Dhu al-Rumma’s simile uses saʿid for the earth’s surface, where a fly strikes with its proboscis at midday.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r1.anchor: كأنه بالضحى ترمي الصعيد به ذبابة في عظام الرأس خرطوم

TABRISI:4:43#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:4:43#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says saʿid is the earth’s surface, whether soil or another material, named for the farthest surface one rises to from the earth’s interior.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الصعيد ليس هو التراب إنما هو وجه الأرض ترابا كان أو غيره

TABRISI:4:43#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#2/r3.claim: The clause is circumstantial, governed by taqrabu, with the address pronoun as its subject.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r3.anchor: وأنتم سكارى جملة منصوبة الموضع على الحال

TABRISI:4:43#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#2/r4.claim: Junuban is coordinated with the preceding circumstantial phrase and means a plural group; abiri sabil is an accusative exception.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r4.anchor: جنبا إنما انتصب لكونه عطفا عليه والمراد به الجمع

TABRISI:4:43#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#2/r5.claim: Taʿlamu is subjunctive after an implicit أن governed by حتى, with the final nūn dropped.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r5.anchor: وتعلموا منصوب بإضمار أن وعلامة النصب سقوط النون

TABRISI:4:43#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#2/r6.claim: On a journey is accusative by coordination with sick, understood as or while traveling.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r6.anchor: على سفر في موضع نصب عطفا على قوله:

TABRISI:4:43#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#2/r7.claim: After commanding worship in the previous verse, God next mentions prayer as one of the greatest acts of worship.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r7.anchor: لما أمر سبحانه في الآية المتقدمة بالعبادة ذكر عقيبها ما هو من أكبر العبادات

TABRISI:4:43#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وابن زيد
TABRISI:4:43#2/r8.claim: One interpretation is do not perform prayer while intoxicated.

TABRISI:4:43#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r9.speaker: عبد الله وسعيد بن المسيب والضحاك وعكرمة والحسن
TABRISI:4:43#2/r9.claim: Another interpretation is do not approach mosques for prayer or otherwise; the exception for passing supports this because crossing is physical movement through a place.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r9.anchor: معناه لا تقربوا أماكن الصلاة أي المساجد

TABRISI:4:43#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:4:43#2/r10.claim: The intoxication means drunkenness from wine, later abrogated by wine’s prohibition; the account is also related from Musa ibn Jaʿfar.

TABRISI:4:43#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#2/r11.claim: One answer says some intoxication leaves enough reason for commands; another says the prohibition is against exposing oneself to intoxication when prayer is due.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r11.anchor: أنه قد يكون سكران من غير أن يخرج

TABRISI:4:43#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r12.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:4:43#2/r12.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says they must repeat a prayer performed while intoxicated.
TABRISI:4:43#2/r12.anchor: وأجاب أبو علي الجبائي بجواب ثالث وهو أن النهي إنما دل على إعادة الصلاة

TABRISI:4:43#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#2/r13.speaker: الضحاك وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:4:43#2/r13.claim: Another view takes intoxication to mean sleepiness; Aisha reports the Prophet told a drowsy worshipper to leave in case he unknowingly prayed against himself.

TABRISI:4:43#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#3/r1.claim: The condition means discerning what one says; another explanation is retaining what one recites from the Quran.
TABRISI:4:43#3/r1.anchor: أي حتى تميزوا ما تقولون من الكلام

TABRISI:4:43#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#3/r2.speaker: علي وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
TABRISI:4:43#3/r2.claim: One interpretation forbids prayer in janaba except for travelers, who may pray using tayammum even though it does not remove janaba.
TABRISI:4:43#3/r2.anchor: أن المراد به لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم جنب إلا أن تكونوا مسافرين

TABRISI:4:43#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#3/r3.speaker: جابر والحسن وعطاء والزهري وإبراهيم
TABRISI:4:43#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation forbids a person in janaba from entering mosques except to pass through; it is also reported from Abu Jaʿfar.
TABRISI:4:43#3/r3.anchor: لا تقربوا مواضع الصلاة من المساجد وأنتم جنب إلا مجتازين

TABRISI:4:43#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#3/r4.claim: Al-Tabrisi prefers the mosque-entry interpretation: the ending already gives the junub’s rule when water is unavailable, so reading the opening as prayer would repeat that rule.
TABRISI:4:43#3/r4.anchor: وهذا القول الأخير أقوى لأنه سبحانه بين حكم الجنب في آخر الآية

TABRISI:4:43#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r1.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about an ill man from the Ansar who could not rise to perform ablution.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r1.anchor: قيل: نزلت في رجل من الأنصار كان مريضا

TABRISI:4:43#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود والسدي والضحاك ومجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:4:43#4/r2.claim: One view permits tayammum for wounds, fractures, and sores when the person fears harm from water.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r2.anchor: فالمرض الذي يجوز معه التيمم مرض الجراح، والكسر، والقروح

TABRISI:4:43#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
TABRISI:4:43#4/r3.claim: Another view permits it when illness makes someone unable to handle water and no one can bring it; Hasan did not allow an injured person to use tayammum.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r3.anchor: هو المرض الذي لا يستطيع معه تناول الماء ولا يكون هناك من يناوله

TABRISI:4:43#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r4.speaker: السيدان الباقر والصادق
TABRISI:4:43#4/r4.claim: Al-Baqir and al-Sadiq are reported to permit tayammum in all the foregoing circumstances.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r4.anchor: والمروي عن السيدين الباقر والصادق ع جواز التيمم في جميع ذلك

TABRISI:4:43#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r5.claim: The phrase means that you are travelers.

TABRISI:4:43#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r6.claim: Coming from the ghait is a euphemism for relieving oneself; or can mean and, because illness and travel permit tayammum while using the toilet requires purification.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r6.anchor: وهو كناية عن قضاء الحاجة. قيل: إن أو ههنا بمعنى الواو

TABRISI:4:43#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r7.speaker: علي وابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وقتادة
TABRISI:4:43#4/r7.claim: One interpretation takes touching women to mean intercourse; Abu Hanifa and al-Jubbaʾi adopt it.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r7.anchor: المراد به الجماع عن علي ع وابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وقتادة واختاره أبو حنيفة

TABRISI:4:43#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود والشعبي وعطاء
TABRISI:4:43#4/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes it as touching a woman by hand or otherwise; al-Shafiʿi adopts this view.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r8.anchor: المراد به اللمس باليد وغيرها عن عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود والشعبي

TABRISI:4:43#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r9.claim: Al-Tabrisi prefers intercourse: the verse already addresses the junub when water is present and must state the junub’s rule when absent as well as the rule for one who relieved himself.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r9.anchor: والصحيح الأول، لأن الله سبحانه بين حكم الجنب في حال وجود الماء

TABRISI:4:43#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r10.claim: Touching and mutual touch have the same meaning, since one cannot touch a woman without her touching him.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r10.anchor: واللمس والملامسة معناهما واحد لأنه لا يلمسها إلا وهي تلمسه

TABRISI:4:43#4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:4:43#4/r11.claim: When Arabs and non-Arabs disagreed whether it meant intercourse or touching, Ibn Abbas said the non-Arabs were right: it means intercourse, called touch because it leads to intercourse.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r11.anchor: فارتفعت أصواتهم إلى ابن عباس. فقال: غلب الموالي.

TABRISI:4:43#4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r12.claim: The condition covers sick people and travelers: a traveler lacks water, while a sick person may have no one to wash him or fear harm from water.

TABRISI:4:43#4/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r13.claim: Tayammamu means deliberately aim, seek, and intend.

TABRISI:4:43#4/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r14.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:4:43#4/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj says linguists agree saʿid is the earth’s surface, supporting the view that tayammum is valid using stone even without soil.
TABRISI:4:43#4/r14.anchor: قال الزجاج: لا أعلم خلافا بين أهل اللغة في أن الصعيد وجه الأرض

TABRISI:4:43#4/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#4/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#4/r15.anchor: وهذا يوافق مذهب أصحابنا في أن التيمم يجوز بالحجر سواء كان عليه تراب أو لم يكن { طيبا } أي طاهرا

TABRISI:4:43#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r2.claim: Another gloss takes ṭayyib as productive soil, contrasted with barren salt land, as in 7:58.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r2.anchor: وقيل: منبتا عن السبخة التي لا تنبت كقوله:

TABRISI:4:43#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r3.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء وأبو حنيفة والشافعي
TABRISI:4:43#5/r3.claim: Most jurists, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafiʿi, and some of al-Tabrisi’s school require one strike, wiping the hands to the elbows.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r3.anchor: أنه ضربة لليدين إلى المرفقين وهو قول أكثر الفقهاء وأبي حنيفة والشافعي

TABRISI:4:43#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r4.speaker: عمار بن ياسر ومكحول والطبري
TABRISI:4:43#5/r4.claim: Ammar and Makhul hold for two strikes, one for the face and one for the hands to the wrists; al-Tabari prefers this view.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r4.anchor: وثانيها: أنه ضربة للوجه، وضربة لليدين من الزندين وإليه ذهب عمار بن ياسر، ومكحول، واختاره الطبري

TABRISI:4:43#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r5.claim: Al-Tabrisi’s school uses that two-strike method when tayammum replaces the major ablution after sexual impurity.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r5.anchor: وهو مذهبنا في التيمم إذا كان بدلا من الجنابة

TABRISI:4:43#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TABRISI:4:43#5/r6.claim: A report from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says one strike suffices when tayammum replaces wudu: wipe the face from hairline to nose tip and hands from wrists to fingertips.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r6.anchor: يمسح بها وجهه من قصاص شعره إلى طرف أنفه ويديه من زنديه إلى أطراف أصابعهما وهو المروي عن سعيد بن المسيب

TABRISI:4:43#5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r7.speaker: الزهري
TABRISI:4:43#5/r7.claim: Al-Zuhri reports a third view: wipe to the armpits.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r7.anchor: وثالثها: أنه إلى الإبطين عن الزهري.

TABRISI:4:43#5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r8.claim: God accepts the concession of tayammum in place of wudu, making the obligation easier.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r8.anchor: يقبل منكم العفو لأن في قبوله التيمم بدلا من الوضوء تسهيل الأمر علينا

TABRISI:4:43#5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:43#5/r9.claim: An alternative gloss takes ʿafūw as abundant pardon and forbearance.

TABRISI:4:43#5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r10.claim: Ghafūr describes God as frequently covering the sins of His servants.

TABRISI:4:43#5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r11.claim: The verse shows that a drunk person’s prayer is invalid.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r11.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن السكران لا تصح صلاته

TABRISI:4:43#5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r12.claim: Consensus requires the intoxicated person to make up the prayer.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r12.anchor: وقد حصل الإجماع على أنه يلزمه القضاء ولا يصح

TABRISI:4:43#5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r13.claim: A drunk person’s contracts, including marriage, sale, and purchase, are invalid; acts that terminate contracts are also ineffective except for the disputed case of divorce.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r13.anchor: ولا يصح من السكران شيء من العقود كالنكاح والبيع والشراء

TABRISI:4:43#5/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
TABRISI:4:43#5/r14.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that a drunk person’s divorce takes effect.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r14.anchor: وفي الطلاق خلاف بين الفريقين فعند أبي حنيفة يقع طلاقه

TABRISI:4:43#5/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r15.speaker: الشافعي
TABRISI:4:43#5/r15.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds in one of his two positions that a drunk person’s divorce does not take effect.
