TABRISI:4:43#5/r15.anchor: وعند الشافعي لا يقع في أحد القولين فأما ما يلزم به الحدود

TABRISI:4:43#5/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:43#5/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:43#5/r16.claim: In al-Tabrisi’s school, a drunk person remains liable to all fixed penalties and retaliation, including amputation for theft and punishment for slander or adultery, based on general verses and the school’s consensus.
TABRISI:4:43#5/r16.anchor: فعندنا أنه يلزمه جميع ذلك فيقطع بالسرقة، ويحد بالقذف والزنى

FARRA:v1p268/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r9.speaker: أصحاب محمد
FARRA:v1p268/r9.claim: The verse was revealed after some Companions drank and came to prayer with the Prophet before wine was finally prohibited.
FARRA:v1p268/r9.anchor: نزلت في نفر من أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم شربوا وحضروا الصلاة

FARRA:v1p268/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r10.claim: They were told not to approach prayer with the Prophet while intoxicated, but to pray in their own homes.
FARRA:v1p268/r10.anchor: لا تقربوا الصلاة مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولكن صلوها

FARRA:v1p268/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r11.claim: A person in major ritual impurity may not approach prayer until washing, except while traveling and unable to find water.
FARRA:v1p268/r11.anchor: ثم قال ولا جنبا أي لا تقربوها جنبا حتى تغتسلوا.

FARRA:v1p268/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r12.claim: The exception is a traveler unable to find water.
FARRA:v1p268/r12.anchor: إلا عابري سبيل يقول: إلا أن تكونوا مسافرين لا تقدرون على الماء

FARRA:v1p268/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r13.claim: Tayammum means intending clean earth wherever it may be found.
FARRA:v1p268/r13.anchor: ثم قال فتيمموا والتيمم: أن تقصد الصعد الطيب حيث كان.

FARRA:v1p268/r14.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r14.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r14.claim: Tayammum consists of one strike for the face and one for the hands, for a person in major impurity or otherwise.
FARRA:v1p268/r14.anchor: وليس التيمم إلا ضربة للوجه وضربة لليدين للجنب وغير الجنب.

THALABI:v3p311#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p311#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Companions who drank wine and came to prayer intoxicated, unable to tell how many units they prayed or what they said.
THALABI:v3p311#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا يشربون الخمرة

THALABI:v3p311#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p311#2/r2.claim: The word means intoxicated with wine; سكارى is the plural of سكران.

THALABI:v3p311#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
THALABI:v3p311#2/r3.claim: Al-Nakha'i reads جنبًا as another of the two Arabic forms for the word.

THALABI:v3p312/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p312/r1.claim: The phrase means knowing and reciting what one says in prayer; after this verse they avoided intoxication at prayer times until wine was prohibited in al-Ma'idah.
THALABI:v3p312/r1.anchor: حتى تعلموا ما تقولون وتقرؤون في صلاتكم، وكانوا بعد نزول هذه الآية

THALABI:v3p312/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r2.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
THALABI:v3p312/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the drunkenness here as sleepiness, not wine intoxication.
THALABI:v3p312/r2.anchor: سلمة بن نبيط عن الضحاك بن مزاحم: لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى، قال

THALABI:v3p312/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r3.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p312/r3.claim: The Prophet said that a person who becomes drowsy in prayer should sleep until alert, lest he seek forgiveness while actually cursing himself.
THALABI:v3p312/r3.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا نعس أحدكم وهو في الصلاة،

THALABI:v3p312/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r4.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p312/r4.claim: The Prophet said a sleepy person praying should leave, since he might unknowingly pray against himself.
THALABI:v3p312/r4.anchor: عن عائشة، قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا نعس الرجل وهو يصلي، فلينصرف

THALABI:v3p312/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v3p312/r5.claim: The Prophet said that if a night worshipper's tongue stumbles over the Qur'an and he does not know what he is saying, he should lie down.
THALABI:v3p312/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا قام أحدكم من الليل

THALABI:v3p312/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r6.speaker: عبيدة السلماني
THALABI:v3p312/r6.claim: Ubayda al-Salmani says the verse includes a person holding back urine; he cites the prohibition on praying while resisting the two impurities.
THALABI:v3p312/r6.anchor: عبيدة السلماني في هذه الآية أنه قال: هو الحاقن

THALABI:v3p312/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p312/r7.claim: جنبًا is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier: do not approach prayer while in a state of major ritual impurity.
THALABI:v3p312/r7.anchor: ولا جنبا نصب على الحال، يعني ولا تقربوا الصلاة

THALABI:v3p312/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r8.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
THALABI:v3p312/r8.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i reads جنبًا with a quiescent nun.

THALABI:v3p312/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p312/r9.claim: جنب is used unchanged for a man, two people, women, and groups; its verb is أجنب يجنب, and janābah is named for distance because the impure person keeps away until purified.
THALABI:v3p312/r9.anchor: يقال: رجل جنب، ورجلان وامرأتان جنب، ورجال ونساء جنب

THALABI:v3p312/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r10.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن جبير وابن زيد ومجاهد والحكم والحسن بن مسلم وابن كثير
THALABI:v3p312/r10.claim: One group understands the exception as travelers who lack water, allowing them to use dry ablution.
THALABI:v3p312/r10.anchor: فقال: بعضهم: الا إن يكونوا مسافرين ولا يجدون الماء فيتيمموا، وهذا قول علي

THALABI:v3p312/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r11.speaker: عبد الله وابن المسيب وابن يسار والضحاك والحسن وعكرمة وإبراهيم وعطاء الخراساني والنخعي والزيدي
THALABI:v3p312/r11.claim: Another group takes the exception to mean passing through a mosque without remaining there while in major impurity; here الصلاة means the mosque or prayer place.
THALABI:v3p312/r11.anchor: وقال الآخرون: معناه إلا مجتازين فيه للخروج منه مثل أن ينام في المسجد، فيجنب

THALABI:v3p312/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p312/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p312/r12.claim: Ansar whose doors opened into the mosque became impure and lacked another route to water; the report explains the permission to pass through.
THALABI:v3p312/r12.anchor: ما روى الليث عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب أن رجالا من الأنصار كانت أبوابهم في المسجد

THALABI:v3p313/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p313/r1.claim: The root sense of عبور is crossing or traversing; one says a person crossed a road or river when passing through it.
THALABI:v3p313/r1.anchor: وأصل العبور: القطع يقال: عبر الطريق والنهر إذا قطعهما

THALABI:v3p313/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p313/r2.claim: مرضى is the plural of مريض.

THALABI:v3p313/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r3.speaker: أم سلمة
THALABI:v3p313/r3.claim: A report from Umm Salama says the Prophet declared his mosque forbidden to menstruating women and men in major impurity, except Muhammad and his family: Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn.
THALABI:v3p313/r3.anchor: عن أم سلمة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألا إن مسجدي حرام على كل حائض

THALABI:v3p313/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r4.speaker: جماعة من الفقهاء
THALABI:v3p313/r4.claim: Jurists allow dry ablution for illnesses harmed by water, including smallpox, wounds, sores, and a fracture covered with splints.
THALABI:v3p313/r4.anchor: وأراد به مرضا يضره مساس الماء كالجدري والجروح والقروح، أو كسر قد وضع عليه الجبائر

THALABI:v3p313/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r5.speaker: عطاء والحسن
THALABI:v3p313/r5.claim: Ata and al-Hasan deny dry ablution when water is available, citing the verse's condition that water not be found.
THALABI:v3p313/r5.anchor: عطاء والحسن أنه لا يتيمم مع وجود الماء، واحتجا بقوله تعالى فلم تجدوا ماء

THALABI:v3p313/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r6.speaker: جابر
THALABI:v3p313/r6.claim: Jabir recounts that an injured man in a campaign washed after a wet dream despite his companions' advice and died; the Prophet condemned them and prescribed dry ablution, a wound covering, wiping it, and washing the rest.
THALABI:v3p313/r6.anchor: روى عطاء عن جابر قال: خرجنا في سفر وأصاب رجلا معنا حجر فشجه في رأسه

THALABI:v3p313/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p313/r7.claim: The author rejects Ata and al-Hasan's restriction, using the Prophet's instruction to the injured man to show that harmful water may be avoided even when present.
THALABI:v3p313/r7.anchor: وهذا غلط، لما روى عطاء عن جابر قال: خرجنا في سفر وأصاب رجلا معنا حجر

THALABI:v3p313/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p313/r8.claim: Travel permits dry ablution when water is lacking, whether the journey is long or short.
THALABI:v3p313/r8.anchor: أو على سفر طويلا كان أو قصيرا، فله التيمم عند عدم الماء

THALABI:v3p313/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r9.speaker: الشافعي ومحمد بن الحسن
THALABI:v3p313/r9.claim: If water unexpectedly disappears in a city or village, al-Shafi'i and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan require dry ablution and prayer, followed by repeating the prayer.
THALABI:v3p313/r9.anchor: ففيه ثلاث مذاهب: ذهب الشافعي ومحمد بن الحسن إلى أن عليه التيمم والصلاة ويعيد الصلاة

THALABI:v3p313/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r10.speaker: مالك والأوزاعي وأبو يوسف
THALABI:v3p313/r10.claim: Malik, al-Awza'i, and Abu Yusuf require dry ablution and prayer in this case, without repeating it later.
THALABI:v3p313/r10.anchor: وذهب مالك والأوزاعي وأبو يوسف إلى إنه يتيمم ويصلي ولا إعادة عليه،

THALABI:v3p313/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
THALABI:v3p313/r11.claim: Abu Hanifa says not to use dry ablution or pray in this situation; wait until water is found, perform ablution, and then pray.
THALABI:v3p313/r11.anchor: وذهب أبو حنيفة إلى أنه لا يتيمم ولا يصلي، ولكنه يصبر حتى يجد الماء

THALABI:v3p313/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r12.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v3p313/r12.claim: Al-Zuhri reads الغيط instead of الغائط.
THALABI:v3p313/r12.anchor: قرأ الزهري: (من الغيط) ، والغيط والغوط والغائط كلها بمعنى واحد

THALABI:v3p313/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r13.speaker: مجاهد والحسن والمؤرخ
THALABI:v3p313/r13.claim: The related forms الغيط, الغوط, and الغائط denote low ground: Mujahid says a valley, al-Hasan a valley's hollow, and al-Mu'arrikh a concealed low basin surrounded by vines.
THALABI:v3p313/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو الوادي، الحسن: الغور من الأودية، وتصوب . المؤرخ: قرارة من الأرض

THALABI:v3p313/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p313/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p313/r14.claim: Because people relieved themselves in such secluded low places, الغائط became a euphemism for bowel needs; its plural is غيطان, with the verbs غاط يغوط and تغوط يتغوط.
THALABI:v3p313/r14.anchor: وكانوا يتبرزون هناك فكنى عن الحديث بالغائط مثل العذرة والحدث، وهو هاهنا كناية

THALABI:v3p314/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
THALABI:v3p314/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read لمستم without the alif here and in al-Ma'idah; Abu Ubayd prefers this reading.
THALABI:v3p314/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف: (لمستم) . بغير ألف هاهنا، وفي المائدة

THALABI:v3p314/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r2.speaker: الباقون وأبو حاتم
THALABI:v3p314/r2.claim: The remaining readers retain the alif in both places, the reading preferred by Abu Hatim.
THALABI:v3p314/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالألف فيهما وهو اختيار أبي حاتم.

THALABI:v3p314/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
THALABI:v3p314/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada interpret touching women as sexual intercourse.
THALABI:v3p314/r3.anchor: فقال قوم: المجامعة، وهو قول ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

THALABI:v3p314/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p314/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Sa'id ibn Jubayr that the Arabs' interpretation prevailed: touch, contact, and direct intimacy are euphemisms for intercourse, since touch leads to it; he compares cloud and rain both being called sky, as in the cited verse.
THALABI:v3p314/r4.anchor: فأتيت ابن عباس فذكرت له، فقال: من أي الفريقين كنت؟ قلت: من الموالي. قال: غلب فريق الموالي

THALABI:v3p314/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر وأبو عبيدة ومنصور وعبيدة والشعبي والنخعي وحماد والحكم
THALABI:v3p314/r5.claim: Another group interprets touching as contact between the two skins, whether or not intercourse occurs.
THALABI:v3p314/r5.anchor: وقال الآخرون: هو التقاء البشرتين سواء كان بجماع أو غير جماع، وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عمر

THALABI:v3p314/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r6.speaker: الشافعي وابن مسعود وابن عمر والزهري وربيعة
THALABI:v3p314/r6.claim: Al-Shafi'i and the listed authorities hold that a man's touching any part of a woman's body, by hand or otherwise, invalidates ablution.
THALABI:v3p314/r6.anchor: فقال الشافعي: إذا أفضى الرجل بشيء من بدنه إلى شيء من بدن المرأة سواء كان باليد

THALABI:v3p314/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي
THALABI:v3p314/r7.claim: Al-Awza'i says touching with the hand invalidates ablution, but contact with another part of the body does not, by analogy with touching the genitals.
THALABI:v3p314/r7.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي: إن كان للمس باليد نقض الطهر، وإن كان بغير اليد لم ينقضه

THALABI:v3p314/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r8.speaker: مالك والليث بن سعد وأحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق بن راهويه
THALABI:v3p314/r8.claim: Malik, al-Layth, Ahmad, and Ishaq say lustful touching invalidates ablution, while touch without desire does not.
THALABI:v3p314/r8.anchor: وقال مالك والليث بن سعد، وأحمد بن حنبل، وإسحاق بن راهويه: إذا كان اللمس للشهوة

THALABI:v3p314/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف
THALABI:v3p314/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf require an obscene, desire-arousing contact for ablution to be invalidated.
THALABI:v3p314/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف: إن كانت ملامسة فاحشة نقضت وإلا لم تنقض،

THALABI:v3p314/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p314/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن البصري ومحمد بن الحسين
THALABI:v3p314/r10.claim: A group, including Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, holds that touching never invalidates ablution.
THALABI:v3p314/r10.anchor: وذهبت طائفة إلى إن الملامسة لا تنقض الطهارة بحال، وبه قال من الصحابة ابن عباس

THALABI:v3p315/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r1.speaker: الثوري
THALABI:v3p315/r1.claim: Al-Thawri has two reports: one follows the view that touch does not invalidate ablution, while the other follows Malik's view that touch of the hand does.
THALABI:v3p315/r1.anchor: وعن الثوري روايتان: إحداهما هذا ، والثانية مثل

THALABI:v3p315/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r2.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v3p315/r2.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues that لمس most often means hand contact, citing the Prophetic prohibition on mulamasa sales and a poem using لمس for touching with the palm.
THALABI:v3p315/r2.anchor: واللمس أكثر ما يستعمل في لمس اليد، وأنشد الشافعي:

THALABI:v3p315/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r3.speaker: أبيه
THALABI:v3p315/r3.claim: A report says he touched her with his hand, supporting the hand-contact sense of mulamasa.
THALABI:v3p315/r3.anchor: روى الزهري عن سالم عن أبيه قال: جسها بيده من الملامسة

THALABI:v3p315/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r4.speaker: معاذ
THALABI:v3p315/r4.claim: Muadh reports that when a man asked about enjoying an unrelated woman short of intercourse, the Prophet instructed him to perform a thorough ablution.
THALABI:v3p315/r4.anchor: ما روى عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى عن معاذ أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الرجل ينال من امرأة

THALABI:v3p315/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r5.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p315/r5.claim: Aisha says she slept in front of the Prophet with her feet toward his prayer direction; when he prostrated he nudged her feet, and she folded them.
THALABI:v3p315/r5.anchor: روى مالك عن أبي النضر عن أبي سلمة عن عائشة قالت: كنت أنام بين يدي رسول الله

THALABI:v3p315/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r6.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p315/r6.claim: Aisha says that while she lay across before the Prophet as he prayed, he touched her foot when he wanted to perform the witr prayer.
THALABI:v3p315/r6.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن القاسم عن عائشة قالت

THALABI:v3p315/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r7.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p315/r7.claim: Aisha recounts finding the Prophet prostrating and invoking God's refuge; some reports add that he asked whether her devil had come, after her hand touched his foot during prayer.
THALABI:v3p315/r7.anchor: وروي الأعرج عن أبي هريرة عن عائشة قالت: فقدت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة، فجعلت

THALABI:v3p315/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p315/r8.claim: These reports explain why the jurists who count touch as invalidating ablution limit that rule to contact with desire.
THALABI:v3p315/r8.anchor: ولأجل هذه الأخبار خص من ذكرنا مس الشهوة بنقض الوضوء

THALABI:v3p315/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p315/r9.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p315/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet kissed one of his wives and then prayed without performing ablution.
THALABI:v3p315/r9.anchor: روى أبو روق عن إبراهيم التيمي عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقبل بعض أزواجه

THALABI:v3p316/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r1.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v3p316/r1.claim: In al-Shafi'i's school, intentional direct touching of a young adult woman, living or dead, invalidates ablution.
THALABI:v3p316/r1.anchor: فالذي ينقض الوضوء ملامسة الرجل المرأة الشابة [ ... ] متعمدا حية كانت أو ميتة

THALABI:v3p316/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r2.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v3p316/r2.claim: In al-Shafi'i's school, touching hair, teeth, or nails does not invalidate ablution.
THALABI:v3p316/r2.anchor: والذي لا ينقضه ملامسة الشعر والسن والظفر

THALABI:v3p316/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r3.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v3p316/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i has two views on touching a little girl, an older woman, or an unmarriageable female relative: it invalidates because intentional, or does not because desire is absent.
THALABI:v3p316/r3.anchor: والذي اختلف فيه هو أن يلمس فتاة صغيرة، أو امرأة كبيرة، أو واحدة من ذوات محارمه

THALABI:v3p316/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r4.speaker: أبو قتادة
THALABI:v3p316/r4.claim: Abu Qatada reports that the Prophet prayed while carrying Umama, daughter of Zaynab; he set her down when prostrating and lifted her when standing.
THALABI:v3p316/r4.anchor: ما روي عن أبي قتادة السلمي الانصاري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي وهو حامل أمامة

THALABI:v3p316/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r5.speaker: الجمهور
THALABI:v3p316/r5.claim: The majority say that touch invalidates ablution regardless of whether a barrier is thick or thin.
THALABI:v3p316/r5.anchor: هذا قول الجمهور. وقال مالك: ينقضها إن كان رقيقا ولا ينقضها إن كان صفيقا

THALABI:v3p316/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r6.speaker: مالك
THALABI:v3p316/r6.claim: Malik says contact through a thin barrier invalidates ablution, but contact through a thick barrier does not.
THALABI:v3p316/r6.anchor: وقال مالك: ينقضها إن كان رقيقا ولا ينقضها إن كان صفيقا

THALABI:v3p316/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r7.speaker: الليث وربيعة
THALABI:v3p316/r7.claim: Al-Layth and Rabi'a say contact invalidates ablution whether the barrier is thick or thin.
THALABI:v3p316/r7.anchor: وقال الليث وربيعة: ينقضها سواء كان صفيقا أو رقيقا

THALABI:v3p316/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p316/r8.claim: The author argues that contact through a barrier does not invalidate ablution: the verse names touching the woman, whereas with a barrier one touches the barrier; an oath not to touch her likewise remains unbroken.
THALABI:v3p316/r8.anchor: فإذا لمسها مع الحائل فما لمسها وإنما لمس الحائل، وعليه إنه لو حلف ألا يلمسها

THALABI:v3p316/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r9.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v3p316/r9.claim: Al-Shafi'i has two views on whether the person touched loses ablution: yes, because both share in pleasure; or no, as in Aisha's report of touching the Prophet's foot.
THALABI:v3p316/r9.anchor: وأما الملموس فهل ينتقض به طهره أم لا؟ فعلى قولين للشافعي

THALABI:v3p316/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p316/r10.claim: Dry ablution is a distinctive privilege of this Muslim community.
THALABI:v3p316/r10.anchor: قوله تعالى: فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا اعلم أن التيمم من خصائص هذه الأمة

THALABI:v3p316/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p316/r11.speaker: حذيفة
THALABI:v3p316/r11.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet saying that this community was favored with angel-like prayer rows, the earth as a mosque, and its soil as purification when water is lacking.
THALABI:v3p316/r11.anchor: عن حذيفة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «فضلنا على الناس بثلاث: جعلت صفوفنا

THALABI:v3p317/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p317/r1.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p317/r1.claim: Aisha recounts losing a borrowed necklace at al-Abwa' or al-Bayda/Dhat al-Jaysh; the party lacked water and was in ritual impurity, so the dry-ablution verse was revealed. Her camel was later moved and the necklace found beneath it; Usayd called it one of the family's blessings.
THALABI:v3p317/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأبواء ، حتى إذا كنا بالبيداء

THALABI:v3p317/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p317/r2.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن حمزة ومالك والشافعي والليث بن سعد وأحمد بن حنبل
THALABI:v3p317/r2.claim: One position requires prayer time to enter before dry ablution, though one ablution may cover two obligatory prayers; its proponents treat it as emergency purification like that of a woman with irregular bleeding.
THALABI:v3p317/r2.anchor: أحدها: دخول وقت الصلاة، فلا يجوز التيمم إلا بعد دخول وقت الصلاة، وقد يجمع بالتيمم

THALABI:v3p317/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p317/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p317/r3.claim: The proponents cite the Prophet's instruction to perform dry ablution and pray wherever the prayer time catches a person.
THALABI:v3p317/r3.anchor: ولأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «فأينما أدركتكم الصلاة فتيمموا وصلوا» .

THALABI:v3p317/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p317/r4.speaker: علي
THALABI:v3p317/r4.claim: Ali is reported to have said: perform dry ablution for each prayer.
THALABI:v3p317/r4.anchor: وروى أبو إسحاق عن الحريث عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: «تيمموا لكل صلاة» .

THALABI:v3p317/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p317/r5.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
THALABI:v3p317/r5.claim: Amr ibn Qays says one should renew dry ablution for every prayer even without an intervening ritual impurity.
THALABI:v3p317/r5.anchor: وروي ابن المهدي عن عاصم الأحول عن عمرو بن قيس قال: بل تتيمم لكل صلاة

THALABI:v3p318/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والحسن والثوري وأبو عبيدة
THALABI:v3p318/r1.claim: Another group treats dry ablution like water purification: it may precede prayer time and may serve multiple obligatory and voluntary prayers, even after major impurity.
THALABI:v3p318/r1.anchor: وذهبت طائفة إلى أن التيمم كالطهارة بالماء يجوز تقديمه على وقت الصلاة ويصلي من الحدث الأكبر

THALABI:v3p318/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p318/r2.claim: This group cites the Prophet's statement that clean earth is a Muslim's ablution even if water is unavailable for ten years.
THALABI:v3p318/r2.anchor: واحتجوا بقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «الصعيد الطيب وضوء المسلم ولو لم يجد الماء عشر حجج» .

THALABI:v3p318/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p318/r3.claim: The second condition for dry ablution is searching for water: check one's baggage, companions, surrounding directions, high ground, and any approaching person; most jurists invalidate ablution made before searching.
THALABI:v3p318/r3.anchor: والشرط الثاني من الشرائط المبيحة للتيمم: طلب الماء، وكيفية الطلب أن يطلبه في رحله

THALABI:v3p318/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
THALABI:v3p318/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa treats searching as recommended rather than required, so dry ablution before searching is valid; he argues that the condition would otherwise apply to voluntary prayer too and that the verse does not require a search.
THALABI:v3p318/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: طلب الماء ليس بشرط في جواز التيمم بل مستحب

THALABI:v3p318/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
THALABI:v3p318/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa's analogy: someone told to buy one item and, if unavailable, another is liable if he buys the second before looking for the first.
THALABI:v3p318/r5.anchor: والدليل عليه أنه لو وكل وكيلا ليشتري له شيئا فإن لم يجد فخيره فاشترى الشيء الثاني قبل طلبه الأول ضمن.

THALABI:v3p318/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p318/r6.claim: The third condition is genuine lack of access after searching: thieves, enemies, dangerous animals, fire, risk to life or property, or an inaccessible well all count as lacking water.
THALABI:v3p318/r6.anchor: والشرط الثالث: إعوازه بعد طلبه، فأما إذا كان بينه وبين الماء حائل من لص أو عدو

THALABI:v3p318/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p318/r7.claim: The fourth condition is an excuse of illness or travel, as named in the verse.
THALABI:v3p318/r7.anchor: والشرط الرابع: العذر من مرض أو سفر لقوله: وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر

THALABI:v3p318/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p318/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p318/r8.claim: Illness without harm from water does not permit dry ablution; fear of death does, and a wound feared to be fatal may be avoided with ablution and prayer repeated once the blood can be washed.
THALABI:v3p318/r8.anchor: والمرض على ثلاثة أضرب: مرض لا يضر استعمال الماء معه، فلا يجوز التيمم معه

THALABI:v3p319/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
THALABI:v3p319/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa allows dry ablution when using water would prolong recovery.
THALABI:v3p319/r1.anchor: الأول: أنه يجوز التيمم، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة.

THALABI:v3p319/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p319/r2.claim: The second view disallows dry ablution for delayed recovery; if only some limbs are injured, wash the safe parts and use dry ablution for the injured, without relying on either alone. Abu Hanifa instead rules by whether most of the body is sound or injured.
THALABI:v3p319/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه لا يجوز فإن كانت الجراحة في بعض جسده دون بعض، غسل ما لا ضرر عليه وتيمم

THALABI:v3p319/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p319/r3.claim: The author states that water cannot be used on some limbs while dry ablution is used for others, then presents the Shafi'i disagreement over what to do with an insufficient amount of water.
THALABI:v3p319/r3.anchor: قال: (ولا يجوز الجمع بين استعمال الماء في بعض الأعضاء والتيمم في بعضها)

THALABI:v3p319/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r4.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومالك والمزني
THALABI:v3p319/r4.claim: One Shafi'i view, also held by Abu Hanifa, Malik, and al-Muzani, drops the duty to use insufficient water and accepts dry ablution alone.
THALABI:v3p319/r4.anchor: أحدهما: أنه يسقط فرض استعماله الماء ويكفيه التيمم، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة ومالك والمزني.

THALABI:v3p319/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r5.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v3p319/r5.claim: The other Shafi'i view requires using whatever water is available, then completing dry ablution: for major impurity wash any part first; for minor impurity wash in order and use dry ablution for the remaining parts.
THALABI:v3p319/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني: يلزمه استعمال القدر الذي وجده، والتيمم كما حدثته ، وإن كان جنبا غسل به

THALABI:v3p319/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p319/r6.claim: A splint should cover only the fracture and be applied after ritual purification; while the excuse remains one may wipe over it as over leather socks.
THALABI:v3p319/r6.anchor: وإن انكسر بعض أعضائه فجبرها، فإنه لا يعدو في الجبائر موضع الكسر، ولا يضعها إلا على وضوء

THALABI:v3p319/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r7.speaker: المزني
THALABI:v3p319/r7.claim: Jurists differ over repeating prayers performed while wiping over splints; al-Muzani chooses that no repetition is required.
THALABI:v3p319/r7.anchor: والثاني: لا إعادة عليه، وهو اختيار المزني،

THALABI:v3p319/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r8.speaker: علي
THALABI:v3p319/r8.claim: A report through Zayd ibn Ali, his father, and grandfather says Hazm broke a forearm and the Prophet ordered him to wipe over the splints; al-Shafi'i says he would accept it if authentic but remains uncertain.
THALABI:v3p319/r8.anchor: أن حزما انكسر إحدى زنديه فأمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يمسح على الجبائر ، قال الشافعي: إن صح حديث علي

THALABI:v3p319/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p319/r9.claim: If a splint was applied without purification or extends beyond the fracture, remove it if safe; if removal risks injury, wash what is possible and repeat the prayer when removal becomes safe.
THALABI:v3p319/r9.anchor: وإن وضعها على غير الطهارة وعدا بها إلى غير موضع الكسر ينظر فإن لم يخش تلف يديه

THALABI:v3p319#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p319#2/r1.claim: Any journey qualifying by the name of travel permits the ruling, whether short or long, since God made no distinction.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r1.anchor: وأما السفر فهو أقل ما يقع عليه اسم سفر، طالت أو قصرت لأن الله تعالى لم يفرق بينهما

THALABI:v3p319#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v3p319#2/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reportedly made dry ablution near Medina after returning from al-Jurf, prayed Asr, entered the city while the sun was still high, and did not repeat the prayer.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر: إنه أقبل من الجرف حتى إذا كان بالمدينة تيمم فمسح وجهه ويديه وصلى العصر

THALABI:v3p319#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p319#2/r3.claim: The fifth condition for dry ablution is an inward intention.

THALABI:v3p319#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p319#2/r4.claim: The command means to intend clean soil.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا عنى: اقصدوا ترابا طيبا

THALABI:v3p319#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
THALABI:v3p319#2/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa allows dry ablution on earth and materials of its kind even without particles sticking to the hand, including minerals, plaster, crushed stone, dust, and smooth rock; metal filings are excluded.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: يجوز التيمم بالأرض ومما كان من جنسها، وإن لم يعلق بيده منها شيء

THALABI:v3p319#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r6.speaker: مالك
THALABI:v3p319#2/r6.claim: Malik permits dry ablution on earth and what is connected to it, including kinds of soil and trees.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r6.anchor: قال مالك: يجوز بالأرض وبكل ما اتصل فيها، فأجاز التيمم بأجناس الأرض والشجر

THALABI:v3p319#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي والثوري
THALABI:v3p319#2/r7.claim: Al-Awza'i and al-Thawri allow dry ablution on earth and anything on it, including trees, stones, clods, ice, and snow.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r7.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي والثوري: يجوز بالأرض وبكل ما عليها من الشجر والحجر والمدر

THALABI:v3p319#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r8.speaker: أبو جهيم
THALABI:v3p319#2/r8.claim: Abu Juhaym reports that the Prophet, after a greeting, wiped his face and hands against a wall before returning the greeting.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r8.anchor: عن عمير مولى ابن عباس أنه سمعه يقول: أقبلت أنا وعبد الله بن يسار مولى ميمونة

THALABI:v3p319#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p319#2/r9.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v3p319#2/r9.claim: Al-Shafi'i's preferred medium is pure, dusty soil that sticks to the hand: the author says sa'id means soil, tayyib means fertile, and infertile ground is not tayyib; the Prophet's wording singles out soil.
THALABI:v3p319#2/r9.anchor: وذهب الشافعي إلى أن الممسوح به تراب طاهر ذو غبار تعلق باليد وهو الاختيار لهذا

THALABI:v3p320/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r1.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v3p320/r1.claim: Al-Zuhri holds that tayammum wipes the face and hands up to the armpits and shoulders, citing a report about the Prophet's journey and Aisha's lost necklace.
THALABI:v3p320/r1.anchor: فقال الزهري: تمسح على الوجه واليدين إلى الآباط والمناكب، واحتج بما روى

THALABI:v3p320/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p320/r2.claim: Ammar reports that on a journey the tayammum verse was revealed; they struck earth without taking up dust and wiped faces, hands to shoulders, then hand interiors to armpits.
THALABI:v3p320/r2.anchor: بما روى عبد الله ابن عتبة عن ابن عباس عن عمار بن ياسر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v3p320/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r3.speaker: ابن سيرين، عبد الله بن عمر، جابر بن عبد الله، الحسن البصري، الشعبي، أبو حنيفة، وحنبل، ومالك، والليث
THALABI:v3p320/r3.claim: They hold that tayammum takes three strikes: one for the face, one for the hands, and one for the elbows.
THALABI:v3p320/r3.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: ثلاث ضربات: ضربة للوجه، وضربة لليدين، وضربة للمرفقين، وبه قال

THALABI:v3p320/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p320/r4.claim: A report from Abu al-Samma says the Prophet performed tayammum and wiped his face and forearms, supporting the broader hand extent.
THALABI:v3p320/r4.anchor: ما روى الأعرج عن أبي الصمة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تيمم فمسح وجهه وذراعيه.

THALABI:v3p320/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p320/r5.claim: Abu Umama and Ibn Umar report the Prophet's instruction that tayammum is two strikes, for the face and hands to the elbows.
THALABI:v3p320/r5.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة وابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «التيمم ضربتان: ضربة للوجه،

THALABI:v3p320/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p320/r6.claim: Asla reports that when he was junub the Prophet said the available earth sufficed, then demonstrated striking twice and wiping the arms on both sides.
THALABI:v3p320/r6.anchor: وروى ربيع بن سبرة عن أبيه عن جده عن أسلع قال: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v3p320/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r7.speaker: علي
THALABI:v3p320/r7.claim: Ali says tayammum is two strikes: one for the face and one for the palms.
THALABI:v3p320/r7.anchor: وقال علي- كرم الله وجهه-: «هو ضربتان: ضربة للوجه وضربة للكفين» .

THALABI:v3p320/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب، والأوزاعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق
THALABI:v3p320/r8.claim: They hold that one strike suffices for the face and palms, arguing that unqualified hands mean the palm through the wrist, as in the thief's hand-cutting rule.
THALABI:v3p320/r8.anchor: وذهبت طائفة إلى أنه ضربة واحدة للوجه والكفين، وهو قول سعيد بن المسيب،

THALABI:v3p320/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p320/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p320/r9.claim: The one-strike view cites Ammar's report that the Prophet said one strike for the face and palms and that tayammum for major impurity is like tayammum for minor impurity.
THALABI:v3p320/r9.anchor: فاحتجوا بما روى سعيد بن عبد الرحمن عن أبيه عن عمار بن ياسر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

THALABI:v3p321/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p321/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p321/r1.claim: The author says a junub person without water performs tayammum like someone in minor impurity; the only contrary report is from Umar and Ibn Masud, who forbid it and say to wait for water and wash.
THALABI:v3p321/r1.anchor: فإذا عدم الجنب الماء تيمم كما يتيمم المحدث بلا خلاف فيه إلا ما روي عن عمر بن الخطاب

THALABI:v3p321/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p321/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v3p321/r2.claim: Ibn Masud explains touching women here as touch by hand, not sexual intercourse.
THALABI:v3p321/r2.anchor: أو لامستم النساء أراد اللمس باليد دون الجماع.

THALABI:v3p321/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p321/r3.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
THALABI:v3p321/r3.claim: Ammar reminds Umar that both were once junub on a mission, he rolled in dust, and the Prophet taught him a sufficient substitute; Umar rebuked him, and Ammar offered not to repeat it.
THALABI:v3p321/r3.anchor: فقال عمار بن ياسر: أما تذكر حين بعثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنا وأنت وأجنبت فتمعكت في التراب،

THALABI:v3p321/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p321/r4.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
THALABI:v3p321/r4.claim: In another account, Ammar recalls their shared event to Umar, describes the Prophet's demonstration, and says Umar later entrusted him with a responsibility after warning him.
THALABI:v3p321/r4.anchor: وروى عمار بن ياسر عن سلمة بن كُهَيل عن سعيد بن عبد الرحمن بن أزي، قال: كنت عند عمر

THALABI:v3p321/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p321/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v3p321/r5.claim: Shqiq reports that Ibn Masud told Abu Musa a junub person without water should not pray; he resisted Ammar's precedent because he had not seen Umar accept it and feared people would use earth whenever water was cold.
THALABI:v3p321/r5.anchor: وروى الأعمش عن شقيق قال: كنت جالسا مع عبد الله وأبي موسى، فقال أبو موسى:

THALABI:v3p322/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p322/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v3p322/r1.claim: Ibn Masud argues that allowing tayammum could lead people to use earth whenever they find water cold; al-Amas reports that Shqiq viewed the refusal as affection for Umar.
THALABI:v3p322/r1.anchor: أما إنا لو رخصنا لهم في هذا لكان أحدهم إذا وجد برد الماء تيمم بالصعيد ، قال الأعمش:

THALABI:v3p322/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p322/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p322/r2.claim: The author concludes that a junub person may pray after tayammum, citing Imran ibn Husayn's account of the Prophet directing a man with no water to use earth.
THALABI:v3p322/r2.anchor: قال: يدل علي أن صلاة الجنب بالتيمم جايز، ما روى ابن عوف عن أبي رجاء،

THALABI:v3p322/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p322/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p322/r3.claim: Imran ibn Husayn reports that the Prophet asked an abstaining man why he had not prayed; on hearing he was junub with no water, he told him to use clean earth, which sufficed.
THALABI:v3p322/r3.anchor: ما روى ابن عوف عن أبي رجاء، قال: سمعت عمران بن حصين يقول: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا

THALABI:v3p322/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p322/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p322/r4.claim: A Muslim report from Imran says the Prophet ordered a junub man to perform tayammum and pray, then wash when water became available, without repeating the prayer.
THALABI:v3p322/r4.anchor: وروى مسلم عن أبي رجاء عن عمران بن حصين قال: صليت خلف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v3p322/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p322/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p322/r5.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet's saying that clean earth is a Muslim's purification even if water is unavailable for ten years.
THALABI:v3p322/r5.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الصعيد الطيب وضوء المسلم وإن لم يجد الماء عشر سنين»

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r1.claim: The prohibition concerns entering mosques while in major impurity, except to pass through without staying or settling there.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r1.anchor: يعني المساجد لا تقربوها وأنتم جنب إلا مجتازين غير مقيمين ولا مطمئنين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r2.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ means excretion; originally it meant low-lying ground where people went to relieve themselves, and thus became a euphemism.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r2.anchor: الغائط} الحدث. وأصل الغائط: المطمئن من الأرض.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r3.claim: Tayammamū means to intend or direct yourselves toward something.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#3/r3.anchor:
فتيمموا} أي تعمدوا.
{صعيدا طيبا} أي ترابا نظيفا.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r1.claim: Prayer here means the places of prayer, namely mosques.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r2.claim: Before wine was finally prohibited, Muslims were forbidden to pray or enter a mosque while drunk and avoided intoxication at prayer times.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r2.anchor: نهوا عن الصلاة وعن دخول المسجد في حال السكر، وكان هذا قبل نزول تحريم الخمر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r3.claim: A drunk person has a confused mind, babbles, and cannot sustain speech; if one knows what one says, one is not drunk and may pray and enter the mosque.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r3.anchor: والسكران: المختلط العقل الذي يهذي، ولا يستمر كلامه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r4.claim: A person in major ritual impurity must not approach the mosque except to pass through without staying.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r4.anchor: إلا إذا عبرتم المسجد فدخلتموه من غير إقامة فيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r5.claim: The restriction lasts until one performs the full ritual bath after major impurity.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r5.anchor: من الجنابة { وإن كنتم مرضى } أي: مرضا يضره الماء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r6.claim: The relevant illness is one harmed by water, such as sores, smallpox, or wounds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r6.anchor: أي: مرضا يضره الماء كالقروح، والجدري، والجراحات

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r7.claim: This means being on a journey.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r7.anchor: أي: مسافرين { أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r8.claim: Coming from al-ghāʾiṭ means having a bodily event.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r9.claim: Touching women means touching them with one’s hands.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r9.anchor: { أو لامستم النساء } أي: لمستموهن بأيديكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:43-44/r10.claim: When water is unavailable, perform dry ablution using clean earth that produces vegetation.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r4.claim: After a prayer-related incident, the instruction not to approach prayer drunk was revealed; drinking then sharply declined but continued.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r4.anchor: Bunun üzerine içenler pek azaldı ise de yine vardı.

ELMALILI:4:41-42/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r6.claim: The following discussion develops inner and outer purity: prayer follows faith, purification is prayer's first condition, and major ablution connects closely to marriage and family rules; both require a sound mind.
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r6.anchor: tahâret-i bâtına ve zâhire ile وَٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ emrine bir inkişaf verilmek ve imandan sonra ibadetin akdemi namaz ve namazın ilk şartı da necasetten ve hadesten taharet olduğu

ELMALILI:4:43/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r1.claim: A report identifies the occasion of revelation as the banquet incident of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, detailed under 2:219.
ELMALILI:4:43/r1.anchor: Bu âyetin sebeb-i nüzûlü Abdurrahman b. Avf hazretlerinin ziyafeti hâdisesi olduğu mervîdir

ELMALILI:4:43/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r2.claim: Pairing intoxication with janaba and avoidance with purification eloquently conveys the prohibition and impurity of intoxicants, stated explicitly at 5:90.
ELMALILI:4:43/r2.anchor: Sarhoşluğun cünüplük ile ve ondan sakınmanın da tahâret ve gusül ile müterâfık olarak mevzû‘-i bahis edilmesi ve bu hâlde mü’minin namaza yaklaşmaktan men‘i

ELMALILI:4:43/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ELMALILI:4:43/r3.claim: Some commentators take salat here to mean the mosque or prayer-place, so the prohibition bars drunk people from entering mosques.
ELMALILI:4:43/r3.anchor: murad mescid ve musallâdır, bununla sarhoşlar mescidlere duhulden men‘edilmişlerdir demiş

ELMALILI:4:43/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r4.claim: Elmalılı says there is no need to depart from salat's basic meaning: an intoxicated person who cannot understand his words cannot pray validly, and intoxication is forbidden.
ELMALILI:4:43/r4.anchor: bu mânayı anlamak için salâtı ma‘nâ-yı aslîsinden çıkarmaya lüzum yoktur. Bu nehiy, söylediğini bilmeyen sarhoşun namazı sahih olmadığına

ELMALILI:4:43/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r5.claim: By indication, the verse also bars drunk and junub people from entering or even approaching the mosque; the exception for passing through applies only to junub people, not the drunk.
ELMALILI:4:43/r5.anchor: Demek ki söylediğini bilmez sarhoşların mescid civarından geçmelerine de mesağ yoktur. Çünkü esasen sarhoşluğa mesağ yoktur

ELMALILI:4:43/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r6.claim: Junub denotes a person in janaba after emission; it can be used as a singular noun or a plural.
ELMALILI:4:43/r6.anchor: inzal vâki‘olmuş bulunandır ki, masdar gibi müfred veya cem‘e ıtlak olunur

ELMALILI:4:43/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r7.claim: Igtisal means to bathe, washing the whole body.

ELMALILI:4:43/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r8.claim: Abirin sabil means people traveling on the road or in a state of travel; the exception concerns tayammum.
ELMALILI:4:43/r8.anchor: Yolda gidenler, sefer hâlinde bulunanlar demektir.

ELMALILI:4:43/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r9.claim: The phrase may also permit a junub person to pass along the road beside a mosque, but not enter the mosque; it has no bearing on drunk people.
ELMALILI:4:43/r9.anchor: sâlihtir. Bu itibar ile de cünübün namaz kılınan mescidden değil, fakat yanındaki yoldan geçmesi câiz olduğuna bir işaret olur

ELMALILI:4:43/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r10.claim: Ghait means a low hollow place and euphemistically refers to a latrine; coming from it means relieving oneself and having minor ritual impurity.
ELMALILI:4:43/r10.anchor: engin, çukur yer demek olup halâya işarettir, bundan gelmek de hadesten, abdest bozmaktan kinayedir

ELMALILI:4:43/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r11.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf al-Ashir read lamastum without the alif, from lams rather than mulamasah; both forms mean touching women.
ELMALILI:4:43/r11.anchor: Kisâî, Halef-i Âşir kıraatlerinde elifsiz أَوْ لَٰمَسْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ okunur.

ELMALILI:4:43/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r12.claim: The wording is agreed to signify intercourse, specifically the meeting of the circumcised parts, which requires ghusl.
ELMALILI:4:43/r12.anchor: Bunun da sûret-i mahsûsada bir dokunmak demek olan iltikā-i hıtâneyn mânasını ifade ettiğinde ittifak vardır ve gusül îcâb eder

ELMALILI:4:43/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r13.claim: The Hanafi view, followed by Elmalılı, excludes mere skin contact from the meaning; touching a woman's body alone does not invalidate ablution.
ELMALILI:4:43/r13.anchor: Biz Hanefiyyece bu maksud değildir. Binâen‘aleyh kadının bir tarafına mücerred dokunuvermekle abdest bozulmaz

ELMALILI:4:43/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r14.speaker: Zâhiriyye
ELMALILI:4:43/r14.claim: The Zahiris hold that mere touch invalidates ablution, but only for the person who touches, not the person touched.
ELMALILI:4:43/r14.anchor: Zâhiriyye ve Şâfi‘iyye bozulur, gusül değil fakat abdest almak lâzım gelir demişlerdir

ELMALILI:4:43/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r15.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
ELMALILI:4:43/r15.claim: Shafi'i holds that mere touch invalidates both people's ablution, without requiring ghusl.
ELMALILI:4:43/r15.anchor: İmam Şâfiî ise ikisininki de bozulacağına kāil olmuştur

ELMALILI:4:43/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r16.claim: Elmalılı characterizes the Hanafi approach as lenient and the Shafi'i approach as following stricter precaution.
ELMALILI:4:43/r16.anchor: Hanefiyye tahfîfe, Şâfi‘iyye de teşdid ve ihtiyâta riayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:4:43/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r17.claim: When illness or travel accompanies a state requiring ghusl or ablution, and water is unavailable, one may turn to tayammum; illness makes inability to find water include actual or legal inability.
ELMALILI:4:43/r17.anchor: bulamamak hakikaten veya hükmen bulamamaktan e‘am olmuş oluyor

ELMALILI:4:43/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r18.claim: Tayammum literally means intending, so intention is intrinsic to it.
ELMALILI:4:43/r18.anchor: Lügaten kasd demektir, binâen‘aleyh niyetsiz teyemmüm olmaz, mahiyetinde dâhildir

ELMALILI:4:43/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r19.claim: Sa'id means the earth's surface, including stone and soil, so tayammum on a stone is valid even without dust adhering to the hand.
ELMALILI:4:43/r19.anchor: de yeryüzü demektir ki taşa toprağa şâmildir.

ELMALILI:4:43/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r20.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
ELMALILI:4:43/r20.claim: Shafi'i requires at least a little soil or dust to adhere.
ELMALILI:4:43/r20.anchor: İmam Şâfiî birazcık olsun toprak bulaşmalı demiştir

ELMALILI:4:43/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r21.claim: Tayyib means thoroughly clean, excluding contaminated or doubtful material.
ELMALILI:4:43/r21.anchor: tertemiz demektir. Binâen‘aleyh mülevves veya şüpheli olmamalıdır

ELMALILI:4:43/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r22.claim: The practical method is to strike the earth once and wipe the face, then strike again and wipe both hands up to the elbows.
ELMALILI:4:43/r22.anchor: mesh etmeli, bir kere de vurup dirseklerine kadar ellerini mesh etmelidir

ELMALILI:4:43/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r23.claim: The concession teaches that inward purity is foundational, but outward cleanliness also matters; neither can replace the other.
ELMALILI:4:43/r23.anchor: Tahâret-i kalbiye asıldır. Kalbi pis olan ne yapsa temizlenemez

ELMALILI:4:43/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r24.claim: In necessity, tayammum is primarily an inward act that preserves the material condition and outward form as fully as possible.
ELMALILI:4:43/r24.anchor: teyemmüm esasen bir tahâret-i kalbiye işi olmakla beraber şart-ı maddî ve şekl-i zâhirînin de مَا لاَ يُدْرَكُ كُل ُّهُ لاَ يـُتـْرَكُ كُل ُّهُ medlûlü üzere en güzel bir muhafazasıdır

ELMALILI:4:43/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r25.claim: God's pardon explains the tayammum concession; it does not license intoxication or neglecting purification.
ELMALILI:4:43/r25.anchor: Bunun için teyemmüme de ruhsat verir. Fakat sarhoşluğa ve cenâbet durmaya müsaade etmez

ELMALILI:4:43/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:43/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:43/r26.claim: The discussion moves from sound mind and bodily and spiritual purity toward intellectual and moral education, then draws attention to the conduct of misguided aggressors.
ELMALILI:4:43/r26.anchor: muhâfaza-i akl ü şuura ve tahâret-i maddiye ve mâneviyeye müntehî olmakla bilhassa terbiye-i akliye ve fikriyeye revnak ve ahlâk u diyânete metanet verilmek

MAJAZ:v1p126/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p126/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p126/r8.claim: The omitted noun is the prayer place: an impure person may pass through it but may not sit there.
MAJAZ:v1p126/r8.anchor: ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل» (42) معناه فى هذا الموضع: لا تقربوا المصلى جنبا إلا عابر سبيل يقطعه، ولا يقعد فيه

MAJAZ:v1p128/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p128/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p128/r1.claim: ʿAlā safar means ‘on a journey,’ equivalent to fī safar; idiomatically it can also mean being prepared to travel.
MAJAZ:v1p128/r1.anchor: أو على سفر» (42) : أو فى سفر، وتقول: أنا على سفر، فى معنى آخر: تقول: أنا متهى له.

MAJAZ:v1p128/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p128/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p128/r2.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ is a euphemism for a bowel movement; literally it is a broad, sloping lowland larger than a valley.
MAJAZ:v1p128/r2.anchor: أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط» (42) : كناية عن حاجة ذى البطن، والغائط: الفيح من الأرض المتصوب وهو أعظم من الوادي.

MAJAZ:v1p128/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p128/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p128/r3.claim: The phrase means sexual intercourse; both lamastum and lāmastum occur, with the latter form more common.
MAJAZ:v1p128/r3.anchor: أو لامستم النساء» (42) : اللماس النكاح: لمستم، ولامستم أكثر.

MAJAZ:v1p128/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p128/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p128/r4.claim: Tayammamū means deliberately aim for or use it; ṣaʿīd is the earth’s surface.
MAJAZ:v1p128/r4.anchor: فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا» (42) أي فتعمدوا ذاك، والصعيد: وجه الأرض.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r1.claim: Wine, called hamr by Arabs, was not prohibited immediately after Islam began, so Muslims accustomed to it continued drinking and becoming intoxicated.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r2.claim: After 2:219 said wine and gambling had greater harms than benefits, some Companions glossed ism as harm or injury and argued they drank for benefits, continuing to drink.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r3.claim: The restriction signaled that intoxicants would soon be forbidden and psychologically prepared drinkers to give them up.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r3.anchor: Ancak bu âyet şarap ve benzeri sarhoşluk veren içkilerin yakında yasaklanacağına işaret ediyor, içenleri psikolojik olarak bunu bırakmaya hazırlıyordu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r4.claim: Three years later, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf hosted a meal; guests drank and became drunk, the imam misrecited al-Kafirun in a way that changed its meaning, and this verse was revealed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r4.anchor: Abdurrahman b. Avf yemek hazırlamış, arkadaşlarını davet etmişti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r5.claim: After this verse, Muslims reportedly drank wine only after the morning and night prayers, when they could sober up before the next prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r5.anchor: Artık müslümanlar şarabı, ancak sabah ve yatsı namazlarından sonra içmeye başladılar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r6.claim: The commentary points to 5:90 for the definitive prohibition of intoxicants.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r6.anchor: içkinin kesin olarak yasaklanması hakkında bilgi için bk. Mâide 5/90

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r7.claim: An intoxicated person must wait until knowing what they say, and a person in major ritual impurity must wait until performing ghusl before prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r7.anchor: sarhoş olanlar ne söylediklerini bilecek hale gelinceye, cünüp olanlar ise boy abdesti (gusül) alıncaya kadar namaz kılmayacaklardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r8.claim: The literal meaning of abiri sabil is people passing along a way; since the verse shortly uses ala safar for travelers, the earlier phrase should have a different sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r8.anchor: bu ifadenin lafzî tercümesi ise “yolu geçenler”dir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r9.speaker: tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r9.claim: Exegetes using explanatory reports interpret the phrase as people passing through a mosque, entering one side and leaving the other without staying.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r9.anchor: tefsirciler bu ifadeyi “yolu mescidden geçenler, mescidde oturmadan bir tarafından girip diğer tarafından çıkarak yoluna devam edenler” şeklinde anlamışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r10.claim: Some Companions' homes stood around the first mosque in Medina and their routes passed through it; the verse permitted junub people to pass when necessary. Reports say the Prophet redirected the routes, with exceptions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r10.anchor: Mescidin çevresinde de bir kısım ashabın evleri vardı, bu evlerin şehre açılan yolu mescidden geçiyordu, bu sebeple bazan cünüp olarak mescidden geçmek gerekebiliyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r11.claim: On the mosque-passage interpretation, prayer means the act of worship for the intoxicated, but the mosque as the place of prayer for the junub.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r11.anchor: bu tefsiri yapanlar içinde İbn Mes‘ûd, İbn Dînâr, Nehaî, Mâlik, Şâfiî gibi âlimler vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r12.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd, İbn Dînâr, Nehaî, Mâlik ve Şâfiî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r12.claim: Those scholars allow junub people to enter and exit a mosque for a need if they do not sit there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r12.anchor: Cünüp olanlar, içinde oturmamak üzere –ihtiyaca binaen– mescide girip çıkabilirler; bu tefsiri yapanlar içinde İbn Mes‘ûd, İbn Dînâr, Nehaî, Mâlik, Şâfiî gibi âlimler vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r13.speaker: Ali, İbn Abbas, İbn Cübeyr, Mücâhid, Ebû Hanîfe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r13.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Abu Hanifa understand passers as travelers, the translation's choice; travel can make water unavailable or too necessary to use, so tayammum is allowed for a junub traveler.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r13.anchor: Âyeti farklı yorumlayan, aralarında Ali, İbn Abbas, İbn Cübeyr, Mücâhid, Ebû Hanîfe gibi âlimlerin de bulunduğu diğer gruba göre “yolu geçenler”den maksat, bizim meâlinde tercih ettiğimiz gibi yolculardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r14.claim: Although the verse later explicitly refers to travelers, this interpretation says the phrase is repeated because water is less available or more needed during travel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r14.anchor: şeklinde farklı bir ifade ile yolcular geçeceği halde burada zikredilmesi, suyun bulunmaması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r15.claim: Scholars agree tayammum is permissible during travel when water is absent or an obstacle prevents its use.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r15.anchor: Yolculukta su bulunmadığı veya onu kullanmaya bir engel bulunduğu takdirde teyemmümün câiz olduğu hükmünde ittifak vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r16.speaker: Şâfiî ve bazı müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r16.claim: Some jurists, including Shafi'i, hold that a resident with water may not perform tayammum unless using water threatens life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r16.anchor: Şâfiî gibi bazı müctehidler su mevcut ise hazarda (yolcu olmayanlar için) hayatî tehlike bulunmadıkça teyemmümün câiz olmadığı hükmünü benimsemişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r17.claim: The commentary reads this verse as stating the tayammum substitute during travel and 5:6 as stating it for residents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r17.anchor: Nisâ sûresindeki bu âyet sefer halinde, Mâide sûresindeki 6. âyet ise hazar halinde teyemmümün gusül ve abdest yerine geçtiğini ifade etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r18.claim: After intending tayammum, one touches clean soil, clay, sand, or stone with the palms, wipes the face, touches again, then wipes arms to the elbows.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r18.anchor: niyet edildikten sonra yer kabuğuna ait temiz toprak, kil, kum, taş gibi bir nesneye iki elin içi ile dokunup yüzü, sonra bir daha dokunup dirseklere kadar kolları meshederek yapılmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r19.claim: Tayammum substitutes for ablution and, for a person in major impurity, ghusl.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r19.anchor: hem abdest hem de –cünüpler için– gusül yerine geçmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r20.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r20.claim: Ghusl was known and practiced by pre-Islamic Arabs; they may have learned it through Abrahamic tradition or from Jews.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r21.claim: Tayammum is a distinctively Islamic spiritual preparation for worship that instills cleanliness awareness though it does not clean the body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r21.anchor: Teyemmüm İslâm’a mahsus bir ibadet hazırlığı ve mânevî temizlik aracıdır. Bununla beden temizlenmese de Allah’ın huzuruna durup namaz kılacak olan kul bir temizlik şuuru kazanmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r22.claim: The tayammum verse was revealed in 6 AH during the Muraysi expedition, when Aisha lost her necklace, searching consumed time, water could not be reached, and prayer time was nearly over.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r22.anchor: Teyemmüm âyeti hicretten sonra 6. yılda Müreysî seferinde gelmiştir. Bu seferde Hz. Âişe’nin bir gerdanlığı kaybolmuş, aramak için vakit harcanmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r23.claim: There is uncertainty whether the tayammum passage occasioned by Aisha's necklace was this verse or 5:6 in al-Maida.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r23.anchor: Bu âyetin konumuz olan Nisâ sûresi âyeti mi, yoksa Mâide sûresinin 6. âyeti mi olduğu hususunda tereddüt vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r24.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r24.claim: Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi says the prohibition portion followed the intoxication incident, while tayammum followed Aisha's incident and appears in 5:6; al-Nisa repeats it because relevant. Bukhari's treatment in both commentaries supports this account.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r25.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r25.claim: Ibn Ashur notes the contrary view but argues al-Nisa preceded al-Maida and leans toward Aisha having meant the al-Nisa verse, as Qurtubi also held.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r25.anchor: Nisâ sûresinin Mâide’den önce geldiğini ileri süren İbn Âşûr, Kurtubî’nin de aynı görüşü paylaştığından hareketle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r26.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r26.claim: Together, these verses explain what intoxicated, junub, and ritually impure people cannot do in normal and exceptional circumstances and provide solutions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r26.anchor: bu iki âyet birbirini tamamlayarak hazarda ve seferde, sarhoş, cünüp ve abdestsiz olanların yapamayacakları bazı şeyleri açıklamakta, olağan ve olağan dışı durumlara ait çözümler getirmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r27.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r27.claim: Lems and mulamasa literally mean touching with a hand or part of the body, while figuratively they mean sexual intercourse.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r27.anchor: Âyette kullanılan lems ve mülâmese kelimesinin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r28.claim: The synonymous word mess is also used for intercourse in 2:236–237.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r28.anchor: Lems ile eş anlamlı olan mess kelimesi Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de cinsel ilişki mânasında da kullanılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r29.speaker: Hz. Ali, İbn Abbas, Mücâhid ve Ebû Hanîfe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r29.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Hanifa, and others take the phrase to mean intercourse; mere skin contact invalidates neither ghusl nor ablution.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r29.anchor: Hz. Ali, İbn Abbas, Mücâhid ve Ebû Hanîfe’nin aralarında bulunduğu bir gruba göre maksat

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r30.speaker: Mâlik, Ahmed, İshak
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r30.claim: Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq hold that touching with sexual pleasure invalidates ablution, while touching without that aim does not.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r30.anchor: Mâlik, Ahmed ve İshak’a göre cinsî haz almak maksadıyla dokunma abdesti bozar, böyle bir maksat bulunmadan dokunmak abdesti bozmaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r31.speaker: Şâfiî, İbn Mes‘ûd, İbn Ömer, Zührî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r31.claim: Shafi'i holds that skin contact invalidates ablution whether or not sexual pleasure is intended; this view is also transmitted from Ibn Masud, Ibn Umar, and Zuhri.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r31.anchor: Şâfiî’ye göre cinsî haz maksadı bulunsun bulunmasın deri teması abdesti bozar; bu anlayış İbn Mes‘ûd, İbn Ömer, Zührî gibi müctehidlerden de nakledilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r32.speaker: Evzâî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r32.claim: Al-Awza'i holds that touching with the hand invalidates ablution, but touching with another part of the body does not.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r32.anchor: Evzâî’ye göre el ile dokunmak abdesti bozar, bedenin diğer bir yeri ile dokunmak bozmaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r33.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r33.claim: Al-Shawkani says the word fits both senses, so neither can determine a ruling; Prophetic and Companion practice shows skin contact alone does not invalidate ablution and intercourse is meant. The commentary endorses this.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r33.anchor: Şevkânî bu görüşleri naklettikten sonra bizce de doğru olan şu açıklamada bulunmuştur: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in burada kullandığı kelime her iki mâna için de uygundur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r34.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r34.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r34.claim: Illness or travel alone does not grant the tayammum dispensation; water must also be unavailable or unusable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r34.anchor: ifadesinden yalnızca hastalık veya yolculuk halinin teyemmüm ruhsatı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r35.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r35.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r35.claim: Because residents and healthy people may also perform tayammum when water is absent, the commentary asks why illness and travel are singled out.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r35.anchor: Su bulunmadığında hasta ve yolcu olmayanlar da teyemmüm edebildiklerine göre burada

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r36.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r36.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r36.claim: If al-Nisa came before al-Maida, one answer is that al-Nisa explains the dispensation for travelers and al-Maida for residents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r36.anchor: Eğer Nisâ sûresinin –özellikle bu âyetin– Mâide’den daha önce indiği kabul edilirse bu soruya şu cevap verilebilir:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r37.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r37.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r37.claim: Another answer is that illness and travel are singled out because water is more likely to be absent or unusable then.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r37.anchor: Suyun bulunmama ve kullanılamama ihtimali hastalık ve yolculuk halinde daha fazla olduğundan bu iki durum özellikle zikredilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r38.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r38.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r38.claim: Not finding water can figuratively mean that water exists but cannot be used because of need, fear, or harm; such circumstances are more common for travelers and the sick.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:43/r38.anchor: b) Suyu bulamamak mecazen “bulunduğu halde ihtiyaç, korku, zarar görme gibi bir sebeple onu kullanma imkânından mahrum olmak” mânasına da gelmektedir.

BURHAN:v3p446#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p446#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p446#2/r1.claim: Tawriya subtly evokes one of a word’s meanings while intending another; istikhdām employs both meanings together, each cued by a separate contextual indicator.
BURHAN:v3p446#2/r1.anchor: كثيرا ما تلتبس التورية بالاستخدام والفراق بينهما أن التورية استعمال المعنيين في اللفظ وإهمال الآخر وفي الاستخدام استعمالهما معا بقرينتين

BURHAN:v3p446#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p446#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p446#2/r3.claim: In the prohibition on approaching prayer while intoxicated or impure, ṣalāt means the prayer itself in “until you know what you say,” but its place in “except as passersby.”
BURHAN:v3p446#2/r3.anchor: فإن الصلاة تحتمل إرادة نفس الصلاة وتحتمل إرادة موضعها

NAHHAS:v1p457/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p457/r1.claim: The circumstantial phrase is a subject-predicate clause; sukārā is diptote because it ends in the feminine alif.
NAHHAS:v1p457/r1.anchor: ابتداء وخبر في موضع نصب على الحال ويقال سكارى ولم ينصرف لأن في آخره ألف التأنيث

NAHHAS:v1p457/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p457/r2.anchor: نصب بحتى ( ولا جنبا ) عطف على الموضع

NAHHAS:v1p457/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p457/r3.claim: Junuban is coordinated to the syntactic position, meaning do not approach prayer while in major ritual impurity; ʿābirī sabīl is circumstantial accusative, like “do not come except riding.”
NAHHAS:v1p457/r3.anchor: عطف على الموضع أي ولا تقربوا الصلاة جنبا ( إلا عابري سبيل ) نصب على الحال

NAHHAS:v1p457/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r4.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v1p457/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets sukārā as sleep, but al-Naḥḥās rejects this: Arabic usage and reports oppose it, sleepers are not commanded while asleep, and knowing what one says shows one is not drunk.
NAHHAS:v1p457/r4.anchor: قال الضحاك لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى أي من النوم وهذا القول خطأ من جهات

NAHHAS:v1p457/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن مسعود
NAHHAS:v1p457/r5.claim: One view takes the exception to mean travelers may pray after becoming junub, implying that a junub may use tayammum only while traveling; this is attributed to ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd.
NAHHAS:v1p457/r5.anchor: هذا قول عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وعبد الله بن مسعود رحمه الله

NAHHAS:v1p457/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وأنس بن مالك
NAHHAS:v1p457/r6.claim: Another view understands prayer as its place, the mosque: a junub may pass through, and may use tayammum while resident; this is attributed to ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Anas.
NAHHAS:v1p457/r6.anchor: وهذا مذهب علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وابن عباس وأنس بن مالك رحمهم الله

NAHHAS:v1p457/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p457/r7.claim: Illness means inability to use water or fear of death from cold or wounds; travel means lacking water.
NAHHAS:v1p457/r7.anchor: أي مرضى لا تقدرون معه على تناول الماء أو تخافون التلف من برد أو جراح ( أو على سفر ) لا تجدون فيه الماء

NAHHAS:v1p457/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r8.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
NAHHAS:v1p457/r8.claim: Some jurists say aw here means “and”; skilled grammarians reject that because the listed conditions differ, preferring a shifted word order that makes the clauses fit together.
NAHHAS:v1p457/r8.anchor: أن بعض الفقهاء قال أو بمعنى الواو وإنما احتاج إلى هذا لأن المرض والسفر ليسا بحدثين والغائط حدث

NAHHAS:v1p457/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p457/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p457/r9.claim: The proposed word order is “do not approach prayer drunk, or after relieving yourselves or touching women; and if junub and seeking prayer, purify yourselves,” a shift comparable to 20:129.
NAHHAS:v1p457/r9.anchor: والتقديم والتأخير لا ينكر كما قال الله جل وعز ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما

BURHAN:v2p303/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p303/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p303/r4.claim: The Qur'an euphemizes intercourse with terms for touching, intimacy, marital union, entry, and covering, drawing on bodily contact and clothing or cultivation metaphors.
BURHAN:v2p303/r4.anchor: ومن عادة القرآن العظيم الكناية عن الجماع باللمس والملامسة والرفث والدخول والنكاح ونحوهن

BURHAN:v2p303/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p303/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p303/r6.claim: Though al-ghāʾiṭ originally meant a low place where people went out of sight to relieve themselves, its common use became equivalent to explicit mention; legal instruction needed familiar Arab wording.
BURHAN:v2p303/r6.anchor: قلنا لانه جاء على خطاب العرب وما يالفون والمراد تعريفهم الاحكام فكان لا بد من التصريح به على ان الغائط ايضا كناية عن النجو

ITQAN:v4p484/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p484/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p484/r1.claim: Different explanations reported from Companions for one verse can reflect different readings rather than disagreement.
ITQAN:v4p484/r1.anchor: من المهم معرفة التفاسير الواردة عن الصحابة بحسب قراءة مخصوصة وذلك أنه قد يرد عنهم تفسيران في الآية الواحدة مختلفان فيظن اختلافا وليس باختلاف

ITQAN:v4p484/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p484/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p484/r8.claim: The reported difference over whether لامستم means intercourse or touching by hand is no disagreement: intercourse fits لامستم, and hand-touch fits لمستم.
ITQAN:v4p484/r8.anchor: وقد خرجت على هذا قديما الاختلاف الوارد عن ابن عباس وغيره

ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.claim: Al-Tayalisi transmits Ibn Umar's account of alcohol's three-stage prohibition: first 2:219 left people free to benefit, then 4:43 prohibited drinking near prayer, and finally 5:90 prompted the Prophet to declare it forbidden.
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.anchor: روى الطيالسي في مسنده عن ابن عمر قال نزل في الخمر ثلاث آيات فأول شيء

ITQAN:v4p494/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p494/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p494/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Gabriel told the Prophet that Ibn ʿAbbas would become the community’s learned authority, and the Prophet was to treat him well.
ITQAN:v4p494/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بريدة عن ابن عباس قال انتهيت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده جبريل فقال له جبريل إنه كائن حبر هذه الأمة

ITQAN:v4p494/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p494/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p494/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet told him, “You are an excellent interpreter of the Quran.”
ITQAN:v4p494/r2.anchor: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( نعم ترجمان القرآن أنت )

ITQAN:v4p494/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p494/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p494/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud calls ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas the interpreter of the Quran.
ITQAN:v4p494/r3.anchor: نعم ترجمان القرآن عبد الله بن عباس

ITQAN:v4p494/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p494/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v4p494/r4.claim: Mujahid says Ibn ʿAbbas was called “the ocean” because of the extent of his knowledge.
ITQAN:v4p494/r4.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم عن مجاهد قال كان ابن عباس يسمى البحر لكثرة علمه

ITQAN:v4p494/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p494/r5.speaker: ابن الحنفية
