ITQAN:v4p494/r5.claim: Ibn al-Hanafiyya calls Ibn ʿAbbas the learned authority of the community.
ITQAN:v4p494/r5.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن الحنفية قال كان ابن عباس حبر هذه الأمة

ITQAN:v4p494/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p494/r6.speaker: الحسن
ITQAN:v4p494/r6.claim: Al-Hasan recounts ʿUmar’s praise of Ibn ʿAbbas as a young man among elders, with an inquisitive tongue and discerning heart.
ITQAN:v4p494/r6.anchor: ذا كم فتى الكهول إن له لسانا سئولا وقلبا عقولا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r1.speaker: علي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf served wine at a meal; when intoxicated, ʿAlī led Maghrib and confused the recitation, prompting the prohibition on approaching prayer drunk.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r1.anchor: روى أبو داود والترمذي والنسائي والحاكم عن علي قال صنع لنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف طعاما فدعانا وسقانا من الخمر

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r2.speaker: علي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r2.claim: ʿAlī says the clause about being ritually impure except when passing through concerns a traveler who became impure, performed dry ablution, and prayed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج الفرياني وابن أبي حاتم وابن المنذر عن علي قال نزلت هذه الآية قوله ﴿ ولا جنبا ﴾ في المسافر تصيبه الجنابة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r3.speaker: الأسلع بن شريك
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r3.claim: Al-Aslaʿ b. Sharīk reports that, fearing illness or death from bathing in icy water after becoming impure while tending the Prophet's camel, he told the Prophet and the whole verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن الأسلع بن شريك قال كنت أرجل ناقة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأصابتني جنابة في ليلة باردة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r4.speaker: الأسلع بن شريك
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r4.claim: In al-Ṭabarānī's report, Jibrīl brought the dry-earth verse after al-Aslaʿ told the Prophet he was impure; the Prophet demonstrated one strike for the face and one for the hands to the elbows.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r4.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عن الأسلع قال كنت أخدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأرحل له فقال لي ذات يوم يا أسلع قم فارحل فقلت يا رسول الله أصابتني جنابة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r5.speaker: يزيد بن أبي حبيب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r5.claim: Yazīd b. Abī Ḥabīb says some Anṣār had doors opening into the mosque and, lacking water while impure, had to cross the mosque to reach it; the passing-through clause was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب أن رجالا من الأنصار كانت أبوابهم في المسجد فكانت تصيبهم جنابة ولا ماء عندهم

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the clause about illness was revealed for an Anṣārī who could not rise to wash and had no servant to bring water, so he told the Prophet.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد قال نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من الأنصار كان مريضا فلم يستطع أن يقوم فيتوضأ

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r7.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r7.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī reports that wounded companions developed injuries and then became ritually impure; after they complained, the whole verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p68#2/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن إبراهيم النخعي قال نال أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جراحة ففشت فيهم ثم ابتلوا بالجنابة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r5.claim: The verse was revealed about companions who drank wine and came to prayer intoxicated, unsure how many cycles they were praying or what they were saying.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r5.anchor: نزلت في أناس من أصحاب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كانوا يشربون الخمر ويحضرون الصلاة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r6.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reports that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf hosted companions who ate and drank; at Maghrib one led prayer and garbled the recitation of al-Kafirun, occasioning the verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p152/r6.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن قال: صنع عبد الرحمن بن عوف طعاما ودعا أناسا من أصحاب رسول الله

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r1.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r1.claim: Aisha reports that when her necklace was lost on a journey, Muhammad and the party stopped without water; after dawn he received the tayammum verse. Usayd ibn Hudayr called it another blessing for Abu Bakr’s family, and the necklace was found under the camel. Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmit this report.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن أبيه، عن عائشة أنها قالت: خرجنا مع رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في بعض أسفاره

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r2.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r2.claim: Ammar ibn Yasir reports that during a stay at Dhat al-Jaysh, Aisha’s Dufar-bead necklace was lost and the party waited without water until dawn; God revealed purification with clean earth, and the Muslims wiped their faces and hands up to the shoulders and armpits.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن عمار بن ياسر قال: عرس رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بذات الجيش ومعه عائشة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r3.speaker: الزهري
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r3.claim: Al-Zuhri says he was told that Abu Bakr called Aisha blessed after the tayammum revelation.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p154/r3.anchor: قال الزهري: وبلغنا أن أبا بكر قال لعائشة: والله إنك ما علمت لمباركة

DAMGHANI:v1p240/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p240/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p240/r13.claim: Sukr can mean the familiar drunkenness caused by drink.
DAMGHANI:v1p240/r13.anchor: السادس : السكر الغطاء على العقل وهو السكر المعروف قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

DAMGHANI:v1p433/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p433/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p433/r2.claim: مرضى can mean people with wounds.

BURHAN:v3p230/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p230/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p230/r5.claim: The verse names passing excrement as the evident, necessary cause of purification; sleep and other cases are left implicit and inferred.
BURHAN:v3p230/r5.anchor: ولم يذكر النوم وغيره لأن السبب الضروري النقاض خروج الخارج

BURHAN:v3p392/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p392/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p392/r3.claim: Some prohibitions target a state or attribute rather than the act itself: do not die except as Muslims means avoid dying outside Islam, like the example about praying only in humility.
BURHAN:v3p392/r3.anchor: أي فلا يكون موتكم إلا على حال كونكم ميتين على الإسلام فالنهي في الحقيقة على خلاف حال الإسلام كقول القائل لا تصل إلا وأنت خاشع

BURHAN:v1p116/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p116/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p116/r7.claim: The al-Māʾida wording adds منه after the phrase about wiping faces and hands; al-Nisāʾ does not.
BURHAN:v1p116/r7.anchor: فى النساء ﴿ فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم ﴾ وفى المائدة بزيادة ﴿ منه ﴾

BURHAN:v2p14/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p14/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p14/r3.claim: An absolute ruling is restricted by a qualified one when that is its only basis; examples include just witnesses, inheritances after bequest or debt, believing-slave expiation, ablution, and blood restricted to flowing blood.
BURHAN:v2p14/r3.anchor: إن وجد دليل على تقييد المطلق صير إليه وإلا فلا والمطلق على إطلاقه والمقيد على تقييده

BURHAN:v4p251/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p251/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p251/r7.claim: باء also appears with objects in examples such as بأيديكم, بالمودة, باسم ربك, and بأيكم المفتون; المفتون is a passive participle, not a verbal noun.
BURHAN:v4p251/r7.anchor: وإما مع المفعول كقوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة ﴾ وقوله ﴿ تلقون إليهم بالمودة ﴾

ITQAN:v2p412/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p412/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p412/r9.claim: Al-ṣalah can refer to places of prayer.
ITQAN:v2p412/r9.anchor: 9 ومواضع الصلاة ﴿ وصلوات ومساجد ﴾ ﴿ لا تقربوا الصلاة ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p374/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r13.claim: Qurb can mean entering into an activity; not approaching prayer means not entering prayer while intoxicated.
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r13.anchor: لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى يقول لا تدخلوا

NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.claim: The two-fatḥa class contains 16 forms across 29 places; the list includes جاء أحد منكم, جاء أجلهم, جاء أمرنا, جاء آل, جاء أحدهم, and شاء أنشره.
NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.anchor: وأما المتفقتان فتحا، ففي ستة عشر لفظا في تسعة وعشرين موضعا

NASHR:v1p29/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p29/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p29/r8.claim: The reading أو لمستم النساء supports scholars who understand لمس as touching; the author adduces Quranic usage, a prophetic saying, and a poem whose verb ألمست means touch.
NASHR:v1p29/r8.anchor: ما يكون حجة بترجيح لقول بعض العلماء كقراءة (أو لمستم النساء) إذ اللمس يطلق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r3.claim: The citation from 4:43 is one of the examples linked to the preceding claim about using a word in literal and figurative senses.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r4.claim: The cited wording about touching women, with references to 4:43 and 5:6, is another example attached to the preceding discussion of literal and figurative usage.
